<subsection changed="added" id="H383AFCD608B5450A91CE47550A7D0860" class="indent0"><num value="r">(r) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definitions</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HFE17FEEC680F45A4A345DDD22AE02F73" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Appropriate congressional committees</inline>.—</heading><content>Unless otherwise defined in this Act, for purposes of this Act the term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means the Committees on Appropriations and Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committees on Appropriations and Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H0F93244585DC4C179C69992616E8CCE6" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Funds appropriated by this act and prior acts</inline>.—</heading><content>Unless otherwise defined in this Act, for purposes of this Act the term “<term>funds appropriated by this Act and prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs</term>” means funds that remain available for obligation, and have not expired.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HBDF33B566BAE48FB804DA1F26A3C8CBF" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">International financial institutions</inline>.—</heading><content>In this Act “international financial institutions” means the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the International Development Association, the International Finance Corporation, the Inter-American Development Bank, the International Monetary Fund, the International Fund for Agricultural Development, the Asian Development Fund, the Inter-American Investment Corporation, the North American Development Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the African Development Bank, the African Development Fund, and the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H08A8988D016D47DB9269AD71A306606A" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Southern kordofan</inline>.—</heading><content>Any reference to Southern Kordofan in this or any other Act making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs shall for this fiscal year, and each fiscal year thereafter, be deemed to include portions of Western Kordofan that were previously part of Southern Kordofan prior to the 2013 division of Southern Kordofan.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H42974A02994E481BB7073F9519D89D1A" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">USAID</inline>.—</heading><content>In this Act, the term “<term>USAID</term>” means the United States Agency for International Development.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HD1C447EAA6F643609C2729B6C4C75436" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Spend plan</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this Act, the term “<term>spend plan</term>” means a plan for the uses of funds appropriated for a particular entity, country, program, purpose, or account and which shall include, at a minimum, a description of—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H499CF0FAB77F4BC4BA131C42CB414D37" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>realistic and sustainable goals, criteria for measuring progress, and a timeline for achieving such goals;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H7188127EA96847F78C51C0650A23F56E" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>amounts and sources of funds by account;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HE8BC1D4D84824DE1B0FC9DE44FB8A4DD" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>how such funds will complement other ongoing or planned programs; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H289042AE03F547608388CB056492EAA5" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>implementing partners, to the maximum extent practicable.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA4BD9E22B802416EB67DA1C1BB67972E" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Successor operating unit</inline>.—</heading><content>Any reference to a particular USAID operating unit or office in this or prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs shall be deemed to include any successor operating unit or office performing the same or similar functions.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<appropriations level="small" changed="added" id="H2B4710CFBD2A4DF3B92ACC3BF83F45E3"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">law enforcement and security</inline></heading></appropriations>
<section changed="added" id="H36BEF82EE370431396594244CDB9F5D1"><num value="7035"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7035. </inline></num><subsection id="H0B54F7FDB53D4A75804784D6251EA4A3" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HA33D2E1E25194CE89C6B9E092A197045" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Community-based police assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds made available under titles III and IV of this Act to carry out the provisions of chapter 1 of part I and chapters 4 and 6 of part II of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, may be used, notwithstanding section 660 of that Act, to enhance the effectiveness and accountability of civilian police authority through training and technical assistance in human rights, the rule of law, anti-corruption, strategic planning, and through assistance to foster civilian police roles that support democratic governance, including assistance for programs to prevent conflict, respond to disasters, address gender-based violence, and foster improved police relations with the communities they serve.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H778117C1ADD14C6B9471FCC4FA2044E8" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Counterterrorism partnerships fund</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Nonproliferation, Anti-terrorism, Demining and Related Programs” shall be made available for the Counterterrorism Partnerships Fund for programs in areas liberated from, under the influence of, or adversely affected by, the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria or other terrorist organizations: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such areas shall include the Kurdistan Region of Iraq: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That prior to the obligation of funds made available pursuant to this paragraph, the Secretary of State shall take all practicable steps to ensure that mechanisms are in place for monitoring, oversight, and control of such funds: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That funds made available pursuant to this paragraph shall be subject to prior consultation with the appropriate congressional committees, and the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H8D0E38BEBB274F00A8296789266874C2" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Combat casualty care</inline>.—</heading><subparagraph id="H4EF6A282AAAD42F5AB0F659CFBE02463" class="inline"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Consistent with the objectives of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 and the Arms Export Control Act, funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “Peacekeeping Operations” and “Foreign Military Financing Program” shall be made available for combat casualty training and equipment.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HE936AA8B851F4E789C91215DE51AA4D3" class="indent1"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>The Secretary of State shall offer combat casualty care training and equipment as a component of any package of lethal assistance funded by this Act with funds appropriated under the headings “Peacekeeping Operations” and “Foreign Military Financing Program”: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the requirement of this subparagraph shall apply to a country in conflict, unless the Secretary determines that such country has in place, to the maximum extent practicable, functioning combat casualty care treatment and equipment that meets or exceeds the standards recommended by the Committee on Tactical Combat Casualty Care: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That any such training and equipment for combat casualty care shall be made available through an open and competitive process.</proviso></content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H424E11D5E0C745679528C406F3B840C8" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Training related to international humanitarian law</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State shall offer training related to the requirements of international humanitarian law as a component of any package of lethal assistance funded by this Act with funds appropriated under the headings “Peacekeeping Operations” and “Foreign Military Financing Program”: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the requirement of this paragraph shall not apply to a country that is a member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), is a major non-NATO ally designated by section 517(b) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, or is complying with international humanitarian law: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That any such training shall be made available through an open and competitive process.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H4DDA0B1AC7A94A92BA370B016ECCC283" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Security force professionalization</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement” and “Peacekeeping Operations” shall be made available to increase the capacity of foreign military and law enforcement personnel to operate in accordance with appropriate standards relating to human rights and the protection of civilians in the manner specified under this section in Senate Report 116–126, following consultation with the Committees on Appropriations: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That funds made available pursuant to this paragraph shall be made available through an open and competitive process.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H1CD4311EEAE04E99AC456BCFEAD8195A" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Global security contingency fund</inline>.—</heading><content>Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, up to $7,500,000 from funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “Peacekeeping Operations” and “Foreign Military Financing Program” may be transferred to, and merged with, funds previously made available under the heading “Global Security Contingency Fund”, subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H8FB0200D2C434346BFB96D8126FFFFA2" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">International prison conditions</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “Development Assistance”, “Economic Support Fund”, and “International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement”, not less than $7,500,000 shall be made available for assistance to eliminate inhumane conditions in foreign prisons and other detention facilities, notwithstanding section 660 of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the Secretary of State and the USAID Administrator shall consult with the Committees on Appropriations on the proposed uses of such funds prior to obligation and not later than 60 days after enactment of this Act: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That such funds shall be in addition to funds otherwise made available by this Act for such purpose.</proviso></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HA13A8927A0F4471B8F995B78F0AC2DD6" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorities</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H6A94DD4FF2E34BEEA3E7BB2401F0C67F" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reconstituting civilian police authority</inline>.—</heading><content>In providing assistance with funds appropriated by this Act under section 660(b)(6) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, support for a nation emerging from instability may be deemed to mean support for regional, district, municipal, or other sub-national entity emerging from instability, as well as a nation emerging from instability.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3270B350E2924649A1FBA39E759B374C" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 7034(d) of the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2015 (division J of Public Law 113–235) shall continue in effect during fiscal year 2020.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H52772CA0518F4FDDBF100CEEDA6B331D" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Extension of war reserves stockpile authority</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H808BD51D63AE459AAB051709461FD33B" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Section 12001(d) of the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2005 (Public Law 108–287; 118 Stat. 1011) is amended by striking “of this section” and all that follows through the period at the end and inserting “of this section after September 30, 2021.”.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H9028F8A28D8B40AC85BD0FA87FBE7115" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Section 514(b)(2)(A) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2321h(b)(2)(A)) is amended by striking “and 2020” and inserting “2020, and 2021”.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HEB629A921B5043D18CA6D16DFE74D260" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Commercial leasing of defense articles</inline>.—</heading><content>Notwithstanding any other provision of law, and subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations, the authority of section 23(a) of the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2763) may be used to provide financing to Israel, Egypt, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), and major non-NATO allies for the procurement by leasing (including leasing with an option to purchase) of defense articles from United States commercial suppliers, not including Major Defense Equipment (other than helicopters and other types of aircraft having possible civilian application), if the President determines that there are compelling foreign policy or national security reasons for those defense articles being provided by commercial lease rather than by government-to-government sale under such Act.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HADC9B3F666E84524ACE1E2F635D21D46" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Special defense acquisition fund</inline>.—</heading><content>Not to exceed $900,000,000 may be obligated pursuant to section 51(c)(2) of the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2795(c)(2)) for the purposes of the Special Defense Acquisition Fund (the Fund), to remain available for obligation until September 30, 2022: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the provision of defense articles and defense services to foreign countries or international organizations from the Fund shall be subject to the concurrence of the Secretary of State.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H7B6298D2D9AB4CEB8BBA33432A85CC47" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Public disclosure</inline>.—</heading><content>For the purposes of funds appropriated by this Act and prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs that are made available for assistance for units of foreign security forces, the term “<term>to the maximum extent practicable</term>” in section 620M(d)(7) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2378d) means that the identity of such units shall be made publicly available unless the Secretary of State, on a case-by-case basis, determines and reports to the appropriate congressional committees that disclosure would endanger the safety of human sources or reveal sensitive intelligence sources and methods, or that non-disclosure is in the national security interest of the United States: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That any such determination shall include a detailed justification, and may be submitted in classified form.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H78C69CCD09044BB3B455C2BD1FD349B9" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Duty to inform</inline>.—</heading><content>If assistance to a foreign security force is provided in a manner in which the recipient unit or units cannot be identified prior to the transfer of assistance, the Secretary of State shall provide a list of units prohibited from receiving such assistance pursuant to section 620M of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to the recipient government.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H555F74A77B4D4E1DBFEB32A44DE28605" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitations</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H2D9052F9B3214946842EABC9F9365705" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Child soldiers</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act should not be used to support any military training or operations that include child soldiers.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5AD29DC7271247F4AAB21C56E98C9575" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Landmines and cluster munitions</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H9C8271D010B24C1A93515C5101BA9B9B" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Landmines</inline>.—</heading><content>Notwithstanding any other provision of law, demining equipment available to the United States Agency for International Development and the Department of State and used in support of the clearance of landmines and unexploded ordnance for humanitarian purposes may be disposed of on a grant basis in foreign countries, subject to such terms and conditions as the Secretary of State may prescribe.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H02EC58B0779D4B76805440BFE0876B3B" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Cluster munitions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>No military assistance shall be furnished for cluster munitions, no defense export license for cluster munitions may be issued, and no cluster munitions or cluster munitions technology shall be sold or transferred, unless—</chapeau>
<clause id="H57F7E43E3C5D45D4BD334F129F5F7116" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>the submunitions of the cluster munitions, after arming, do not result in more than 1 percent unexploded ordnance across the range of intended operational environments, and the agreement applicable to the assistance, transfer, or sale of such cluster munitions or cluster munitions technology specifies that the cluster munitions will only be used against clearly defined military targets and will not be used where civilians are known to be present or in areas normally inhabited by civilians; or</content></clause>
<clause id="HA7A09740BA8141EBBA201F5A5BB3EF47" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>such assistance, license, sale, or transfer is for the purpose of demilitarizing or permanently disposing of such cluster munitions.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE474890BD16E41A79116B45015B9DE5E" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Crowd control items</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act should not be used for tear gas, small arms, light weapons, ammunition, or other items for crowd control purposes for foreign security forces that use excessive force to repress peaceful expression, association, or assembly in countries that the Secretary of State determines are undemocratic or are undergoing democratic transitions.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H6B75547188734ECB9E4ED3C0BCE94E8E" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reports</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H4F1FC64C59F7455DAAF11B9F4F3C52E8" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Security assistance report</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 120 days after enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations a report on funds obligated and expended during fiscal year 2019, by country and purpose of assistance, under the headings “Peacekeeping Operations”, “International Military Education and Training”, and “Foreign Military Financing Program”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HE9209C9808284518BB86D1297FDF8260" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Annual foreign military training report</inline>.—</heading><content>For the purposes of implementing section 656 of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, the term “<term>military training provided to foreign military personnel by the Department of Defense and the Department of State</term>” shall be deemed to include all military training provided by foreign governments with funds appropriated to the Department of Defense or the Department of State, except for training provided by the government of a country designated by section 517(b) of such Act (22 U.S.C. 2321k(b)) as a major non-North Atlantic Treaty Organization ally.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<appropriations level="small" changed="added" id="H2837825B50144C1197C4CAAD63458EB9"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">arab league boycott of israel</inline></heading></appropriations>
<section changed="added" id="HF5C0C4D5B644478A8FA557AD3F99B291"><num value="7036"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7036. </inline></num><chapeau class="inline">It is the sense of the Congress that—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H31D9142D31CB426C91AA318C73C940D8" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the Arab League boycott of Israel, and the secondary boycott of American firms that have commercial ties with Israel, is an impediment to peace in the region and to United States investment and trade in the Middle East and North Africa;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H978EBCF0D5C84477822A7B2CB9C86BF6" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the Arab League boycott, which was regrettably reinstated in 1997, should be immediately and publicly terminated, and the Central Office for the Boycott of Israel immediately disbanded;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD1F481C4DC4D45E1B6AB5AF79B7397F6" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>all Arab League states should normalize relations with their neighbor Israel;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3E3316448F494B269FD3CA63AFF24D39" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>the President and the Secretary of State should continue to vigorously oppose the Arab League boycott of Israel and find concrete steps to demonstrate that opposition by, for example, taking into consideration the participation of any recipient country in the boycott when determining to sell weapons to said country; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HEE37FCD29C2A4499984B89A38587497F" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>the President should report to Congress annually on specific steps being taken by the United States to encourage Arab League states to normalize their relations with Israel to bring about the termination of the Arab League boycott of Israel, including those to encourage allies and trading partners of the United States to enact laws prohibiting businesses from complying with the boycott and penalizing businesses that do comply.</content></paragraph></section>
<appropriations level="small" changed="added" id="HF922B5D53A6A494EAC34F10927876EDF"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">palestinian statehood</inline></heading></appropriations>
<section changed="added" id="H77948F677B5C4B2B8FF1949F276579AE"><num value="7037"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7037. </inline></num><subsection id="H55F4564726874392A7384FBA022B4C5A" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitation on Assistance</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>None of the funds appropriated under titles III through VI of this Act may be provided to support a Palestinian state unless the Secretary of State determines and certifies to the appropriate congressional committees that—</chapeau>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H41A06111B9A34526BF3568D917B51846" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><chapeau>the governing entity of a new Palestinian state—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HB965004F9611448582170C9B2196A79B" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>has demonstrated a firm commitment to peaceful co-existence with the State of Israel; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H1B18B513613142F997EEC732A25B4CD0" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>is taking appropriate measures to counter terrorism and terrorist financing in the West Bank and Gaza, including the dismantling of terrorist infrastructures, and is cooperating with appropriate Israeli and other appropriate security organizations; and</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H74171716DED2498AA3D83101C57C6C9E" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><chapeau>the Palestinian Authority (or the governing entity of a new Palestinian state) is working with other countries in the region to vigorously pursue efforts to establish a just, lasting, and comprehensive peace in the Middle East that will enable Israel and an independent Palestinian state to exist within the context of full and normal relationships, which should include—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H03A9D9A3F9E84F788119E95268B24AF9" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>termination of all claims or states of belligerency;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HB6DFA451C3A349BE90505A8C9D657AA4" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>respect for and acknowledgment of the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of every state in the area through measures including the establishment of demilitarized zones;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HE269ABA555CF47A2809A548E375E005C" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>their right to live in peace within secure and recognized boundaries free from threats or acts of force;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H7DEE38204A454F238330D661FCF3A664" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>freedom of navigation through international waterways in the area; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H7B8A903E61DC423394F0EB083C0080F0" class="indent2"><num value="E">(E) </num><content>a framework for achieving a just settlement of the refugee problem.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H503C9024C8224BB983E47B28361E0FDF" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><content>It is the sense of Congress that the governing entity should enact a constitution assuring the rule of law, an independent judiciary, and respect for human rights for its citizens, and should enact other laws and regulations assuring transparent and accountable governance.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H3E037B131E6D4E219457F7726FF54F07" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Waiver</inline>.—</heading><content>The President may waive subsection (a) if the President determines that it is important to the national security interest of the United States to do so.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HF77D9FCDE9444998BA0CF5484A3AC85D" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exemption</inline>.—</heading><content>The restriction in subsection (a) shall not apply to assistance intended to help reform the Palestinian Authority and affiliated institutions, or the governing entity, in order to help meet the requirements of subsection (a), consistent with the provisions of section 7040 of this Act (“Limitation on Assistance for the Palestinian Authority”).</content></subsection></section>
<appropriations level="small" changed="added" id="HA00005BB3ADD4EF7BA6DB1B9692F2D5A"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">prohibition on assistance to the palestinian broadcasting corporation</inline></heading></appropriations>
<section changed="added" id="H2512E6A37F0E4B5BAB00E540B049A5A9"><num value="7038"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7038. </inline></num><chapeau class="inline">None of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available by this Act may be used to provide equipment, technical support, consulting services, or any other form of assistance to the Palestinian Broadcasting Corporation.</chapeau>
<appropriations level="small" id="H427312E4C4104D869AF236A99E02893A"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">assistance for the west bank and gaza</inline></heading></appropriations></section>
<section changed="added" id="H16C9AAF57E0847A5B35A1DBA45565D90"><num value="7039"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7039. </inline></num><subsection id="HA576F72F417D4944913BCEA8AFF4F581" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Oversight</inline>.—</heading><content>For fiscal year 2020, 30 days prior to the initial obligation of funds for the bilateral West Bank and Gaza Program, the Secretary of State shall certify to the Committees on Appropriations that procedures have been established to assure the Comptroller General of the United States will have access to appropriate United States financial information in order to review the uses of United States assistance for the Program funded under the heading “Economic Support Fund” for the West Bank and Gaza.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H5B1AA2F1F4E643A292AC74B1CB0107FB" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Vetting</inline>.—</heading><content>Prior to the obligation of funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Economic Support Fund” for assistance for the West Bank and Gaza, the Secretary of State shall take all appropriate steps to ensure that such assistance is not provided to or through any individual, private or government entity, or educational institution that the Secretary knows or has reason to believe advocates, plans, sponsors, engages in, or has engaged in, terrorist activity nor, with respect to private entities or educational institutions, those that have as a principal officer of the entity’s governing board or governing board of trustees any individual that has been determined to be involved in, or advocating terrorist activity or determined to be a member of a designated foreign terrorist organization: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the Secretary of State shall, as appropriate, establish procedures specifying the steps to be taken in carrying out this subsection and shall terminate assistance to any individual, entity, or educational institution which the Secretary has determined to be involved in or advocating terrorist activity.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection id="HFA7202ABCC5C4864BED9EECAA3D6B477" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prohibition</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HF4FDC9EFDE6B4760B5E7A87A5076A930" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Recognition of acts of terrorism</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>None of the funds appropriated under titles III through VI of this Act for assistance under the West Bank and Gaza Program may be made available for—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HB7FF7CCCF1114E4296413CE50D4E108B" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the purpose of recognizing or otherwise honoring individuals who commit, or have committed acts of terrorism; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H8603AB12336B4194928CBF03A50AAD8C" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>any educational institution located in the West Bank or Gaza that is named after an individual who the Secretary of State determines has committed an act of terrorism.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF7DD8A04975A44F49BB8A7EA5A2CD90A" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Security assistance and reporting requirement</inline>.—</heading><content>Notwithstanding any other provision of law, none of the funds made available by this or prior appropriations Acts, including funds made available by transfer, may be made available for obligation for security assistance for the West Bank and Gaza until the Secretary of State reports to the Committees on Appropriations on the benchmarks that have been established for security assistance for the West Bank and Gaza and reports on the extent of Palestinian compliance with such benchmarks.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H99FDFA2036D24B8C831AC78E32311726" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Oversight by the United States Agency for International Development</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H332709D8347540AD823ABB27901309F0" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>The Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development shall ensure that Federal or non-Federal audits of all contractors and grantees, and significant subcontractors and sub-grantees, under the West Bank and Gaza Program, are conducted at least on an annual basis to ensure, among other things, compliance with this section.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H00EB6E76D29A40DC9ABA8C59C39730B2" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act, up to $1,000,000 may be used by the Office of Inspector General of the United States Agency for International Development for audits, investigations, and other activities in furtherance of the requirements of this subsection: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds are in addition to funds otherwise available for such purposes.</proviso></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HF6D4B851CEA540F7AEB550F9182385C4" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Comptroller General of the United States Audit</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Subsequent to the certification specified in subsection (a), the Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct an audit and an investigation of the treatment, handling, and uses of all funds for the bilateral West Bank and Gaza Program, including all funds provided as cash transfer assistance, in fiscal year 2020 under the heading “Economic Support Fund”, and such audit shall address—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HDBDB5752002049E79E42F9ADE5D26264" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the extent to which such Program complies with the requirements of subsections (b) and (c); and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5A1F111781FA4076AAC5EB1C46516E2B" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>an examination of all programs, projects, and activities carried out under such Program, including both obligations and expenditures.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H86A9D2CD6C814742BA83EF8E4D0A7F2C" class="indent0"><num value="f">(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Notification Procedures</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds made available in this Act for West Bank and Gaza shall be subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</content></subsection></section>
<appropriations level="small" changed="added" id="H12ED4B50E9224D5B829292E149BDE5C4"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">limitation on assistance for the palestinian authority</inline></heading></appropriations>
<section changed="added" id="H8C7990F85B6040BCA756D7B3627221F1"><num value="7040"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7040. </inline></num><subsection id="H699EC361776A472A86F660086AB4A378" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prohibition of Funds</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act to carry out the provisions of chapter 4 of part II of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 may be obligated or expended with respect to providing funds to the Palestinian Authority.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H1CCAAC0E3A08463F8B506635815FAFD3" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Waiver</inline>.—</heading><content>The prohibition included in subsection (a) shall not apply if the President certifies in writing to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the President pro tempore of the Senate, and the Committees on Appropriations that waiving such prohibition is important to the national security interest of the United States.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HF9E13E072B2E4554AA04D2B3107F13B3" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Period of Application of Waiver</inline>.—</heading><content>Any waiver pursuant to subsection (b) shall be effective for no more than a period of 6 months at a time and shall not apply beyond 12 months after the enactment of this Act.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H8DBE476AF1184E0DA5BE973F8DB16537" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report</inline>.—</heading><content>Whenever the waiver authority pursuant to subsection (b) is exercised, the President shall submit a report to the Committees on Appropriations detailing the justification for the waiver, the purposes for which the funds will be spent, and the accounting procedures in place to ensure that the funds are properly disbursed: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the report shall also detail the steps the Palestinian Authority has taken to arrest terrorists, confiscate weapons and dismantle the terrorist infrastructure.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H57BD384B4B5D4B0D9EAC2566956F6D4F" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Certification</inline>.—</heading><content>If the President exercises the waiver authority under subsection (b), the Secretary of State must certify and report to the Committees on Appropriations prior to the obligation of funds that the Palestinian Authority has established a single treasury account for all Palestinian Authority financing and all financing mechanisms flow through this account, no parallel financing mechanisms exist outside of the Palestinian Authority treasury account, and there is a single comprehensive civil service roster and payroll, and the Palestinian Authority is acting to counter incitement of violence against Israelis and is supporting activities aimed at promoting peace, coexistence, and security cooperation with Israel.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HE2280B1C9F9E4E57A8A6A09F2DD795A5" class="indent0"><num value="f">(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prohibition to Hamas and the Palestine Liberation Organization</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H78E8AEEBD06E4DE491C963E887D0328C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>None of the funds appropriated in titles III through VI of this Act may be obligated for salaries of personnel of the Palestinian Authority located in Gaza or may be obligated or expended for assistance to Hamas or any entity effectively controlled by Hamas, any power-sharing government of which Hamas is a member, or that results from an agreement with Hamas and over which Hamas exercises undue influence.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HAE1E91D61E2D42D6A71EDCD0ECF72CDC" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Notwithstanding the limitation of paragraph (1), assistance may be provided to a power-sharing government only if the President certifies and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that such government, including all of its ministers or such equivalent, has publicly accepted and is complying with the principles contained in section 620K(b)(1) (A) and (B) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, as amended.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H37228B0ADB75456BB45B68E98A6B1530" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>The President may exercise the authority in section 620K(e) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, as added by the Palestinian Anti-Terrorism Act of 2006 (Public Law 109–446) with respect to this subsection.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HED203F4AE1EB4D5FA70B83CED2821C58" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>Whenever the certification pursuant to paragraph (2) is exercised, the Secretary of State shall submit a report to the Committees on Appropriations within 120 days of the certification and every quarter thereafter on whether such government, including all of its ministers or such equivalent are continuing to comply with the principles contained in section 620K(b)(1) (A) and (B) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, as amended: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the report shall also detail the amount, purposes and delivery mechanisms for any assistance provided pursuant to the abovementioned certification and a full accounting of any direct support of such government.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFE37F2B7AF3B43CC8E692EDDF91798BD" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>None of the funds appropriated under titles III through VI of this Act may be obligated for assistance for the Palestine Liberation Organization.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<appropriations level="small" changed="added" id="HBDDEBB6317E6492488F35CAABBBFA2CD"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">middle east and north africa</inline></heading></appropriations>
<section changed="added" id="HAD814E34254D4C1E855FD9C97D78C7B8"><num value="7041"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7041. </inline></num><subsection id="HC2D2D74636A34C0DA6F8EF2583A91911" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Egypt</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HB1F01A6C23B146C3BEAD3D1BD0D22E48" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Certification and report</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Funds appropriated by this Act that are available for assistance for Egypt may be made available notwithstanding any other provision of law restricting assistance for Egypt, except for this subsection and section 620M of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, and may only be made available for assistance for the Government of Egypt if the Secretary of State certifies and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that such government is—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H45C120760D1F42E591214770FE22B63A" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>sustaining the strategic relationship with the United States; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H85AA0571985F4A60B43F026E72AB8E2B" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>meeting its obligations under the 1979 Egypt-Israel Peace Treaty.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HDB1974FA4133488780550A37246DA7C1" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Economic support fund</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Economic Support Fund”, not less than $125,000,000 shall be made available for assistance for Egypt, of which not less than $40,000,000 should be made available for higher education programs, including not less than $15,000,000 for scholarships for Egyptian students with high financial need to attend not-for-profit institutions of higher education in Egypt that are currently accredited by a regional accrediting agency recognized by the United States Department of Education, or meets standards equivalent to those required for United States institutional accreditation by a regional accrediting agency recognized by such Department: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds shall be made available for democracy programs, and for development programs in the Sinai: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That such funds may not be made available for cash transfer assistance or budget support unless the Secretary of State certifies and reports to the appropriate congressional committees that the Government of Egypt is taking consistent and effective steps to stabilize the economy and implement market-based economic reforms.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H3006A82B3F2D43E1AE540EA681A8E297" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Foreign military financing program</inline>.—</heading><subparagraph id="H09E3C89B9D20405CA5845EA956C6D5F4" class="inline"><num value="A">(A) </num><chapeau>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Foreign Military Financing Program”, $1,300,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2021, should be made available for assistance for Egypt: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds may be transferred to an interest bearing account in the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, following consultation with the Committees on Appropriations, and the uses of any interest earned on such funds shall be subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That $300,000,000 of such funds shall be withheld from obligation until the Secretary of State certifies and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that the Government of Egypt is taking sustained and effective steps to—</proviso></chapeau>
<clause changed="added" id="HB5396073FE78400A82D7270D7CB87DAE" class="indent2"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>strengthen the rule of law, democratic institutions, and human rights in Egypt, including to protect religious minorities and the rights of women, which are in addition to steps taken during the previous calendar year for such purposes;</content></clause>
<clause changed="added" id="HFC454516C66843C5A4D5E03B36EAF8B8" class="indent2"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>implement reforms that protect freedoms of expression, association, and peaceful assembly, including the ability of civil society organizations, human rights defenders, and the media to function without interference;</content></clause>
<clause changed="added" id="H439A89587B1E49ED944778BB1C5496AB" class="indent2"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>release political prisoners and provide detainees with due process of law;</content></clause>
<clause changed="added" id="H5F7A066250D3404F9243CF0F03BDF9A1" class="indent2"><num value="iv">(iv) </num><content>hold Egyptian security forces accountable, including officers credibly alleged to have violated human rights;</content></clause>
<clause changed="added" id="H60928946C83B462B908C19034ED67ACA" class="indent2"><num value="v">(v) </num><content>investigate and prosecute cases of extrajudicial killings and forced disappearances; and</content></clause>
<clause changed="added" id="H4C177381437B49208F46E9474A49E323" class="indent2"><num value="vi">(vi) </num><content>provide regular access for United States officials to monitor such assistance in areas where the assistance is used:</content></clause></subparagraph>
<continuation class="indent0" changed="added" role="paragraph"> <proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That the certification requirement of this paragraph shall not apply to funds appropriated by this Act under such heading for counterterrorism, border security, and nonproliferation programs for Egypt.</proviso></continuation>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HF8679142A63E4E05BDD12CFB80C74C61" class="indent1"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>The Secretary of State may waive the certification requirement in subparagraph (A) if the Secretary determines and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that to do so is important to the national security interest of the United States, and submits a report to such Committees containing a detailed justification for the use of such waiver and the reasons why any of the requirements of subparagraph (A) cannot be met: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the report required by this paragraph shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may be accompanied by a classified annex.</proviso></content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HC9EF4483756F4322AB7A99D3B1DC41BC" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 30 days after enactment of this Act, and every 60 days thereafter, the Secretary of State shall submit a report to the appropriate congressional committees describing and assessing the actions taken by the Government of Egypt during the previous 60 days to fairly compensate April Corley for injuries and losses sustained as a result of the attack on her tour group by the Egyptian military on September 13, 2015, and progress in resolving her case: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That if the Secretary reports that no progress has been made in the previous 60 days, the report shall include the reasons for the lack of progress.</proviso></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H5CCD51C67834434BB6DAE19D2C17E6F3" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Iran</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H8AF00C7B6576491797A4F800F2AE5F4B" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Funding</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “Diplomatic Programs”, “Economic Support Fund”, and “Nonproliferation, Anti-terrorism, Demining and Related Programs” shall be made available for the programs and activities described under this section in House Report 116–78.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA2090D2768134ABB85FA58F6D30BB0D3" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reports</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="HED84DA80FCF349C1A1DC70E5F805092E" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Semi-annual report</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations the semi-annual report required by section 135(d)(4) of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (42 U.S.C. 2160e(d)(4)), as added by section 2 of the Iran Nuclear Agreement Review Act of 2015 (Public Law 114–17).</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H4BC30C0352BA4D168BBB4FCD85780C1B" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sanctions report</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report on—</chapeau>
<clause id="H0A35801D7823454F8BDD9A772E547DC6" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>the status of United States bilateral sanctions on Iran;</content></clause>
<clause id="HF0374E5397A04459B5E09929A9B57931" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>the reimposition and renewed enforcement of secondary sanctions; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H18D07FB3F7F8459981F0AA54A1ED4FD3" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>the impact such sanctions have had on Iran’s destabilizing activities throughout the Middle East.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H260F1FA3C4A24D85B14F0F1803FE9468" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Iraq</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HE44EACE159D541D881943D92B1A60D9A" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Purposes</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Funds appropriated under titles III and IV of this Act shall be made available for assistance for Iraq for—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H05A641473BBE4E7C96BED8C4E596E261" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>bilateral economic assistance and international security assistance, including in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq and for the Marla Ruzicka Iraqi War Victims Fund;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H3479B24E6287483DADE595C20B97C291" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>stabilization assistance, including in Anbar Province;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H4ACF4E68AD864B00AC393781619A2C24" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>humanitarian assistance, including in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H1DF297D4FD7042A6999F742AD41C6265" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>programs to protect and assist religious and ethnic minority populations in Iraq, including as described under this section in the explanatory statement described in section 4 (in the matter preceding division A of this consolidated Act).</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFBC09DDEC32D4C5E9E562C21DD5173EA" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">United states consulate general basrah</inline>.—</heading><content>Any change in the status of operations at United States Consulate General Basrah, including the return of Consulate property located adjacent to the Basrah International Airport to the Government of Iraq, shall be subject to prior consultation with the appropriate congressional committees and the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF309F7AB2B574C289ADE679F552DAA7E" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Basing rights agreement</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available by this Act may be used by the Government of the United States to enter into a permanent basing rights agreement between the United States and Iraq.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H3DBC478B1F514B91BF74C8F8B614135E" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Jordan</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H034CA0D2149447668A7465D5861F61A3" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance appropriated by this act</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under titles III and IV, not less than $1,525,000,000 shall be made available for assistance for Jordan, of which: not less than $1,082,400,000 shall be made available under the heading “Economic Support Fund”, of which not less than $745,100,000 shall be made available for budget support for the Government of Jordan; and not less than $425,000,000 shall be made available under the heading “Foreign Military Financing Program”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H259104D7747D43F9A8E2C39EA9283A29" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance appropriated by prior acts</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated under the heading “Economic Support Fund” in prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs, not less than $125,000,000 shall be made available for assistance for Jordan, of which $100,000,000 shall be made available for budget support for the Government of Jordan and $25,000,000 shall be made available for programs to increase electricity transmission to neighboring countries, including Iraq: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds are in addition to amounts otherwise made available for such purposes.</proviso></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HAD4D7D3CB43F4ADE9272E88028F905B2" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Lebanon</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HD7582DE735FD43788E69281CAA252553" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated under titles III and IV of this Act shall be made available for assistance for Lebanon: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds made available under the heading “Economic Support Fund” may be made available notwithstanding section 1224 of the Foreign Relations Authorization Act, Fiscal Year 2003 (Public Law 107–228; 22 U.S.C. 2346 note).</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1DC5E80A9EC4425DA8273388BDE9FD6F" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Security assistance</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H755072197CF54952919CC70A3DD74DE8" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement” and “Foreign Military Financing Program” that are made available for assistance for Lebanon may be made available for programs and equipment for the Lebanese Internal Security Forces (ISF) and the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) to address security and stability requirements in areas affected by conflict in Syria, following consultation with the appropriate congressional committees.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H3404AD6E0EDA49CD8679551A3D406A46" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><chapeau>Funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Foreign Military Financing Program” that are made available for assistance for Lebanon may only be made available for programs to—</chapeau>
<clause id="HAE46445ADF9E4D3B989D72B4C6124D2F" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>professionalize the LAF to mitigate internal and external threats from non-state actors, including Hizballah;</content></clause>
<clause id="HED53665096A842E9B7700ABAED8FC53F" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>strengthen border security and combat terrorism, including training and equipping the LAF to secure the borders of Lebanon and address security and stability requirements in areas affected by conflict in Syria, interdicting arms shipments, and preventing the use of Lebanon as a safe haven for terrorist groups; and</content></clause>
<clause id="HA5AD02E6BCDB47358C72823D719D25E9" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>implement United Nations Security Council Resolution 1701:</content></clause>
<continuation class="indent0" role="subparagraph"> <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That prior to obligating funds made available by this subparagraph for assistance for the LAF, the Secretary of State shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations a spend plan, including actions to be taken to ensure equipment provided to the LAF is used only for the intended purposes, except such plan may not be considered as meeting the notification requirements under section 7015 of this Act or under section 634A of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, and shall be submitted not later than September 1, 2020: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That any notification submitted pursuant to such section shall include any funds specifically intended for lethal military equipment.</proviso></continuation></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H85220B5EF0624F1F874E5CBDC4858620" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitation</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act may be made available for the ISF or the LAF if the ISF or the LAF is controlled by a foreign terrorist organization, as designated pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1189).</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HBF93EC23B21B4DF39638099DCB2CD974" class="indent0"><num value="f">(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Libya</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H2A5A9557FD3C46408EF4EF0905B28E07" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated under titles III and IV of this Act shall be made available for stabilization assistance for Libya, including support for a United Nations-facilitated political process and border security: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the limitation on the uses of funds for certain infrastructure projects in section 7041(f)(2) of the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2014 (division K of Public Law 113–76) shall apply to such funds.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H046AE15E6190471E9BE8D9EA8A53138F" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Certification</inline>.—</heading><content>Prior to the initial obligation of funds made available by this Act for assistance for Libya, the Secretary of State shall certify and report to the Committees on Appropriations that all practicable steps have been taken to ensure that mechanisms are in place for monitoring, oversight, and control of such funds.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H938EE97044E44C8ABF82C9D488745D3A" class="indent0"><num value="g">(g) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Morocco</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H4CF5BC7C3B1242478E4B49BEDD8F35B3" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Availability and consultation requirement</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated under title III of this Act shall be made available for assistance for the Western Sahara: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That not later than 90 days after enactment of this Act and prior to the obligation of such funds, the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, shall consult with the Committees on Appropriations on the proposed uses of such funds.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD54EF42042CA4E1BBBF6E01214818100" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Foreign military financing program</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Foreign Military Financing Program” that are available for assistance for Morocco may only be used for the purposes requested in the Congressional Budget Justification, Foreign Operations, Fiscal Year 2017.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HFFCE61E3F0894C3BAEE9CF4523877391" class="indent0"><num value="h">(h) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Saudi Arabia</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HCA6837A10376479F9F34B31E8E4A5B6D" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">International military education and training</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “International Military Education and Training” may be made available for assistance for the Government of Saudi Arabia.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HED2B201AACA3496CBCF356E675DAEB85" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Export-import bank</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>None of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available by this Act and prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs should be obligated or expended by the Export-Import Bank of the United States to guarantee, insure, or extend (or participate in the extension of) credit in connection with the export of nuclear technology, equipment, fuel, materials, or other nuclear technology-related goods or services to Saudi Arabia unless the Government of Saudi Arabia—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HEFC0697539BE47DEA850A0E1CC7D64F8" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>has in effect a nuclear cooperation agreement pursuant to section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (42 U.S.C. 2153);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H05E8087EF61D4B4682772A3A8A43594D" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>has committed to renounce uranium enrichment and reprocessing on its territory under that agreement; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD270E6E4ECC4431DB73D322EFF8C85BA" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>has signed and implemented an Additional Protocol to its Comprehensive Safeguards Agreement with the International Atomic Energy Agency.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HAF6F621A8B5E45C99E4B772E9BF44FB1" class="indent0"><num value="i">(i) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Syria</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H7529C4E7413F4FF897DAF945108DFD04" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Non-lethal assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “Economic Support Fund”, “International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement”, and “Peacekeeping Operations”, not less than $40,000,000 shall be made available, notwithstanding any other provision of law, for non-lethal stabilization assistance for Syria, of which not less than $7,000,000 shall be made available for emergency medical and rescue response and chemical weapons use investigations.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H7A8C0F22305F4F6592FFEFE6F1F72C3D" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitations</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Funds made available pursuant to paragraph (1) of this subsection—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H76690B01BEE64B6B8CE785482F273BB9" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>may not be made available for a project or activity that supports or otherwise legitimizes the Government of Iran, foreign terrorist organizations (as designated pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1189)), or a proxy of Iran in Syria;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H51EF20C157F14D7EA44BEB25F3F00DB4" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>may not be made available for activities that further the strategic objectives of the Government of the Russian Federation that the Secretary of State determines may threaten or undermine United States national security interests; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HE4FEEF3E98CE4CDFAB803D6F54A7A09D" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>should not be used in areas of Syria controlled by a government led by Bashar al-Assad or associated forces.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6F679B2081004168A532524F8AC2C538" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Monitoring and oversight</inline>.—</heading><content>Prior to the obligation of any funds appropriated by this Act and made available for assistance for Syria, the Secretary of State shall take all practicable steps to ensure that mechanisms are in place for monitoring, oversight, and control of such assistance inside Syria.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4508382FBED14BA4858865ADF85DA57A" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Consultation and notification</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds made available pursuant to this subsection may only be made available following consultation with the appropriate congressional committees, and shall be subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H25573F7EBEBD4B91B402F41663D3FA95" class="indent0"><num value="j">(j) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Tunisia</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H7EDF2E0125014BE7A634A8A9EC7E0293" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance appropriated by this act</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated under titles III and IV of this Act, not less than $191,400,000 shall be made available for assistance for Tunisia.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HDE2CADEED7CE40FC97A004E6185A7A7D" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance appropriated by prior acts</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated under the heading “Economic Support Fund” in prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs, not less than $50,000,000 shall be made available for assistance for Tunisia: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds are in addition to amounts otherwise made available for such purposes.</proviso></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HD0D5D902D680443FB90AAF458AC9BB7E" class="indent0"><num value="k">(k) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">West Bank and Gaza</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HD7621EB492C44711A55D0A0C6168F039" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report on assistance</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Prior to the initial obligation of funds made available by this Act under the heading “Economic Support Fund” for assistance for the West Bank and Gaza, the Secretary of State shall report to the Committees on Appropriations that the purpose of such assistance is to—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HBD3133048D934AE587987D45D560D3FB" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>advance Middle East peace;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HEC2AED0B24D54A23865C9B85BDB136D8" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>improve security in the region;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HE12496E882AC468EB9078C16D25CD792" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>continue support for transparent and accountable government institutions;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HEB55BA5CAB4B48FA8C29D3F2C155C5C2" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>promote a private sector economy; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HBD73C51B765C431788A1AB3ADC01EA65" class="indent2"><num value="E">(E) </num><content>address urgent humanitarian needs.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA8D65A5CE1D54D718E6087A3132D098E" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitations</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H6977D64C3E0647509E339E3CF74E34AC" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A)</num><clause id="H998164421BBC43DD965894614ADF6D3B" class="inline"><num value="i">(i) </num><chapeau>None of the funds appropriated under the heading “Economic Support Fund” in this Act may be made available for assistance for the Palestinian Authority, if after the date of enactment of this Act—</chapeau>
<subclause changed="added" id="H6CAE56844B5E41CA8978C6D85735B986" class="indent3"><num value="I">(I) </num><content>the Palestinians obtain the same standing as member states or full membership as a state in the United Nations or any specialized agency thereof outside an agreement negotiated between Israel and the Palestinians; or</content></subclause>
<subclause changed="added" id="H1875038AECCB4801AD113D508F78743C" class="indent3"><num value="II">(II) </num><content>the Palestinians initiate an International Criminal Court (ICC) judicially authorized investigation, or actively support such an investigation, that subjects Israeli nationals to an investigation for alleged crimes against Palestinians.</content></subclause></clause>
<clause changed="added" id="H7044119007E54EC19B3B1F18D748829B" class="indent2"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>The Secretary of State may waive the restriction in clause (i) of this subparagraph resulting from the application of subclause (I) of such clause if the Secretary certifies to the Committees on Appropriations that to do so is in the national security interest of the United States, and submits a report to such Committees detailing how the waiver and the continuation of assistance would assist in furthering Middle East peace.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H849F70B36E874D3D9A5075A58F249271" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B)</num><clause id="H51383532FF7E400EB33E085E40B90745" class="inline"><num value="i">(i) </num><chapeau>The President may waive the provisions of section 1003 of the Foreign Relations Authorization Act, Fiscal Years 1988 and 1989 (Public Law 100–204) if the President determines and certifies in writing to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the President pro tempore of the Senate, and the appropriate congressional committees that the Palestinians have not, after the date of enactment of this Act—</chapeau>
<subclause changed="added" id="HF906E28051D047EEBE3DC4C04724F855" class="indent3"><num value="I">(I) </num><content>obtained in the United Nations or any specialized agency thereof the same standing as member states or full membership as a state outside an agreement negotiated between Israel and the Palestinians; and</content></subclause>
<subclause changed="added" id="H43E418AF22194BCCBF17FEC271FC4073" class="indent3"><num value="II">(II) </num><content>initiated or actively supported an ICC investigation against Israeli nationals for alleged crimes against Palestinians.</content></subclause></clause>
<clause changed="added" id="H9F729717A44240C3AC25A69F9B9D01A8" class="indent2"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>Not less than 90 days after the President is unable to make the certification pursuant to clause (i) of this subparagraph, the President may waive section 1003 of Public Law 100–204 if the President determines and certifies in writing to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the President pro tempore of the Senate, and the Committees on Appropriations that the Palestinians have entered into direct and meaningful negotiations with Israel: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That any waiver of the provisions of section 1003 of Public Law 100–204 under clause (i) of this subparagraph or under previous provisions of law must expire before the waiver under the preceding sentence may be exercised.</proviso></content></clause>
<clause changed="added" id="H0C0F20EA1DF54E7CA0B7B0B74930697E" class="indent2"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>Any waiver pursuant to this subparagraph shall be effective for no more than a period of 6 months at a time and shall not apply beyond 12 months after the enactment of this Act.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H73CEC1527FFE46EFBDFB663524241DCD" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reduction</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State shall reduce the amount of assistance made available by this Act under the heading “Economic Support Fund” for the Palestinian Authority by an amount the Secretary determines is equivalent to the amount expended by the Palestinian Authority, the Palestine Liberation Organization, and any successor or affiliated organizations with such entities as payments for acts of terrorism by individuals who are imprisoned after being fairly tried and convicted for acts of terrorism and by individuals who died committing acts of terrorism during the previous calendar year: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the Secretary shall report to the Committees on Appropriations on the amount reduced for fiscal year 2020 prior to the obligation of funds for the Palestinian Authority.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4650685664E44245A696242159F4EF29" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Private sector partnership programs</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act and prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs may be made available for private sector partnership programs for the West Bank and Gaza if such funds are authorized: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That funds made available pursuant to this paragraph shall be subject to prior consultation with the appropriate congressional committees, and the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCA14AF0159144045829F998690A7D240" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Security report</inline>.—</heading><content>The reporting requirements in section 1404 of the Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2008 (Public Law 110–252) shall apply to funds made available by this Act, including a description of modifications, if any, to the security strategy of the Palestinian Authority.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H90D6B6BABDDD459FB09BAB69F6245FDA" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Incitement report</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 90 days after enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State shall submit a report to the appropriate congressional committees detailing steps taken by the Palestinian Authority to counter incitement of violence against Israelis and to promote peace and coexistence with Israel.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HF70202F63E234DECABB9CEA23FF34566" class="indent0"><num value="l">(l) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Yemen</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated under title III of this Act and prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs shall be made available for stabilization assistance for Yemen.</content></subsection></section>

<subsection changed="added" id="H8EE3CF6F492A4500B6F8DBE4ED9D9903" class="indent0"><num value="h">(h) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">South Sudan</inline>.—</heading>

<subparagraph changed="added" id="HFC72DB6DBCC448AC8A7ECA3D2CFEC1F2" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>assistance to support South Sudan peace negotiations or to advance or implement a peace agreement; and</content></subparagraph>

<subsection changed="added" id="HD9D27FFACCEC42879A214514439DA0E7" class="indent0"><num value="i">(i) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sudan</inline>.—</heading>

<subparagraph changed="added" id="HBF609ECF37FD4F78A4D6081D98EF5634" class="indent1"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act may be made available for the cost, as defined in section 502 of the Congressional Budget Act of 1974, of modifying loans and loan guarantees held by the Government of Sudan, including the cost of selling, reducing, or canceling amounts owed to the United States, and modifying concessional loans, guarantees, and credit agreements.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE3C4F7A72E8B428B965189E0E75434D5" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exclusions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The limitations of paragraph (1) shall not apply to—</chapeau>
