<subsection changed="added" id="HADECB7AF5B964B5CA23A0474F0FCD685" class="indent0"><num value="j">(j) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Zimbabwe</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HDD3E215AD8E0406ABF8A0F8965AB7EA2" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Instruction</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of the Treasury shall instruct the United States executive director of each international financial institution to vote against any extension by the respective institution of any loan or grant to the Government of Zimbabwe, except to meet basic human needs or to promote democracy, unless the Secretary of State certifies and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that the rule of law has been restored, including respect for ownership and title to property, and freedoms of expression, association, and assembly.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD858E89CF4944D04BA8CA54F26218D80" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitation</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act shall be made available for assistance for the central Government of Zimbabwe, except for health and education, unless the Secretary of State certifies and reports as required in paragraph (1).</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<appropriations level="small" changed="added" id="H506DECD3EC084A148958E95E39F21420"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">east asia and the pacific</inline></heading></appropriations>
<section changed="added" id="H4FEC263AC238405B977B7AB7A131578B"><num value="7043"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7043. </inline></num><subsection id="H2AA4D0A7DCD2409F87583906A60E0F9B" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Burma</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H18AA53B9D623401FBB8E0E22DD7699E6" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Bilateral economic assistance</inline>.—</heading><subparagraph id="HEE89633DE3684B0CA4ECC15A8B75E5B2" class="inline"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Of the funds appropriated under title III of this Act, not less than $131,450,000 shall be made available for assistance for Burma: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds may be made available notwithstanding any other provision of law and following consultation with the appropriate congressional committees: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That such funds shall be made available for programs to promote ethnic and religious tolerance and to combat gender-based violence, including in Kachin, Karen, Rakhine, and Shan states: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That such funds may be made available for ethnic groups and civil society in Burma to help sustain ceasefire agreements and further prospects for reconciliation and peace, which may include support to representatives of ethnic armed groups for this purpose.</proviso></content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H2A1DD17F221344C0AE50E430888B5A22" class="indent1"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Funds appropriated under title III of this Act for assistance for Burma shall be made available for community-based organizations operating in Thailand to provide food, medical, and other humanitarian assistance to internally displaced persons in eastern Burma, in addition to assistance for Burmese refugees from funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Migration and Refugee Assistance”: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds may be available for programs to support the return of Kachin, Karen, Rohingya, Shan, and other refugees and internally displaced persons to their locations of origin or preference in Burma only if such returns are voluntary and consistent with international law.</proviso></content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HB125586763A9494885735008F0163FDA" class="indent1"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>Funds appropriated under title III of this Act for assistance for Burma that are made available for assistance for the Government of Burma to support the implementation of Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement conferences, committees, and other procedures may only be made available if the Secretary of State reports to the Committees on Appropriations that such conferences, committees, and procedures are directed toward a sustainable peace and the Government of Burma is implementing its commitments under such Agreement.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HAC99AAF7E3F044BF888B8CED2A047CC1" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">International security assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “International Military Education and Training” and “Foreign Military Financing Program” may be made available for assistance for Burma: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the Department of State may continue consultations with the armed forces of Burma only on human rights and disaster response in a manner consistent with the prior fiscal year, and following consultation with the appropriate congressional committees.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H0476C7A4D0094455890D6A2A137A91FF" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitations</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated under title III of this Act for assistance for Burma may be made available to any organization or entity controlled by the armed forces of Burma, or to any individual or organization that advocates violence against ethnic or religious groups or individuals in Burma, as determined by the Secretary of State for programs administered by the Department of State and USAID or the President of the National Endowment for Democracy (NED) for programs administered by NED.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H9B943C52E4AE43D9986063BDF5406FAD" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Consultation</inline>.—</heading><content>Any new program or activity in Burma initiated in fiscal year 2020 shall be subject to prior consultation with the appropriate congressional committees.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HC5E8D1D6A82F4162A054F02FD00CC95A" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Cambodia</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HEE0F01FC6C374953A6C58EF99FF7E21B" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated under title III of this Act, not less than $82,505,000 shall be made available for assistance for Cambodia.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H7956540BF24D4F0E80F389970CAC04DC" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Certification and exceptions</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="HB9639911DE6A413DB534964E6E2192D1" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Certification</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>None of the funds appropriated by this Act that are made available for assistance for the Government of Cambodia may be obligated or expended unless the Secretary of State certifies and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that such Government is taking effective steps to—</chapeau>
<clause id="HD560A307C56541828062C8CEF178EC63" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>strengthen regional security and stability, particularly regarding territorial disputes in the South China Sea and the enforcement of international sanctions with respect to North Korea;</content></clause>
<clause id="H0D7E57C269F046F08A9DED1C8F68E766" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>assert its sovereignty against interference by the People’s Republic of China, including by verifiably maintaining the neutrality of Ream Naval Base, other military installations in Cambodia, and dual use facilities such as the Dara Sakor development project; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H3DC5A2AF375A435780E8CED092689CDB" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>respect the rights, freedoms, and responsibilities enshrined in the Constitution of the Kingdom of Cambodia as enacted in 1993.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HB7489F48FCA347A69DB3BFC92A1F5B69" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exceptions</inline>.—</heading><content>The certification required by subparagraph (A) shall not apply to funds appropriated by this Act and made available for democracy, health, education, and environment programs, programs to strengthen the sovereignty of Cambodia, and programs to educate and inform the people of Cambodia of the influence efforts of the People’s Republic of China in Cambodia.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H429C61878F064F2C9BAFF846441A23D0" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Uses of funds</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Funds appropriated under title III of this Act for assistance for Cambodia shall be made available for—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H4C7CEF85012F41C9B6BE58883A71EA0E" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>research and education programs associated with the Khmer Rouge in Cambodia; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H16CDFDF7B4374FEFB103CC1561B2F715" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>programs in the Khmer language to monitor, map, and publicize the efforts by the People’s Republic of China to expand its influence in Cambodia, including in Sihanoukville, Bavet, Poipet, Koh Kong, and areas bordering Vietnam.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HB687281B75A342B587A1D9B9D64C5BAC" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Indo-Pacific Strategy and the Asia Reassurance Initiative Act of 2018</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H633737ADD4B247B8A43A9F15580E96C7" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated under titles III and IV of this Act, not less than $1,482,000,000 shall be made available to support the implementation of the Indo-Pacific Strategy and the Asia Reassurance Initiative Act of 2018 (Public Law 115–409).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H803B66DB17AA4E8599CA95192FB427B9" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Countering chinese influence fund</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “Development Assistance”, “Economic Support Fund”, “International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement”, “Nonproliferation, Anti-terrorism, Demining and Related Programs”, and “Foreign Military Financing Program”, not less than $300,000,000 shall be made available for a Countering Chinese Influence Fund to counter the influence of the People’s Republic of China globally, which shall be subject to prior consultation with the Committees on Appropriations: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds are in addition to amounts otherwise made available for such purposes: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That such funds appropriated under such headings may be transferred to, and merged with, funds appropriated under such headings: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That such transfer authority is in addition to any other transfer authority provided by this Act or any other Act, and is subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H65E07D4097504460843B3BF366550466" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Restriction on uses of funds</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>None of the funds appropriated by this Act and prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs may be made available for any project or activity that directly supports or promotes—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H3C5E4FA8392D4DFCB0D4DADF788A4678" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the Belt and Road Initiative or any dual-use infrastructure projects of the People’s Republic of China; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HA066B35BB9474F479CAACC352E0A51D4" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the use of technology, including biotechnology, digital, telecommunications, and cyber, developed by the People’s Republic of China unless the Secretary of State, in consultation with the USAID Administrator and the Chief Executive Officer of the United States International Development Finance Corporation, as appropriate, determines that such use does not adversely impact the national security of the United States.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H469B01D78C894666B217F4017805EC58" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Laos</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated under title III of this Act, not less than $34,280,000 shall be made available for assistance for Laos.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H9BAD7C1683C0424DB92DC215C760F3C8" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">North Korea</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HFA58D191E05C4D9E821053A9F5DDEFFC" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Cybersecurity</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act or prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs may be made available for assistance for the central government of a country the Secretary of State determines and reports to the appropriate congressional committees engages in significant transactions contributing materially to the malicious cyber-intrusion capabilities of the Government of North Korea: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the Secretary of State shall submit the report required by section 209 of the North Korea Sanctions and Policy Enhancement Act of 2016 (Public Law 114–122; 22 U.S.C. 9229) to the Committees on Appropriations: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That the Secretary of State may waive the application of the restriction in this paragraph with respect to assistance for the central government of a country if the Secretary determines and reports to the appropriate congressional committees that to do so is important to the national security interest of the United States, including a description of such interest served.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA42DB0B8A79D44D49C865AD6688261BD" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Broadcasts</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “International Broadcasting Operations” shall be made available to maintain broadcasting hours into North Korea at levels not less than the prior fiscal year.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H21946AA281BF4BFCBD56A539138F5B19" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Human rights promotion and limitation on use of funds</inline>.—</heading><subparagraph id="HC8B1F709ECA84160A0CA9922713DE5DD" class="inline"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “Economic Support Fund” and “Democracy Fund” shall be made available for the promotion of human rights in North Korea: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the authority of section 7032(b)(1) of this Act shall apply to such funds.</proviso></content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HFC17EA475ECF474795204E4FEF04C8E3" class="indent1"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>None of the funds made available by this Act under the heading “Economic Support Fund” may be made available for assistance for the Government of North Korea.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H04AA00C50224402394E5401D3CDE4917" class="indent0"><num value="f">(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">People’s Republic of China</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H281771BB57A1415BAD9064B28CBA3DFD" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitation on use of funds</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated under the heading “Diplomatic Programs” in this Act may be obligated or expended for processing licenses for the export of satellites of United States origin (including commercial satellites and satellite components) to the People’s Republic of China (PRC) unless, at least 15 days in advance, the Committees on Appropriations are notified of such proposed action.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HDC8DAD9D2AAA4FD0B94154073A4C8A79" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">People’s liberation army</inline>.—</heading><content>The terms and requirements of section 620(h) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 shall apply to foreign assistance projects or activities of the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) of the PRC, to include such projects or activities by any entity that is owned or controlled by, or an affiliate of, the PLA: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That none of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available pursuant to this Act may be used to finance any grant, contract, or cooperative agreement with the PLA, or any entity that the Secretary of State has reason to believe is owned or controlled by, or an affiliate of, the PLA.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCE7927D4A2E64A689360854368F76158" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">United states-china friendship volunteer program</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 90 days after enactment of this Act and following consultation with the heads of other relevant Federal agencies, the Director of the Peace Corps shall submit a report to the appropriate congressional committees on the United States-China Friendship Volunteer Program, including a description of program coordination, implementation, and oversight, and the goals and objectives served: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the Director shall also consult with the Committees on Appropriations on such report.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9BD3DC7D588D4AAD8FB6DBF6B35F9BE4" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Hong kong</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="HC3D928B9F84641ED90A61D3E75D414C3" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Democracy programs</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Democracy Fund” for the Human Rights and Democracy Fund of the Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor, Department of State, not less than $1,500,000 shall be made available for democracy programs for Hong Kong, including legal and other support for democracy activists.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H1B26A4C3497041FF8F9ECF04FD76318D" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Funds appropriated under title I of this Act shall be made available to prepare and submit to Congress the report required by section 301 of the United States-Hong Kong Policy Act of 1992 (22 U.S.C. 5731), which shall also include a description of—</chapeau>
<clause id="HFEA58BFFD7DF42589DF275E7359ABCC2" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>efforts by the Hong Kong authorities and the Government of the People’s Republic of China to prevent free assembly and communications by the people of Hong Kong;</content></clause>
<clause id="H02045310D5FA40D49B1B8816920865E4" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>the technical surveillance equipment and methods used by the Hong Kong authorities and the Government of the People’s Republic of China to monitor the movement and communications of the Hong Kong population;</content></clause>
<clause id="HAC7FE466F65C4A089BA6EFC03B9D3DD0" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>the application of social and political control tools developed by the Government of the People’s Republic of China and used by such Government and the Hong Kong authorities in Hong Kong;</content></clause>
<clause id="H96579BD8D1A14BEE8B9AE3C7521ED567" class="indent3"><num value="iv">(iv) </num><content>the disinformation and political influence campaigns conducted by the Government of the People’s Republic of China in Hong Kong and overseas with respect to the situation in Hong Kong; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H14A50566CE1B469EAD0436CD4C76B81C" class="indent3"><num value="v">(v) </num><content>the mission and activities of the People’s Armed Police, the People’s Liberation Army, the Ministries of Public Security and State Security in Beijing, the Government of the People’s Republic of China, and other Chinese security forces in Hong Kong, including their respective roles in human rights abuses against the people of Hong Kong.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HE3DC57BE437E4A719FCDF21F914F0BB5" class="indent0"><num value="g">(g) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Philippines</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement” may be made available for counternarcotics assistance for the Philippines, except for drug demand reduction, maritime law enforcement, or transnational interdiction.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H094C14257A90473DB4941615E87E5C51" class="indent0"><num value="h">(h) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Tibet</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H61D56F76FFA9408780D1928D55E7F284" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Financing of projects in tibet</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of the Treasury should instruct the United States executive director of each international financial institution to use the voice and vote of the United States to support financing of projects in Tibet if such projects do not provide incentives for the migration and settlement of non-Tibetans into Tibet or facilitate the transfer of ownership of Tibetan land and natural resources to non-Tibetans, are based on a thorough needs-assessment, foster self-sufficiency of the Tibetan people and respect Tibetan culture and traditions, and are subject to effective monitoring.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H7FDE4BB081CE4FDF9E6DF7B2BE67B29B" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Programs for tibetan communities</inline>.—</heading><subparagraph id="H599A17A9DAEB477E9A282243BDAB1EC7" class="inline"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Notwithstanding any other provision of law, of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Economic Support Fund”, not less than $8,000,000 shall be made available to nongovernmental organizations to support activities which preserve cultural traditions and promote sustainable development, education, and environmental conservation in Tibetan communities in the Tibet Autonomous Region and in other Tibetan communities in China.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H0B04DA4C18764C82A7A069680DC19E43" class="indent1"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Economic Support Fund”, not less than $6,000,000 shall be made available for programs to promote and preserve Tibetan culture and language in the refugee and diaspora Tibetan communities, development, and the resilience of Tibetan communities and the Central Tibetan Administration in India and Nepal, and to assist in the education and development of the next generation of Tibetan leaders from such communities: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds are in addition to amounts made available in subparagraph (A) for programs inside Tibet.</proviso></content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H39B6A2A594FC42E7B086CBCD67649D28" class="indent1"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Economic Support Fund”, not less than $3,000,000 shall be made available for programs to strengthen the capacity of the Central Tibetan Administration: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds shall be administered by the United States Agency for International Development.</proviso></content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H2BC296E1CA614DE4998105BBD96B754A" class="indent0"><num value="i">(i) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Vietnam</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Of the funds appropriated under titles III and IV of this Act, not less than $159,634,000 shall be made available for assistance for Vietnam, of which not less than—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H15E7C8F69D9B4B55A6CF2C4C268C4AC1" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>$13,000,000 shall be made available for health and disability programs in areas sprayed with Agent Orange and contaminated with dioxin, to assist individuals with severe upper or lower body mobility impairment or cognitive or developmental disabilities;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD8C96AA1336E431B872EB85E52CD135E" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>$20,000,000 shall be made available, notwithstanding any other provision of law, for activities related to the remediation of dioxin contaminated sites in Vietnam and may be made available for assistance for the Government of Vietnam, including the military, for such purposes; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCCA16F9DA9A14892ACE6B11CB87C4C1B" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>$1,500,000 shall be made available for a war legacy reconciliation program.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>

<section changed="added" id="H64C39EFE0A6545C29B8908B366EC3E61"><num value="7044"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7044. </inline></num><subsection id="HD9AF3D6818E74A0D8497156E5EBFF963" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Afghanistan</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H6AED148D5155497082E94D3E2298CE39" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Funding and limitations</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “Economic Support Fund” and “International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement” that are made available for assistance for Afghanistan—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H0E2247D85EB94E419F73AED4F8420E92" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>shall be made available to implement the South Asia Strategy, the Revised Strategy for United States Engagement in Afghanistan, and the United States Agency for International Development Country Development Cooperation Strategy for Afghanistan;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD4181091DEC343DE9F14D4974570E1F7" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>shall be made available to continue support for institutions of higher education in Kabul, Afghanistan that are accessible to both women and men in a coeducational environment, including for the costs for operations and security for such institutions;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H893F129222BE4F93BF16BD20895C6C2C" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>shall be made available for programs that protect and strengthen the rights of Afghan women and girls and promote the political and economic empowerment of women including their meaningful inclusion in political processes: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such assistance to promote the economic empowerment of women shall be made available as grants to Afghan organizations, to the maximum extent practicable; and</proviso></content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HF7557C9F469F43C3A33F80C7C116D37E" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>may not be made available for any program, project, or activity pursuant to section 7044(a)(1)(C) of the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2019 (division F of Public Law 116–6).</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H5E9E87875E7C433E81D82EC71CC6855D" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Afghan women</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="HD4619E3465844FAB8C922D0064AE4CC6" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State shall promote the meaningful participation of Afghan women in ongoing peace and reconciliation processes in Afghanistan in a manner consistent with the Women, Peace, and Security Act of 2017 (Public Law 115–68), including advocacy for the inclusion of Afghan women leaders in ongoing and future dialogue and negotiations and efforts to ensure that any peace agreement reached with the Taliban protects the rights of women and girls and ensures their freedom of movement, rights to education and work, and access to healthcare and legal representation.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HB645117D1ED5429E9395142E0A4C0191" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act and prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs under the heading “Economic Support Fund” shall be made available for an endowment pursuant to paragraph (3)(A)(iv) of this subsection for an institution of higher education in Kabul, Afghanistan that is accessible to both women and men in a coeducational environment: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such endowment shall be established in partnership with a United States-based American higher education institution that will serve on its board of trustees: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That prior to the obligation of funds for such an endowment, the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development shall submit a report to the Committees on Appropriations describing the governance structure, including a proposed board of trustees, and financial safeguards, including regular audit and reporting requirements, in any endowment agreement: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That the USAID Administrator shall provide a report on the expenditure of funds generated from such an endowment to the Committees on Appropriations on an annual basis.</proviso></content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HD29FBC3EE77F475BA705839733656A48" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorities</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H92B83E75EBCE4E8EB97E0F7A0CAF18A9" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><chapeau>Funds appropriated by this Act under titles III through VI that are made available for assistance for Afghanistan may be made available—</chapeau>
<clause id="H2FF1999BC492452292A67049019B9A86" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>notwithstanding section 7012 of this Act or any similar provision of law and section 660 of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961;</content></clause>
<clause id="H7F0B5AB4EA80433FBE632A889407B139" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>for reconciliation programs and disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration activities for former combatants who have renounced violence against the Government of Afghanistan, including in accordance with section 7046(a)(2)(B)(ii) of the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2012 (division I of Public Law 112–74);</content></clause>
<clause id="HF37B68D717174E36A37D3FE35C670F73" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>for an endowment to empower women and girls; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H1166410CC0584B4F8051E6DB80ACDF31" class="indent3"><num value="iv">(iv) </num><content>for an endowment for higher education.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HC51D4E804C2D4BC0AAF67F4D582A7E09" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Section 7046(a)(2)(A) of the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2012 (division I of Public Law 112–74) shall apply to funds appropriated by this Act for assistance for Afghanistan.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HC0B5A36124F843469B903668D390C510" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Diplomatic Programs”, up to $3,000,000 may be transferred to any other appropriation of any department or agency of the United States Government, upon the concurrence of the head of such department or agency, to support operations in, and assistance for, Afghanistan and to carry out the provisions of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That any such transfer shall be subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</proviso></content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H74ADFD6AB0104D1892EF5FF1B8341F2B" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Agreement and certification</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Funds appropriated by this Act shall be made available for the following purposes—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H25B7B8BC072D4491A8E776046C5F02A1" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the submission to the appropriate congressional committees by the President of a copy of any agreement or arrangement between the Government of the United States and the Taliban relating to the United States presence in Afghanistan or Taliban commitments on the future of Afghanistan, which shall be submitted not later than 30 days after finalizing such an agreement or arrangement; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H3F612CFD15034D9CB88C616F2B9AFFCB" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the submission to the appropriate congressional committees of a joint certification by the Secretary of State and Secretary of Defense that such agreement or arrangement will further the objective of setting conditions for the long-term defeat of al Qaeda and Islamic State and will not make the United States more vulnerable to terrorist attacks originating from Afghanistan or supported by terrorist elements in Afghanistan.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H2DE1C0C1F119451ABE7366082B69ADCD" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Basing rights agreement</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds made available by this Act may be used by the United States Government to enter into a permanent basing rights agreement between the United States and Afghanistan.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HEB0961DB07354568A747FB727BFD4BA4" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Bangladesh</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Of the funds appropriated under titles III and IV of this Act, not less than $198,323,000 shall be made available for assistance for Bangladesh, of which—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HAE3A5EAD06304D3A847A98768D0C0100" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>not less than $23,500,000 shall be made available to address the needs of communities impacted by refugees from Burma;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4A1A366E233B4B80A4DDFDE97034268F" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>not less than $10,000,000 shall be made available for programs to protect freedom of expression and due process of law; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6D7914098CA8444C8452955C1BECB1D5" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>not less than $23,300,000 shall be made available for democracy programs, of which not less than $2,000,000 shall be made available for such programs for the Rohingya community in Bangladesh.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H5F6F81BA8EB241FEBBAB53BCC960310C" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Nepal</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H6C39AC0C11D34072A9A64D8756E73483" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated under titles III and IV of this Act, not less than $130,265,000 shall be made available for assistance for Nepal, including for earthquake recovery and reconstruction programs and democracy programs.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H838D9BBE9A55495FB36A60B01E08273F" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Foreign military financing program</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Foreign Military Financing Program” shall only be made available for humanitarian and disaster relief and reconstruction activities in Nepal, and in support of international peacekeeping operations: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds may only be made available for any additional uses if the Secretary of State certifies and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that the Government of Nepal is investigating and prosecuting violations of human rights and the laws of war, and the Nepal Army is cooperating fully with civilian judicial authorities in such cases.</proviso></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HFD3C6BC5069947F1B6A81D99B6AC1611" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Pakistan</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HD30A21985B094650B88398DDC516EAEC" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Terms and conditions</inline>.—</heading><content>The terms and conditions of section 7044(c) of the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2019 (division F of Public Law 116–6) shall continue in effect during fiscal year 2020.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB6419F85B8FB4811A059EC54AB7DF4AC" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated under title III of this Act that are made available for assistance for Pakistan, not less than $15,000,000 shall be made available for democracy programs and not less than $10,000,000 shall be made available for gender programs.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H2C118A944D89479486D7B04154D177E9" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sri Lanka</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H714B79881E3E4474975635FDC780D620" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated under title III of this Act shall be made available for assistance for Sri Lanka for democracy and economic development programs, particularly in areas recovering from ethnic and religious conflict: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds shall be made available for programs to assist in the identification and resolution of cases of missing persons.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5B41DD28CDAA458BAF61DB4569BE0FDE" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Certification</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Funds appropriated by this Act for assistance for the central Government of Sri Lanka, except for funds made available for humanitarian assistance, victims of trauma, and technical assistance to promote fiscal transparency and sovereignty, may be made available only if the Secretary of State certifies and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that such Government is taking effective and consistent steps to—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H1C1C59338639491BB15F649995BF1510" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>respect and uphold the rights and freedoms of the people of Sri Lanka regardless of ethnicity and religious belief, including by investigating violations of human rights and holding perpetrators of such violations accountable;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H2B0E78C5B0E44F6B864471980BA140E1" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>assert its sovereignty against interference by the People’s Republic of China; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H234575F811A045B39794B9F97B24608F" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>promote reconciliation between ethnic and religious groups arising from past conflict in Sri Lanka, including by addressing land confiscation and ownership issues, resolving cases of missing persons, and reducing the presence of the armed forces in former conflict zones.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA5466511D49744E19DDE9A3E9E7BDB3E" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">International security assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Foreign Military Financing Program”, not to exceed $500,000 may be made available for assistance for Sri Lanka: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds may be made available only for programs to support humanitarian and disaster response preparedness and maritime security, including professionalization and training for the navy and coast guard: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That funds made available under the heading “Peacekeeping Operations” may only be made available subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</proviso></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H854BE7F07F714772B40F30E05EA26789" class="indent0"><num value="f">(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Regional Programs</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act shall be made available for assistance for Afghanistan, Pakistan, and other countries in South and Central Asia to significantly increase the recruitment, training, and retention of women in the judiciary, police, and other security forces, and to train judicial and security personnel in such countries to prevent and address gender-based violence, human trafficking, and other practices that disproportionately harm women and girls.</content></subsection></section>

<section changed="added" id="H06DA42E3EC2E49C5B054FF079AA128A5"><num value="7045"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7045. </inline></num><subsection id="H637E3A62770344A79D50CD5B46E38E89" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Central America</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H64D88D12267A49BEACFBB979DB818A88" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="HF1B96172FFC1433FA93223B60E0A7887" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Fiscal year 2020</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under titles III and IV, not less than $519,885,000 should be made available for assistance for Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama, including through the Central America Regional Security Initiative: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such assistance shall be prioritized for programs and activities that addresses the key factors that contribute to the migration of unaccompanied, undocumented minors to the United States and such funds shall be made available for global health, humanitarian, development, democracy, border security, and law enforcement programs for such countries, including for programs to reduce violence against women and girls and to combat corruption, and for support of commissions against corruption and impunity, as appropriate: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That not less than $45,000,000 shall be for support of offices of Attorneys General and of other entities and activities to combat corruption and impunity in such countries.</proviso></content></subparagraph>

<paragraph changed="added" id="HE67E19F2DC9442F59C16B2CD928B4C5E" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Northern triangle</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H53D5C61703B3452F871E4003CE74B78B" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitation on assistance to certain central governments</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Of the funds made available pursuant to paragraph (1) under the heading “Economic Support Fund” and under title IV of this Act that are made available for assistance for each of the central governments of El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras, 50 percent may only be obligated after the Secretary of State certifies and reports to the appropriate congressional committees that such government is—</chapeau>
<clause id="H89610BB52A9143F79D4D3DE3A05D2FA6" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>combating corruption and impunity, including prosecuting corrupt government officials;</content></clause>
<clause id="HD45484CA09134D8293BA38190E676AC5" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>implementing reforms, policies, and programs to increase transparency and strengthen public institutions;</content></clause>
<clause id="H1D101C27238644898BAA3ECC920FE0AB" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>protecting the rights of civil society, opposition political parties, and the independence of the media;</content></clause>
<clause id="HA2BF8F8197474801BEFEE5E0FD3E668E" class="indent3"><num value="iv">(iv) </num><content>providing effective and accountable law enforcement and security for its citizens, and upholding due process of law;</content></clause>
<clause id="H87727E8A8CC24D54AE477810FCCF5468" class="indent3"><num value="v">(v) </num><content>implementing policies to reduce poverty and promote equitable economic growth and opportunity;</content></clause>
<clause id="H7DC123143903437A839948701C0F94B8" class="indent3"><num value="vi">(vi) </num><content>supporting the independence of the judiciary and of electoral institutions;</content></clause>
<clause id="H6C2B1960638747E38B7EFA069B0FEADD" class="indent3"><num value="vii">(vii) </num><content>improving border security;</content></clause>
<clause id="H444AAB95ADC641C19FAB3DDD5D368D4E" class="indent3"><num value="viii">(viii) </num><content>combating human smuggling and trafficking and countering the activities of criminal gangs, drug traffickers, and transnational criminal organizations; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H28C2BFCFC5B040B5A5649A361CACCB61" class="indent3"><num value="ix">(ix) </num><content>informing its citizens of the dangers of the journey to the southwest border of the United States.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H583133F559754146B161C0CED4E02814" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reprogramming</inline>.—</heading><content>If the Secretary is unable to make the certification required by subparagraph (A) for one or more of the governments, such assistance for such central government shall be reprogrammed for assistance for other countries in Latin America and the Caribbean, notwithstanding the minimum funding requirements of this subsection and of section 7019 of this Act: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That any such reprogramming shall be subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</proviso></content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H55BFC31B5D4D47CD927BA7ECB0BBB0A4" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exceptions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The limitation of subparagraph (A) shall not apply to funds appropriated by this Act that are made available for—</chapeau>
<clause id="H8FB153C6D1E94C55B0BF2200A93D5E29" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>the Mission to Support the Fight Against Corruption and Impunity in Honduras, the International Commission Against Impunity in El Salvador, and support of offices of Attorneys General and of other entities and activities related to combating corruption and impunity;</content></clause>
<clause id="H44F5E656857C4505B55E74F4AA7C4899" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>programs to combat gender-based violence;</content></clause>
<clause id="H1DA59C5C548B41E3A59FD2119FB99D13" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>humanitarian assistance; and</content></clause>
<clause id="HC0306213C1284CF6A66403138988D1E5" class="indent3"><num value="iv">(iv) </num><content>food security programs.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H577A7F7E0D4247C2A73B5C0CF2506BB4" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Colombia</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H8DB3BDA0789844229CC813BB5CCD6AAF" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under titles III and IV, not less than $448,253,000 shall be made available for assistance for Colombia: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds shall be made available for the programs and activities described under this section in the explanatory statement described in section 4 (in the matter preceding division A of this consolidated Act).</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE46800F7B43B4722B037BA1A48BF3507" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Withholding of funds</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H7860C89BCE0F47D99CAB08BE64269679" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Counternarcotics</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement” and made available for assistance for Colombia, 20 percent may be obligated only after the Secretary of State certifies and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that the Government of Colombia is continuing to implement a national whole-of-government counternarcotics strategy intended to reduce by 50 percent cocaine production and coca cultivation levels in Colombia by 2023.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H82868B168CD1477BA2E3A6DC647992A1" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Human rights</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Foreign Military Financing Program” and made available for assistance for Colombia, 20 percent may be obligated only after the Secretary of State certifies and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that—</chapeau>
<clause id="H88E6208D77824812BC54EF9C3854FE09" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>the Special Jurisdiction for Peace and other judicial authorities are taking effective steps to hold accountable perpetrators of gross violations of human rights in a manner consistent with international law, including for command responsibility, and sentence them to deprivation of liberty;</content></clause>
<clause id="HFBAD2BDCCBAA40BCA0F21254A1DAF9C8" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>the Government of Colombia is taking effective steps to prevent attacks against human rights defenders and other civil society activists, trade unionists, and journalists, and judicial authorities are prosecuting those responsible for such attacks; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H0C8D0315882B47DA889837EFE2FBC9B7" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>senior military officers responsible for ordering, committing, and covering up cases of false positives are being held accountable, including removal from active duty if found guilty through criminal or disciplinary proceedings.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6F0B42817AF44C89A38844863697A01C" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exceptions</inline>.—</heading><content>The limitations of paragraph (2) shall not apply to funds made available for aviation instruction and maintenance, and maritime and riverine security programs.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFC2B0CF12378463EB9E9E6C03103935E" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authority</inline>.—</heading><content>Aircraft supported by funds appropriated by this Act and prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs and made available for assistance for Colombia may be used to transport personnel and supplies involved in drug eradication and interdiction, including security for such activities, and to provide transport in support of alternative development programs and investigations by civilian judicial authorities.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H945333CF7C3442C581E8AF1E9B24059F" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitation</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act or prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs that are made available for assistance for Colombia may be made available for payment of reparations to conflict victims or compensation to demobilized combatants associated with a peace agreement between the Government of Colombia and illegal armed groups.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HF0FE8553E8ED49DD84D36431156A56CD" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Haiti</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H1D0403EA551D4BAA987250BD9D4F614C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Certification</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Economic Support Fund” that are made available for assistance for Haiti may not be made available for assistance for the central Government of Haiti unless the Secretary of State certifies and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that such government is taking effective steps, which are steps taken since the certification and report submitted during the prior year, if applicable, to—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HFD16A0C97E39444CADADED10CC26888E" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><chapeau>strengthen the rule of law in Haiti, including by—</chapeau>
<clause id="H13616F3CB36A43E6B40C96D66414A9DF" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>selecting judges in a transparent manner based on merit;</content></clause>
<clause id="H3E00E049CD9546E2B22B7EAC82670139" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>reducing pre-trial detention;</content></clause>
<clause id="HE4EE8611728947419AF5BF40181DE599" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>respecting the independence of the judiciary; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H136B8FFFC1F04B2BA0CBB39D593B3008" class="indent3"><num value="iv">(iv) </num><content>improving governance by implementing reforms to increase transparency and accountability, including through the penal and criminal codes;</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H38BB98EB0F4648E58C5C316684D51ED8" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>combat corruption, including by implementing the anti-corruption law enacted in 2014 and prosecuting corrupt officials;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H2452EFC3112E44FB9C6A0CD197F7C0C6" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>increase government revenues, including by implementing tax reforms, and increasing expenditures on public services; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H4B1C26277CFA4A44BD2E18FB424AF837" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>resolve commercial disputes between United States entities and the Government of Haiti.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD4CFF5DC0ACB429D9B9CB80270747CCB" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Haitian coast guard</inline>.—</heading><content>The Government of Haiti shall be eligible to purchase defense articles and services under the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2751 et seq.) for the Coast Guard.</content></paragraph>
