<section changed="notChanged" id="HD4CC98BC01CD423D98FF1AA5E8142182"><num value="7047"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7047. </inline></num><subsection id="H83A4AE4DDF0A4EA593CFB93874A52DA1" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitation</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act may be made available for assistance for the central Government of the Russian Federation.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H2C782764A08540268AE541C35A71A92F" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Annexation of Crimea</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HDE450B43C1254A03BB98C6DB6BF335AB" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prohibition</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act may be made available for assistance for the central government of a country that the Secretary of State determines and reports to the Committees on Appropriations has taken affirmative steps intended to support or be supportive of the Russian Federation annexation of Crimea or other territory in Ukraine: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That except as otherwise provided in subsection (a), the Secretary may waive the restriction on assistance required by this paragraph if the Secretary determines and reports to such Committees that to do so is in the national interest of the United States, and includes a justification for such interest.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H116233063070418AAFAD898ECF7B0D63" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitation</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>None of the funds appropriated by this Act may be made available for—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H679FAD2885BA4D69A76C789C6942D69D" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the implementation of any action or policy that recognizes the sovereignty of the Russian Federation over Crimea or other territory in Ukraine;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HB17207A6A6B84E3BA61E4099AAD36A7E" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the facilitation, financing, or guarantee of United States Government investments in Crimea or other territory in Ukraine under the control of Russian-backed separatists, if such activity includes the participation of Russian Government officials, or other Russian owned or controlled financial entities; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H281374F1CB86453EB37E8B88570DFD8F" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>assistance for Crimea or other territory in Ukraine under the control of Russian-backed separatists, if such assistance includes the participation of Russian Government officials, or other Russian owned or controlled financial entities.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB599BB2191584A1A8203FB425EFD0BC0" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">International financial institutions</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of the Treasury shall instruct the United States executive directors of each international financial institution to use the voice and vote of the United States to oppose any assistance by such institution (including any loan, credit, or guarantee) for any program that violates the sovereignty or territorial integrity of Ukraine.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1E31103682D142B9900B2D61D6014236" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Duration</inline>.—</heading><content>The requirements and limitations of this subsection shall cease to be in effect if the Secretary of State determines and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that the Government of Ukraine has reestablished sovereignty over Crimea and other territory in Ukraine under the control of Russian-backed separatists.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HAEF3CBFC933649828479ED3EBC46278D" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Occupation of the Georgian Territories of Abkhazia and Tskhinvali Region/South Ossetia</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H17A5D88FBDF4451CBE21DD1128E99520" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prohibition</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act may be made available for assistance for the central government of a country that the Secretary of State determines and reports to the Committees on Appropriations has recognized the independence of, or has established diplomatic relations with, the Russian Federation occupied Georgian territories of Abkhazia and Tskhinvali Region/South Ossetia: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the Secretary shall publish on the Department of State website a list of any such central governments in a timely manner: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That the Secretary may waive the restriction on assistance required by this paragraph if the Secretary determines and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that to do so is in the national interest of the United States, and includes a justification for such interest.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H76AA10F745CA40519B321222B838CC5A" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitation</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act may be made available to support the Russian Federation occupation of the Georgian territories of Abkhazia and Tskhinvali Region/South Ossetia.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCDF23D17239149E8A8D15098A4633D41" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">International financial institutions</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of the Treasury shall instruct the United States executive directors of each international financial institution to use the voice and vote of the United States to oppose any assistance by such institution (including any loan, credit, or guarantee) for any program that violates the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Georgia.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H0CA407C459D9450D9F5F9DFD1FADAECC" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Countering Russian Influence Fund</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HCF2463790D4540ABA0FD7D3E3F0E2351" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “Assistance for Europe, Eurasia and Central Asia”, “International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement”, “International Military Education and Training”, and “Foreign Military Financing Program”, not less than $290,000,000 shall be made available to carry out the purposes of the Countering Russian Influence Fund, as authorized by section 254 of the Countering Russian Influence in Europe and Eurasia Act of 2017 (Public Law 115–44; 22 U.S.C. 9543) and notwithstanding the country limitation in subsection (b) of such section, and programs to enhance the capacity of law enforcement and security forces in countries in Europe, Eurasia, and Central Asia and strengthen security cooperation between such countries and the United States and the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, as appropriate.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFACF7D69D53247FF8914D3392F812940" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Economics and trade</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act and made available for assistance for the Eastern Partnership countries shall be made available to advance the implementation of Association Agreements and trade agreements with the European Union, and to reduce their vulnerability to external economic and political pressure from the Russian Federation.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H5AE34A2EA3164859945F201A5769DEDC" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Democracy Programs</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act shall be made available to support democracy programs in the Russian Federation and other countries in Europe, Eurasia, and Central Asia, including to promote Internet freedom: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That not later than 90 days after enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a comprehensive, multiyear strategy for the promotion of democracy in such countries.</proviso></content></subsection></section>
<appropriations level="small" changed="added" id="H90838F31B04C4217B9862885A15F858F"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">united nations</inline></heading></appropriations>
<section changed="added" id="H8453B45AA7474E83AE012CEAF2154775"><num value="7048"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7048. </inline></num><subsection id="H52EB114226DC423D90893136D951338F" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Transparency and Accountability</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HAD949F6401D0456FA1037EA201D46653" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Withholding of funds</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Of the funds appropriated under the heading “Contributions to International Organizations” in title I and “International Organizations and Programs” in title V of this Act that are available for contributions to the United Nations (including the Department of Peacekeeping Operations), any United Nations agency, or the Organization of American States, 15 percent may not be obligated for such organization, department, or agency until the Secretary of State determines and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that the organization, department, or agency is—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HD4BF85C35B314C6EA8FC75C6D7611994" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>posting on a publicly available website, consistent with privacy regulations and due process, regular financial and programmatic audits of such organization, department, or agency, and providing the United States Government with necessary access to such financial and performance audits;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H623E4528082B46759B8CB02DB5A243A0" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><chapeau>effectively implementing and enforcing policies and procedures which meet or exceed best practices in the United States for the protection of whistleblowers from retaliation, including—</chapeau>
<clause id="H44C94593EF3949BFAB20682A3047B225" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>protection against retaliation for internal and lawful public disclosures;</content></clause>
<clause id="HA5CBE8386C5F483C8B74848379FF4EB5" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>legal burdens of proof;</content></clause>
<clause id="H72E2EF3F4FFC4B89B88BA4FDA2C5B226" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>statutes of limitation for reporting retaliation;</content></clause>
<clause id="HD0DBA39CE6694FCBB79A76F964A36B29" class="indent3"><num value="iv">(iv) </num><content>access to binding independent adjudicative bodies, including shared cost and selection external arbitration; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H8252902892ED4B72BD1B0C7FAC6AD4E1" class="indent3"><num value="v">(v) </num><content>results that eliminate the effects of proven retaliation, including provision for the restoration of prior employment; and</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD1DD8B374289490DBC87509562A087CF" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>effectively implementing and enforcing policies and procedures on the appropriate use of travel funds, including restrictions on first class and business class travel.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H7F7121E03B844131930C275613E540DA" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Waiver</inline>.—</heading><content>The restrictions imposed by or pursuant to paragraph (1) may be waived on a case- by-case basis if the Secretary of State determines and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that such waiver is necessary to avert or respond to a humanitarian crisis.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HCFE00CC07B4A4229811C3B74A782CF2C" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Restrictions on United Nations Delegations and Organizations</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H73F1AA45C042474F98686E8AF81BD677" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Restrictions on united states delegations</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds made available by this Act may be used to pay expenses for any United States delegation to any specialized agency, body, or commission of the United Nations if such agency, body, or commission is chaired or presided over by a country, the government of which the Secretary of State has determined, for purposes of section 1754(c) of the Export Reform Control Act of 2018 (50 U.S.C. 4813(c)), supports international terrorism.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE4E27B6A4F12499A97B1C455D1E3122C" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Restrictions on contributions</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds made available by this Act may be used by the Secretary of State as a contribution to any organization, agency, commission, or program within the United Nations system if such organization, agency, commission, or program is chaired or presided over by a country the government of which the Secretary of State has determined, for purposes of section 620A of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, section 40 of the Arms Export Control Act, section 1754(c) of the Export Reform Control Act of 2018 (50 U.S.C. 4813(c)), or any other provision of law, is a government that has repeatedly provided support for acts of international terrorism.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H475922310BDD48378ADB7DDECB26944D" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Waiver</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State may waive the restriction in this subsection if the Secretary determines and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that to do so is important to the national interest of the United States, including a description of the national interest served.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HB8685F3660494C8BB36E244BDE6DB52F" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">United Nations Human Rights Council</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act may be made available in support of the United Nations Human Rights Council unless the Secretary of State determines and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that participation in the Council is important to the national interest of the United States and that such Council is taking significant steps to remove Israel as a permanent agenda item and ensure integrity in the election of members to such Council: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such report shall include a description of the national interest served and the steps taken to remove Israel as a permanent agenda item and ensure integrity in the election of members to such Council: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That the Secretary of State shall report to the Committees on Appropriations not later than September 30, 2020, on the resolutions considered in the United Nations Human Rights Council during the previous 12 months, and on steps taken to remove Israel as a permanent agenda item and ensure integrity in the election of members to such Council.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H0380BA2F3981449FAE40E721591481E8" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">United Nations Relief and Works Agency</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Prior to the initial obligation of funds for the United Nations Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA), the Secretary of State shall report to the Committees on Appropriations, in writing, on whether UNRWA is—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HB5A5D1BC4B7649BF8F7034B91080BB20" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>utilizing Operations Support Officers in the West Bank, Gaza, and other fields of operation to inspect UNRWA installations and reporting any inappropriate use;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3F4B6AC7EBFF4252AF41C99BF9628488" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>acting promptly to address any staff or beneficiary violation of its own policies (including the policies on neutrality and impartiality of employees) and the legal requirements under section 301(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA42901417B934CA388510EB60F8905F8" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>implementing procedures to maintain the neutrality of its facilities, including implementing a no-weapons policy, and conducting regular inspections of its installations, to ensure they are only used for humanitarian or other appropriate purposes;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1EA002214A3F4B8FA2D8AE6B57D5FA19" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>taking necessary and appropriate measures to ensure it is operating in compliance with the conditions of section 301(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 and continuing regular reporting to the Department of State on actions it has taken to ensure conformance with such conditions;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H267BBC18E1DC4514B5C5D2EB7515C7A2" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>taking steps to ensure the content of all educational materials currently taught in UNRWA-administered schools and summer camps is consistent with the values of human rights, dignity, and tolerance and does not induce incitement;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4E4EA04F588C4535BB3339680CF0429B" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>not engaging in operations with financial institutions or related entities in violation of relevant United States law, and is taking steps to improve the financial transparency of the organization; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H50CEFB6B45AE4F9AB03E1A5182E21ED4" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>in compliance with the United Nations Board of Auditors’ biennial audit requirements and is implementing in a timely fashion the Board’s recommendations.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HDE1D2B76E0BE4CC6898E98896B9E5DE1" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prohibition of Payments to United Nations Members</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds appropriated or made available pursuant to titles III through VI of this Act for carrying out the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, may be used to pay in whole or in part any assessments, arrearages, or dues of any member of the United Nations or, from funds appropriated by this Act to carry out chapter 1 of part I of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, the costs for participation of another country’s delegation at international conferences held under the auspices of multilateral or international organizations.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HBA6B5472B8C441C588809EB974F1B042" class="indent0"><num value="f">(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 45 days after enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State shall submit a report to the Committees on Appropriations detailing the amount of funds available for obligation or expenditure in fiscal year 2020 for contributions to any organization, department, agency, or program within the United Nations system or any international program that are withheld from obligation or expenditure due to any provision of law: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the Secretary shall update such report each time additional funds are withheld by operation of any provision of law: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That the reprogramming of any withheld funds identified in such report, including updates thereof, shall be subject to prior consultation with, and the regular notification procedures of, the Committees on Appropriations.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H3B70F7CFBA384F7A8448CE5191B86F0C" class="indent0"><num value="g">(g) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sexual Exploitation and Abuse in Peacekeeping Operations</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State should withhold assistance to any unit of the security forces of a foreign country if the Secretary has credible information that such unit has engaged in sexual exploitation or abuse, including while serving in a United Nations peacekeeping operation, until the Secretary determines that the government of such country is taking effective steps to hold the responsible members of such unit accountable and to prevent future incidents: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the Secretary shall promptly notify the government of each country subject to any withholding of assistance pursuant to this paragraph, and shall notify the appropriate congressional committees of such withholding not later than 10 days after a determination to withhold such assistance is made: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That the Secretary shall, to the maximum extent practicable, assist such government in bringing the responsible members of such unit to justice.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HACFDC5FAD0C14A57B446BCE2CAB3973A" class="indent0"><num value="h">(h) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Additional Availability</inline>.—</heading><content>Subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations, funds appropriated by this Act which are returned or not made available due to the implementation of subsection (a), the third proviso under the heading “Contributions for International Peacekeeping Activities” in title I of this Act, or section 307(a) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2227(a)), shall remain available for obligation until September 30, 2021: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the requirement to withhold funds for programs in Burma under section 307(a) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 shall not apply to funds appropriated by this Act.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H942E6129BF41418E8E422DE46C95E4D7" class="indent0"><num value="i">(i) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">National Security Interest Withholding</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HCC296F000F474F93869A0F84BAF92150" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Withholding</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State shall withhold 5 percent of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Contributions to International Organizations” for a specialized agency or other entity of the United Nations if the Secretary, in consultation with the United States Ambassador to the United Nations, determines and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that such agency or entity has taken an official action that is against the national security interest of the United States or an ally of the United States, including Israel.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H406AE3BF93CF4413AB106766EE2B8A02" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Release of funds</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, in consultation with the United States Ambassador to the United Nations, may release funds withheld pursuant to paragraph (1) if the Secretary determines and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that such agency or entity is taking steps to address the action that resulted in the withholding of such funds.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFBFC164DB88948A7AF00507BA58AD86A" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reprogramming</inline>.—</heading><content>Should the Secretary of State be unable to make a determination pursuant to paragraph (2) regarding the release of withheld funds, such funds may be reprogrammed for other purposes under the heading “Contributions to International Organizations”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H101F8DB6056145CF985B564A66944A23" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Waiver</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, following consultation with the Committees on Appropriations, may waive the requirements of this subsection if the Secretary determines that to do so in the national interest.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<appropriations level="small" changed="added" id="H3EBB5E79C3FC44C68859FF925A4B1578"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">war crimes tribunals </inline></heading></appropriations>
<section changed="added" id="HD920C38367E84E4AB6BEE7E4D1C77EDC"><num value="7049"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7049. </inline></num><subsection id="H3436E828725E478691170E84BA5D8C8F" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><content>If the President determines that doing so will contribute to a just resolution of charges regarding genocide or other violations of international humanitarian law, the President may direct a drawdown pursuant to section 552(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 of up to $30,000,000 of commodities and services for the United Nations War Crimes Tribunal established with regard to the former Yugoslavia by the United Nations Security Council or such other tribunals or commissions as the Council may establish or authorize to deal with such violations, without regard to the ceiling limitation contained in paragraph (2) thereof: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the determination required under this section shall be in lieu of any determinations otherwise required under section 552(c): </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That funds made available pursuant to this section shall be made available subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H73DF1D492EA64B61BE4651482E8E6643" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><content>None of the funds appropriated by this Act may be made available for a United States contribution to the International Criminal Court: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That funds may be made available for technical assistance, training, assistance for victims, protection of witnesses, and law enforcement support related to international investigations, apprehensions, prosecutions, and adjudications of genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That the previous proviso shall not apply to investigations, apprehensions, or prosecutions of American service members and other United States citizens or nationals, or nationals of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) or major non-NATO allies initially designated pursuant to section 517(b) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961.</proviso></content></subsection></section>
<appropriations level="small" changed="added" id="HCD2A7772D00043539335F47DFB19B945"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">global internet freedom</inline></heading></appropriations>
<section changed="added" id="HDB5119CB05344A54845D9ED46EA456B9"><num value="7050"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7050. </inline></num><subsection id="H68186609957B4FF6842DFFABB7871764" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Funding</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds available for obligation during fiscal year 2020 under the headings “International Broadcasting Operations”, “Economic Support Fund”, “Democracy Fund”, and “Assistance for Europe, Eurasia and Central Asia”, not less than $65,500,000 shall be made available for programs to promote Internet freedom globally: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such programs shall be prioritized for countries whose governments restrict freedom of expression on the Internet, and that are important to the national interest of the United States: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That funds made available pursuant to this section shall be matched, to the maximum extent practicable, by sources other than the United States Government, including from the private sector.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HF075B1DB29B0460C9C5CB7F1A4E0BE37" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requirements</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HD54EE71A089B46B7B96836663A9B6DA5" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Department of state and united states agency for international development</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “Economic Support Fund”, “Democracy Fund”, and “Assistance for Europe, Eurasia and Central Asia” that are made available pursuant to subsection (a) shall be—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H4C0D828D7F7F4E59ABB05A35B7E0C33E" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>coordinated with other democracy programs funded by this Act under such headings, and shall be incorporated into country assistance and democracy promotion strategies, as appropriate;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H6049452609DD4B1590D612B7E30627BF" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>for programs to implement the May 2011, International Strategy for Cyberspace, the Department of State International Cyberspace Policy Strategy required by section 402 of the Cybersecurity Act of 2015 (division N of Public Law 114–113), and the comprehensive strategy to promote Internet freedom and access to information in Iran, as required by section 414 of the Iran Threat Reduction and Syria Human Rights Act of 2012 (22 U.S.C. 8754);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HA0F7A69E21BA43D094E27E50CA936648" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>made available for programs that support the efforts of civil society to counter the development of repressive Internet-related laws and regulations, including countering threats to Internet freedom at international organizations; to combat violence against bloggers and other users; and to enhance digital security training and capacity building for democracy activists;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HC212307D78E340CE99613D25ABB88CEE" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>made available for research of key threats to Internet freedom; the continued development of technologies that provide or enhance access to the Internet, including circumvention tools that bypass Internet blocking, filtering, and other censorship techniques used by authoritarian governments; and maintenance of the technological advantage of the United States Government over such censorship techniques: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the United States Agency for Global Media (USAGM), shall coordinate any such research and development programs with other relevant United States Government departments and agencies in order to share information, technologies, and best practices, and to assess the effectiveness of such technologies; and</proviso></content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H73DDE440ED8546748F6F5354FE9F3B97" class="indent2"><num value="E">(E) </num><chapeau>made available only after the Assistant Secretary for Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor, Department of State, concurs that such funds are allocated consistent with—</chapeau>
<clause id="HE87E79495A0B441C9C44289B14F17311" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>the strategies referenced in subparagraph (B) of this paragraph;</content></clause>
<clause id="H6B716AF4E9C3434293893D3541FC8975" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>best practices regarding security for, and oversight of, Internet freedom programs; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H6D62682F2F174CBA90C13A5BA6E5A566" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>sufficient resources and support for the development and maintenance of anti-censorship technology and tools.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1B0BD70A872B44A0BC47200228A27CA6" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">United states agency for global media</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “International Broadcasting Operations” that are made available pursuant to subsection (a) shall be—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HE0A1366A0D36493193756A18FE9DD2FF" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>made available only for tools and techniques to securely develop and distribute USAGM digital content, facilitate audience access to such content on websites that are censored, coordinate the distribution of USAGM digital content to targeted regional audiences, and to promote and distribute such tools and techniques, including digital security techniques;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HF340BA9B1A1745D493EDC85E9779BF08" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>coordinated with programs funded by this Act under the heading “International Broadcasting Operations”, and shall be incorporated into country broadcasting strategies, as appropriate;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H8D2BC5632F27484DB068CF6E7102AA4A" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>coordinated by the USAGM CEO to provide Internet circumvention tools and techniques for audiences in countries that are strategic priorities for the USAGM and in a manner consistent with the USAGM Internet freedom strategy; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H7B698688948B4366B5CEE8577F283666" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>made available for the research and development of new tools or techniques authorized in subparagraph (A) only after the USAGM CEO, in consultation with the Secretary of State and other relevant United States Government departments and agencies, evaluates the risks and benefits of such new tools or techniques, and establishes safeguards to minimize the use of such new tools or techniques for illicit purposes.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HA6265483607347A09D81309CEE5A0D66" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Coordination and Spend Plans</inline>.—</heading><content>After consultation among the relevant agency heads to coordinate and de-conflict planned activities, but not later than 90 days after enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State and the USAGM CEO shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations spend plans for funds made available by this Act for programs to promote Internet freedom globally, which shall include a description of safeguards established by relevant agencies to ensure that such programs are not used for illicit purposes: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the Department of State spend plan shall include funding for all such programs for all relevant Department of State and the United States Agency for International Development offices and bureaus.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H95F1EF78C2F44586AEB9A5D385CC2422" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Security Audits</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds made available pursuant to this section to promote Internet freedom globally may only be made available to support technologies that undergo comprehensive security audits conducted by the Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor, Department of State to ensure that such technology is secure and has not been compromised in a manner detrimental to the interest of the United States or to individuals and organizations benefiting from programs supported by such funds: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the security auditing procedures used by such Bureau shall be reviewed and updated periodically to reflect current industry security standards.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H0D8C8121AAF142828C99133A8A93E5A0" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Surge</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Economic Support Fund”, up to $2,500,000 may be made available to surge Internet freedom programs in closed societies if the Secretary of State determines and reports to the appropriate congressional committees that such use of funds is in the national interest: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds are in addition to amounts made available for such purposes: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That such funds may be transferred to, and merged with, funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “International Broadcasting Operations” following consultation with, and the regular notification procedures of, the Committees on Appropriations.</proviso></content></subsection></section>

<subsection changed="added" id="HB153730E74154B178A2C6707B78F8EE1" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Aircraft Coordination</inline>.—</heading>

<paragraph id="H36BE732F5F40480FBAEE436A5BD347DE" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Scope</inline>.—</heading><content>The requirement and authorities of this subsection shall only apply to aircraft, the primary purpose of which is the transportation of personnel.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H4C8508D2B9B340EC84E532B93799BCE2" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Aircraft Operations and Maintenance</inline>.—</heading><content>To the maximum extent practicable, the costs of operations and maintenance, including fuel, of aircraft funded by this Act shall be borne by the recipient country.</content></subsection></section>

<section changed="added" id="HBFA5B68A3B2642688F21E5F893E57232"><num value="7056"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7056. </inline></num><chapeau class="inline">None of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available under titles III through VI of this Act may be obligated or expended to provide—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H906E737B620F4DDD970BE94B972D2EA7" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>any financial incentive to a business enterprise currently located in the United States for the purpose of inducing such an enterprise to relocate outside the United States if such incentive or inducement is likely to reduce the number of employees of such business enterprise in the United States because United States production is being replaced by such enterprise outside the United States;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4DB7EB7059394A3E9C0DD80168204593" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>assistance for any program, project, or activity that contributes to the violation of internationally recognized workers’ rights, as defined in section 507(4) of the Trade Act of 1974, of workers in the recipient country, including any designated zone or area in that country: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the application of section 507(4)(D) and (E) of such Act (19 U.S.C. 2467(4)(D) and (E)) should be commensurate with the level of development of the recipient country and sector, and shall not preclude assistance for the informal sector in such country, micro and small-scale enterprise, and smallholder agriculture;</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8539AFB8F707439F85791A77928CBC7B" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>any assistance to an entity outside the United States if such assistance is for the purpose of directly relocating or transferring jobs from the United States to other countries and adversely impacts the labor force in the United States; or</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H2AC0E32349944D0A8DCDB7F065F8C32C" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><chapeau>for the enforcement of any rule, regulation, policy, or guidelines implemented pursuant to the Supplemental Guidelines for High Carbon Intensity Projects approved by the Export-Import Bank of the United States on December 12, 2013, when enforcement of such rule, regulation, policy, or guidelines would prohibit, or have the effect of prohibiting, any coal-fired or other power-generation project the purpose of which is to—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HDBB1AAB79237430199FD273D8F868B91" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>provide affordable electricity in International Development Association (IDA)-eligible countries and IDA-blend countries; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H07C4CB9AE2F240949C562D5FF39B32E7" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>increase exports of goods and services from the United States or prevent the loss of jobs from the United States.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></section>

<section changed="added" id="H0715CE2F37B142008101B3C8A40B9D46"><num value="7057"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7057. </inline></num><subsection id="H2E882B6C6B0F4749ADBB1DC6E52CD8EC" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Contribution</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds made available under the heading “International Organizations and Programs” in this Act for fiscal year 2020, $32,500,000 shall be made available for the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA).</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HFBD1327AECC94EB0A9545B87F75EB00B" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Availability of Funds</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act for UNFPA, that are not made available for UNFPA because of the operation of any provision of law, shall be transferred to the “Global Health Programs” account and shall be made available for family planning, maternal, and reproductive health activities, subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H13D9FBD967A74D6F876256C55B547158" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prohibition on Use of Funds in China</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds made available by this Act may be used by UNFPA for a country program in the People’s Republic of China.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HE0F521CC1E934130835FCF753FB9CFDD" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Conditions on Availability of Funds</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Funds made available by this Act for UNFPA may not be made available unless—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HDF931130A5EF44E78E215DF5B5798355" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>UNFPA maintains funds made available by this Act in an account separate from other accounts of UNFPA and does not commingle such funds with other sums; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H49AF4F9EBBA840A0A32FB8597F02825C" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>UNFPA does not fund abortions.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HCA0EC1C4AE1245F883B178588D4DC1A0" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report to Congress and Dollar-for-dollar Withholding of Funds</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H7F5844DA993B45D29F6B0A08A3580FAE" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>Not later than 4 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State shall submit a report to the Committees on Appropriations indicating the amount of funds that UNFPA is budgeting for the year in which the report is submitted for a country program in the People’s Republic of China.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H944DFFDDBC54429CA3A16F9B40F0D623" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>If a report under paragraph (1) indicates that UNFPA plans to spend funds for a country program in the People’s Republic of China in the year covered by the report, then the amount of such funds UNFPA plans to spend in the People’s Republic of China shall be deducted from the funds made available to UNFPA after March 1 for obligation for the remainder of the fiscal year in which the report is submitted.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<appropriations level="small" changed="added" id="HB56A45FA910A421688670540EBAEDE5F"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">global health activities</inline></heading></appropriations>
<section changed="added" id="H4979FAC697464286B177C01A455B92C3"><num value="7058"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7058. </inline></num><subsection id="H18967AD622974B74BB08AA45D2FA5E9C" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by titles III and IV of this Act that are made available for bilateral assistance for child survival activities or disease programs including activities relating to research on, and the prevention, treatment and control of, HIV/AIDS may be made available notwithstanding any other provision of law except for provisions under the heading “Global Health Programs” and the United States Leadership Against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Act of 2003 (117 Stat. 711; 22 U.S.C. 7601 et seq.), as amended: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That of the funds appropriated under title III of this Act, not less than $575,000,000 should be made available for family planning/reproductive health, including in areas where population growth threatens biodiversity or endangered species.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HAF84678E2FF3411FADED225FADD432DF" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Infectious Disease Outbreaks</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HF975A69633DF4B959EC3B2CFA26BD45C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps"> Extraordinary measures</inline>.—</heading><content>If the Secretary of State determines and reports to the Committees on Appropriations that an international infectious disease outbreak is sustained, severe, and is spreading internationally, or that it is in the national interest to respond to a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “Global Health Programs”, “Development Assistance”, “International Disaster Assistance”, “Complex Crises Fund”, “Economic Support Fund”, “Democracy Fund”, “Assistance for Europe, Eurasia and Central Asia”, “Migration and Refugee Assistance”, and “Millennium Challenge Corporation” may be made available to combat such infectious disease or public health emergency, and may be transferred to, and merged with, funds appropriated under such headings for the purposes of this paragraph.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H54B4C7E864264CFBB7B19523B9BDAB13" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Emergency reserve fund</inline>.—</heading><content>Up to $10,000,000 of the funds made available under the heading “Global Health Programs” may be made available for the Emergency Reserve Fund established pursuant to section 7058(c)(1) of the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2017 (division J of Public Law 115–31): <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds shall be made available under the same terms and conditions of such section.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE76BDFB16E084C3FBB3C47C68C509E23" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Ebola virus disease</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act and prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs under the heading “International Disaster Assistance” that are made available to respond to the Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, including in countries affected by, or at risk of being affected by, such outbreak, shall be the responsibility of the Assistant Administrator for Democracy, Conflict, and Humanitarian Assistance, USAID, or successor official responsible for USAID Ebola response.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H260DAFF6468E4DC5A7D3642697F50DBF" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Consultation and notification</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds made available by this subsection shall be subject to prior consultation with the appropriate congressional committees and the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<appropriations level="small" changed="added" id="H936EE8F7567A4FAEBAF31C6AEFE63AEA"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">gender equality</inline></heading></appropriations>
<section changed="added" id="HB003672BC3AD4D1D82C57BF8E6863847"><num value="7059"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7059. </inline></num><subsection id="HC995C873A65E4C29A38F61121E7BEE4F" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Women’s Empowerment</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HD895F19A44884D339A8D54705492A2F3" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Gender equality</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act shall be made available to promote gender equality in United States Government diplomatic and development efforts by raising the status, increasing the participation, and protecting the rights of women and girls worldwide.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H9CBFF37F183443F0A2101549E95DC96D" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Women’s economic empowerment</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act are available to implement the Women’s Entrepreneurship and Economic Empowerment Act of 2018 (Public Law 115–428): <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the Secretary of State and the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, as appropriate, shall consult with the Committees on Appropriations on the implementation of such Act.</proviso></content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H989DD80E1CF3478F99BBD4EA72BDCAFB" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Women’s global development and prosperity fund</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated under title III of this Act, up to $100,000,000 may be made available for the Women’s Global Development and Prosperity Fund.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H9556B55B11784506A9CF3224FCCB901A" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Women’s Leadership</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by title III of this Act, not less than $50,000,000 shall be made available for programs specifically designed to increase leadership opportunities for women in countries where women and girls suffer discrimination due to law, policy, or practice, by strengthening protections for women’s political status, expanding women’s participation in political parties and elections, and increasing women’s opportunities for leadership positions in the public and private sectors at the local, provincial, and national levels.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H4695612EFEB348D58E0D76BBE33FADF5" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Gender-Based Violence</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H641C8FFCB119469D8D0DBE448427B8E1" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>Of the funds appropriated under titles III and IV of this Act, not less than $165,000,000 shall be made available to implement a multi-year strategy to prevent and respond to gender-based violence in countries where it is common in conflict and non-conflict settings.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8BBBAB485965445BBE9C409015C10894" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Funds appropriated under titles III and IV of this Act that are available to train foreign police, judicial, and military personnel, including for international peacekeeping operations, shall address, where appropriate, prevention and response to gender-based violence and trafficking in persons, and shall promote the integration of women into the police and other security forces.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HE7DAA8CF96D046649B9C07015EFBEC12" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Women, Peace, and Security</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “Development Assistance”, “Economic Support Fund”, “Assistance for Europe, Eurasia and Central Asia”, and “International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement” should be made available to support a multi-year strategy to expand, and improve coordination of, United States Government efforts to empower women as equal partners in conflict prevention, peace building, transitional processes, and reconstruction efforts in countries affected by conflict or in political transition, and to ensure the equitable provision of relief and recovery assistance to women and girls.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H33EB47A79A2B42158C2D8E6E9D8A8F7F" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Women and Girls at Risk From Extremism and Conflict</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Economic Support Fund”, not less than $15,000,000 shall be made available to support women and girls who are at risk from extremism and conflict, and for the activities described in section 7059(e)(1) of the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2018 (division K of Public Law 115–141): <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds are in addition to amounts otherwise made available by this Act for such purposes, and shall be made available following consultation with, and the regular notification procedures of, the Committees on Appropriations.</proviso></content></subsection></section>
<appropriations level="small" changed="added" id="H07C958F836604D9498B9167C5D8BB446"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">sector allocations</inline></heading></appropriations>
<section changed="added" id="H82FC489BCB274BD18D7F8623311E7A53"><num value="7060"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7060. </inline></num><subsection id="H5174BB5D6C9146F49CBE4FFBB5972C5D" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Basic Education and Higher Education</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H2B6EE4D0CF1F4682A87E5392CB2081E3" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Basic education</inline>.—</heading><subparagraph id="H950CA3D2AC69439A9E7DEDE54E0558F4" class="inline"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Of the funds appropriated under title III of this Act, not less than $875,000,000 shall be made available for assistance for basic education, and such funds may be made available notwithstanding any other provision of law that restricts assistance to foreign countries: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds shall also be used for secondary education activities: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, following consultation with the Committees on Appropriations, may reprogram such funds between countries: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That funds made available under the headings “Development Assistance” and “Economic Support Fund” for the support of non-state schools in this Act and prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs shall be subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</proviso></content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H5CC30A4FCC9B474888753413A5800F9D" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Of the funds appropriated under title III of this Act for assistance for basic education programs, not less than $125,000,000 shall be made available for contributions to multilateral partnerships that support education.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HCC612FBBB31E4D3DBF8AA84898734AC7" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Higher education</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by title III of this Act, not less than $235,000,000 shall be made available for assistance for higher education: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds may be made available notwithstanding any other provision of law that restricts assistance to foreign countries, and shall be subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That of such amount, not less than $35,000,000 shall be made available for new and ongoing partnerships between higher education institutions in the United States and developing countries focused on building the capacity of higher education institutions and systems in developing countries: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That not later than 45 days after enactment of this Act, the USAID Administrator shall consult with the Committees on Appropriations on the proposed uses of funds for such partnerships.</proviso></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H22B75DC95DDE4B6ABD51EFD39CF5D19D" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Development Programs</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Development Assistance”, not less than $17,000,000 shall be made available for cooperative development programs of USAID and not less than $30,000,000 shall be made available for the American Schools and Hospitals Abroad program.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HC073B1D3AA074F1390BC62FBD710840F" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Environment Programs</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HDA8F66027EBA489E9F4A009CA9DEF559" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1)</num><subparagraph id="H53D5F98B870D48CD9641D731AA57ECFE" class="inline"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Funds appropriated by this Act to carry out the provisions of sections 103 through 106, and chapter 4 of part II, of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 may be used, notwithstanding any other provision of law, except for the provisions of this subsection, to support environment programs.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H421E7A0E707A4AEE8115C58DC42FD221" class="indent1"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Funds made available pursuant to this subsection shall be subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE9BB4088A24B47F380206C3D294E29E6" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2)</num><subparagraph id="HE7EE59A8946B4A94A4DA3D26018FDC01" class="inline"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Of the funds appropriated under title III of this Act, not less than $315,000,000 shall be made available for biodiversity conservation programs.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H137FDB98F5EA4559B1DABDA4ED7C7191" class="indent1"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Not less than $100,664,000 of the funds appropriated under titles III and IV of this Act shall be made available to combat the transnational threat of wildlife poaching and trafficking.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H3CF8D1B7F7F04C39A4C9DB0342244715" class="indent1"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>None of the funds appropriated under title IV of this Act may be made available for training or other assistance for any military unit or personnel that the Secretary of State determines has been credibly alleged to have participated in wildlife poaching or trafficking, unless the Secretary reports to the appropriate congressional committees that to do so is in the national security interest of the United States.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H5E695AE59C654AB69672A27CFC61A0ED" class="indent1"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>Funds appropriated by this Act for biodiversity programs shall not be used to support the expansion of industrial scale logging or any other industrial scale extractive activity into areas that were primary/intact tropical forests as of December 30, 2013, and the Secretary of the Treasury shall instruct the United States executive directors of each international financial institutions (IFI) to use the voice and vote of the United States to oppose any financing of any such activity.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H34A19ADA61584B31AC8507356C7B40F9" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>The Secretary of the Treasury shall instruct the United States executive director of each IFI that it is the policy of the United States to use the voice and vote of the United States, in relation to any loan, grant, strategy, or policy of such institution, regarding the construction of any large dam consistent with the criteria set forth in Senate Report 114–79, while also considering whether the project involves important foreign policy objectives.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA7A0C24A123B402B983C7219662F27C9" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>Of the funds appropriated under title III of this Act, not less than $135,000,000 shall be made available for sustainable landscapes programs.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB786549D9443455EB873D3E7B81C20DF" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>Of the funds appropriated under title III of this Act, not less than $177,000,000 shall be made available for adaptation programs.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H612F45B19FC14C69BCF42C3C22070582" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>Of the funds appropriated under title III of this Act, not less than $179,000,000 shall be made available for renewable energy programs.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H49EA1B37E9F6427DB41C3326346D1DF2" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Food Security and Agricultural Development</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by title III of this Act, not less than $1,005,600,000 shall be made available for food security and agricultural development programs to carry out the purposes of the Global Food Security Act of 2016 (Public Law 114–195): <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That funds may be made available for a contribution as authorized by section 3202 of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 (Public Law 110–246), as amended by section 3310 of the Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 (Public Law 115–334).</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HACFCD8A1793A495EB184168E3D2408F9" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Micro, Small, and Medium-Sized Enterprises</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act, not less than $265,000,000 shall be made available to support the development of, and access to financing for, micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises that benefit the poor, especially women.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H3ACC2DB69C81423EB634040C0CE6E04A" class="indent0"><num value="f">(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Programs To Combat Trafficking in Persons</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the headings “Development Assistance”, “Economic Support Fund”, “Assistance for Europe, Eurasia and Central Asia”, and “International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement”, not less than $67,000,000 shall be made available for activities to combat trafficking in persons internationally, of which not less than $45,000,000 shall be from funds made available under the heading “International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement”: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That funds appropriated by this Act that are made available for programs to end modern slavery shall be in addition to funds made available by this subsection to combat trafficking in persons.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H4F470C536AA9447989D744DAC6B9139F" class="indent0"><num value="g">(g) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reconciliation Programs</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act under the heading “Development Assistance”, not less than $30,000,000 shall be made available to support people-to-people reconciliation programs which bring together individuals of different ethnic, religious, and political backgrounds from areas of civil strife and war, including between Israelis and Palestinians living in the West Bank and Gaza: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That the USAID Administrator shall consult with the Committees on Appropriations, prior to the initial obligation of funds, on the uses of such funds, and such funds shall be subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further,</i> That to the maximum extent practicable, such funds shall be matched by sources other than the United States Government: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That such funds shall be administered by the Office of Conflict Management and Mitigation, USAID.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H31E36E8BDD504746B74AEA5F4169E345" class="indent0"><num value="h">(h) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Water and Sanitation</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the funds appropriated by this Act, not less than $450,000,000 shall be made available for water supply and sanitation projects pursuant to section 136 of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, of which not less than $225,000,000 shall be for programs in sub-Saharan Africa, and of which not less than $15,000,000 shall be made available to support initiatives by local communities in developing countries to build and maintain safe latrines.</content></subsection></section>

<section changed="added" id="HF51D03F52ABE4C8CB5BB1ED95E2EAB4A"><num value="7061"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 7061. </inline></num><subsection id="H42FAABBC77F1482AB1579FB3A8C2DF57" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Operating Plans</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 45 days after enactment of this Act, each department, agency, or organization funded in titles I, II, and VI of this Act, and the Department of the Treasury and Independent Agencies funded in title III of this Act, including the Inter-American Foundation and the United States African Development Foundation, shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations an operating plan for funds appropriated to such department, agency, or organization in such titles of this Act, or funds otherwise available for obligation in fiscal year 2020, that provides details of the uses of such funds at the program, project, and activity level: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such plans shall include, as applicable, a comparison between the congressional budget justification funding levels, the most recent congressional directives or approved funding levels, and the funding levels proposed by the department or agency; and a clear, concise, and informative description/justification: </proviso><proviso><i> Provided further</i>, That operating plans that include changes in levels of funding for programs, projects, and activities specified in the congressional budget justification, in this Act, or amounts specifically designated in the respective tables included in the explanatory statement described in section 4 (in the matter preceding division A of this consolidated Act), as applicable, shall be subject to the notification and reprogramming requirements of section 7015 of this Act.</proviso></content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H02A35D7CE60F4AED8C748E7EBA274357" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Spend Plans</inline>.—</heading>
