<section id="H3F4478975ADA4629AD4D0A6012C7D37E" styleType="traditional"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">reporting on financing related to china</inline></heading><num value="408"><inline class="smallCaps">Sec. 408. </inline></num>
<subsection id="H7264FEB04D684154983C027E23A53499" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">National Interest Report</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Before authorizing a loan or guarantee for a transaction in an amount greater than $25,000,000 for which the end user, lender, or obligor is the government of China, the President of the Export-Import Bank of the United States (in this section referred to as the “Bank”) shall—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HDE91741DBD55431791A6FB7D9F163AC6" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>report to the Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate that the Bank has consulted with the Secretary of State and any other relevant department or agency, as deemed appropriate by the President of the United States, to assess any risks posed by the entity or the transaction to the national interest of the United States; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3DDDF9C2CEBF4A979559F238E1189663" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>include a summary of the transaction and the consultation.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H6F3A0DF97DA2469C9C56D81C3804462A" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Form of Report</inline>.—</heading><content>The report described in subsection (a) shall be submitted in unclassified form but may include a classified annex.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H923C44AD731B49208F32BD762DFD051C" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Related Policies</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H84CDB8F087CF4876AC85B00A24954682" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><chapeau>The Board of Directors of the Bank shall prescribe policies for the Bank with respect to—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H6034B0C8D51F405FBF7742C55754A258" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>procedures required by the consultation described in subsection (a)(1);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HB7D435D35B374A299FA70CBABAC75714" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>establishment of a period of not less than 25 days to complete the consultations described in subsection (a) during which time consulted parties may submit any appropriate information to the Bank; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H4182CB96975344B686BA2F7231A518DE" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>efforts by the Bank to assess and determine ownership or control by the government of China pursuant to the requirements of subsection (a).</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HDA5F95459DDD427BBFC09B9D414C106C" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><chapeau>In prescribing the policies described under paragraph (1) of this subsection, the Board of Directors of the Bank shall—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HB1E4F54E4D094049933AD3DA6FCB782E" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><chapeau>consult with the Secretary of State with respect to the procedures referred to in subparagraphs (A) and (B) of paragraph (1) of this subsection, and seek to ensure that the procedures—</chapeau>
<clause id="HDB522808475F4A9AA109EED0796518B4" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>are consistent, wherever appropriate, with national interest determinations made under section 2(b)(1)(B) of the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H6D5246207AFF419F8A5AE28CF188D8A8" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>include coordination between the Secretary of State and the Director of National Intelligence, wherever appropriate; and</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HC00964A4B5C24635B7CBE6030E575184" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>consult with the Secretary of the Treasury with respect to the efforts described in paragraph (1)(C) of this subsection.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HBBF9BC87627B4A8194E907A5ED406080" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definition</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>For the purposes of this section, the term “government of China” means any person that the Bank has reason to believe is—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HE9AA607A0CAF424A9FC981E188F6B5D3" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the state and the government of China, as well as any political subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1FF345E636034E39AA8EFE1803C6CBCB" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>any entity controlled, directly or indirectly, by any of the foregoing, including any partnership, association, or other entity in which any of the foregoing owns a 50 percent or greater interest or a controlling interest, and any entity which is otherwise controlled by any of the foregoing;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1C30BECDC36F4CD285327F5E052606B9" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>any person that is or has been acting or purporting to act, directly or indirectly, for or on behalf of any of the foregoing; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H39C70E57D9C443DCAAAC1CD8E42AFB36" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>any other person which the Secretary of the Treasury has notified the Bank is included in any of the foregoing.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HF46468238DA941EC9A93C9B5E7A73AB7" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sunset</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>This section shall have no force or effect on the earlier of-—</chapeau>

<division id="HA059E4850BC74508BA526DA8E48B1F19" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="J">DIVISION J—</num><heading>FOREIGN POLICY</heading>
<title id="H44A41A9AF70D49179C2F8DF98E8D03EB" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="I">TITLE I—</num><heading class="inline">VENEZUELA ASSISTANCE</heading>
<section id="HE11C37C99D3F4E75AA4E513118D6F944" styleType="OLC"><num value="101">SEC. 101. </num><heading>SHORT TITLES.</heading><content class="block">This title may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="title">Venezuela Emergency Relief, Democracy Assistance, and Development Act of 2019</shortTitle>” or the “<shortTitle role="title">VERDAD Act of 2019</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<subtitle id="H9CB7A35CFA374AE89FB16D99F24EF6AE" styleType="OLC"><num value="A">Subtitle A—</num><heading>Support for the Interim President of Venezuela and Recognition of the Venezuelan National Assembly</heading>
<section id="H4481FCFA81FD450192C24112982EEE79" styleType="OLC"><num value="111">SEC. 111. </num><heading>FINDINGS; SENSE OF CONGRESS IN SUPPORT OF THE INTERIM PRESIDENT OF VENEZUELA.</heading>
<subsection id="HEC129804DCD04FA3906B3840EA09EEEF" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Findings</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Congress makes the following findings:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HE47B2E8882294E54BE1E135775FA1212" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>Venezuela’s electoral event on May 20, 2018 was characterized by widespread fraud and did not comply with international standards for a free, fair, and transparent electoral process.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFAE9569121AC4E1485A39FCD3F471372" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Given the fraudulent nature of Venezuela’s May 20, 2018 electoral event, Nicolás Maduro’s tenure as President of Venezuela ended on January 10, 2019.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HEE34E94A7DDB4009B3AA0BBD3B567121" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>The National Assembly of Venezuela approved a resolution on January 15, 2019 that terminated Nicolás Maduro’s authority as the President of Venezuela.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H671722A03F3D41FDAB5BCB120D5E71A5" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>On January 23, 2019, the President of the National Assembly of Venezuela was sworn in as the Interim President of Venezuela.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H7F327B9B510D4DB4AF6A3A759AA9A012" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>It is the sense of Congress—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H89CDC418049F44C5B28652BF34ACFD8E" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>to support the decisions by the United States Government, more than 50 governments around the world, the Organization of American States, the Inter-American Development Bank, and the European Parliament to recognize National Assembly President Juan Guaidó as the Interim President of Venezuela;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA3F6D56866994BD78F3D54E95880CD58" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>to encourage the Interim President of Venezuela to advance efforts to hold democratic presidential elections in the shortest possible period; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF8896399E2DC4EF4906F97AFF18E02EF" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>that the Organization of American States, with support from the United States Government and partner governments, should provide diplomatic, technical, and financial support for a new presidential election in Venezuela that complies with international standards for a free, fair, and transparent electoral process.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H563ADB61C84F4550ABAAEB74B2E8F641" styleType="OLC"><num value="112">SEC. 112. </num><heading>RECOGNITION OF VENEZUELA’S DEMOCRATICALLY ELECTED NATIONAL ASSEMBLY.</heading>
<subsection id="H3C979D018EF046908A40D9DF0438201F" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Findings</inline>.—</heading><content>Congress finds that Venezuela’s unicameral National Assembly convened on January 6, 2016, following democratic elections that were held on December 6, 2015.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HB43F5A0A5D4149D89941E6F8EF47CAD4" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><content>It is the sense of Congress that Venezuela’s democratically elected National Assembly is the only national level democratic institution remaining in the country.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HDF27AB7668834532BE23223F959543EA" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Policy</inline>.—</heading><content>It is the policy of the United States to recognize the democratically elected National Assembly of Venezuela as the only legitimate national legislative body in Venezuela.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H127A9DA3D1774E94B1F17A5AB523AF0A" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance to Venezuela’s National Assembly</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, in coordination with the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, shall prioritize efforts to provide technical assistance to support the democratically elected National Assembly of Venezuela in accordance with section 143.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="HB1A27DABA31C4F6DBCB07BCBA880DDB1" styleType="OLC"><num value="113">SEC. 113. </num><heading>ADVANCING A NEGOTIATED SOLUTION TO VENEZUELA’S CRISIS.</heading>
<subsection id="HEFF6BB976CEE422FA5D9DB61B7D38DCA" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>It is the sense of Congress that—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HDF6854D21AB3438AA5C4838E3B0EDA9B" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><chapeau>direct, credible negotiations led by the Interim President of Venezuela and members of Venezuela’s democratically elected National Assembly—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HC0BD6300FF604137B22973662C8DDCEF" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>are supported by stakeholders in the international community that have recognized the Interim President of Venezuela;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H5DC62C0E80544546B2B89D11FCD23584" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>include the input and interests of Venezuelan civil society; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HA815677C97364C5D900B2EDB1E96FC8E" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><chapeau>represent the best opportunity to reach a solution to the Venezuelan crisis that includes—</chapeau>
<clause id="HBF3EA57C1C304B05B426D5C895D4400E" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>holding a new presidential election that complies with international standards for a free, fair, and transparent electoral process;</content></clause>
<clause id="H416074EF4B66431C9DF27726939D50A8" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>ending Nicolás Maduro’s usurpation of presidential authorities;</content></clause>
<clause id="H85677CBEC07C471689261B21A28B632D" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>restoring democracy and the rule of law;</content></clause>
<clause id="HBFCDCA76B61448F59075E48CE9BFB8C7" class="indent3"><num value="iv">(iv) </num><content>freeing political prisoners; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H2B1C8569B0DF47D0BCEF401758D439C8" class="indent3"><num value="v">(v) </num><content>facilitating the delivery of humanitarian aid;</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H922257725DBA486DBA3CF957B291146B" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>dialogue between the Maduro regime and representatives of the political opposition that commenced in October 2017, and were supported by the Governments of Mexico, of Chile, of Bolivia, and of Nicaragua, did not result in an agreement because the Maduro regime failed to credibly participate in the process; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6B77C9120E39403D8A75DC6E24C3EFB2" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>negotiations between the Maduro regime and representatives of the political opposition that commenced in October 2016, and were supported by the Vatican, did not result in an agreement because the Maduro regime failed to credibly participate in the process.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HA859757FE95C43168A194350623AEB3F" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Policy</inline>.—</heading><content>It is the policy of the United States to support diplomatic engagement in order to advance a negotiated and peaceful solution to Venezuela’s political, economic, and humanitarian crisis that is described in subsection (a)(1).</content></subsection></section></subtitle>
<subtitle id="H7C101803A50C4CEA8A0A851203B7DEF1" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="B">Subtitle B—</num><heading>Humanitarian Relief for Venezuela</heading>
<section id="H45FEF3A30E254163970FAD462D00BD6F" styleType="OLC"><num value="121">SEC. 121. </num><heading>HUMANITARIAN RELIEF FOR THE VENEZUELAN PEOPLE.</heading>
<subsection id="HA8E511F8FC8F4C35B20F3B999244A178" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>It is the sense of Congress that—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H15B63B877CC04EA58A577D8A038A4825" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the United States Government should expand efforts to peacefully address Venezuela’s humanitarian crisis; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8A3F4D70DED347B6875E6F7EFD8F5DF6" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><chapeau>humanitarian assistance—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H7BB25554716A4A2E8B26884E409AE558" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>should be targeted toward those most in need and delivered through partners that uphold internationally recognized humanitarian principles; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H27FDDDCC7DE14796A0A3013FB4BC6201" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>should not be passed through the control or distribution mechanisms of the Maduro regime.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HD24A79F4011E4C539D08C2AD699EB617" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Humanitarian Relief</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HF264B247A97A42AEB4F5617116324DA1" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Secretary of State, in coordination with the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, shall provide—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HDF960200E7874939BAC4B796F170B1D6" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><chapeau>humanitarian assistance to individuals and communities in Venezuela, including—</chapeau>
<clause id="H60EEDE8B02384359BBFD4A599FA4BF5A" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>public health commodities and services, including medicines and basic medical supplies and equipment;</content></clause>
<clause id="H81618DE5CB80483393D592EC4FC219A7" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>basic food commodities and nutritional supplements needed to address growing malnutrition and improve food security for the people of Venezuela, with a specific emphasis on the most vulnerable populations; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H812F0E2487CD417889E2258B981F63AF" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>technical assistance to ensure that health and food commodities are appropriately selected, procured, targeted, and distributed; and</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HB68CCC4325904BCCAEDFF12A364B56E9" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><chapeau>Venezuelans and hosting communities, as appropriate, in neighboring countries with humanitarian aid, such as—</chapeau>
<clause id="H6153EAD48BA944639D4EADBCF44260DD" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>urgently needed health and nutritional assistance, including logistical and technical assistance to hospitals and health centers in affected communities;</content></clause>
<clause id="H09CA6E169DFA416FA52A6B3BF39692B2" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>food assistance for vulnerable individuals, including assistance to improve food security for affected communities; and</content></clause>
<clause id="HD9CFA83985714A35B846406BC9AA5243" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>hygiene supplies and sanitation services.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H588375F8159D4694B223CEDD9A2891CC" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Aid to venezuelans in neighboring countries</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The aid described in paragraph (1)(B)—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HF75AF281E7A642E6BD2061EEAA8ED35E" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><chapeau>may be provided—</chapeau>
<clause id="H89B2F68504B247C49029FF6BEB297386" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>directly to Venezuelans in neighboring countries, including countries of the Caribbean; or</content></clause>
<clause id="HF8A7F7A9E27448E1A0EB7C7159119D93" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>indirectly through the communities in which the Venezuelans reside; and</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HFAE6DE6B00C04630B3384D139446CC73" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>should focus on the most vulnerable Venezuelans in neighboring countries.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H43142C0735534B2EAB98A2A761B498C0" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Humanitarian Assistance Strategy Update</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, shall submit, to the appropriate congressional committees, an update to the Venezuela humanitarian assistance strategy described in the conference report accompanying the Consolidated Appropriations Act (Public Law 116–6), to cover a 2-year period and include—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H0F3F6D6EED344290A4F2043F243ED722" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>a description of the United States humanitarian assistance provided under this section;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA6EDA4B7DF1B454589B503B5F7AA6D87" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>a description of United States diplomatic efforts to ensure support from international donors, including regional partners in Latin America and the Caribbean, for the provision of humanitarian assistance to the people of Venezuela;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H375CFFE41A3A4F038B45CAA9C06016FD" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>the identification of governments that are willing to provide financial and technical assistance for the provision of such humanitarian assistance to the people of Venezuela and a description of such assistance; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3F409DE28AC144B98544CBF1342AF3E6" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>the identification of the financial and technical assistance to be provided by multilateral institutions, including the United Nations humanitarian agencies, the Pan American Health Organization, the Inter-American Development Bank, and the World Bank, and a description of such assistance.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H8BF0630E89C444A888C7BA6DB2BA8185" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Diplomatic Engagement</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, shall work with relevant foreign governments and multilateral organizations to coordinate a donors summit and carry out diplomatic engagement to advance the strategy required under subsection (c).</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H397AB0B5957F4BE08C3F6142785C28C3" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorization of Appropriations</inline>.—</heading><content>There is authorized to be appropriated $400,000,000 for fiscal year 2020 to carry out the activities set forth in subsection (b).</content></subsection>
<subsection role="definitions" id="H73D6914CEECE49779C2B46197BDFBB4F" class="indent0"><num value="f">(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Defined Term</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section, the term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HC5AD6E77E5304CD5B0C386B0DE99D21F" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSFR00">Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1FE4E42959B74929B2DD794200F15CF0" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSAP00">Committee on Appropriations of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCF147C658C9D46EBB5B857E0167D2B49" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives</committee>; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4FBE154BE0AE458D8483A0CF167D1725" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives</committee>.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="HEB662DFAEE15471FAF7D9672A71E265E" styleType="OLC"><num value="122">SEC. 122. </num><heading>SUPPORT FOR EFFORTS AT THE UNITED NATIONS ON THE HUMANITARIAN CRISIS IN VENEZUELA.</heading>
<subsection id="HCBA188FE448E4BBB81320FDEAA2C63F9" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>It is the sense of Congress that the United Nations humanitarian agencies should conduct and publish independent assessments of the humanitarian situation in Venezuela, including—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H08306C6C4F5045DC8ED71CB6F9AE172B" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the extent and impact of the shortages of food, medicine, and medical supplies in Venezuela;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H54B37928801141DEAAC7650D2CEDBD22" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>basic health indicators in Venezuela, such as maternal and child mortality rates and the prevalence and treatment of communicable diseases; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H31A3EAD1DEC94A8FB617E820A3CA019F" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>the efforts needed to resolve the shortages identified in paragraph (1) and to improve the health indicators referred to in paragraph (2).</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H3B999141924B40019063067EA0ED9F71" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">United Nations Resident Coordinator</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The President should instruct the Permanent Representative to the United Nations to use the voice, vote, and influence of the United States at the United Nations to support the efforts of the Resident Coordinator for Venezuela in a manner that—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HBDCE39016A714C1DA02A65C3976FAD8E" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>contributes to Venezuela’s long-term recovery; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6430BFD8108946E6941CA4D04DDF665B" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>advances humanitarian efforts in Venezuela and for Venezuelans residing in neighboring countries.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="HDA0AF7F8984845C48D67FFD5E1D1F677" styleType="OLC"><num value="123">SEC. 123. </num><heading>COORDINATION AND DISTRIBUTION OF HUMANITARIAN ASSISTANCE TO THE PEOPLE OF VENEZUELA.</heading>
<subsection id="H24B23B3CE70147D985DE1FEB90203BCF" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Short Title</inline>.—</heading><content>This section may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="section">Humanitarian Assistance to the Venezuelan People Act of 2019</shortTitle>”.</content></subsection>
<subsection role="definitions" id="HB29128680F1E489E895B09C9F35C7A35" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Defined Term</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section, the term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H1CD36CA44DB14E859F7F87BA56026ACE" changed="added" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSFR00" addedDisplayStyle="italic">Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3D5F3072BAED47A29A48137E30010409" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSAP00">Committee on Appropriations of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H081C8F942D034E0B88AB91A9634ECADE" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSBK00">Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4466D68FB09644E5A61A664CCAC84278" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HEBB05DA333734BBB934AB6E8973E4DBA" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives</committee>; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE7F5A1DCE3584471B552AFAF3DB14B9C" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives</committee>.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H2A32729BB73E4F34B4252FB0E37F41DF" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report on the Coordination and Distribution of Humanitarian Assistance to the People of Venezuela Including Strategy on Future Efforts</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H614341D118714D318316BD2AFBCE29F3" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, shall submit a report to the appropriate congressional committees that evaluates the delivery and coordination of humanitarian assistance to the people of Venezuela since the onset of the humanitarian crisis, whether residing in Venezuela or elsewhere in the Western Hemisphere.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4B80E1CB11A24174B51D10E53F9A57A7" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Matters to be included</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The report required under paragraph (1) shall—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H9455E928828247E7A7D18CD5A7145973" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>identify how United States Agency for International Development and Department of State best practices are being utilized in providing humanitarian assistance to Venezuela and countries in the region, including a description of coordination efforts with United States embassies and USAID missions throughout the region;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HFC76A890D4374F8A91ABA3D6DC136007" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>describe the current and anticipated challenges to distributing humanitarian assistance in Venezuela and countries hosting Venezuelan migrants;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HEF2288E73A5D41FD855C3CFE5D8CFBD8" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>describe the coordination of United States assistance with foreign donors; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H8DDAD983B8654895899C587D0A58EEE1" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><chapeau>describe how the distribution of humanitarian assistance is being monitored and evaluated, including—</chapeau>
<clause id="H69A0A9014E8347D5B31DCBFE945C8209" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>the number of beneficiaries receiving such assistance;</content></clause>
<clause id="H4422C29E6E2C4615BD74C5651303A3D5" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>an assessment of how humanitarian and development assistance is benefitting Venezuelan migrants inside and outside of the country; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H54057FE24B974904BF89F801D220858B" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>what additional staff may be necessary to manage such assistance.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle>
<subtitle id="H8AF59F83818648CF93FDE2F66C05EFEC" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="C">Subtitle C—</num><heading>Addressing Regime Cohesion</heading>
<section id="H5104461B0C2148B197626A318B0418E4" styleType="OLC"><num value="131">SEC. 131. </num><heading>CLASSIFIED BRIEFING ON DECLINING COHESION INSIDE THE VENEZUELAN MILITARY AND THE MADURO REGIME.</heading>
<subsection id="H6E377AE39820491EAD03E1725604E38F" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reporting Requirement</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, acting through the Bureau of Intelligence and Research, and in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, shall provide a briefing to the appropriate congressional committees that assesses the declining cohesion inside the Venezuelan military and security forces and the Maduro regime.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H38197F44932E48FAA4D0B302B5FE3F76" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Additional Elements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The briefing required under subsection (a) shall—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HA2A6C158024C4604964E7929949F7710" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>identify senior members of the Venezuelan military and the Maduro regime, including generals, admirals, cabinet ministers, deputy cabinet ministers, and the heads of intelligence agencies, whose loyalty to Nicolás Maduro is declining;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB20078811EB1445ABD1448CEC6AB9F77" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><chapeau>describe the factors that would accelerate the decision making of individuals identified in paragraph (1)—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HE0C2FF598C5945949C1D8F43A60686E9" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>to break with the Maduro regime; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HAAE9E063369D4C97BA2273AE530FA1BA" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>to recognize the Interim President of Venezuela and his government; and</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB6016BB562D54129B542CD7F51B62837" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>assess and detail the massive number of desertions and defections that have occurred at the officer and enlisted levels inside the Venezuelan military and security forces.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="definitions" id="H4606FA72B2484197A059B5B349A22FD7" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Appropriate Congressional Committees</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section, the term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HF92B0E56610441F48F5F4F1CC7070037" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSFR00">Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9BA7A0D665014C3B85089D4B186CF1A4" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SLIN00">Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4ED9D435428B43AB801AA5E81DAA300C" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives</committee>; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC24FB73D8F724424ABF9C66B28F38DC2" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>the <committee>Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives</committee>.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="HC020206D51BB4AF6A8570BB67147F5CE" styleType="OLC"><num value="132">SEC. 132. </num><heading>ADDITIONAL RESTRICTIONS ON VISAS.</heading>
<subsection id="H24A0A549D0304A23A84E3EE06B04EE1F" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Secretary of State shall impose the visa restrictions described in subsection (c) on any foreign person who the Secretary determines—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H223858C34245436699FA7F3DEB756170" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><chapeau>is a current or former senior official of the Maduro regime, or any foreign person acting on behalf of such regime, who is knowingly responsible for, complicit in, responsible for ordering, controlling, or otherwise directing, or participating in (directly or indirectly) any activity in or in relation to Venezuela, on or after January 23, 2019, that significantly undermines or threatens the integrity of—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H76F806F711CA43289A298D39755A5AAB" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the democratically-elected National Assembly of Venezuela; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H138A8C639182456485086A3C789832C6" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the President of such National Assembly, while serving as Interim President of Venezuela, or the senior government officials under the supervision of such President;</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFC84344488204F8991394312D1A4C990" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>is the spouse or adult child of a foreign person described in paragraph (1); or</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H370951945BDB4A96B36DAED800F55052" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><chapeau>is the spouse or adult child of Venezuelan person sanctioned under—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H3D789C04431E4A848ADA816EF5E198DC" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>section 5(a) of the Venezuela Defense of Human Rights and Civil Society Act of 2014 (Public Law 113–278), as amended by section 163 of this title;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD86DCC3B2BC14A8FBE8D403E59B0A196" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>section 804(b) of the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act (21 U.S.C. 1903(b)); or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD143EA796165486AA15685C5A933F422" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>Executive Orders 13692 (50 U.S.C. 1701 note) and 13850.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HE5300F157EA14A9EA9957D5CE848A8A2" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Removal From Visa Revocation List</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Pursuant to such procedures as the Secretary of State may establish to implement this section—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H80E7FD3E12F048E29005AB35A88F6028" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>if any person described in subsection (a)(1) recognizes and pledges support for the Interim President of Venezuela or a subsequent democratically elected government of Venezuela, that person and any family members of that person who were subject to visa restrictions pursuant to subsection (a)(2) shall no longer be subject to such visa restrictions; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFDDBEE92A2EF449BA7C13221D754B96A" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>if any person described in subparagraphs (A) through (C) of subsection (a)(3) recognizes and pledges support for the Interim President of Venezuela or a subsequent democratically elected government of Venezuela, any family members of that person who were subject to visa restrictions pursuant to subsection (a)(3) shall no longer be subject to such visa restrictions.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HE44C3569352C4ED0834AC215075A8C31" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Visa Restrictions Described</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HD9CA14BA20894ED19F7B10E8BFF6EAD8" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Visas, admission, or parole</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>An alien described in subsection (a) is—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H593AB434D52748818CCB92FABD5609F7" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>inadmissible to the United States;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H68BE2ED71F024A5DA5C41DD4F0633EC6" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>ineligible to receive a visa or other documentation to enter the United States; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HB184F978A11A4E679A926752FDC94C27" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>otherwise ineligible to be admitted or paroled into the United States or to receive any benefit under the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101 et seq.).</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5FF96C24817A4877A0CD7AD4E759D4B3" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Current visas revoked</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H2FBA323E2101473185C49E7887E9F854" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>An alien described in subsection (a) is subject to revocation of any visa or other entry documentation regardless of when the visa or other entry documentation is or was issued.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H585CB2AA29A14CBAB10F0D225B200F42" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Immediate effect</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>A revocation under subparagraph (A) shall—</chapeau>
<clause id="HDAE8F498DF66432784307E7AC518074B" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>take effect immediately; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H11EE7D6223D24DD686F5A8BD638BDC41" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>automatically cancel any other valid visa or entry documentation that is in the alien’s possession.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCF4D53694907430AACAE0B25C006C9EB" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exceptions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Sanctions under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall not apply with respect to an alien if admitting or paroling the alien into the United States is necessary—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H412835F36AF649BAB83602AC9981E29A" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>to permit the United States to comply with the Agreement regarding the Headquarters of the United Nations, signed at Lake Success June 26, 1947, and entered into force November 21, 1947, between the United Nations and the United States, or other applicable international obligations; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H194B2DA844984104AD9C195B5729FF53" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>to carry out or assist law enforcement activity in the United States.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H3213FBC4099E4BADAEFFE76C7E50455B" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Rulemaking</inline>.—</heading><content>The President shall issue such regulations, licenses, and orders as may be necessary to carry out this section.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="HB9C2B1C68E914F21B4AA3664D238C0D2" styleType="OLC"><num value="133">SEC. 133. </num><heading>WAIVER FOR SANCTIONED OFFICIALS THAT RECOGNIZE THE INTERIM PRESIDENT OF VENEZUELA.</heading>
<subsection id="HA413870B040043A788CE8952FA632AC2" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Removal of Sanctions</inline>.—</heading><content>If a person sanctioned under any of the provisions of law described in subsection (b) recognizes and pledges supports for the Interim President of Venezuela or a subsequent democratically elected government, the person shall no longer be subject to such sanctions, pursuant to such procedures as the Secretary of State and the Secretary of the Treasury may establish to implement this section.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H8DD493FA06F64054A055D8AC6F73800C" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sanctions Described</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The sanctions described in this subsection are set forth in the following provisions of law:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HF8AFC208FFC74D279850C746D9F0592C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1)</num><subparagraph id="HC65B0EF7E6E647ACB18F92ECB0B4DA9C" class="inline"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Paragraphs (3) and (4) of section 5(a) of the Venezuela Defense of Human Rights and Civil Society Act of 2014 (Public Law 113–278), as amended by section 163 of this title.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H31C2044BE4BB46309C8E62840912C3C4" class="indent1"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Paragraph (5) of section 5(a) of such Act, to the extent such paragraph relates to the sanctions described in paragraph (3) or (4) of such subsection.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFA776E1E917B417CB1FDDD931E0AFACC" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2)</num><subparagraph id="H0A20600E5BA5440DA0FF957BD3EDA913" class="inline"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Clauses (1) and (4) of section 1(a)(ii)(A) of Executive Order 13692 (50 U.S.C. 1701 note).</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HF8E744921CA9412EB213FBED9B069BF2" class="indent1"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Subparagraph (D)(2) of section 1(a)(ii) of such Executive Order, to the extent such subparagraph relates to the provisions of law cited in subparagraph (A).</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC17CBE9A5714416999ACF70A650BCD31" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3)</num><subparagraph id="H9E916F268DA34349AD57AF8AE0CE689C" class="inline"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Section 1(a)(ii) of Executive Order 13850.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HCBFC5C98E66C41DF9BDAB9CA35F0A89B" class="indent1"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Paragraph (iii) of section 1(a) of such Executive Order, to the extent such paragraph relates to the provision of law cited in subparagraph (A).</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H15140B74C7B4451699FF094853BAE99A" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Rulemaking</inline>.—</heading><content>The President shall issue such regulations, licenses, and orders as may be necessary to carry out this section.</content></subsection></section></subtitle>
<subtitle id="HE82FF8D8DF764AE7A0CF7014B9BDCB3C" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="D">Subtitle D—</num><heading>Restoring Democracy and Addressing the Political Crisis in Venezuela</heading>
<section id="H36413F19F66045F09A5F1FA21B153C13" styleType="OLC"><num value="141">SEC. 141. </num><heading>SUPPORT FOR THE ORGANIZATION OF AMERICAN STATES AND THE LIMA GROUP.</heading>
<subsection id="H5FECDB7DCB3C47E1AF44EAB9FFF5315F" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>It is the sense of Congress that the Secretary of State should—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H8D761587F6CB4DDA99C03A214C9E49CA" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>take additional steps to support ongoing efforts by the Secretary General of the Organization of American States to promote diplomatic initiatives to foster the restoration of democracy and the rule of law in Venezuela;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6C9B618754DD43C0B96F05A794A5D65F" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>conduct diplomatic engagement in support of efforts by the Lima Group to restore democracy and the rule of law in Venezuela and facilitate the delivery of humanitarian assistance for the Venezuelan people; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H86856091D59445F1923B36EFD8F9A7F8" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>engage with the International Contact Group on Venezuela to advance a peaceful and democratic solution to the current crisis.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H70BB0BB8D6E64C5FAF849C625175D044" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Defined Terms</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section:</chapeau>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HCC12B41205B14936A1E0990DCAF00B3C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">International contact group on venezuela</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The “<term>International Contact Group on Venezuela</term>” refers to a diplomatic bloc—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HC836B9B183FE47318591284495FC3736" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>whose members include the European Union, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Ecuador, Costa Rica, and Uruguay; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HF0399D6E44084183BCC088F88AA76DDB" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>which was established to advance a peaceful and democratic solution to the current crisis in Venezuela.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H3BDA9F2F319F4089B2E7A4390F0336F6" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Lima group</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The “<term>Lima Group</term>” refers to a diplomatic bloc—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H46E172606FD74D79B8C373DD3746BE96" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>whose members include Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Guyana, Honduras, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, and Saint Lucia; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H092094C5342F4828913C3D36BBFE41CE" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>which was established to address the political, economic, and humanitarian crises in Venezuela.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H20C512589DB4465198859336E77DEFA0" styleType="OLC"><num value="142">SEC. 142. </num><heading>ACCOUNTABILITY FOR CRIMES AGAINST HUMANITY.</heading>
<subsection id="HD3374863812B4381B51C3B717622A2FC" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><content>It is the sense of Congress that the Secretary of State should conduct robust diplomatic engagement in support of efforts in Venezuela, and on the part of the international community, to ensure accountability for possible crimes against humanity and serious violations of human rights.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H5460989F15BB4EA1AB88FF3008629656" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State shall submit a report to Congress that—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H66F117BF71FB462F99256D32A6033ABB" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>evaluates the degree to which the Maduro regime and its officials, including members of the Venezuelan security forces, have engaged in actions that constitute possible crimes against humanity and serious violations of human rights; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H958061095E094B41A571A4E146CD5E39" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>provides options for holding accountable the perpetrators identified under paragraph (1).</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H3A4E93B7F5C943D78925CE8BCAF44488" styleType="OLC"><num value="143">SEC. 143. </num><heading>SUPPORT FOR INTERNATIONAL ELECTION OBSERVATION AND DEMOCRATIC CIVIL SOCIETY.</heading>
<subsection id="HE1801FAEDC0540938CA1A1DD320FE289" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Secretary of State, in coordination with the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HC568C280138C4E56AF50746D8AF80EB7" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>shall work with the Organization of American States to ensure credible international observation of future elections in Venezuela that contributes to free, fair, and transparent democratic electoral processes; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4BC546775A7F4D2199033C63209DF4EE" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><chapeau>shall work with nongovernmental organizations—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H06BD9295D4A34D90B0754A8A5AAE90E1" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>to strengthen democratic governance and institutions, including the democratically elected National Assembly of Venezuela;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HB79EE1770B2F400897A3700464AC5AA9" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>to defend internationally recognized human rights for the people of Venezuela, including support for efforts to document crimes against humanity and violations of human rights;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HF6457CD442054D8EB0BB3735840391FE" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>to support the efforts of independent media outlets to broadcast, distribute, and share information beyond the limited channels made available by the Maduro regime; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HB3853BE6FAE5428789CD911549D0B5BB" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>to combat corruption and improve the transparency and accountability of institutions that are part of the Maduro regime.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HABB4D64BFE604B529EAC120262771F45" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Engagement at the Organization of American States</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, acting through the United States Permanent Representative to the Organization of American States, should advocate and build diplomatic support for sending an election observation mission to Venezuela to ensure that democratic electoral processes are organized and carried out in a free, fair, and transparent manner.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H2C9B573C14C74D6CAA017A5DBDB91EAF" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Briefing Requirement</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, shall provide a briefing on the strategy to carry out the activities described in subsection (a) to—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HB9E8B062CC54474588E93EDA33A56326" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSFR00">Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H73774D8755334FEABC22C9FADDC0F083" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSAP00">Committee on Appropriations of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H94456B81E9144E518529BBC7F08CE399" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives</committee>; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9034B967092F4BE7875C96817E670BFD" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives</committee>.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HB75073E076684197B7AAFB5937D85884" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorization of Appropriations</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H95E41B73AF3741358897A6A6BC30C804" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary of State for fiscal year 2020, $17,500,000 to carry out the activities set forth in subsection (a).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB7D02CA464FE42ABB1E8A2B2BF1AE88B" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Notification requirements</inline>.—</heading><content>Amounts appropriated pursuant to paragraph (1) are subject to the notification requirements applicable to expenditures from the Economic Support Fund under section 531(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2346(c)) and from the Development Assistance Fund under section 653(a) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2413(a)), to the extent that such funds are expended.</content></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle>
<subtitle id="H5FD5A6EAB89E423A8372F9A308F1B244" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="E">Subtitle E—</num><heading>Supporting the Reconstruction of Venezuela</heading>
<section id="H77862C2218134E0F8B1E459C4A4019EC" styleType="OLC"><num value="151">SEC. 151. </num><heading>RECOVERING ASSETS STOLEN FROM THE VENEZUELAN PEOPLE.</heading>
<subsection id="H343B0913D32A40808EA38448F06DDC0C" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Recovering Assets</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The President, acting through the Secretary of State and in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, shall advance a coordinated international effort—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H409A61013ED643BD95466E70B2344380" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><chapeau>to work with foreign governments—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HB2CA9C4643B64F7C84C89A90ED25D9BE" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>to share financial investigations intelligence, as appropriate;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HB58748F217FF42578A828A572C25E7CE" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>to block the assets identified pursuant to paragraph (2); and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H011F311120D645BA80329CB0AA8BED08" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>to provide technical assistance to help governments establish the necessary legal framework to carry out asset forfeitures; and</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H405634F4392B4666BE2D2CDED9F302E2" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>to carry out special financial investigations to identify and track assets taken from the people and institutions of Venezuela through theft, corruption, money laundering, or other illicit means.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HBAD671288E1647A38B2BF892DEB15D20" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Strategy Requirement</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H34612398200B4D038917DE9C24D123B9" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the President, acting through the Secretary of State and in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, shall submit a strategy for carrying out the activities described in subsection (a) to Congress.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HAE9288E31AF447ACA08BA7F4E2A7D55E" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Additional elements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The strategy required under paragraph (1) shall—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HCEF5A81357B5446380A90BD55D7AE59A" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>assess whether the United States or another member of the international community should establish a managed fund to hold the assets identified pursuant to subsection (a)(2) that could be returned to a future democratic government in Venezuela; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H45E09B3D9F0744C38B0C29C36364A8B0" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>include such recommendations as the President and the Secretary of State consider appropriate for legislative or administrative action in the United States that would be needed to establish and manage the fund described in subparagraph (A).</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle>
<subtitle id="H095A348DC1414F05BCD8D1697C3CA9F1" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="F">Subtitle F—</num><heading>Restoring the Rule of Law in Venezuela</heading>
<section id="H9641CE3EDFF840A39B51A404CAE4CA88" styleType="OLC"><num value="161">SEC. 161. </num><heading>DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING A COORDINATED SANCTIONS STRATEGY WITH PARTNERS IN THE WESTERN HEMISPHERE AND THE EUROPEAN UNION.</heading>
<subsection id="HDCDE5A37F0664C97832C40C8A50CE9AD" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Strengthening Sanctions Capacity in Latin America and the Caribbean</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, shall offer to provide technical assistance to partner governments in Latin America and the Caribbean to assist such governments in establishing the legislative and regulatory frameworks needed to impose targeted sanctions on officials of the Maduro regime who—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H110CD6ED75994860A38A051CC26EA149" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>are responsible for human rights abuses;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB0ACF656D0E945DFAE006BB90F0BC8A2" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>have engaged in public corruption; or</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H19712AE512034E3198EE6A601C94914C" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>are undermining democratic institutions and processes in Venezuela.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HA1E70A90F777490199958F5C5A499049" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Coordinating International Sanctions</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, shall engage in diplomatic efforts with partner governments, including the Government of Canada, governments in the European Union, and governments in Latin America and the Caribbean, to impose targeted sanctions on the Maduro regime officials described in subsection (a).</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HCFE7F025691445028944F82D1B7474C0" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Strategy Requirement</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, shall submit a strategy for carrying out the activities described in subsection (a) to—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HAF1A36E38F524B81AFB2A1B378E07384" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSFR00">Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H70CDA9B802374A068EE691AFFF70FAE9" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSAP00">Committee on Appropriations of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF0832D3A7675494AA15D89BFCC549717" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSBK00">Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H754E62BF035A483DB472A3EAD947CD5D" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H2B9F4F0C0B7746C087EEE0FA873437B8" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives</committee>; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1D60AC694B3A4783B2BF6DA6264F2345" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives</committee>.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HFFAF61D184FF445B90BB2E4A76FED4D5" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorization of Appropriations</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H605978F79AF24CBEA054AC4BD2454726" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary of State for fiscal year 2020, $3,000,000 to carry out the activities set forth in subsection (a).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H202B6CCBAB4E4D0A9B9E0E10C8511C3C" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Notification requirements</inline>.—</heading><content>Amounts appropriated pursuant to paragraph (1) are subject to the notification requirements applicable to expenditures from the Economic Support Fund under section 531(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2346(c)) and the International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Fund under section 489 of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2291h) to the extent that such funds are expended.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H99F6F16A66434AF3A0EDBED7298A6985" styleType="OLC"><num value="162">SEC. 162. </num><heading>CLASSIFIED BRIEFING ON THE INVOLVEMENT OF VENEZUELAN OFFICIALS IN CORRUPTION AND ILLICIT NARCOTICS TRAFFICKING.</heading>
<subsection id="H3983C69D0A614089A4D1EB7DDB37CFE0" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Briefing Requirement</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, acting through the Bureau of Intelligence and Research, and in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, shall provide a classified briefing to the appropriate congressional committees on the involvement of senior officials of the Maduro regime, including members of the National Electoral Council, the judicial system, and the Venezuelan security forces, in illicit narcotics trafficking and significant acts of public corruption in Venezuela.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HB54F8C2D98EB41A2AFD4656D35DF796B" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Additional Elements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The briefing provided under subsection (a) shall—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HC771D086AEA0475F86471D1B1680E4DF" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>describe how the significant acts of public corruption pose challenges for United States national security and impact the rule of law and democratic governance in countries of the Western Hemisphere;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD74BB7635C9A47B6AA04ED6621179086" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>identify individuals for whom there is credible information that they frustrated the ability of the United States to combat illicit narcotics trafficking;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H24D601880A4D44939DF79CD0C42494E5" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>include an assessment of the relationship between individuals identified under subsection (a) and Nicolás Maduro or members of his cabinet; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HAF23CFA5990A475C9788823E4D902057" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>include input from the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Office of Foreign Assets Control, and the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="definitions" id="HA3EE473C73034D66A4BF0CE28B7DAF99" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Appropriate Congressional Committees</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section, the term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H2EE84C75E64E4B69AE06193AAB994788" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSFR00">Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H491442AFE6C34B9BB1C142CDDF85DD89" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SLIN00">Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8C6838D3F5794131B04E5EB37E6F8EA3" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSBK00">Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB776C8FABB9348D98BF3EE973E2C1764" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB6AF4FE0AB45492989E18831E9330F00" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>the <committee>Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives</committee>; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H19DE1111E2AE4F16A364CD90DE4EF003" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives</committee>.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H8CF49FD68BDB4DA1A42E7E57D1D5C3BC" styleType="OLC"><num value="163">SEC. 163. </num><heading>CONCERNS OVER PDVSA TRANSACTIONS WITH ROSNEFT.</heading>
<subsection id="H3CB2DAD5597540F891F777713E75E41B" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Findings</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Congress makes the following findings:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HB6B2C37F41884403B553FEA7334C74B1" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>In late 2016, Venezuelan state-owned oil company Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. (referred to in this section as “PDVSA”), through a no compete transaction, secured a loan from Russian government-controlled oil company Rosneft, using 49.9 percent of PDVSA’s American subsidiary, CITGO Petroleum Corporation, including its assets in the United States, as collateral. As a result of this transaction, 100 percent of CITGO is held as collateral by PDVSA’s creditors.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8C45C14CA06D4FF782B373C05C3C8674" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>CITGO, a wholly owned subsidiary of PDVSA, is engaged in interstate commerce and owns and controls critical energy infrastructure in 19 States of the United States, including an extensive network of pipelines, 48 terminals, and 3 refineries, with a combined oil refining capacity of 749,000 barrels per day. CITGO’s refinery in Lake Charles, Louisiana, is the sixth largest refinery in the United States.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H276106A0C72A417CB9DDE478EA6A30D0" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>The Department of the Treasury imposed sanctions on Rosneft, which is controlled by the Government of the Russian Federation, and its Executive Chairman, Igor Sechin, following Russia’s military invasion of Ukraine and its illegal annexation of Crimea in 2014.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC729C94CDB1243F4BEF9195808704E49" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>The Department of Homeland Security has designated the energy sector as critical to United States infrastructure.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1D2EB5C1FE3A4A868C12FEC05EC6D30A" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>The growing economic crisis in Venezuela raises the probability that the Maduro regime and PDVSA will default on their international debt obligations, resulting in a scenario in which Rosneft could come into control of CITGO’s United States energy infrastructure holdings.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H10C4D8682A7442CFB58F20BD26982ED7" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>It is the sense of Congress that—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HA0A6680905EE4A1EB41689B9F0400169" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>control of critical United States energy infrastructure by Rosneft, a Russian government-controlled entity currently under United States sanctions that is led by Igor Sechin, who is also under United States sanctions and is a close associate of Vladimir Putin, would pose a significant risk to United States national security and energy security; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF25502FFFCAE49E9AB3A69D7EB329A1D" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>a default by PDVSA on its loan from Rosneft, resulting in Rosneft coming into possession of PDVSA’s United States CITGO assets, would warrant careful consideration by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HFF411F483D0344EB9793051DD35F8962" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Preventing Rosneft From Controlling United States Energy Infrastructure</inline>.—</heading><content>The President shall take all necessary steps to prevent Rosneft from gaining control of critical United States energy infrastructure.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H10A11B752AB94949BB0DC2033E34E035" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Security Risk Report</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the President shall submit a report assessing the national security risks posed by potential Russian acquisition and control of CITGO’s United States energy infrastructure holdings to—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H71916045263B439ABAB785F1693B5683" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSFR00">Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate;</committee></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HBD24878E94F04626A66427BBC947BEE3" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSGA00">Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H33BAE28C90FC47F2B7F5EFFD8AD2779B" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSBK00">Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3D8EC682F5124D4AA193EA7CC3BEFBDB" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives;</committee></content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB1D0BAED10CE40739C21D66ECC53E036" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives</committee>; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HBECB872090914FE4847DCF4D0B22D272" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives</committee>.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H3589CDE69E3743E5B65E2F38F614CB30" styleType="OLC"><num value="164">SEC. 164. </num><heading>CLASSIFIED BRIEFING ON ACTIVITIES OF CERTAIN FOREIGN GOVERNMENTS AND ACTORS IN VENEZUELA.</heading>
<subsection id="H7C9780E138984C288B51FF3CDCF7B11A" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, acting through the Bureau of Intelligence and Research of the Department of State, and in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, shall provide a classified briefing to the appropriate congressional committees on—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H14B9750D3B304FF08ED686FFBEC57452" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the full extent of cooperation by the Government of the Russian Federation, the Government of the People’s Republic of China, the Government of Cuba, and the Government of Iran with the Maduro regime; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H50AD310E20CF4BF7AD074CD099942233" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the activities inside Venezuelan territory of foreign armed groups, including Colombian criminal organizations and defectors from the Colombian guerilla group known as the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia, and foreign terrorist organizations, including the Colombian guerilla group known as the National Liberation Army (ELN).</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="definitions" id="HED417D625711444A9B9A2684FEEFEC30" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Appropriate Congressional Committees</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section, the term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H4436C3AE03D74957996B7AE26288E1B6" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSFR00">Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H34BBEE4328D547FAA10BEAFC192A98B6" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SLIN00">Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H87406C19C6F74358B6B20F1F2BB047B3" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives</committee>; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H18C06E0FA3B54BB2A3BC2ECCF57ADC5E" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>the <committee>Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives</committee>.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="HCDE5672E25A040ACBCA6FF1A4BE2CBDF" styleType="OLC"><num value="165">SEC. 165. </num><heading>COUNTERING RUSSIAN INFLUENCE IN VENEZUELA.</heading>
<subsection id="H1CFF457F09AE4513BE14AACD55C1AD88" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Short Title</inline>.—</heading><content>This section may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="section">Russian-Venezuelan Threat Mitigation Act</shortTitle>”.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HB67A0B70928A44219E62AE23ECD83112" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Threat Assessment and Strategy to Counter Russian Influence in Venezuela</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H214E9CE11137454682EFEA5E7DF34230" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Defined term</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this subsection, the term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H60046968AE8143BB9707922DB396F0DB" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSFR00">Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate</committee>; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H4F9CA083E84D410A87780B9B76B4C05B" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives</committee>.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H54C192F0CCF244D8A0A603715368C33E" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Threat assessment</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State shall submit a report to the appropriate congressional committees regarding—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H0B0014ED61B744E29F770F562B676B44" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>an assessment of Russian-Venezuelan security cooperation;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H5579DD7F771B48A98D2D9198136D2DEC" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the potential threat such cooperation poses to the United States and countries in the Western Hemisphere; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H6BAA368B0EA74F7496365BDBB9AC9414" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>a strategy to counter threats identified in subparagraphs (A) and (B).</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HC8092502D94B4BBCA1C3247448C1A234" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Aliens Ineligible for Visas, Admission, or Parole</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H600A7098DF9348AF90C7C23AE4E6A9F1" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Aliens described</inline>.—</heading><content>An alien described in this paragraph is an alien who the Secretary of State or the Secretary of Homeland Security (or a designee of either Secretary) knows, or has reason to believe, is acting or has acted on behalf of the Government of Russia in direct support of the security forces of the Maduro regime.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD9D7D6217C2E4DB4911862F982FF241B" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Visas, admission, or parole</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>An alien described in paragraph (1) is—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H228871B9506C4D078782F191856C7DAF" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>inadmissible to the United States;</content></subparagraph>
