<subparagraph id="H2F1B2611BD8745C8BDF3809FCB80F1D7" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>ineligible to receive a visa or other documentation to enter the United States; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H56B5A56C4E5D406AAD7E74D106B2C167" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>otherwise ineligible to be admitted or paroled into the United States or to receive any benefit under the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101 et seq.).</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD0615AEA98D841C1A8E027B56275F841" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Current visas revoked</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H071D262F3106447B99DC39679F1D3667" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>An alien described in paragraph (1) is subject to revocation of any visa or other entry documentation regardless of when the visa or other entry documentation is or was issued.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H30210A10BD694849BFFB655709E71FE0" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Immediate effect</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>A revocation under subparagraph (A) shall—</chapeau>
<clause id="H74D816C51CF847CFAC07FDA429C4EEE9" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>take effect immediately; and</content></clause>
<clause id="HB4FFE4F6A2EA41589981F5BFC55D0CE7" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>automatically cancel any other valid visa or entry documentation that is in the alien’s possession.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H52C401E72E09478AB0820AA2C44C509E" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exceptions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Sanctions under paragraphs (2) and (3) shall not apply with respect to an alien if admitting or paroling the alien into the United States is necessary—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H544A977C77D746EB92C3AF13C386090F" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>to permit the United States to comply with the Agreement regarding the Headquarters of the United Nations, signed at Lake Success June 26, 1947, and entered into force November 21, 1947, between the United Nations and the United States, or other applicable international obligations; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H8F7F8582053A41CF8B4B3083728A3E8C" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>to carry out or assist law enforcement activity in the United States.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE1A11362CBB6433586A6FAFD7CCA5534" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">National security</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The President may waive the application of this subsection with respect to an alien if the President—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H516F6FC8EE094E19BBCD55D6EB0DB3A3" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>determines that such a waiver is in the national interest of the United States; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H9E0EA5C501DE488FB1D89650AA053BCA" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>submits a notice of, and justification for, such waiver to the appropriate congressional committees.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HAE652230588F4636BBE1702A3E662DC4" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sunset</inline>.—</heading><content>This subsection shall terminate on the date that is 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H19ABEAE8B46949D3AB0FC7699030CCA6" styleType="OLC"><num value="166">SEC. 166. </num><heading>RESTRICTION ON EXPORT OF COVERED ARTICLES AND SERVICES TO CERTAIN SECURITY FORCES OF VENEZUELA.</heading>
<subsection id="HC1F7F797E38C4B0DBB839517CA255695" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Short Title</inline>.—</heading><content>This section may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="section">Venezuela Arms Restriction Act</shortTitle>”.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HB3258C6972874DFCB7FAEA7226E70EC0" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definitions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section:</chapeau>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HD7B060FC80894413B1E50019FD061020" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Appropriate congressional committees</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H57E98704C4CA4306BC568E7B60A48160" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSFR00">Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate</committee>;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H5B1D578E3E774A96A3848FEDE6AF8E67" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSBK00">Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate</committee>;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H46A08EB3CB9A47F8B31E8B8A34883524" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives</committee>; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H4E364BA1A6194B3C999A9C8D1981477A" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>the <committee>Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives</committee>.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H99051C2D1DAD43F9930830DF9ECE9AAD" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Covered article or service</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term “<term>covered article or service</term>”—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HA7D476C977FB43AE950E5AEE4763F2BE" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><chapeau>for purposes of subsection (c), means—</chapeau>
<clause id="H9EA166C04FBD4835B3D5C5C900585E7F" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>a defense article or defense service (as such terms are defined in section 47 of the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2794)); and</content></clause>
<clause id="H6DD25F155BD1496C80BE46FC4D070E2C" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>any article included on the Commerce Control List set forth in Supplement No. 1 to part 774 of the Export Administration Regulations under subchapter C of chapter VII of title 15, Code of Federal Regulations, and controlled for crime control purposes, if the end user is likely to use the article to violate the human rights of the citizens of Venezuela; and</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H239EB7EF20234D3C895A4D95C7A413AD" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><chapeau>for purposes of subsection (d), means—</chapeau>
<clause id="HD8841890AB7A4022867D0CA7E098607F" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>any defense article or defense service of the type described in section 47 of the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2794); and</content></clause>
<clause id="H87AF9F4E672A45419775A562AB47A50F" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>any article of the type included on the Commerce Control List set forth in Supplement No. 1 to part 774 of the Export Administration Regulations and controlled for crime control purposes.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HCFA9F12CEFEF479D9BEEE2DE35435CF8" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Foreign person</inline>.—</heading><content>The term “<term>foreign person</term>” means a person that is not a United States person.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HC6123600CF574989AF2B7EF336FA3C0F" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Person</inline>.—</heading><content>The term “<term>person</term>” means an individual or entity.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HD4C93FE77E1B42DDA74D4DC347415298" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Security forces of venezuela</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term “<term>security forces of Venezuela</term>” includes—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H1B768F42FFA54DB0B705E41C7C328172" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the Bolivarian National Armed Forces, including the Bolivarian National Guard;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HA9B6805592D94E62A17D127A44ADC81B" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the Bolivarian National Intelligence Service;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H3C17238B7DAA4727BA158B3064C19B73" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>the Bolivarian National Police; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HBD44BF58E74F455EAE66BAAA9E351EDA" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>the Bureau for Scientific, Criminal and Forensic Investigations of the Ministry of Interior, Justice, and Peace.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H07335C14159D4843BDC4C9188D38C112" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">United states person</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term “<term>United States person</term>” means—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HF476C68E674D4D9D9CDE680818965BF0" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>a United States citizen or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence to the United States; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H6D3E032552BA47268071A1A0A3B5C024" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>an entity organized under the laws of the United States or of any jurisdiction within the United States, including a foreign branch of such an entity.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H6EB3DDFCA809403E839E1F76523F0196" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Restriction on Export of Covered Articles and Services to Certain Security Forces of Venezuela</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H043A4F597D0A4886AF64DE720F841C47" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Notwithstanding any other provision of law, covered articles or services may not be exported from the United States to any element of the security forces of the Maduro regime.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3FD8FB50ECBC4E4DB4B2F419AD8D8E32" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Determination</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce and the heads of other departments and agencies, as appropriate, shall—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HCE2AA43F21CD40F392049F11AB64D32B" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>determine, using such information that is available to the Secretary of State, whether any covered article or service has been transferred since July 2017 to the security forces of Venezuela without a license or other authorization as required by law; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H8148371E0E6E4BAB92D03A8C1182B7CC" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>submit such determination in writing to the appropriate congressional committees.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H31105832C94D4FFB9ECE8950F1124456" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H953CCCCD89A44D0AB8E6032AE6C92C3C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce, as appropriate, shall submit a report to the appropriate congressional committees regarding the transfer by foreign persons of covered articles or services to elements of the security forces of Venezuela that are under the authority of the Maduro regime.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HEFEC64EBB30345B8A09789A5A57DB999" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Matters to be included</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The report required under paragraph (1) shall include—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HA0FCC361E9284EF8BEA1C25D41554E7B" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>a list of all significant transfers by foreign persons of covered articles or services to such elements of the security forces of Venezuela since July 2017;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H41D88293394A42A3B5B61644535EAEEF" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>a list of all foreign persons who maintain an existing defense relationship with such elements of the security forces of Venezuela; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H8727CAB5CF4E437A9F36D36CED38EFB4" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>any known use of covered articles or services by such elements of the security forces of Venezuela or associated forces, including paramilitary groups, that have coordinated with such security forces to assault, intimidate, or murder political activists, protesters, dissidents, and other civil society leaders, including Juan Guaidó.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H046351C70FFB44DDB1C51243F7B040AE" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sunset</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>This section shall terminate on the earlier of—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H97568E7A8D9D40F985300CDCEEDFE690" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the date that is 3 years after the date of the enactment of this Act; or</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HBC7AEBEBA7654A59B5E8CC156C089BB4" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the date on which the President certifies to the appropriate congressional committees that the Government of Venezuela has returned to a democratic form of government with respect for the essential elements of representative democracy as set forth in Article 3 of the Inter-American Democratic Charter, adopted by the Organization of American States in Lima on September 11, 2001.</content></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle>

<section id="H756BB3B46D6346459FA9B2D7C4DE5F6A" styleType="OLC"><num value="171">SEC. 171. </num><heading>BRIEFING ON THE IMPACT OF CRYPTOCURRENCIES ON UNITED STATES SANCTIONS.</heading>
<subsection role="definitions" id="H986F0E9E97C54E6FA8338E3488B2ACF3" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definition</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section, the term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HFEE8309B1A31480E91C3035AE005B9BE" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the <committee committeeId="SSFR00">Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate</committee>;</content></paragraph>

<subsection id="H10D39CA191B043D8863BD63BAD6DB698" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Methodology</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State and the Secretary of the Treasury, after consultation with the Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Chairman of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, shall develop a methodology to assess how any digital currency, digital coin, or digital token, that was issued by, for, or on behalf of the Maduro regime is being utilized to circumvent or undermine United States sanctions.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H3DFA36B498AF4DEE9B352CBFB5E62141" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Briefing</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State and the Secretary of the Treasury shall brief the appropriate congressional committees on the methodology developed under subsection (b).</content></subsection></section></subtitle>

<title id="H20D2AC1BC8574C33B8B9AF9AAE446699" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="II">TITLE II—</num><heading class="inline">EASTERN MEDITERRANEAN SECURITY AND ENERGY PARTNERSHIP</heading>
<section id="H3C677D43C1054D00A3363961A933EF2C" styleType="OLC"><num value="201">SEC. 201. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This title may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="title">Eastern Mediterranean Security and Energy Partnership Act of 2019</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section id="H0C7B85360C284ACAA4F5D6191FE7A8B0" styleType="OLC"><num value="202">SEC. 202. </num><heading>FINDINGS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">Congress makes the following findings:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HB69E422337F24269B4FE7F53F3021E1C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>The security of partners and allies in the Eastern Mediterranean region is critical to the security of the United States and Europe.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5D5B2E526B55490A8634C0FD310ABEA3" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Greece is a valuable member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) and a key pillar of stability in the Eastern Mediterranean.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1CF3A3D404D243C0B63DA9C7B59AB9EE" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>Israel is a steadfast ally of the United States and has been designated a “major non-NATO ally” and “major strategic partner”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H89E172DAE3584C84BB392E1942175809" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>Cyprus is a key strategic partner and signed a Statement of Intent with the United States on November 6, 2018, to enhance bilateral security cooperation.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H46CCC82AEEBB4B3EB790B9A6991DDC93" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>The countries of Greece, Cyprus, and Israel have participated in critical trilateral summits to improve cooperation on energy and security issues.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H14D78FD6D77D481085F4F288E368BC75" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>Secretary of State Mike Pompeo participated in the trilateral summit among Israel, Greece, and Cyprus on March 20, 2019.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H0AFFFA929A9C417C9CCA8F1DE110104E" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>The United States, Israel, Greece, and Cyprus oppose any action in the Eastern Mediterranean and the Aegean Sea that could challenge stability, violate international law, or undermine good neighborly relations, and in a joint declaration on March 21, 2019, agreed to “defend against external malign influences in the Eastern Mediterranean and the broader Middle East”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H7D24A01A3F1F45EF8A9A4EED2AC535A5" class="indent1"><num value="8">(8) </num><content>The recent discovery of what may be the region’s largest natural gas field off the Egyptian coast and the newest discoveries of natural gas off the coast of Cyprus could represent a significant and positive development for the Eastern Mediterranean and the Middle East, enhancing the region’s strategic energy significance.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4313882A46494BB8885048F7E3EF2C8D" class="indent1"><num value="9">(9) </num><content>It is in the national security interest of the United States to promote, achieve, and maintain energy security among, and through cooperation with, allies.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF4E014F1637A4D93824E53E0F028E27C" class="indent1"><num value="10">(10) </num><content>Natural gas developments in the Eastern Mediterranean have the potential to provide economic gains and contribute to energy security in the region and Europe, as well as support European efforts to diversify away from natural gas supplied by the Russian Federation.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCAD98C3E9E09407AAAC211184D01ABB2" class="indent1"><num value="11">(11) </num><content>The soon to be completed Trans Adriatic Pipeline is a critical component of the Southern Gas Corridor and the European Union’s efforts to diversify energy resources.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8DD22E6654104850AB7A800B5BA61512" class="indent1"><num value="12">(12) </num><content>The proposed Eastern Mediterranean pipeline, if commercially viable, would provide for energy diversification in accordance with the European Union’s third energy package of reforms.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H121D5B4166864D82B3FBC0D2DB50C323" class="indent1"><num value="13">(13) </num><content>The United States acknowledges the achievements and importance of the Binational Industrial Research and Development Foundation (BIRD) and the United States-Israel Binational Science Foundation (BSF) and supports continued multiyear funding to ensure the continuity of the programs of the Foundations.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H495BE827FD174607A9197777C69FFD2E" class="indent1"><num value="14">(14) </num><content>The United States has welcomed Greece’s allocation of 2 percent of its gross domestic product (GDP) to defense in accordance with commitments made at the 2014 NATO Summit in Wales.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9D2DE048B2F141B0976549886891EDB0" class="indent1"><num value="15">(15) </num><content>Energy exploration in the Eastern Mediterranean region must be safeguarded against threats posed by terrorist and extremist groups, including Hezbollah and any other actor in the region.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE192B4C8A188455EA37986EAFBCD6453" class="indent1"><num value="16">(16) </num><chapeau>The energy exploration in the Republic of Cyprus’s Exclusive Economic Zone and territorial waters—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H08283A74002F42958C7F17432DF8CBFE" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>furthers United States interests by providing a potential alternative to Russian gas for United States allies and partners; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H5B2FF6AA6EAA45008BCE8AFFF7E4DBDA" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>should not be impeded by other sovereign states.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H757CB82156C441FE9B5D429D60CB216D" class="indent1"><num value="17">(17) </num><content>The United States Government cooperates closely with Cyprus, Greece, and Israel through information sharing agreements.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H0CBF8EDEF7D941F995C9B8AE87B2DAD7" class="indent1"><num value="18">(18) </num><content>United States officials have assisted the Government of the Republic of Cyprus with crafting that nation’s national security strategy.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1D3DB4828E784FF0BD86CE9351C38C83" class="indent1"><num value="19">(19) </num><content>The United States Government provides training to Cypriot officials in areas such as cybersecurity, counterterrorism, and explosive ordnance disposal and stockpile management.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFB6E9614B21048EDBCCA832D224D94C1" class="indent1"><num value="20">(20) </num><content>Israel, Greece, and Cyprus are valued members of the Proliferation Security Initiative to combat the trafficking of weapons of mass destruction.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB027924D12D8475086F9437AB5FD11FF" class="indent1"><num value="21">(21) </num><content>The Republic of Cyprus continues to work closely with the United Nations and regional partners in Europe to combat terrorism and violent extremism.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H43D8C6C0002A469DBCCFEE0F7305C2EF" class="indent1"><num value="22">(22) </num><content>Despite robust economic and security relations with the United States, the Republic of Cyprus has been subject to a United States prohibition on the export of defense articles and services since 1987.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9C79E9D1E72B4888A8E0752D91D65AFF" class="indent1"><num value="23">(23) </num><content>The 1987 arms prohibition was designed to restrict United States arms sales and transfers to the Republic of Cyprus and the occupied part of Cyprus to avoid hindering reunification efforts.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA139373CE59747D8ADEBAA7BB3B97409" class="indent1"><num value="24">(24) </num><content>At least 40,000 Turkish troops are stationed in the occupied part of Cyprus with some weapons procured from the United States through mainland Turkey.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC864389859084391AC68DC3FA53A59B0" class="indent1"><num value="25">(25) </num><content>While the United States has, as a matter of policy, avoided the provision of defense articles and services to the Republic of Cyprus, the Government of Cyprus has, in the past, sought to obtain defense articles from other countries, including countries, such as Russia, that pose challenges to United States interests around the world.</content></paragraph></section>
<section id="HDDC6A7978C0443199A155B8F51922A11" styleType="OLC"><num value="203">SEC. 203. </num><heading>STATEMENT OF POLICY.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">It is the policy of the United States—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H3BCAC2D415B8428695B451CBE25B1E29" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>to continue to actively participate in the trilateral dialogue on energy, maritime security, cybersecurity and protection of critical infrastructure conducted among Israel, Greece, and Cyprus;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1680C945A4D44092B9D10B840127208A" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>to support diplomatic efforts with partners and allies to deepen energy security cooperation among Greece, Cyprus, and Israel and to encourage the private sector to make investments in energy infrastructure in the Eastern Mediterranean region;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HAA252579F6304C0AA1654F119E450B88" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>to strongly support the completion of the Trans Adriatic and Eastern Mediterranean Pipelines and the establishment of liquified natural gas (LNG) terminals across the Eastern Mediterranean as a means of diversifying regional energy needs away from the Russian Federation;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H110A041C233545BD8B39E590D7785D6A" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>to maintain a robust United States naval presence and investments in the naval facility at Souda Bay, Greece and develop deeper security cooperation with Greece to include the recent MQ–9 deployments to the Larissa Air Force Base and United States Army helicopter training in central Greece;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC720E3A8E9DF4BA0A5DB0802A09EDE05" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>to welcome Greece’s commitment to move forward with the Interconnector Greece-Bulgaria (IGB pipeline) and additional LNG terminals that will help facilitate delivery of non-Russian gas to the Balkans and central Europe;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HAEAA7A25782B4E6CB9881FAAD1BD30FF" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>to support deepened security cooperation with the Republic of Cyprus through the removal of the arms embargo on the country;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HEF792E4FC0314994B5B24A5BA68FBBF7" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>to support robust International Military Education and Training (IMET) programming with Greece and the Republic of Cyprus;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC5655C2EC8144B25B096F460E29C00AB" class="indent1"><num value="8">(8) </num><content>to leverage relationships within the European Union to encourage investments in Cypriot border and maritime security;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9323BFF510614FDD988FC2812E7AEE35" class="indent1"><num value="9">(9) </num><content>to support efforts to counter Russian Federation interference and influence in the Eastern Mediterranean through increased security cooperation with Greece, Cyprus, and Israel, to include intelligence sharing, cyber, and maritime domain awareness;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HDF22C9E2CE7745459F020DF4319D851B" class="indent1"><num value="10">(10) </num><content>to support the Republic of Cyprus’ efforts to regulate its banking industry to ensure that it is not used as a source of international money laundering and encourage additional measures toward that end;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF176F51210324D83906C04BB49DDEF09" class="indent1"><num value="11">(11) </num><content>to strongly oppose any actions that would trigger mandatory sanctions pursuant to section 231 of the Countering America’s Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (CAATSA) (Public Law 115–44), to include the purchase of military equipment from the Russian Federation;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H47E3BAEA43674B9D89AF00E0AD527343" class="indent1"><num value="12">(12) </num><content>to continue robust official strategic engagement with Israel, Greece, and Cyprus;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H68437D00C1A04024ABE008D1DE13581A" class="indent1"><num value="13">(13) </num><content>to urge countries in the region to deny port services to Russian Federation vessels deployed to support the government of Bashar Al-Assad in Syria;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB8ABE191D6004DB28522608C6DAC0E92" class="indent1"><num value="14">(14) </num><content>to support joint military exercises among Israel, Greece, and Cyprus;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H255360F56501450EB8CB9A371161D6B8" class="indent1"><num value="15">(15) </num><content>to fully implement relevant CAATSA provisions to prevent interference by the Russian Federation in the region;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H56B735E3423943AEAD8BD174043DCD3F" class="indent1"><num value="16">(16) </num><content>to support efforts by countries in the region to demobilize military equipment supplied by the Russian Federation in favor of equipment provided by NATO and NATO-allied member countries; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB2A7552CD4FC4FE0BB83FA9B43B9475D" class="indent1"><num value="17">(17) </num><content>to strongly support the active and robust participation of Israel, Cyprus, and Greece in the Combating Terrorism Fellowship Program.</content></paragraph></section>
<section id="H23A7C4509A09463B92714A11E803DA7F" styleType="OLC"><num value="204">SEC. 204. </num><heading>UNITED STATES-EASTERN MEDITERRANEAN ENERGY COOPERATION.</heading>
<subsection id="HE9C1F3F6FB464295947F3D3B6F444AC9" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretary of Energy, may enter into cooperative agreements supporting and enhancing dialogue and planning involving international partnerships between the United States and Israel, Greece, and the Republic of Cyprus.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HFC9C889261FC4823A41A483253F3D0A0" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Annual Reports</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>If the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretary of Energy, enters into agreements authorized under subsection (a), the Secretary shall submit an annual report to the appropriate congressional committees that describes—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H957F5BD4B8BA42EE8AE476D29A56F6B7" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>actions taken to implement such agreements; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5A53B60C4AB0410C8D463ED2F325921F" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>any projects undertaken pursuant to such agreements.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H25A2BFD8078D4225995660D0F77929A7" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">United States-Eastern Mediterranean Energy Center</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of Energy, in coordination with the Secretary of State, may establish a joint United States-Eastern Mediterranean Energy Center in the United States leveraging the experience, knowledge, and expertise of institutions of higher education and entities in the private sector, among others, in offshore energy development to further dialogue and collaboration to develop more robust academic cooperation in energy innovation technology and engineering, water science, technology transfer, and analysis of emerging geopolitical implications, which include opportunities as well as crises and threats from foreign natural resource and energy acquisitions.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="H108B68DA134C4485B33969FE2EF2072D" styleType="OLC"><num value="205">SEC. 205. </num><heading>REPEAL OF PROHIBITION ON TRANSFER OF ARTICLES ON THE UNITED STATES MUNITIONS LIST TO THE REPUBLIC OF CYPRUS.</heading>
<subsection id="H5C2905A33970400F9BAC228332CFA6A4" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>It is the sense of Congress that—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H8F2075355A4A47BE81871C719A8AB5EA" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>allowing for the export, re-export or transfer of arms subject to the United States Munitions List (part 121 of title 22, Code of Federal Regulations) to the Republic of Cyprus would advance United States security interests in Europe by helping to reduce the dependence of the Government of the Republic of Cyprus on other countries, including countries that pose challenges to United States interests around the world, for defense-related materiel; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3830599D2414471D9753372B112AABCF" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>it is in the interest of the United States to continue to support United Nations-facilitated efforts toward a comprehensive solution to the division of Cyprus.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HAA434BAC22994D35BBC2462AEBA8AC7F" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Modification of Prohibition</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 620C(e) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2373(e)) is amended—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HA5321F7EAFBB479E9008E53110D6A5DB" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>in paragraph (1), by striking “Any agreement” and inserting “Except as provided in paragraph (3), any agreement”; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H870EAF79BE604782AE6CF5E3DE29EAA0" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by adding at the end the following new paragraph:
<quotedContent id="HC8E5FAE64E16472597CA38288342F961" styleType="OLC">
<paragraph id="H478B13EAE2D24BACAF10D57DEBCE9470" class="indent0"><num value="3">“(3) </num><content>The requirement under paragraph (1) shall not apply to any sale or other provision of any defense article or defense service to Cyprus if the end-user of such defense article or defense service is the Government of the Republic of Cyprus.”</content></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H07A1EEFDCFDE449DA77039BAAC859793" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exclusion of the Government of the Republic of Cyprus From Certain Related Regulations</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HD4913FD4A59E4D48BFF88EE206E8AD7C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Subject to subsection (d) and except as provided in paragraph (2), beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State shall not apply a policy of denial for exports, re-exports, or transfers of defense articles and defense services destined for or originating in the Republic of Cyprus if—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HF15904A95AAD407387167207996A6D54" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the request is made by or on behalf of the Government of the Republic of Cyprus; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H6E733DE2D0F44907A9931A912241FCB8" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the end-user of such defense articles or defense services is the Government of the Republic of Cyprus.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA991F4A01B794F0AA8F6F9014937873D" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exception</inline>.—</heading><content>This exclusion shall not apply to any denial based upon credible human rights concerns.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H49F4FBB483834BD4B17159381440FFA0" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitations on the Transfer of Articles on the United States Munitions List to the Republic of Cyprus</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HDC6C76A124784DDFBBBE7C5B4A7B02C0" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The policy of denial for exports, re-exports, or transfers of defense articles on the United States Munitions List to the Republic of Cyprus shall remain in place unless the President determines and certifies to the appropriate congressional committees not less than annually that—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H92F916CCC2F541CF90E1E820FFA15E14" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the Government of the Republic of Cyprus is continuing to cooperate with the United States Government in efforts to implement reforms on anti-money laundering regulations and financial regulatory oversight; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H4E6552386E594B908CB5843A15EF630B" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the Government of the Republic of Cyprus has made and is continuing to take the steps necessary to deny Russian military vessels access to ports for refueling and servicing.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFAF056EA72D64BD9B898CD9BA8843651" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Waiver</inline>.—</heading><content>The President may waive the limitations contained in this subsection for one fiscal year if the President determines that it is essential to the national security interests of the United States to do so.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HF1EFA0F07CAE47DFA668D5517FEFAC77" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Appropriate congressional committees defined</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section, the term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H88A53CA49F444FA0983F04ACD43E9B2C" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the Committee on Foreign Relations and the Committee on Armed Services of the Senate; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H4673443D31204565A85FBF848DF84896" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the Committee on Foreign Affairs and the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="HE03AED2FC87B4E1C8451558B634C45F1" styleType="OLC"><num value="206">SEC. 206. </num><heading>IMET COOPERATION WITH GREECE AND THE REPUBLIC OF CYPRUS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">There is authorized to be appropriated $1,300,000 for fiscal year 2020, $1,500,000 for fiscal year 2021, and $1,800,000 for fiscal year 2022 for International Military Education and Training (IMET) assistance for Greece and $200,000 for fiscal year 2020, $500,000 for fiscal year 2021, and $750,000 for fiscal year 2022 for such assistance for the Republic of Cyprus. The assistance shall be made available for the following purposes:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H66BC32CD5717414792CF8F4A0FF7096D" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>Training of future leaders.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFE646E566D724DC49EC83AC49EB012AB" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Fostering a better understanding of the United States.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H0B9915B11A71429BA77C843C5174C9CD" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>Establishing a rapport between the United States military and the country’s military to build alliances for the future.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H27C4EC4429474ECF8E540D295D5C8CDE" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>Enhancement of interoperability and capabilities for joint operations.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H7139C89865DD413CBCD4134ECDD48283" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>Focusing on professional military education.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H127372D4498B434899933F8A61440674" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>Enabling countries to use their national funds to receive a reduced cost for other Department of Defense education and training.</content></paragraph></section>
<section id="H26A8EA91B68E4E9AB260261C0D8BD3E9" styleType="OLC"><num value="207">SEC. 207. </num><heading>FOREIGN MILITARY FINANCING.</heading>
<subsection id="H78387E4C99194275A689B0D2BC190ED0" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorization of Appropriations</inline>.—</heading><content>There is authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2021 up to $3,000,000 for Foreign Military Financing (FMF) assistance for Greece to assist the country in meeting its commitment as a member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) to dedicate 20 percent of its defense budget to enhance research and development.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H7B87EA00C5A040C1928D34E2937F056E" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><content>It is the sense of Congress that Greece should receive robust support under the European Recapitalization Incentive Program implemented by the Department of Defense.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="H02A0A7895C174348B30739C4E2FBF17D" styleType="OLC"><num value="208">SEC. 208. </num><heading>STRATEGY ON UNITED STATES SECURITY AND ENERGY COOPERATION IN THE EASTERN MEDITERRANEAN.</heading>
<subsection id="H3F369FA3364A42628E0DDD7FA90AB4EB" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Energy, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a strategy on enhanced security and energy cooperation with countries in the Eastern Mediterranean region, including Israel, the Republic of Cyprus, and Greece.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H601928F6247942A69528DD912E7740D3" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Elements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The report required under subsection (a) shall include the following elements:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HB87A7D2610F84E05B31AA0E2B4FCEC03" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>A description of United States participation in and support for the Eastern Mediterranean Natural Gas Forum.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF0110E25742D4C4080E824D5A9A3ED69" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>An evaluation of all possible delivery mechanisms into Europe for natural gas discoveries in the Eastern Mediterranean region.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6FFC7A2642834CAFB3B725D23383C034" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>An evaluation of efforts to protect energy exploration infrastructure in the region, including infrastructure owned or operated by United States companies.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF70FE2CE38814E81B2262A6A04BB72E3" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>An assessment of the capacity of the Republic of Cyprus to host an Energy Crisis Center in the region which could provide basing facilities in support of search and rescue efforts in the event of an accident.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H2EBC302861D54CADB89E98FDB0C186D3" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>An assessment of the timing of potential natural gas delivery in the region as well as an assessment of the ultimate destination countries for the natural gas delivery from the region.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H987B4AB5374F46FB94F4F00DE7699BCD" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>A plan to work with United States businesses seeking to invest in Eastern Mediterranean energy exploration, development, and cooperation.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H418C581C60254CA48959A025226FB169" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Form</inline>.—</heading><content>The report required under subsection (a) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may contain a classified annex.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="H58B72AB436A74BF2B73D5287506573F7" styleType="OLC"><num value="209">SEC. 209. </num><heading>REPORT ON RUSSIAN FEDERATION MALIGN INFLUENCE IN THE EASTERN MEDITERRANEAN.</heading>
<subsection id="H745B6CCABA5E472CA7559B96C29A6AF1" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report on Russian Federation malign influence in the Republic of Cyprus, Greece, and Israel since January 1, 2017.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H6A497BE9EEAF45BDBA591F58B8C08112" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Elements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The report required under subsection (a) shall include the following elements:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HD6AF7D8799BD452EAFB36B644D315795" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>An assessment of security, political, and energy goals of the Russian Federation in the Eastern Mediterranean.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H504461337B724005A7349167F53D1325" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>A description of energy projects of the Government of the Russian Federation in the Eastern Mediterranean.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1A9B1BCE322C40B785EE9BC53C71AE39" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>A listing of Russian national ownership of media outlets in these countries, including the name of the media outlet, approximate viewership, and assessment of whether the outlet promotes pro-Kremlin views.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H64290DD180BE4067871E1EECA1B11181" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>An assessment of military engagement by the Government of the Russian Federation in the security sector, including engagement by military equipment and personnel contractors.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9CE2760039B644899CC00C33A2352654" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>An assessment of efforts supported by the Government of the Russian Federation to influence elections in the three countries, through the use of cyber attacks, social media campaigns, or other malign influence techniques.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H00BA739396704172A55F192456116620" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>An assessment of efforts by the Government of the Russian Federation to intimidate and influence the decision by His All Holiness Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew, leader of 300,000,000 Orthodox Christians worldwide, to grant autocephaly to the Ukrainian Orthodox Church.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H296591DD10D844E98B40FFB29D1AD635" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Form</inline>.—</heading><content>The report required under subsection (a) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may contain a classified annex.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="HCF7A9767BE734D12AB24E9D7929DEF20" styleType="OLC"><num value="210">SEC. 210. </num><heading>REPORT ON INTERFERENCE BY OTHER COUNTRIES IN THE EXCLUSIVE ECONOMIC ZONE OF THE REPUBLIC OF CYPRUS.</heading>
<subsection id="HEE0710D157B742A6AE5926A4FBF1BDEF" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Energy, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report listing incidents since January 1, 2017, determined by the Secretary of State to interfere in efforts by the Republic of Cyprus to explore and exploit natural resources in its Exclusive Economic Zone.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HFB5FCF255DF74D7BA1418428F740BBCD" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Form</inline>.—</heading><content>The report required under subsection (a) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may contain a classified annex.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="H4AF57AB9372B48B2ADB076DED1FF535F" styleType="OLC"><num value="211">SEC. 211. </num><heading>REPORT ON INTERFERENCE BY OTHER COUNTRIES IN THE AIRSPACE OF GREECE.</heading>
<subsection id="H3D4EB7D9F573407CACF5C46C8B844010" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report listing incidents since January 1, 2017, determined by the Secretary of State to be violations of the airspace of the sovereign territory of Greece by its neighbors.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HFD5B7E8F835B4F1EB2ECDED7D8057A99" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Form</inline>.—</heading><content>The report required under subsection (a) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may contain a classified annex.</content></subsection></section>
<section role="definitions" id="H9F9E103EDD9B4B5491D1F0D29768DE5B" styleType="OLC"><num value="212">SEC. 212. </num><heading>APPROPRIATE CONGRESSIONAL COMMITTEES.</heading><content class="block">In this title, the term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives.</content></section></title>
<title id="H5ED499D6D2F4408581884070979D646C" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="III">TITLE III—</num><heading class="inline">END NEGLECTED TROPICAL DISEASES ACT</heading>
<section id="HA0134EFA0AC040AFA9C1B9797C7B5371" styleType="OLC"><num value="301">SEC. 301. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This title may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="title">End Neglected Tropical Diseases Act</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section id="HAF2C49D94DF64771AB6CE3280E53DF53" styleType="OLC"><num value="302">SEC. 302. </num><heading>STATEMENT OF POLICY.</heading><content class="block">It is the policy of the United States to support a broad range of implementation and research and development activities that work toward the achievement of cost-effective and sustainable treatment, control, and, where possible, elimination of neglected tropical diseases for the economic and social well-being of all people.</content></section>
<section role="definitions" id="H12E64B0820954C0EA1B6B69151863CFD" styleType="OLC"><num value="303">SEC. 303. </num><heading>DEFINITION.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">In this title, the terms “<term>neglected tropical diseases</term>” and “<term>NTDs</term>”—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H10ED5DAE56EE4DF688E7A304391C08CA" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>mean infections caused by pathogens, including viruses, bacteria, protozoa, and helminths that disproportionately impact individuals living in extreme poverty, especially in developing countries; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFF15D0B2547D48F1A363FCC17A1A29BB" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><chapeau>include—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H2DDE7FC037204B1BAE803E7AE8A333C0" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Buruli ulcer (Mycobacterium Ulcerans infection);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HA3F7448E8D1445B1B2D00784268A7BA0" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Chagas disease;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H86EFEAE317144F67BF1672A74C90B1C7" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>dengue or severe dengue fever;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H88AE35B7E2324D3F9042CD2FD3C9FC70" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>dracunculiasis (Guinea worm disease);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HF40187918F1541AEA876DC638142A461" class="indent2"><num value="E">(E) </num><content>echinococcosis;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H82CF7B5CBFEA4C94AF1196D61F823179" class="indent2"><num value="F">(F) </num><content>foodborne trematodiases;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H7E32FEB5281D463380F40C2B0CCCCEC5" class="indent2"><num value="G">(G) </num><content>human African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HCA73EBCD59DE41F693843D339C08535F" class="indent2"><num value="H">(H) </num><content>leishmaniasis;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HA32EF1AE82074B2298331B807488E611" class="indent2"><num value="I">(I) </num><content>leprosy;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H1E6252C05EC544A7B620117D326BF3F9" class="indent2"><num value="J">(J) </num><content>lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H709D2C02201749C59F104823A9B64CA1" class="indent2"><num value="K">(K) </num><content>onchocerciasis (river blindness);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H0732ACA64D5B4E72B10BCC60ED791054" class="indent2"><num value="L">(L) </num><content>scabies;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HE5F7FF99F1864DA3861A36C62D4E1A20" class="indent2"><num value="M">(M) </num><content>schistosomiasis;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HA6FCAE93FA8B42938F621EE9B2326A60" class="indent2"><num value="N">(N) </num><content>soil-transmitted helminthiases (STH) (roundworm, whipworm, and hookworm);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HE3063F19586E4820A50BBA9D7AD0CBA2" class="indent2"><num value="O">(O) </num><content>taeniasis/cysticercosis;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H74F0B674F42448FD839CB99A21D4E0DE" class="indent2"><num value="P">(P) </num><content>trachoma; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H48E7D1C170504422B3F04F4B580232EC" class="indent2"><num value="Q">(Q) </num><content>yaws (endemic treponematoses).</content></subparagraph></paragraph></section>
<section id="HA1FA59695BB3441EAE4F78A30F632599" styleType="OLC"><num value="304">SEC. 304. </num><heading>EXPANSION OF UNITED STATES AGENCY FOR INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT NEGLECTED TROPICAL DISEASES PROGRAM.</heading>
<subsection id="H52F8DEAE43B34D06AC6370AAF445D8E4" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>It is the sense of Congress that the Neglected Tropical Diseases Program, as in effect on the date of the enactment of this Act, should—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H745BC62AA170400AADBBEEF450C81EE4" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>provide integrated drug treatment packages to as many individuals suffering from NTDs or at risk of acquiring NTDs, including individuals displaced by manmade and natural disasters, as logistically feasible;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5D37B2BBD4B3454EB8380A15F30D1109" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>better integrate NTD control and treatment tools and approaches into complementary development and global health programs by coordinating, to the extent practicable and appropriate, across multiple sectors, including those relating to HIV/AIDS, malaria, tuberculosis, education, nutrition, other infectious diseases, maternal and child health, and water, sanitation, and hygiene;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE2979B6A649F40048475F8DB8B22CF0B" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>establish low-cost, high-impact community- and school-based NTD programs to reach large at-risk populations, including school-age children, with integrated drug treatment packages, as feasible;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H86B2CC35E67F4C6581FDA88D862D3A0E" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>as opportunities emerge and resources allow, engage in research and development of new tools and approaches to reach the goals relating to the elimination of NTDs as set forth by the 2012 World Health Organization publication “Accelerating Work to Overcome the Global Impact of Neglected Tropical Diseases: A Roadmap for Implementation”, including for Chagas disease, Guinea worm, human African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness), leprosy, and visceral leishmaniasis; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6081230C024A48689D67BA190D03D8C3" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>monitor research on and developments in the prevention and treatment of other NTDs so breakthroughs can be incorporated into the Neglected Tropical Diseases Program, as practicable and appropriate.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HB3D803A995EF4878B62F165792B44DDE" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Program Priorities</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development (referred to in this section as the “Administrator”) should incorporate the following priorities into the Neglected Tropical Diseases Program (as in effect on the date of the enactment of this Act):</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HCF64AC75370A440AB2CB753F2243FCA0" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>Planning for and conducting robust monitoring and evaluation of program investments in order to accurately measure impact, identify and share lessons learned, and inform future NTD control and elimination strategies.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H7EA9CC52E9B24BA9880A18377DD4AD7A" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Coordinating program activities with complementary development and global health programs of the United States Agency for International Development, including programs relating to water, sanitation, and hygiene, food and nutrition security, and education (both primary and secondary), in order to advance the goals of the London Declaration on Neglected Tropical Diseases (2012).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE408815768E343938C30FF17B987A889" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>Including morbidity management in treatment plans for high-burden NTDs.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H060B7B91393444FFA4CC39EBA6F6EB9D" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>Incorporating NTDs included in the Global Burden of Disease Study 2010 into the program as opportunities emerge, to the extent practicable and appropriate.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H2E97C8A52ED14775A0B62FB8BF5E6C6B" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>Continuing investments in the research and development of new tools and approaches that complement existing research investments and ensure that new discoveries make it through the pipeline and become available to individuals who need them most.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="HEC2E683ACAF94257AF150FB656CC03A8" styleType="OLC"><num value="305">SEC. 305. </num><heading>ACTIONS BY DEPARTMENT OF STATE.</heading>
<subsection id="HF5339A1851A24FEAA4350404AD9BC37C" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Office of the Global AIDS Coordinator</inline>.—</heading><content>It is the sense of Congress that the Coordinator of United States Government Activities to Combat HIV/AIDS Globally should fully consider evolving research on the impact of NTDs on efforts to control HIV/AIDS when making future programming decisions, as necessary and appropriate.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H360B282A42484B949332BB193EF8E88F" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Global Programming</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H7DB0CEBBEB06438D9825E80DE8E26ED8" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State should encourage the Global Fund to take into consideration evolving research on the impact of NTDs on efforts to control HIV/AIDS when making programming decisions, particularly with regard to female genital schistosomiasis, which studies suggest may be one of the most significant cofactors in the AIDS epidemic in Africa, as necessary and appropriate.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H6EFA7A77C9DB43269965A4E2ED99A5BF" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Global fund</inline>.—</heading><content>In this subsection, the term “<term>Global Fund</term>” means the public-private partnership known as the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria established pursuant to Article 80 of the Swiss Civil Code.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H476646622AF14213ACEACEFA3F0EC0BB" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">G–20 Countries</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, acting through the Office of Global Health Diplomacy, should encourage G–20 countries to significantly increase their role in the control and elimination of NTDs.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="H18AA9A41F3CE42469E888DEF3BD9491C" styleType="OLC"><num value="306">SEC. 306. </num><heading>MULTILATERAL DEVELOPMENT AND HEALTH INSTITUTIONS.</heading>
<subsection id="H0A5D8F255E2C44F7911919C80925BF77" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Finding</inline>.—</heading><content>Congress finds that the treatment of NTDs, including community- and school-based deworming programs, can be a highly cost-effective intervention, and schools can serve as an effective delivery mechanism for reaching large numbers of children with safe treatment for soil-transmitted helminthiases (roundworm, whipworm, and hookworm) in particular.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HDF042D0315E342A2A42E54EFD1A98D98" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">United Nations</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The President should direct the United States Permanent Representative to the United Nations to use the voice, vote, and influence of the United States to urge the World Health Organization and the United Nations Development Programme to—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H60FEBB3198D84FF8A1897EB499AC4666" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>ensure the dissemination of best practices and programming on NTDs to governments and make data accessible to practitioners in an open and timely fashion;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5D0F81EBAACB48C5A34C7E88FD94C9BE" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>highlight impacts of community- and school-based deworming programs on children’s health and education, emphasizing the cost-effectiveness of such programs;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H88277B52EECB4DCE838791DAD4C99626" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>encourage governments to implement deworming campaigns at the national level;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HEC12A4D0622B4026AD8CE193008F12FF" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>consider the designation of a portion of grant funds of the institutions to deworming initiatives and cross-sectoral collaboration with water, sanitation, and hygiene efforts and nutrition or education programming, as practicable and appropriate;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5758E3676D3A458CBF48D79C58327001" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>encourage accurate monitoring and evaluation of NTD programs, including deworming programs; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9583FD285BC542A69CAB82D6B353C50C" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>engage governments in cross-border initiatives for the treatment, control, prevention, and elimination of NTDs, and assist in developing transnational agreements, when and where necessary.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="HB2E0648593954F68BE250F1BA206D73E" styleType="OLC"><num value="307">SEC. 307. </num><heading>RULE OF CONSTRUCTION.</heading><content class="block">Nothing in this title may be construed to increase authorizations of appropriations for the United States Agency for International Development.</content></section></title>
<title id="H5F565D817FFC443CAE36FE59E857DCFD" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="IV">TITLE IV—</num><heading class="inline">PREVENTING CHILD MARRIAGE IN DISPLACED POPULATIONS</heading>
<section id="H3191A4448B124ABD9498BD816E7953A5" styleType="OLC"><num value="401">SEC. 401. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This title may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="title">Preventing Child Marriage in Displaced Populations Act</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section id="H9ACB363003684E6B80F3F8A785DC0024" styleType="OLC"><num value="402">SEC. 402. </num><heading>FINDINGS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">Congress finds the following:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H0C64F66978F2458D91B5916C9CFFAA7E" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>According to United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), 12,000,000 girls marry before the age of 18 every year.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HAB848E1239EF4440A3C204F9F9006CC5" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Early marriage denies children, especially girls, their right to make vital decisions about their well-being, including relating to their health, family, and career. Child brides are less likely to finish their education, and are at higher risk for abuse, contracting HIV, and dying while pregnant or giving birth.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCF1D5DAD461D429D94F866C3FDC718DD" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>Child marriage also imposes substantial economic costs to developing countries, impeding development and prosperity gains.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF94B96B8695445B5B5DC0C123C53A6BF" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>Displaced populations are particularly vulnerable to child marriage, in communities where poverty, instability, and displacement put pressure on families to marry children, particularly young girls, off at a young age.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H7B6935DAF5314B1B80D4B820ACE02936" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>One United Nations (UN) study found that child marriage rates were 4 times higher among displaced Syrian refugees than among Syrians before the crisis. This indicates that displacement, instability, and poverty are driving child marriages.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H849A70F7D5F84258940AB8B00955D65F" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>United Nations agencies, including UNICEF and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), have acknowledged the dangers of child marriage and taken steps to address its risk in the populations they serve.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9EB8A86D47DC430D88506322461CF4DA" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>The UN Joint Program on Child Marriage supports this work by building the resilience of populations to indirectly prevent child marriage and by generating new data and evidence on the prevalence of child marriage in humanitarian and fragile settings. For example, in Uganda, the UN Joint Program on Child Marriage helped 27,000 adolescent girls strengthen critical skills through school clubs and Go Back to School campaigns, as well as life skills and financial literacy training.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB3348E19087A49B0AB8F777724DAE214" class="indent1"><num value="8">(8) </num><content>After the UN Joint Program on Child Marriage identified Yemen as one of its focus countries, 65,000 people, of whom 45,000 are adolescents, were reached with awareness-raising activities on the harms of child marriage in 2018 alone. As a result, local council representatives, elders, and community leaders from 6 districts signed a pledge to support advocacy efforts to end child marriage.</content></paragraph></section>
<section id="H11DC3BF5B25E4E879ACFEEF4DD5DDE0F" styleType="OLC"><num value="403">SEC. 403. </num><heading>PREVENTING CHILD MARRIAGE IN DISPLACED POPULATIONS.</heading>
<subsection id="HA181C3F41DE84884B712800363C20F7A" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>The President shall direct the United States Permanent Representative to the United Nations to use the voice, vote, and influence of the United States at the United Nations to call for an adoption of an agreed upon definition of “child marriage” across United Nations agencies.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H092C546C119B4523B2F81FCB47EB9899" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Strategy</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The President shall direct the United States Permanent Representative to the United Nations to use the voice, vote, and influence of the United States at the United Nations to call for the development of a comprehensive strategy to address child marriage in refugee settlements administered by the United Nations. The strategy should include the following elements:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H0795DF9CCADC46F4932FD41A0BEFC247" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>A mandate to regularly collect and report data related to the number of known or suspected child marriages taking place inside each such settlement.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8DB5B52B5A464922B971DDC062353E0B" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Protocols for United Nations personnel regarding prevention and monitoring of child marriages inside each such settlement.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCE7F53B83C6D4E9292B04DAC4978173A" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><chapeau>A description of United Nations programs administered at such settlements that include—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HDCE25F41DEF24E6DA0C1DE59821BB6D3" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>physical, mental, and emotional rehabilitation and support to children who have extricated themselves from child marriage; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H77013223BA734D42955186BEE5CE7241" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>alternatives to child marriage, such as education initiatives.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF73BFC619F7141248982CCC28E27D551" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><chapeau>Protocols regarding how United Nations personnel should—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HF84E400210844DBAB89A907792D2BE6F" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>report adults participating in illegal child marriages in each such settlement; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H22F0E0320EE84B4C9370FCA88CB143A7" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>monitor the prosecution of such adults by the authorities of the country in which the settlement at issue is located.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HA58BCCABBA47469681EC9866A8962BAA" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Research</inline>.—</heading><content>The President shall direct the United States Permanent Representative to the United Nations to use the voice, vote, and influence of the United States at the United Nations to advocate for the United Nations and its appropriate agencies to include, as appropriate, in all of its research regarding child marriage, the relationship between child marriage and violence against girls, including young children and infants.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HB7250FCB52D04E0FBE90A4BFC3F5D941" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definitions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section:</chapeau>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HEC31A630B35A429CA1F4D62ECD2C680D" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Child marriage</inline>.—</heading><content>The term “<term>child marriage</term>” means a formal marriage or informal union involving at least one person younger than age 18.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HB2E216D977E44746B33954D1C92C3B78" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Illegal child marriage</inline>.—</heading><content>The term “<term>illegal child marriage</term>” means a child marriage that is illegal under the laws of the country in which the child marriage occurs.</content></paragraph></subsection></section></title>
<title id="H44EBD53B46064AEBB0FC8455E22DFEBE" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="V">TITLE V—</num><heading class="inline">GLOBAL FRAGILITY</heading>
<section id="HFDFC00C50C14402B9C73B45E47DAA30D" styleType="OLC"><num value="501">SEC. 501. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This title may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="title">Global Fragility Act of 2019</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section id="HCFC2786A7C65434D8FBD56445695AB2E" styleType="OLC"><num value="502">SEC. 502. </num><heading>APPROPRIATE CONGRESSIONAL COMMITTEES DEFINED.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">In this title:</chapeau>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H5E49A729966D4102872288165BAB4D9B" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Appropriate congressional committees</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HBFCECF6A83814BF4BE5C1D0F1256AC34" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the Committee on Foreign Relations and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H3B91FE6F9BF04452AD01C5CA3587376A" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the Committee on Foreign Affairs and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H411FD211240E43E6833A1846389EEDD8" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Relevant federal department or agency</inline>.—</heading><content>The term “<term>relevant Federal department or agency</term>” means the Department of State, the United States Agency for International Development, the Department of Defense, the Department of Treasury, and any other Federal department or agency the President determines is relevant to carry out the purposes of this title.</content></paragraph></section>
<section id="H5F7BEA06DCC847A1BEE4B2319E074566" styleType="OLC"><num value="503">SEC. 503. </num><heading>STATEMENT OF POLICY.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">It is the policy of the United States to seek to stabilize conflict-affected areas and prevent violence and fragility globally, including by—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H3507A0E2578646B8A7F2E38AE9B8FFA9" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>ensuring that all relevant Federal departments and agencies coordinate to achieve coherent, long-term goals for programs designed to carry out such policy;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9B1C3D0DFF554BEC8469E5FF549909DA" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>seeking to improve global, regional, and local coordination of relevant international and multilateral development and donor organizations regarding efforts to carry out such policy; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD44FCA91E7784791A9FBA2092E09DC76" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>enhancing the effectiveness of United States foreign assistance programs and activities to carry out such policy, including by improving assessment, monitoring, and evaluation conducted by the relevant Federal departments and agencies.</content></paragraph></section>
<section id="H57448E9B9FCC4F6EA7F5376AC108F052" styleType="OLC"><num value="504">SEC. 504. </num><heading>GLOBAL FRAGILITY STRATEGY.</heading>
<subsection id="HD049B5FC0801425CAD1DEEE2CF43701D" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Strategy</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The President, in coordination with the Secretary of State, the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development (“USAID”), the Secretary of Defense, and the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies, shall establish a comprehensive, integrated, ten-year strategy, to be referred to as the “Global Fragility Strategy”, to contribute to the stabilization of conflict-affected areas, address global fragility, and strengthen the capacity of the United States to be an effective leader of international efforts to prevent extremism and violent conflict. The strategy shall focus on addressing long-term causes of fragility and violence, and shall—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HB907D2FE6D9943E89F4E190768A16AAF" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>consider the causes of fragility and violence at both the local and national levels, the external actors that reinforce and exploit such conditions, and successful prevention strategies and their key features;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA822FF05877742E6AFED047CF4655F95" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>include specific objectives and multisectoral approaches to reduce fragility and the causes of violence, including those that strengthen state-society relations, curb extremist ideology, and make society less vulnerable to the spread of extremism and violence;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H2E5A88613170498F88A0AA318B06A42B" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>encourage and empower local and national actors to address the concerns of their citizens, including those in vulnerable communities, and build community resilience against violence and extremism;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD1987F3FAB2545F8B48BA1733E44F298" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>address the long-term underlying causes of fragility and violence through participatory, locally led programs, empowering marginalized groups such as youth and women, inclusive dialogues and conflict resolutions processes, justice sector reform, good governance, inclusive and accountable service delivery, and community policing and civilian security, including by combatting impunity for security forces implicated in violations of internationally recognized human rights and other serious crimes;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H68D88836AA654E26A937CF9BE4939EBB" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>describe approaches that ensure national leadership where appropriate and participatory engagement by civil society and local partners in the design, implementation, and monitoring of programs;</content></paragraph>
