<paragraph id="H8DF74E7E507D4655B71D5AA1DD34C7F5" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><chapeau>assign roles for relevant Federal departments and agencies to avoid duplication of efforts, while ensuring that—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HE33C2DD3294E444991A824C5CE510E13" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the Department of State is responsible for leading the drafting and execution of the strategy, establishing United States foreign policy, advancing diplomatic and political efforts, and overseeing the planning and implementation of security assistance and related civilian security efforts;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD2B5D44898914BA8A69B64CFC3B5A88A" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>USAID is responsible for overseeing prevention programs, and is the lead implementing agency for development, humanitarian, and related non-security program policy;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H996E89A5AA0F46C588194F7E86E50089" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>activities undertaken or supported by the Department of Defense in relation to the Global Fragility Strategy are established through joint formulation and with the concurrence of the Secretary of State; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HFE925F978D5D4DC0809CB690047104B6" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>other relevant Federal departments and agencies support the activities of the Department of State and USAID as appropriate, with the concurrence of the Secretary of State and the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development;</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1208FADD815C474D8DCAAC316B97A994" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>describe programs that relevant Federal departments and agencies will undertake to achieve the stated objectives, including descriptions of existing programs and funding by fiscal year and account;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H86818D2AF1454364AB33194E57A6DB3B" class="indent1"><num value="8">(8) </num><content>identify mechanisms to improve coordination between the United States, foreign governments, and international organizations, including the World Bank, the United Nations, regional organizations, and private sector organizations;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H33B2CDCDDF02496A8EE40CFA7133EAFD" class="indent1"><num value="9">(9) </num><content>address efforts to expand public-private partnerships and leverage private sector resources;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H26F1BD5DA1744DA080C4C0A7D91B939D" class="indent1"><num value="10">(10) </num><content>describe the criteria, metrics, and mechanisms for monitoring and evaluation of programs and objectives in the strategy to ensure planning, implementation, and coordination are appropriately executed and updated;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF531F3928DF1438F8710D447938B7E85" class="indent1"><num value="11">(11) </num><content>describe how the strategy will ensure that programs are country-led and context-specific; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE08983AD51A04752B3EE874E71BAA59E" class="indent1"><num value="12">(12) </num><content>identify mechanisms or activities to reduce the risk that the programs, policies, or resources of the United States and its partners will facilitate corruption, empower or abet repressive local actors, or be exploited by extremists to gain support for their cause.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H7B6821EB31BD48C3B0C5BD9C79C0D1D0" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Stakeholder Consultation</inline>.—</heading><content>The Global Fragility Strategy required under this section shall be developed in consultation with representatives of civil society and national and local governance entities in countries and regions described in section 505, as well as relevant international development organizations with experience implementing programs in fragile states, multilateral organizations and donors, relevant private, academic, and philanthropic entities, and the appropriate congressional committees.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HA949BC98870F4C119AA178A3C12087F4" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 270 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the President shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report setting forth the strategy described in subsection (a), which shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex if necessary, and shall include, at a minimum, the following elements:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HFEF37806C68547618082245FEA64B2AA" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>The objectives, general and specific, of the strategy.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HEAA76749EC59466EB8C91B77E70E5207" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>An identification of the relevant Federal departments and agencies that will be involved and the assignment of priorities to such departments and agencies.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6C6DB8B55C9A4EA3988F50B3B759EACF" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>A description of the compact-based partnerships that will be established to ensure local leadership of strategies, policy, and programs, as well as mutual accountability for results and resources needed to support such partnerships.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H89F6D0353CE64791A37C7354E037CB23" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>An identification of the authorities, staffing, and other requirements, as necessary and appropriate, needed to effectively implement the Global Fragility Strategy.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H2673129973BD436E9EF431B4B0AD8A30" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>A description of the ways in which United States leadership will be used to enhance overall international prevention efforts, including through increasing the engagement of the member states of the Group of Seven and Group of Twenty.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H7AAAB14ECC664D6A91A169E841105DAF" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>An identification of which officials of the Department of State, USAID, and the Department of Defense, with a rank not lower than Assistant Secretary or Assistant Administrator, will be responsible for leading and overseeing the strategy.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H288B995775144AC1AC07ACC9D8A1038C" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>A list of priority countries and regions selected pursuant to section 505, including descriptions of the rationale for such selections.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="HDF3D00387F9143C987E4FEEBE48C1CF9" styleType="OLC"><num value="505">SEC. 505. </num><heading>SELECTION OF PRIORITY COUNTRIES AND REGIONS.</heading>
<subsection id="HC230A14C75364A7980FD9AF98096BFE5" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The President, in coordination with the Secretary of State, the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, and the Secretary of Defense, and in consultation with the appropriate congressional committees specified in subsection (b), shall select certain countries as “priority countries” and certain regions as “priority regions” for the purpose of implementing the Global Fragility Strategy required under section 504—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H1E2CC80FD16E494099A038D97B459B1A" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><chapeau>on the basis of—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HF0FA2111BAD8420F9001E61C61D3425B" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the national security interests of the United States;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H71FFF2F83D0B46CDABA728730FA535CB" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><chapeau>clearly defined indicators of the levels of violence or fragility in such country or region, such as the country’s or region’s—</chapeau>
<clause id="H3C27DC1C04FB451FA42592BFC07B51E4" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>ranking on recognized global fragility lists, such as the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development States of Fragility report, the Fund for Peace Fragile States Index, the World Bank Harmonized List of Fragile Situations, the Institute for Economics and Peace Global Peace Index, and the Holocaust Museum Early Warning Project Risk Assessment;</content></clause>
<clause id="HA080CBAFE93E4E7588E4438B5959423B" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>ranking on select United States Government conflict and atrocity early warning watch lists;</content></clause>
<clause id="H4F34B76AF1AF472DAC8B3F83998F0FAE" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>levels of violence, including violence committed by armed groups, state actors, and violent extremist organizations, gender-based violence, and violence against children and youth; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H602A64742AB14C668FDFFE9F6F4129FD" class="indent3"><num value="iv">(iv) </num><content>vulnerability to rising sea levels, flooding, drought, wildfires, desertification, deforestation, food insecurity, and human displacement; and</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H053EE30BF2C84A2FBA516C9507E35D99" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><chapeau>an assessment of—</chapeau>
<clause id="H6D3156E14A54457C8404544AC528C39A" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><chapeau>the commitment and capacity of national and sub-national government entities and civil society partners in such country or region to work with relevant Federal departments and agencies on the Global Fragility Strategy, including by demonstrating commitment to—</chapeau>
<subclause id="HF918379CEDA249B690202BE91C07D50A" class="indent4"><num value="I">(I) </num><content>improving inclusive, transparent, and accountable power structures, including effective, legitimate, and resilient national and sub-national institutions; and</content></subclause>
<subclause id="HD5E86CA3D94F435BA847822C141342EE" class="indent4"><num value="II">(II) </num><content>ensuring strong foundations for human rights, rule of law, and equal access to justice; and</content></subclause></clause>
<clause id="HAFDE80AA064A4A15BACE0D4A62BF5336" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>the likelihood that United States assistance under the Global Fragility Strategy would measurably help to reduce fragility, prevent the spread of extremism and violence, and stabilize conflict-affected areas in each such country or region; and</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H55E7B520248242DFB8E97C4DC7920974" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>in a manner that ensures that not fewer than five countries or regions are selected, including not fewer than two in which the priority will be preventing violent conflict and fragility, rather than stabilizing ongoing conflicts.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H96AD27C82E354D4BA6EEC06E928DFE09" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Consultation With Congress</inline>.—</heading><content>Prior to finalization of the selection of priority countries and regions under subsection (a), representatives from the Department of State, USAID, the Department of Defense, and other relevant Federal departments and agencies, as necessary and appropriate, shall brief the appropriate congressional committees on the countries and regions being considered and shall consider congressional input on such prioritization.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="H7C2F7EB0D60346ABB304B4A0A7DB1E78" styleType="OLC"><num value="506">SEC. 506. </num><heading>PRIORITY COUNTRY AND REGIONAL PLANS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the President, in coordination with the Secretary of State, the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, the Secretary of Defense, and the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees ten-year plans to align and integrate under the Global Fragility Strategy established pursuant to section 504 all relevant diplomatic, development, and security assistance and activities of the United States Government with respect to each of the countries and regions selected pursuant to section 505. Each such country and regional plan shall include the following elements:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H8A7AE6A789EB444EBBE2B79EA5F509F3" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>Specific multi-year interagency plans for coordination and implementation under each such plan.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6A6568C3965D487D883395E68B5927B7" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>An up-to-date baseline analysis for each such country or region, including an analysis of the conditions that contribute to violence and fragility.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H26EC22D5A0134081BE211F8D988AF380" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>Prioritized descriptions of the goals and objectives for stabilizing conflict-affected areas, reducing fragility, and preventing the spread of extremism and violence in each such country.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H39A5AD76A80D4A45A480545BDC2DE13B" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>Descriptions of how and when the relevant goals, objectives, plans, and benchmarks for each such country or region will be incorporated into relevant United States country or regional plans and strategies, including the National Security Strategy of the United States, the Stabilization Assistance Review, Department of State Integrated Country Strategies, USAID Country Development Cooperation Strategies, and Department of Defense Campaign Plans, Operational Plans, and Regional Strategies, as well as any equivalent or successor plans or strategies.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE81660179AB94ACAB22EA6F6E2F48E78" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>Interagency plans to ensure that appropriate local actors, including government and civil society entities, have an appropriate ownership stake in developing, implementing, monitoring, and evaluating relevant activities under each such plan.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HAEDFE65C00744AD695445A01CE10900B" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>Interagency plans to integrate existing and planned security assistance and cooperation programs in each such country or region with the strategy, and to mitigate risks associated with such programs, including risks related to corruption, governance, and human rights.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4B137CFBC1CF4CE29C0B89CB32A2CA1F" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>Assessment, monitoring, and evaluation frameworks for diplomatic, development, and security assistance and activities, which shall be informed by consultations with the stakeholders specified in section 504(b), with clear metrics for each such country or region, as well as interagency plans for using such frameworks to adapt such activities on a regular basis.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5ADCBB8331F744EFA0BE90FC299DFE13" class="indent1"><num value="8">(8) </num><content>Descriptions of available policy tools and how such tools will be used to reduce fragility, prevent the spread of extremism and violence, and stabilize conflict-affected areas in each such country or region.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA08ECA5C9993414495A1ED0667E74CB2" class="indent1"><num value="9">(9) </num><chapeau>A description of how planning and implementation of assistance under the Global Fragility Strategy for each such country or region will be coordinated in a manner that strengthens partnerships and leverages the unique expertise and resources of the United States Government and—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H3D33AC50C2BE4114BE6CE26A75FC34E4" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>governments of such countries;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HF7C39D807A794937A8BEC914CF773004" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>international development organizations;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD71899ADF6314256B1EAD3E77C6FB472" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>relevant international donors;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H04C32CE3AEF24D528A58AF47CF2FE3C4" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>multilateral organizations; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H60154A333DE44937965E90F0BE089BD1" class="indent2"><num value="E">(E) </num><content>the private sector.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H89524A37324045C6A8A2593F5B2D63FB" class="indent1"><num value="10">(10) </num><content>A regional component outlining plans to address relevant transnational issues and how each such country is affected by or at risk of regional fragility or violence.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE7DB845535B34B668536DCC5329CA88A" class="indent1"><num value="11">(11) </num><content>When a region is selected, a component outlining plans to address factors at the individual country level that affect regional fragility or violence.</content></paragraph></section>
<section id="HA47CC38FD6904B6594DBE3D7AAD71B35" styleType="OLC"><num value="507">SEC. 507. </num><heading>IMPLEMENTATION.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">The President, in coordination with the Secretary of State, the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, the Secretary of Defense, the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies, relevant United States ambassadors, USAID mission directors, geographic combatant commanders, and other relevant individuals with responsibility over activities in each priority country or region selected pursuant to section 505, shall ensure that—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H381FB6EBA0ED4ED99BB574B2243B13B0" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the Global Fragility Strategy required under section 504, including each of the country plans developed under section 506, is implemented, updated, and coordinated on a regular basis; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFFB6C49D79F44B5EA3A7ED5504900C61" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the strategy is used to guide United States Government policy at a senior level and incorporated into relevant strategies and plans across the United States Government such that the activities of all relevant Federal departments and agencies are consistent with the strategy.</content></paragraph></section>
<section id="H89A6F771F5154DCDB43939FB1903D81A" styleType="OLC"><num value="508">SEC. 508. </num><heading>BIENNIAL REPORTS AND CONGRESSIONAL CONSULTATION.</heading>
<subsection id="H9D080709E32648C2A5A4FF91FB5AA251" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Biennial Reports</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than two years after the submission of the plans required in section 506, and every two years thereafter until the date that is ten years after the date of submission of such plans, the President, the Secretary of State, the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, the Secretary of Defense, and the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies shall jointly submit to the appropriate congressional committees an unclassified report, which may include a classified annex, on progress made and lessons learned with respect to implementation of the Global Fragility Strategy established pursuant to section 504. The report shall include the following elements:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H8F18B9F033E448BBA555E6CCED2DAC99" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>Descriptions of steps taken to incorporate the strategy into any relevant, existing country and regional plans or strategies.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HAC10A88B2F2F48A0A07BFCA68C4D3033" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Accountings of all funding received and obligated to implement each such country and regional plan during the previous two years, and, to the extent feasible, projections of funding to be requested, planned, and implemented for the following two years.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC82CA62541EF44EDBF445695F948BEBF" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>Descriptions of progress made towards achieving specific targets, metrics, and indicators for each priority country and region.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H434A3368AB124B90AE160D1928F8E781" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>Descriptions of any changes made to programs based on the results of assessment, monitoring, and evaluation for each priority country and region.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H99F9BDEBA6AD40808BBB1196CB876B4C" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Congressional Consultation</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, and the Secretary of Defense shall provide to any appropriate congressional committee briefings on the implementation of this title upon the request of any such committee.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="H422D9D50FEF849DCB1D8A0E102020AD6" styleType="OLC"><num value="509">SEC. 509. </num><heading>AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS.</heading>
<subsection id="H095DB35CCC5840B08E40256B77629B62" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prevention and Stabilization Fund</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H835C22832EB646FCB984A8625600DBEE" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Establishment</inline>.—</heading><content>There is established in the Treasury of the United States a fund, which shall be known as the “Prevention and Stabilization Fund” (in this subsection referred to as “The Fund”), to be administered by the Department of State and USAID, as appropriate, to support stabilization of conflict-affected areas and to mitigate fragility, including through the Global Fragility Strategy established pursuant to section 504, which shall replace the Relief and Recovery Fund.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCCDEEFA68435485CBDC676D79746A9A7" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorization of appropriations</inline>.—</heading><content>There is authorized to be appropriated to the Fund $200,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 2020 through 2024.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC96A7F6D7AF94AF7B69E005DBCF9DA3F" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Purposes of the fund</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H0C246C0891B5432F9A5E19E7CDAB345F" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Amounts authorized to be appropriated to the Fund shall be used—</chapeau>
<clause id="H04D1EE28E017423B8D991545BAEF9ECC" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>to support stabilization of conflict-affected areas and prevent global fragility, including through the Global Fragility Strategy established pursuant to section 504; and</content></clause>
<clause id="HAD8C2835E6C744A4B0EAA0AA5E5FA10C" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>to provide assistance to areas liberated or at risk from, or under the control of, the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria, other terrorist organizations, or violent extremist organizations, including for stabilization assistance for vulnerable ethnic and religious minority communities affected by conflict.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HC2203603D6DF463DB937A64527568995" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Amounts in addition</inline>.—</heading><content>Amounts authorized to be appropriated to the Fund under this section are in addition to any funds otherwise made available for the purposes described in paragraph (1).</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE97D574AE8154B76B5F43F6332C74375" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Congressional notification</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds may not be obligated under this section unless the congressional committees specified in section 634A of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2394–1) are notified of the amount and nature of such proposed obligation at least 15 days in advance of such proposed obligation, in accordance with the procedures applicable to notifications regarding reprogrammings pursuant to such section.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H744D8D07014C4520B55C8ACAF3A87369" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Complex Crisis Fund</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H5FD551EA4B324893A4D47C1490F36E63" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Establishment</inline>.—</heading><content>There is established in the Treasury of the United States a fund, which shall be known as the “Complex Crises Fund” (in this subsection referred to as the “Fund”), to be administered by USAID, to support programs and activities to prevent or respond to emerging or unforeseen events overseas, including to support the Global Fragility Strategy established pursuant to section 504.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H82859F743E974A6080FA31D5E59633F8" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorization of appropriations</inline>.—</heading><content>There is authorized to be appropriated to the Fund $30,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 2020 through 2024, which shall remain available until expended.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE69FA7F9C4B141529BDCE26CD9912EA5" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Purposes of the fund</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H537A38C347E94153AB473181CF144122" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Notwithstanding any other provision of law, except section 620M of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2378d), amounts in the Fund may be used to carry out the provisions of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2151 et seq.) to support programs and activities to prevent or respond to emerging or unforeseen foreign challenges and complex crises overseas, including through the Global Fragility Strategy established pursuant to section 504.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H6ABFF605A4C14A9FBE6F877C34C713F1" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Amounts in addition</inline>.—</heading><content>Amounts authorized to be appropriated to the Fund are in addition to any amounts otherwise made available for the purposes described in subparagraph (A).</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCE477B7FEDCD4920A19D3780AD556C0A" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitations</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H9E436F178AA048DCB4AC7F37F175569F" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Amounts in the Fund may not be expended for lethal assistance or to respond to natural disasters.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HFF44081BA13347FBB881FA9769F32FD6" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Administrative expenses</inline>.—</heading><content>Not more than five percent of the amounts in the Fund may be used for administrative expenses.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF03DC85EC4DA44EC80F1B3E4505E50D5" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Congressional notification</inline>.—</heading><content>The United States Agency for International Development shall notify the appropriate congressional committees not less than five days prior to the obligation of amounts in the Fund.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB3D4A3C6EB1B49659714D893C817130F" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Waiver</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The notification requirement under paragraph (5) may be waived if—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H0F6F813FD5D341A0A32D348730F03015" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>notification by the deadline specified in such paragraph would pose a substantial risk to human health or welfare; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HC2B96C1B8BE94EA5AC7287A0A67B81AE" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><chapeau>the appropriate congressional committees—</chapeau>
<clause id="HDD6779898342408E8592397585639C3C" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>are notified as early as practicable but in no event later than three days after an obligation of amounts from the Fund; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H0D09E3DCC2464CDFA3B2A3E3A0A15C11" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>are provided with an explanation of the emergency circumstances that necessitated such waiver.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H581777C01DBC4219BADF967B3465EAE1" styleType="OLC"><num value="510">SEC. 510. </num><heading>IMPROVING AND LEVERAGING ASSISTANCE FOR THE GLOBAL FRAGILITY STRATEGY.</heading>
<subsection id="HC413E1B656F24E828BB0A99B8025FB5C" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>It is the sense of Congress that the President, the Secretary of State, the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, the Secretary of Defense, and the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies should—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HF9A1730505F54BD18763E322BD62ED64" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>develop more adaptive and responsive policy and program planning, implementation, and scaling under the Global Fragility Strategy established pursuant to section 504, and work with the appropriate congressional committees to identify any legislative changes that may be necessary to support such efforts;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC38846121F7348CDA3A509924ED042FD" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>better integrate the strategy and other conflict and violence reduction objectives and activities into other policy and program areas, where appropriate; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9912593641E044BC8F0FF577294B4A7C" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>support transparent and accountable multilateral funds, initiatives, and strategies to enhance and better coordinate private and public efforts to stabilize conflict-affected areas and prevent violence and fragility globally.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H3864080546A24746BCB11F8085F61EED" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Other Funding and Cost Matching</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Global Fragility Strategy established pursuant to section 504—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HDDEAAFEBEFF54B2CBE2ADF73A1868041" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>may, after consultation with the appropriate congressional committees, be supported with funds other than funds authorized to be appropriated pursuant to section 509; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC3854E379CA748C3A398BDA807AAD50D" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>shall seek to leverage funds from sources other than the United States Government in order to promote coordination and cost-matching to the maximum extent practicable.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HF79EBE0A11774BF0AAAA1072CEC88DCD" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Multi-donor Global Fragility Fund</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H7395814E8BEE4C5986BCC7F5FF0FD7F2" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authority</inline>.—</heading><content>Pursuant to sections 607 and 632 of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2357 and 2392), and consistent with subsection (b), and after consultation with the appropriate congressional committees, the Secretary of State is authorized to establish funding mechanisms, to include the establishment of a Global Fragility Fund, to leverage, receive, coordinate, and program funds provided by other donors and private sector partners to carry out the purposes of this title.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HDEDD3AA649534ED3AEEA4BB31B35E32F" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Purposes</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>A funding mechanism established pursuant to paragraph (1) should—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H544E5E593FB74D97A6D3FCDFC4E48B1C" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>include input from and participation by key bilateral and multilateral donors, representatives of civil society, relevant nongovernmental organizations and private sector entities, and developing countries where fragility threatens to exacerbate violent extremism and undermine development;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HEB5DE9ED981D4544813E867A008DA00B" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>enhance donor coordination and cooperation;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H1812A69C126F45C8A90451E548345AD0" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>advance clearly defined goals, objectives, and metrics for monitoring, evaluating, and measuring progress; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HC3F4454F2B39499FBBE7808D16A411A9" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>focus on strengthening national and local good governance and conflict resolution capacity in fragile and conflict-affected areas over the long-term through comprehensive, compact-based agreements that support country-led strategies.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HDC3FCD2E046C45F68DDDD87620C7B159" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Congressional notification</inline>.—</heading><content>Funds may not be obligated under this section except in consultation with the appropriate congressional committees and subject to the notification of such committees of the amount and proposed uses of such funds at least 15 days in advance of such proposed obligation.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H3DDD3DDB87D9401EBB4376CC564541B8" styleType="OLC"><num value="511">SEC. 511. </num><heading>RULE OF CONSTRUCTION.</heading><content class="block">Nothing in this title shall be construed as a declaration of war or an authorization for the use of military force.</content></section></title>
<title id="HBAB0C4A3EBD441D1AF51D85469937C00" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="VI">TITLE VI—</num><heading class="inline">COMBATING WILDLIFE TRAFFICKING</heading>
<section id="HB448A3B53C61421AAC9FA65B6CAB2B54" styleType="OLC"><num value="601">SEC. 601. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This title may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="title">Rescuing Animals With Rewards Act of 2019</shortTitle>” or the “<shortTitle role="title">RAWR Act</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section id="HEEDC484125A94BD5A2296390BEA271D7" styleType="OLC"><num value="602">SEC. 602. </num><heading>FINDINGS; SENSE OF CONGRESS.</heading>
<subsection id="HBC942E861A044E6E8D2D67D3321E74EC" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Findings</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Congress finds the following:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H3DDD2D3C22A44E589BAC4EB69B56F91C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>Wildlife trafficking is a major transnational crime that is estimated to generate over $10 billion a year in illegal profits and which is increasingly perpetrated by organized, sophisticated criminal enterprises, including known terrorist organizations.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H0D54B3CF9FDD48B58693775863C7C30F" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Wildlife trafficking not only threatens endangered species worldwide, but also jeopardizes local security, spreads disease, undermines rule of law, fuels corruption, and damages economic development.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H730BD6BDE2E74869AE30855087AA4B0F" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>Combating wildlife trafficking requires a coordinated and sustained approach at the global, regional, national, and local levels.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HBDAF3AED59794CD5916F085CE548B4C4" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>Congress stated in the Eliminate, Neutralize, and Disrupt Wildlife Trafficking Act of 2016 that it is the policy of the United States to take immediate actions to stop the illegal global trade in wildlife and wildlife products and associated trans­na­tion­al organized crime.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HBDB1631D770642CB80FCC8F139E384A2" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><content>It is the sense of Congress that the Department of State’s rewards program is a powerful tool in combating sophisticated international crime and that the Department of State and Federal law enforcement should work in concert to offer rewards that target wildlife traffickers.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="H2E83D5B4887347129E34AE6EC1DEF855" styleType="OLC"><num value="603">SEC. 603. </num><heading>WILDLIFE TRAFFICKING PREVENTION AWARDS PROGRAM.</heading><content class="block">Subparagraph (B) of section 36(k)(5) of the State Department Basic Authorities Act of 1956 (22 U.S.C. 2708(k)(5)) is amended by inserting “wildlife trafficking (as defined by section 2(12) of the Eliminate, Neutralize, and Disrupt Wildlife Trafficking Act of 2016 (16 U.S.C. 7601(12); Public Law 114–231)) and” after “includes”.</content></section></title>
<title id="HF03AA7BD407E4E81AD9458B7ED1FABEA" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="VII">TITLE VII—</num><heading class="inline">CHAMPIONING AMERICAN BUSINESS THROUGH DIPLOMACY</heading>
<section id="H00A37A0B2AC8450DB18034773C81309A" styleType="OLC"><num value="701">SEC. 701. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This title may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="title">Championing American Business Through Diplomacy Act of 2019</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section id="H377CF69DA6C045318C9D02DB2253F572" styleType="OLC"><num value="702">SEC. 702. </num><heading>FINDINGS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">Congress makes the following findings:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H5F8F83155285457B958CA77E16BA0CE1" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>According to the 2017 National Security Strategy of the United States of America, “Retaining our position as the world’s preeminent economic actor strengthens our ability to use the tools of economic diplomacy for the good of Americans and others.”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8FCE48DB72C5499392CE015F6765F15B" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>A November 7, 2018, cable from Secretary of State Michael R. Pompeo to all diplomatic and consular posts—“Boosting Commercial Diplomacy Around the World”—stated that “helping American companies is a foreign policy priority…Promoting broad-based, responsible, and sustainable economic growth helps to stabilize regions and creates new and growing markets for U.S. companies. A transparent and level playing field for U.S. investment in these countries counters real and growing challenges such as China’s Belt and Road initiative.”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H74D36036E2E94A179AA7AAC1BB8CD965" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>In the January–February 2019 issue of The Foreign Service Journal, Ambassador Barbara Stephenson, the President of the American Foreign Service Association, wrote, “Foreign Service support for American business…is a major reason why the U.S. Foreign Service was created.”.</content></paragraph></section>
<section id="HE14148B9958A438D8AF9C8750DB8FC00" styleType="OLC"><num value="703">SEC. 703. </num><heading>ECONOMIC DIPLOMACY WITHIN THE DEPARTMENT OF STATE.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">Subsection (c) of section 1 of the State Department Basic Authorities Act of 1956 (22 U.S.C. 2651a) is amended—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H133C13563CD54446831F8A62328FD326" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by redesignating paragraph (3) as paragraph (4); and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H2756EC706B294251A8C868D482BB9F4A" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by inserting after paragraph (2) the following new paragraph:
<quotedContent id="HE4CDAB693A6340FC9B9F851055D2B60B" styleType="OLC">
<paragraph id="HB8A1A587C02A48CD807F0E831F856679" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistant secretary for economic and business matters</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="HE45BABDF07F348129A8BE7C7BE57757E" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Subject to the numerical limitation specified in paragraph (1), there is authorized to be established in the Department of State an Assistant Secretary of State who shall be responsible to the Secretary of State for matters pertaining to international economics and business matters in the conduct of foreign policy.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H11C6FC35F43E4C1F9185724D06886909" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Matters contemplated</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The matters referred to in subparagraph (A) include the following:</chapeau>
<clause id="H4F0C232723B14DD092A13CD7A5135EDC" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>International trade and investment policy.</content></clause>
<clause id="HDBB2DA9659AB4057A96C0C1E0709AEDE" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>International finance, economic development, and debt policy.</content></clause>
<clause id="H516B92E8BE5D4CD3B0C08290232AF937" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>Economic sanctions and combating terrorist financing.</content></clause>
<clause id="HA9FE8F0060FF45899D07C0DDD7C648EA" class="indent3"><num value="iv">“(iv) </num><content>International transportation policy.</content></clause>
<clause id="H9250E6478D834E1FAF25696FDF2641F3" class="indent3"><num value="v">“(v) </num><content>Support for United States businesses.</content></clause>
<clause id="H7758C563B1104A27971F493DD94FF1DD" class="indent3"><num value="vi">“(vi) </num><content>Economic policy analysis and private sector outreach.</content></clause>
<clause id="HF29186F0C90B4F4DAAB7DFC533C01AFE" class="indent3"><num value="vii">“(vii) </num><content>International data privacy and innovation policies.</content></clause>
<clause id="H3AD7877BC54D45B0BDF69E8870C9AC0D" class="indent3"><num value="viii">“(viii) </num><content>Such other related duties as the Secretary may from time to time designate.”</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph></section>
<section id="HEA9364953CE34EB3AAADEBFF766A3F0D" styleType="OLC"><num value="704">SEC. 704. </num><heading>CHIEF OF MISSION RESPONSIBILITIES.</heading><content>Section 207 of the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (22 U.S.C. 3927) is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:
<quotedContent id="HEE0EEC78CE474FFEB59347FA372BBCDC" styleType="OLC">
<subsection id="HC9D595C457C54ED1830DF789A735308C" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Promotion of United States Economic Interests</inline>.—</heading><content>Each chief of mission to a foreign country shall have as a principal duty the promotion of United States economic and commercial interests in such country.”</content></subsection></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></section>
<section id="H7A3B563A31AF4722A2FD7738377416EE" styleType="OLC"><num value="705">SEC. 705. </num><heading>INCREASED TRAINING IN ECONOMIC AND COMMERCIAL DIPLOMACY.</heading><content>Section 708 of the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (22 U.S.C. 4028) is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:
<quotedContent id="H5E6CD489CBCA4E38AEBFE566542C17AE" styleType="OLC">
<subsection id="H5FC56BCD1113499D8129376CDAC2F3F7" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Economic and Commercial Diplomacy</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, with the assistance of other relevant officials and the private sector, shall establish as part of the standard training provided for economic and commercial officers of the Foreign Service, chiefs of mission, and deputy chiefs of mission, training on matters related to economic and commercial diplomacy, with particular attention to market access and other elements of an enabling framework for United States businesses, commercial advocacy, and United States foreign economic policy, in addition to awareness about the support of the United States Government available to United States businesses, including support provided by the Department of Agriculture, the Department of Commerce, the Export-Import Bank of the United States, the Millennium Challenge Corporation, the Trade and Development Agency, the Department of the Treasury, the United States Agency for International Development, and the United States International Development Finance Corporation.”</content></subsection></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></section>
<section id="HE554B878F3B54B48BE3F986A2850D84C" styleType="OLC"><num value="706">SEC. 706. </num><heading>REPORT FROM EACH MISSION ON MATTERS OF COMMERCIAL RELATIONS.</heading>
<subsection id="H156B91C1599F4999B6DFD60CD567CA0D" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act and annually thereafter, the chief of mission at each bilateral diplomatic mission of the United States and the Director of the American Institute in Taiwan shall submit to the Secretary of State mission plans that include the following:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H16A7185BA107453C8DBF655B1A483DA7" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>Data and other information regarding actions taken by each such mission or Institute during the previous year to foster commercial relations and safeguard United States economic and business interests in the country or region in which each such chief of mission and the Director serves.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8DBC5D8B83EC496AA4F7488254CEB82F" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Each such mission’s and Institute’s anticipated economic and commercial priorities for the coming year.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H657E14F4A4EC40CBA585B073DD4AC87E" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report to Congress</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, after receiving the information required under subsection (a), shall submit to the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate a report, disaggregated by country or region, on activities and initiatives, including with appropriate examples, to create an enabling environment and otherwise promote United States economic and business interests in each such country or region, as well as information about significant foreign competition to United States businesses in the relevant country or region, including state-directed investments by foreign governments and United States strategic competitors in such country or region.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="HADBB198D93C54C668D0EEDF1A53A08DD" styleType="OLC"><num value="707">SEC. 707. </num><heading>CONSOLIDATED REPORT ON UNIFIED INVESTMENT CLIMATE STATEMENT AND COUNTRY COMMERCIAL GUIDE.</heading>
<subsection id="H56546185D6A3464B9A53CA801172C2E5" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State and the Secretary of Commerce shall jointly produce and make publicly available on a United States Government internet website an annual country- and region-specific report regarding commercial relations with foreign countries and regions and safeguarding United States economic and business interests abroad, including with regard to United States exports and investments, including by small- and medium-size enterprises.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H131EF689FBDE4F9DA52E4DE6A316DBC6" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Matters To Be Included</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Each report required under subsection (a) shall include the following with respect to each country or region covered by each such report:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H39581E3EE987489E8F67ADC9F87968EC" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>Information about doing business in each country or region.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE4390C5B12A146CD9D82E9BC8514D86B" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Background information about each country’s or region’s political environment.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD4B5B02D3EA94915B84B5A76F3BDF46C" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>Information about selling United States products and services in each country or region.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9AFE8F8906164DA79B1FB62727EE3667" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>Leading sectors for United States exports and investment in each country or region.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H20752D3FEDD3458991F7F11A276737B6" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><chapeau>Information about trade regulations, customs, and standards in each country or region, such as—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HE1C3EBCF3A214C1AA9C3B77D5452D75D" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>information on import tariffs; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H9DB139D1DA8C4C668C8912090320B593" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>documentation about which United States businesses should be aware when exporting, including any prohibited items or temporary entry procedures.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H0F70464C6006454EB440E9F09032E40F" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><chapeau>Investment climate statements describing each country’s or region’s openness to foreign investments, such as information relating to each country’s or region’s—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H08DBF314532944649621DAAF2BCD7AE5" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>investment policies;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H0713D7BE1523477E9AB85CF55101F3D9" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>market barriers;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H8FB309E3FC914326950FAB949B4F4C9D" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>business risks;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H31A160A852914078AE0A646AE477E7F8" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>legal and regulatory system, including dispute resolution;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H6ADAF33B18D445459C1706CC51ACDBE8" class="indent2"><num value="E">(E) </num><content>level of public and private sector corruption;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H6BCCA43F94DD453ABF819FB114DE39D5" class="indent2"><num value="F">(F) </num><content>level of political violence and instability;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H2DADA06C67BB4C59B0E79D6D56273A03" class="indent2"><num value="G">(G) </num><content>adherence to internationally recognized core labor standards; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H8471D9C78FB94B34AE506728423540D9" class="indent2"><num value="H">(H) </num><content>protection of property rights.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H2E1D01C70D8E43E892DCD2175EF8AE96" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><chapeau>Information about trade and project financing in each country or region, such as each country’s or region’s—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H7464F66731E04A699056DDFEE6159969" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>banking and financial system, and how United States businesses typically get paid;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HF0D7C7E7B16242129C759AD2815D0F3D" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>foreign exchange controls; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H9303E9901ED1462886109AB90F568A56" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>important sources of funding for project financing.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6BCD159593694FC88CC4FE0DA2813D08" class="indent1"><num value="8">(8) </num><content>Relevant business travel information and business customs in each country or region.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF962395C73754F3187C5B9311F8F0BDE" class="indent1"><num value="9">(9) </num><content>Information about services and personnel of the diplomatic mission of the United States available to United States businesses to support their activities in each country or region.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFD93346F5FC443EEA86674100F221E0D" class="indent1"><num value="10">(10) </num><content>Any significant trade or commercial agreement that exists between the United States and each country or region.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H7D6CF2B73CFA40AE86F171E76BE18C55" class="indent1"><num value="11">(11) </num><content>A point of contact at the diplomatic or consular mission of the United States in each country or region for United States businesses.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H81F08D9FEFCC4079B457602B45B26F4A" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Rule of Construction</inline>.—</heading><content>Nothing in this section may be construed to require the duplication of existing reports.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="H98E9124AA6A345F0BCD7690A480FD8A8" styleType="OLC"><num value="708">SEC. 708. </num><heading>WHOLE-OF-GOVERNMENT COORDINATION AND CONSULTATION TO SUPPORT UNITED STATES ECONOMIC AND BUSINESS INTERESTS.</heading>
<subsection id="H7FB9125913CC4A078635499BB3EE579B" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the United States Trade Representative, shall have primary responsibility for coordinating a whole-of-government effort to expand United States efforts in supporting United States economic and business interests abroad. The Secretary may delegate responsibilities under this Act to a senior, Senate-confirmed Department of State official.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HC7A5E3699E924E64A67AA165258ED4CD" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Responsibilities</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Secretary shall—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HC46ABE56B970432999C5733241F3FB1C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>chair the interagency coordinating committee established under subsection (c);</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB5E5A94F4ED84757AC0DBA705E3F054A" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>develop and implement the joint strategic plan required under subsection (c)(4) for all United States trade-related and trade capacity building and related technical assistance programs, in consultation with the coordinating committee established under subsection (c);</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H0A0E4323EAF2482B9099C76CFC9E3BC5" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>advise the Federal departments and agencies designated by the President to participate in the interagency coordinating committee under this section in identifying the most needed and effective ways for United States diplomatic and consular posts and the departments and agencies that staff such posts to support the expansion of United States trade relations with host governments;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCDEE6E1478F3432EAB7B5B42F153C44A" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>consult with the private sector in the development of government-wide trade expansion efforts, including establishing a point of contact and lead office within the Department of State to receive private-sector recommendations and comments concerning trade capacity assistance, coordination, consultations, and country-specific issues;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9B8253BD720D4674A85B2ADC98034ED8" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>consult with the Office of Management and Budget regarding the administrative and human resources needs that may be required to implement the provisions of this title; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H234EEAE969C7494392213A2E3197F197" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>brief Congress on trade capacity building programs and make recommendations, as appropriate, to Congress for improvements in trade capacity building efforts.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H7539586F53BA451C8AEAD56674919CEC" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Economic Diplomacy Action Group</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H4E13A6A36F8C4ADFBD358975973FA14B" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Establishment</inline>.—</heading><content>The President shall establish an interagency coordinating committee, to be known as the “Economic Diplomacy Action Group”, to coordinate and carry out the purposes of this section.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD5C2909A693E4447A2C409BC0C7D9106" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Leadership</inline>.—</heading><content>The Group shall be chaired by the Secretary of State and the vice-chairs shall be the United States Trade Representative and the Secretary of Commerce. The Secretaries and the United States Trade Representative may delegate responsibilities under this Act to appropriate, senior, Senate-confirmed officials.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H89E424E0DEBB41B493EFEFC44133C8C9" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Membership</inline>.—</heading><content>The President may appoint to the Group senior officials from the United States Agency for International Development, the Department of Agriculture, the Department of the Treasury, the Export-Import Bank, the United States Development Finance Corporation, and any such other relevant executive branch department or agency as the President determines to be substantially involved in trade capacity building and related assistance efforts in developing countries.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1C0044A3B21D465E9E6E2D17B0DD1B66" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Development of joint strategic plan</inline>.—</heading><content>The Group shall develop a joint strategic plan for all United States capacity building and technical assistance programs.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HCE248F5DB348416ABA955AEE4477DCB8" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Diplomacy Trade Expansion Advisory Committee</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HDAEFCD57AD2B47E8933B1385E0512A41" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Establishment of teac</inline>.—</heading><content>The Chair and Vice-Chairs of the Economic Diplomacy Action Group shall establish a trade expansion advisory committee with selected representatives of the United States private sector and other organizations, including labor organizations, with direct and relevant operational experience in importing from and exporting into developing countries, as appropriate, to provide comment and advice on priorities for trade expansion initiatives. The Chair and Vice-Chairs of the Group may also appoint representatives from select non-profit organizations to the advisory committee if such representatives can demonstrate both a presence in and relevant operational or programmatic experience with trade capacity building efforts in developing countries.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H453BA8F32964441CACC6E090A3C1213C" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Meetings</inline>.—</heading><content>The trade expansion advisory committee shall convene at least twice annually or more often as necessary at the call of the Chair and Vice-Chairs of the Group.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HDBA0ED460BBE4709B458B624814C6C2F" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Strategic planning advice</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The trade expansion advisory committee shall advise the Chair and Vice-Chairs of the Group on ways that embassies can better support the United States private sector abroad, including assisting the Chair and Vice-Chairs—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HDED87AF0B6D043B3BF21DD32BDE5D2BD" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>in soliciting private-sector advice;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HFDE969236710479F882E27D5210070E0" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>with respect to implementation of strategic planning; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H27C246F7616145719B8E0A616F560467" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>in advancing the overall mission and goals of United States national security.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="HC2CA948A0E924C3796ACB437A2A432C5" styleType="OLC"><num value="709">SEC. 709. </num><heading>PRIVATE SECTOR CONSULTATION AND COORDINATION.</heading>
<subsection id="HD624E12D8845444AB9C1DD5410F998B4" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Consultation With Private Sector by Embassy</inline>.—</heading><content>In developing the priorities for trade expansion initiatives described in section 708(d), embassy mission teams shall convene local representatives of the United States private sector and the private sector of host countries to consult on issues affecting trade at the borders of such countries and take into account the private sector’s operational expertise and experience confronting the trade barriers in such countries as well as its recommendations for reform and best practices.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H266C5FE01B85486E8C7A8EE5F84B65B0" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Inclusion of Private-sector Comments in Mission Plans</inline>.—</heading><content>Written comments from local United States private sector representatives shall be included in the trade expansion component of mission plans submitted by the chief of mission to the Secretary of State, with recommendations and comments from the mission team, for the purpose of informing the development of the joint strategic plan on trade expansion priorities required pursuant to section 708(c)(4) and recommended funding for the implementation of such plan.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HBF15E0ACF45D45C99F2CD1D25CD7D918" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Designated Embassy Point of Contact for Private Sector Consultation</inline>.—</heading><content>Each chief of mission shall designate an appropriate point of contact within the embassy who shall receive recommendations from appropriate private sector representatives regarding the implementation of the strategic plan required under section 708(c)(4) and ongoing trade barriers negatively impacting priority trade expansion. The chief of mission shall ensure that the designated point of contact shall be reasonably available for consultations with appropriate private sector representatives and to receive recommendations with respect to country-specific issues that may arise that will foreseeably disrupt trade.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H6B0B9F09CF024F6D963BBE92D353F7B3" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requirement to Protect Business Confidential Information</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H00F5355576E24DA28D760F15BAD4D7FB" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, Secretary of Commerce, and United States Trade Representative as well as the heads of all other agencies involved in the Economic Diplomacy Action Group established under section 708(c) shall protect from disclosure any proprietary information submitted by any private sector representative and marked as “business confidential information”, unless the party submitting the confidential business information had notice, at the time of submission, that such information would be released by the head of any such department or agency, or such party subsequently consents to the release of the information. To the extent business confidential information is provided, a non-confidential version of the information shall also be provided, in which the business confidential information is summarized or, if necessary, deleted.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H09B1DD5C704D483B90C7D01CCFFBA122" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Treatment as trade secrets</inline>.—</heading><content>Proprietary information submitted by a private party in accordance with this Act shall be considered to be a matter falling within the meaning of trade secrets and commercial or financial information exemption under section 552(b)(4) of title 5, United States Code, and shall be exempt from disclosure without the express approval of the private party.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H5940EDE829E246BB850EA5B155F2F732" styleType="OLC"><num value="710">SEC. 710. </num><heading>IMPROVING AWARENESS OF UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT TOOLS AND SERVICES TO SUPPORT UNITED STATES BUSINESSES OVERSEAS.</heading><content class="block">The Secretary of State and the Secretary of Commerce shall take actions to improve the awareness of United States businesses with respect to United States Government tools and services to assist such businesses overseas, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, including by coordinating with State trade agencies, Export Assistance Centers, and Small Businesses Development Centers.</content></section>
<section id="H5DCE108DD4654C5DB06FD3D4BF3B74EA" styleType="OLC"><num value="711">SEC. 711. </num><heading>REPORT BY COMPTROLLER GENERAL OF THE UNITED STATES.</heading>
<subsection id="H2E7C770F61844C939F384DCB07A865AA" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 2 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate a report on United States economic and commercial diplomacy.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H7410BF94221E404498B811867353E585" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Matters To Be Included</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The report required under subsection (a) shall include an assessment of the following:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HCC4AE45FDF1C4F10906E25EBD572394A" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>What is known about the effectiveness of United States economic and commercial diplomacy in influencing foreign governments and supporting United States businesses abroad.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4276024D16144E24B1C0DC9808CB2BA1" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Coordination between the Department of State and the Department of Commerce with respect to United States economic and commercial diplomacy.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3792CAAF9894446AA244977C18ADA4CB" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>The effectiveness of training provided pursuant to subsection (d) of section 708 of the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (as added by section 705 of this title) on matters relating to economic and commercial diplomacy.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA1B7034D8D7645EB9B7EB3683A4CD61C" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>The status and effectiveness of actions taken by the Secretary of State under section 710 of this title regarding commercial relations with foreign countries and regions and safeguarding United States economic and business interests abroad.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H0104852E21534D1DA00DEB42572B0E48" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>The status of the U.S. Commercial Service of the Department of Commerce and its effectiveness in advancing the economic and business interests of the United States abroad.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCADC7AF490AC40A3B3065A3E902BB16B" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>The status of the Foreign Service economics officers and their effectiveness in advancing the economic and business interests of the United States abroad.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HEF022D987D0945EB967C82B22D8FB997" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>Recommendations to improve United States economic and commercial diplomacy.</content></paragraph></subsection></section></title>
<title id="HDBCB007D5CBB48E18ECB041052F40675" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="VIII">TITLE VIII—</num><heading class="inline">UNITED STATES COMMISSION ON INTERNATIONAL RELIGIOUS FREEDOM REAUTHORIZATION</heading>
<section id="HC10A4411E6AC4D35B3F5EFF39A658E1E" styleType="OLC"><num value="801">SEC. 801. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This title may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="title">United States Commission on International Religious Freedom Reauthorization Act of 2019</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section id="H4EBAB24083524B48BE2CCF7162FE1B74" styleType="OLC"><num value="802">SEC. 802. </num><heading>REAUTHORIZATION.</heading><content class="block">Section 209 of the International Religious Freedom Act of 1998 (22 U.S.C. 6436) is amended by striking “2019” and inserting “2022”.</content></section>

<section id="HD590591A0E6F4BE6AF16174CEA0C9A9B" styleType="OLC"><num value="805">SEC. 805. </num><heading>COMMISSION PERSONNEL MATTERS.</heading>
<subsection id="H0FDDBBFFD4E54050B19DE6C48A26F1FF" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 204 of the International Religious Freedom Act of 1998 (22 U.S.C. 6432b) is amended—</chapeau>

<quotedContent id="H896D969DE1024A70B37D7730A2C66AB9" styleType="OLC">
