<section id="HA674E364FD124074AC6B22959C655D49" styleType="OLC"><num value="901">SEC. 901. </num><heading>SPECIAL RULES FOR CERTAIN MONTHLY WORKERS’ COMPENSATION PAYMENTS AND OTHER PAYMENTS FOR DEPARTMENT OF STATE PERSONNEL UNDER CHIEF OF MISSION AUTHORITY.</heading>
<subsection id="HCBA0D9A62A0C4FF498966130D743C62A" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Adjustment of Compensation for Certain Injuries</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H086F1A5ACC8843C18CFF12BDCE869AD0" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Increase</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Secretary of State may pay an additional monthly monetary benefit, provided that the covered employee is receiving benefits under section 8105 or 8106 of title 5, United States Code, and may determine the amount of each monthly monetary benefit amount by taking into account—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HE8D10C63827D4307BDAA6E90ABE88C05" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the severity of the qualifying injury;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD5D39FFB871F4D928D92212D47AEDDD4" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the circumstances by which the covered employee became injured; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HBEDC988B0E3A4D558BD7149A5234B3F9" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>the seniority of the covered employee, particularly for purposes of compensating for lost career growth.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H93950FAE7A294ABF8FDA1C44B9AAAE3E" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Maximum</inline>.—</heading><content>Notwithstanding chapter 81 of title 5, United States Code, the total amount of monthly compensation increased under paragraph (1) may not exceed the monthly pay of the maximum rate of basic pay for GS–15 of the General Schedule under section 5332 of such title.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HF45081C64BA148518195BF126E8069D3" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Costs for Treating Qualifying Injuries</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Secretary of State may pay the costs of or reimburse for diagnosing and treating—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HA6D87A7520D1440392FB6A694F3FBB06" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>a qualifying injury of a covered employee for such costs, that are not otherwise covered by chapter 81 of title 5, United States Code, or other provision of Federal law; or</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H2FC3F98EFEE64AF08638C73054C0386C" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>a covered individual, or a covered dependent, for such costs that are not otherwise covered by Federal law.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H7D1AE23DDC4D4172AC7371A8B78FDE25" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Information Exchange</inline>.—</heading><content>To avoid duplicate or otherwise improper payments under this subsection, the Secretary of Labor and the Secretary of State shall exchange information about the amounts paid for treatment of qualifying injuries.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H628F550AFFB445298D17FC3871A4B65D" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Regulations</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State shall—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H6380472A66AD4C65BA3460CFCBBFF480" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>prescribe regulations ensuring the fair and equitable implementation of this section; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H87B0060857DA4F0CA358A70F291C6D59" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>submit to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives such regulations.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H01446E23C77249CB9ADA3B5589930E4A" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definitions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section:</chapeau>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HCBCFE0C554C34B22A4D9755D09DB0D0F" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Covered dependent</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term “<term>covered dependent</term>” means a family member (as defined by the Secretary of State) of a employee who, on or after January 1, 2016—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HF69F8BCA90504C8FA300589F3C85FDD1" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>accompanies the employee to an assigned duty station in a foreign country under chief of mission authority; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H47E5836728404F22A27A4FAD34D9762E" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>becomes injured by reason of a qualifying injury.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HA6900ED7237D4A458F8FC901B49FABE9" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Covered employee</inline>.—</heading><content>The term “<term>covered employee</term>” means an employee of the Department of State who, on or after January 1, 2016, becomes injured by reason of a qualifying injury and was assigned to a duty station in the Republic of Cuba, the People’s Republic of China, or another foreign country designated by the Secretary of State pursuant to subsection (f).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H9DEF023F51D14FBD891120A41CC6EB9E" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Covered individual</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term “<term>covered individual</term>” means an individual who, on or after January 1, 2016, becomes injured by reason of a qualifying injury and is—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H27E5F9E6AB344D53842B1F425794539F" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>detailed to a duty station in the Republic of Cuba, the People’s Republic of China, or another foreign country designated by the Secretary of State pursuant to subsection (f); or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H5B97DC4141054E289F0643D1D724382C" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>affiliated with the Department of State, as determined by the Secretary of State.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H42F038C36B6F4A9BBF6D6C528AA5C742" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Qualifying injury</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term “qualifying injury” means the following:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HFCFF842982174C31816266B3A68EA976" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><chapeau>With respect to a covered dependent, an injury incurred—</chapeau>
<clause id="H995FD15C22A842F59D36B571B94EC85E" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>during a period in which the covered dependent is accompanying an employee to an assigned duty station in the Republic of Cuba, the People’s Republic of China, or another foreign country designated by the Secretary of State pursuant to subsection (f);</content></clause>
<clause id="H7271F0567E674D28B5227ED5D87801BE" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>in connection with war, insurgency, hostile act, terrorist activity, or other incident designated by the Secretary of State; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H40F804597FA54B0EA839D567BF624DCA" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>that was not the result of the willful misconduct of the covered dependent.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HE74B065FB2004AF091C03D41AD243A00" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><chapeau>With respect to a covered employee or a covered individual, an injury incurred—</chapeau>
<clause id="H502F9D189C224B20A031B55835873011" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>during a period of assignment to a duty station in the Republic of Cuba, the People’s Republic of China, or another country designated by the Secretary of State pursuant to subsection (f);</content></clause>
<clause id="H5A70D4214C764E638F82C8531D9EE685" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>in connection with war, insurgency, hostile act, terrorist activity, or other incident designated by the Secretary of State; and</content></clause>
<clause id="HCC584119C8EE456A89F03A16EC3472F6" class="indent3"><num value="iii">(iii) </num><content>that was not the result of the willful misconduct of the covered employee or the covered individual.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H8308A1393CF64D9881A98654B6FF8D7B" class="indent0"><num value="f">(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Designation by the Secretary of State of Another Foreign Country or Duty Station</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Secretary of State may designate another foreign country for the purposes of this section, provided that the Secretary reports such designation to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives, and includes in such report a rationale for each such designation. The Secretary of State may not designate an added foreign country or duty station for purposes of providing additional monetary benefit pursuant to subsection (a) or (b) for a qualifying injury to covered employees, covered dependents, or covered individuals under this section unless the Secretary of State—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H8EA4A8C35A504FE1B68A9DEE2A7A58F4" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>provides to the Committees on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives 30 days’ notice of the designation of a particular additional country or duty station and the rationale for such addition; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3C537C15F53B447BB5A29035ABACF18C" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>provides no such additional monetary benefit pursuant to subsection (a) or (b) to covered employees, covered dependents, or covered individuals for a qualifying injury until the 30-day notice period expires, unless there is written agreement by both the Chair and Ranking Members of both the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives that there is no objection to proceeding with provision of such monetary benefit compensation in less than 30 days.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H7E988738575B407E987F405A75E021DB" class="indent0"><num value="g">(g) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Treatment of Amounts</inline>.—</heading><content>For purposes of section 104 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, amounts paid pursuant to this section shall be treated as amounts described in subsection (a)(5) of such section.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H027BBA0DC8AB4A7EA671BC98634B5003" class="indent0"><num value="h">(h) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Application</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H2F4DD36AA6B54781BAE20EA06443733E" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>This section shall apply with respect to—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HF73D2E44A97F43A098AA3E928071E8F0" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>payments made to covered employees (as defined in such section) under section 8105 or 8106 of title 5, United States Code, beginning on or after January 1, 2016; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H6985BE218FA944B5A39F61CEE2921AA3" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>diagnosis or treatment described in subsection (b) occurring on or after January 1, 2016.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H52762136057C4543BB251F5D3D605E34" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Rule of construction</inline>.—</heading><content>Nothing in this section shall modify or otherwise supersede chapter 81 of title 5, or chapter 11 of title 42 United States Code. Monetary benefits and treatment expenses paid under this section shall not be considered payments under any workers’ compensation law.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H083158ACCC3D439E933DFA8F569F451D" styleType="OLC"><num value="902">SEC. 902. </num><heading>DECLASSIFICATION OF INFORMATION RELATED TO CERTAIN ACTIONS BY SAUDI ARABIAN OFFICIALS.</heading><content class="block">Not later than 30 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, shall declassify, with any redactions necessary to protect intelligence sources and methods, any and all information related to whether the Government of Saudi Arabia materially assisted or facilitated any citizen or national of Saudi Arabia in departing from the United States while the citizen or national was awaiting trial or sentencing for a criminal offense committed in the United States.</content></section>
<section id="HB80EBC4AFAF74228B8BCD1F13918BFB1" styleType="OLC"><num value="903">SEC. 903. </num><heading>PROMOTING SECURITY AND JUSTICE FOR VICTIMS OF TERRORISM.</heading>
<subsection id="HDC8F34B0845E4FB7B46F9CFD47BB1ED4" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Short Title</inline>.—</heading><content>This section may be cited as the Promoting Security and Justice for Victims of Terrorism Act of 2019.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H5DAC4C72521941759F544AA4AF605C80" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Facilitation of the Settlement of Terrorism-related Claims of Nationals of the United States</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H6DE25E4EFA9C49879C16272F4716F065" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Comprehensive process to facilitate the resolution of anti-terrorism act claims</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Attorney General, shall, not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act, develop and initiate a comprehensive process for the Department of State to facilitate the resolution and settlement of covered claims.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H7D9D384B002E4B398510468463995EB9" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Elements of comprehensive process</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The comprehensive process developed under paragraph (1) shall include, at a minimum, the following:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HA2CAE539058B45FCBBAAD84D6E9E7DE5" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Not later than 45 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Department of State shall publish a notice in the Federal Register identifying the method by which a national of the United States, or a representative of a national of the United States, who has a covered claim, may contact the Department of State to give notice of the covered claim.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H2D54712819DE42618135BBCE52A86251" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, or a designee of the Secretary, shall meet (and make every effort to continue to meet on a regular basis thereafter) with any national of the United States, or a representative of a national of the United States, who has a covered claim and has informed the Department of State of the covered claim using the method established pursuant to subparagraph (A) to discuss the status of the covered claim, including the status of any settlement discussions with the Palestinian Authority or the Palestine Liberation Organization.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H8BF080FEC42240FE835A4C5450E0F9CC" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, or a designee of the Secretary, shall make every effort to meet (and make every effort to continue to meet on a regular basis thereafter) with representatives of the Palestinian Authority and the Palestine Liberation Organization to discuss the covered claims identified pursuant to subparagraph (A) and potential settlement of the covered claims.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H24A111ED73E24714828EB71E074E811D" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report to congress</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State shall, not later than 240 days after the date of enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter for 5 years, submit to the Committee on the Judiciary and the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on the Judiciary and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives a report describing activities that the Department of State has undertaken to comply with this subsection, including specific updates regarding subparagraphs (B) and (C) of paragraph (2).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H59E348A4D2C042D387A754B1FC4FDCE9" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of congress</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>It is the sense of Congress that—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HBE977F2A31D948A7BBF551D54651FE62" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>covered claims should be resolved in a manner that provides just compensation to the victims;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HEB884DD2D03B41ABB2B17063BB91CDF0" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>covered claims should be resolved and settled in favor of the victim to the fullest extent possible and without subjecting victims to unnecessary or protracted litigation;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HE9E7EE83654E4C32A69D29C3B7405471" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>the United States Government should take all practicable steps to facilitate the resolution and settlement of all covered claims, including engaging directly with the victims or their representatives and the Palestinian Authority and the Palestine Liberation Organization; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HC2A54C10842B484FA7CB0D611E0F3735" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>the United States Government should strongly urge the Palestinian Authority and the Palestine Liberation Organization to commit to good-faith negotiations to resolve and settle all covered claims.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H8CF96080653340F4B124E4BC6A3259DE" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definition</inline>.—</heading><content>In this subsection, the term “<term>covered claim</term>” means any pending action by, or final judgment in favor of, a national of the United States, or any action by a national of the United States dismissed for lack of personal jurisdiction, under section 2333 of title 18, United States Code, against the Palestinian Authority or the Palestine Liberation Organization.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H8ABB6B50C7B74E71805D057B283EE45C" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Jurisdictional Amendments to Facilitate Resolution of Terrorism-related Claims of Nationals of the United States</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H59965390095A4DE19469E59B85398101" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 2334(e) of title 18, United States Code, is amended—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H2A3C5BDFA9E340DC832E95588AF8416A" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>by striking paragraph (1) and inserting the following:
<quotedContent id="H9D3737E00A9C4D45AFDB7470F80D05FC" styleType="OLC">
<paragraph id="H19A906C8E38B4C988D31575AAE0F19D0" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Except as provided in paragraph (2), for purposes of any civil action under section 2333 of this title, a defendant shall be deemed to have consented to personal jurisdiction in such civil action if, regardless of the date of the occurrence of the act of international terrorism upon which such civil action was filed, the defendant—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H314CE1CF2E184CDE992D41CC1AEFA3F7" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><chapeau>after the date that is 120 days after the date of the enactment of the Promoting Security and Justice for Victims of Terrorism Act of 2019, makes any payment, directly or indirectly—</chapeau>
<clause id="HCE50CDD55224461BB86FB27FD1597F24" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>to any payee designated by any individual who, after being fairly tried or pleading guilty, has been imprisoned for committing any act of terrorism that injured or killed a national of the United States, if such payment is made by reason of such imprisonment; or</content></clause>
<clause id="HB442FE76BD044EC7AA70D7C829E7D7A6" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>to any family member of any individual, following such individual’s death while committing an act of terrorism that injured or killed a national of the United States, if such payment is made by reason of the death of such individual; or</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H61667A290E17438AB7D3A59AC646CC89" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><chapeau>after 15 days after the date of enactment of the Promoting Security and Justice for Victims of Terrorism Act of 2019—</chapeau>
<clause id="HDFEB806D20F14A0983B0E5662F14399B" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>continues to maintain any office, headquarters, premises, or other facilities or establishments in the United States;</content></clause>
<clause id="H4909BD4524D44CC092179E28AC8E8777" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>establishes or procures any office, headquarters, premises, or other facilities or establishments in the United States; or</content></clause>
<clause id="H6EFDA7F7DBAA4E01B8CE2DE84763BA51" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>conducts any activity while physically present in the United States on behalf of the Palestine Liberation Organization or the Palestinian Authority.”</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">;</inline></content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H93F94CC5817D41148B00E14CE00C06A6" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>in paragraph (2), by adding at the end the following: “Except with respect to payments described in paragraph (1)(A), no court may consider the receipt of any assistance by a nongovernmental organization, whether direct or indirect, as a basis for consent to jurisdiction by a defendant.”; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H58AB86B6A3714F6F910E2AF0DB81F92C" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>by adding at the end the following:
<quotedContent id="H585665BC00D948AA8C3C1123FB3ABCC8" styleType="OLC">
<paragraph id="H6522723FE9F94C78B092DCDF5F3819EB" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exception for certain activities and locations</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In determining whether a defendant shall be deemed to have consented to personal jurisdiction under paragraph (1)(B), no court may consider—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H11555C612C0F464FA183357CBF627C07" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>any office, headquarters, premises, or other facility or establishment used exclusively for the purpose of conducting official business of the United Nations;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H771F43A1B90B4F22B7C3019B6B8B05A8" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>any activity undertaken exclusively for the purpose of conducting official business of the United Nations;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H8304C82AE7AE4ABF880FB85FCEA6C0EF" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>any activity involving officials of the United States that the Secretary of State determines is in the national interest of the United States if the Secretary reports to the appropriate congressional committees annually on the use of the authority under this subparagraph;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H597ADE1FAFA8464198C75D2C24E0129C" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><content>any activity undertaken exclusively for the purpose of meetings with officials of the United States or other foreign governments, or participation in training and related activities funded or arranged by the United States Government;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H59CFF012CA1944CEB6146EF6C4C364CD" class="indent2"><num value="E">“(E) </num><chapeau>any activity related to legal representation—</chapeau>
<clause id="H6C34D54DF62E417BB9A71284F2247030" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>for matters related to activities described in this paragraph;</content></clause>
<clause id="H0DFEA236B12B4D238F7EE36B925AC343" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>for the purpose of adjudicating or resolving claims filed in courts of the United States; or</content></clause>
<clause id="H60B8D7F7872E4036ACF43C4EBAF465E7" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>to comply with this subsection; or</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H196786FAB8AF498FA1770C95DEEEC306" class="indent2"><num value="F">“(F) </num><content>any personal or official activities conducted ancillary to activities listed under this paragraph.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5ED09431B673411CB81E089503C74565" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Rule of construction</inline>.—</heading><content>Notwithstanding any other law (including any treaty), any office, headquarters, premises, or other facility or establishment within the territory of the United States that is not specifically exempted by paragraph (3)(A) shall be considered to be in the United States for purposes of paragraph (1)(B).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HCCAEA3DEC07E4BFA9BF775D096749C2D" class="indent1"><num value="5">“(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Defined term</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this subsection, the term ‘<term>defendant</term>’ means—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H307AC850EC4B423BAF19732E3A842FA4" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>the Palestinian Authority;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H7E2F0F3348344B8F9ACBC2FD9D42652D" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>the Palestine Liberation Organization;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H93024556E35E4F78950ADDAEFC781563" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>any organization or other entity that is a successor to or affiliated with the Palestinian Authority or the Palestine Liberation Organization; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD8A39F7543F24B2FAEBCD5D650870CEF" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><chapeau>any organization or other entity that—</chapeau>
<clause id="H882445A4D3024E21AA42F81233E0DADE" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>is identified in subparagraph (A), (B), or (C); and</content></clause>
<clause id="H497A6454192D43F0AFB3001F984FB1B6" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>self identifies as, holds itself out to be, or carries out conduct in the name of, the ‘State of Palestine’ or ‘Palestine’ in connection with official business of the United Nations.”</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF594DEDF90ED4AE39E50B0A14B7FECF6" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prior consent not abrogated</inline>.—</heading><content>The amendments made by this subsection shall not abrogate any consent deemed to have been given under section 2334(e) of title 18, United States Code, as in effect on the day before the date of enactment of this Act.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HBBD581D05D564EEA8393911B7AA5B825" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Rules of Construction; Applicability; Severability</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H56283E04D8694A6CBD291977BC51B58D" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Rules of construction</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H601E30BD12A443938965828EC14429BA" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>This section, and the amendments made by this section, should be liberally construed to carry out the purposes of Congress to provide relief for victims of terrorism.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD721562D66534BF8820959370648C05C" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Cases against other persons</inline>.—</heading><content>Nothing in this section may be construed to affect any law or authority, as in effect on the day before the date of enactment of this Act, relating to a case brought under section 2333(a) of title 18, United States Code, against a person who is not a defendant, as defined in paragraph (5) of section 2334(e) of title 18, United States Code, as added by subsection (c)(1) of this section.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6774C2DD64CD46B5B166821DC8610271" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Applicability</inline>.—</heading><content>This section, and the amendments made by this section, shall apply to any case pending on or after August 30, 2016.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H60C90BFA27584EF088029BFC6DFB4E6C" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Severability</inline>.—</heading><content>If any provision of this section, an amendment made by this section, or the application of such provision or amendment to any person or circumstance is held to be unconstitutional, the remainder of this section, the amendments made by this section, and the application of such provisions to any person or circumstance shall not be affected thereby.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H4C3463932CC3479D8E446F5B7F7A95AB" styleType="OLC"><num value="904">SEC. 904. </num><heading>DEBT RELIEF FOR SOMALIA.</heading>
<subsection id="H8CB520C55B6E4A2A96A377F7B349D415" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Debt Relief</inline>.—</heading><paragraph id="H5189B3018B4146C999734842FDEFB6F7" class="inline"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>Of the funds appropriated under titles III and IV of division G of this Act and under such titles in prior Acts making appropriations for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs, not to exceed $35,000,000 may be transferred to the “Department of the Treasury, Debt Restructuring” account for the same purposes and under the same authorities and conditions (other than the period of availability) as other funds provided under that heading for the cost, as defined in section 502 of the Congressional Budget Act of 1974, of modifying loans and loan guarantees, as the President may determine, or for the cost of selling, reducing, or cancelling amounts owed to the United States as a result of loans made to Somalia, in the event that Somalia meets the domestic and internationally-agreed conditions and the transfer is consistent with United States law and foreign policy considerations.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H267A5D9744BD4D2091C7DE493397504A" class="indent0"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>For the purposes of this section, no amounts may be transferred from amounts designated for Overseas Contingency Operations/Global War on Terrorism or as emergency requirements pursuant to a concurrent resolution on the budget or section 251(b)(2)(A) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6A09A186A3C24596991643914D040B50" class="indent0"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>Prior to the initial obligation of funds made available pursuant to this section, the Secretary of State shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report on the outcome of the Paris Club meeting on debt cancellation for Somalia, the estimate of amounts needed and over what time period, and the proposed sources of funds to be transferred pursuant to this section: <proviso><i> Provided</i>, That such funds shall also be subject to prior consultation with the appropriate congressional committees and the regular notification procedures of such committees.</proviso></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HD55ED429656A45169C4C700B4EED7584" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Debt Restructuring</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 501(i) of title V of H.R. 3425, as enacted into law by section 1000(a)(5) of Public Law 106–113 (113 Stat. 1501A–313), as most recently amended by section 699H(b)(1) of division J of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2008 (Public Law 110–161; 121 Stat. 2372), is further amended by striking “2000–2010” and inserting “2000–2021”.</content></subsection>
<subsection role="definitions" id="H70E529F504034204ADFDA6002E96C9F7" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Appropriate Congressional Committees Defined</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section, the term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HD6E1B1C16DAB494CB4F1C181E9AA097C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the Committee on Foreign Relations and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6FE93844DC49473B833462B4DD7D0A21" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the Committee on Foreign Affairs and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives. </content></paragraph></subsection></section></title></division>
<division id="H34C4C86F0F4E43B9B4E3EFABA1746E76" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="K">DIVISION K—</num><heading>NATIONAL LAW ENFORCEMENT MUSEUM COMMEMORATIVE COIN</heading>
<section id="H9646714B98FA46DAB4EA9FB5D19B0CD4" styleType="OLC"><num value="101">SEC. 101. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This division may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="division">National Law Enforcement Museum Commemorative Coin Act</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section id="H0B6F85517B184F438BFFBEA21E588E31" styleType="OLC"><num value="102">SEC. 102. </num><heading>FINDINGS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">The Congress finds the following:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H6ADF2314A72F4A4B8ED445A9B061255E" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>In 2000, Congress passed and President William J. Clinton signed into law the National Law Enforcement Museum Act (Public Law 106–492), which authorized the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Fund, Inc., to build the National Law Enforcement Museum on Federal land in the District of Columbia to honor and commemorate the service and sacrifice of law enforcement officers in the United States.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HABE9A46E2EBA4B2789938BF767BB6CAB" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>In April 2016, construction began on the National Law Enforcement Museum in the District of Columbia across the street from the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial in Judiciary Square.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H0ECBD83373164D82ACFF7C1E958D7D7E" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>The National Law Enforcement Museum formally opened in October of 2018.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB8C5C0FA02B74E29BD94B34122CB68B3" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><chapeau>The National Law Enforcement Museum’s mission is—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HDA04D1413DE14C4CA59480C938E0DA95" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>to honor and commemorate the extraordinary service and sacrifice of America’s law enforcement officers;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H265CEC9AE056483ABE0C027EB26FEFD7" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>to serve as an important bridge between law enforcement’s past and present, between the heroes of yesteryear and those who have followed in their footsteps, and between America’s peace officers and the public they serve;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H6E57B63C21054F5F88DA083ADBB39E49" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>increase public understanding and support for law enforcement and to promote law enforcement safety; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H571B7B4E89354F98A956CEDD5A1D1CFD" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>strengthen the relationship between law enforcement and the communities they serve with thought-provoking programs at the Museum and around the country that promote dialogue on topics of current interest.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></section>
<section id="HF11220C1A5A44F6886AA5BFACA3E6CB9" styleType="OLC"><num value="103">SEC. 103. </num><heading>COIN SPECIFICATIONS.</heading>
<subsection id="HB6051A338E034FD397197FD1730C1E9A" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Denominations</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Secretary of the Treasury (hereafter in this Act referred to as the “Secretary”) shall mint and issue the following coin:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HE0B0620980104602ABB05F0F6CF6ADE1" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">$5 gold coins</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not more than 50,000 $5 coins, which shall—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H78DF08E0532345FBBC28202CA06D0BF4" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>weigh 8.359 grams;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD7786C918F1A4F2CAE2508CA4AE7F48E" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>have a diameter of 0.850 inches; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H302E7EA752C44EFB98C1A6E06A9D9F60" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>contain not less than 90 percent gold.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC06C405275B1433FB9C2E420A7E1017B" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">$1 silver coins</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not more than 400,000 $1 coins, which shall—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H5DB6DB8446B9446389CFB3A7E2A3CB39" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>weigh 26.73 grams;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H4F40901A2F324094A4018F0370CFC5BB" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>have a diameter of 1.500 inches; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H4656250690D149B495553B64D2862D26" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>contain not less than 90 percent silver.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H81F2FAD7BD6A481E895D3ED21AFC662F" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Half-dollar clad coins</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not more than 750,000 half-dollar coins which shall—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H4A793FAF55D248B08459ADA6C8F5D85F" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>weigh 11.34 grams;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H2466E370618F4C7CA002D65D45142B32" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>have a diameter of 1.205 inches; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H0F76382291254487A23A099A999116B2" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>be minted to the specifications for half-dollar coins contained in section 5112(b) of title 31, United States Code.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H756B409557EA4F1281A88B3DD50BE456" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Legal Tender</inline>.—</heading><content>The coins minted under this Act shall be legal tender, as provided in section 5103 of title 31, United States Code.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H285163A07F954CA6A98E0CE472C9B31A" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Numismatic Items</inline>.—</heading><content>For purposes of section 5134 of title 31, United States Code, all coins minted under this Act shall be considered to be numismatic items.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="HB500A7FE58DC4ADB9F8D5BEE3D836023" styleType="OLC"><num value="104">SEC. 104. </num><heading>DESIGN OF COINS.</heading>
<subsection id="HE858A12231EC43FA8B387A1E346CBABD" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Design Requirements</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H25D881CF06F947B9BED46AFF45925853" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>The design of the coins minted under this Act shall be emblematic of the National Law Enforcement Museum and the service and sacrifice of law enforcement officers throughout the history of the United States.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H509468DB0F8249DD8F225A3B20460CE4" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Designation and inscriptions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>On each coin minted under this Act there shall be—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H01C26E87A39B4EC98F7FD2B3B3FB3E78" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>a designation of the value of the coin;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HFAB0AA13523B447C883FB26BD66205A3" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>an inscription of the year “2021”; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H3739E380887044D9A2A3BFC73E1AE0F1" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>inscriptions of the words “Liberty”, “In God We Trust”, “United States of America”, and “E Pluribus Unum”.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H18A53B289C7540289D81C9CB31EA8298" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Selection</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The design for the coins minted under this Act shall be—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HB476C744E00443139FA7E309DE15AA9F" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>selected by the Secretary after consultation with the Commission of Fine Arts and the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Fund, Inc.; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF203702F94A04BB39F595B08EF9B49A7" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>reviewed by the Citizens Coinage Advisory Committee.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H8ADBC18D771E4747944B78BF51BE3612" styleType="OLC"><num value="105">SEC. 105. </num><heading>ISSUANCE OF COINS.</heading>
<subsection id="HFE43400A3DEA4F1D84476A42CE9FC86E" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Quality of Coins</inline>.—</heading><content>Coins minted under this Act shall be issued in uncirculated and proof qualities.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H7F14F559AD774F6388ABA051310CF827" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Mint Facilities</inline>.—</heading><content>Only one facility of the United States Mint may be used to strike any particular quality of the coins minted under this Act.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HDEB9948A884649DE87D80AD614230556" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Period for Issuance</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary may issue coins minted under this Act only during the 1-year period beginning on January 1, 2021.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="HF2BF94C08A574C12AA3045F42906A601" styleType="OLC"><num value="106">SEC. 106. </num><heading>SALE OF COINS.</heading>
<subsection id="H4CB46F221CF64917B9114B1DD69CF9BE" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sale Price</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The coins issued under this Act shall be sold by the Secretary at a price equal to the sum of—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H7594A02BF6614A30AD9371DD9D78EB4E" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the face value of the coins;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H990CC8578FC1487F9BC619D9C0024717" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>the surcharge provided in section 107(a) with respect to such coins; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC4B3E8F41F634E46869AF5E690DCE9C7" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>the cost of designing and issuing the coins (including labor, materials, dies, use of machinery, overhead expenses, marketing, and shipping).</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H39D21B2377634665B3523AA65B8B783F" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Bulk Sales</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary shall make bulk sales of the coins issued under this Act at a reasonable discount.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H9183AF76574C411190269292D10807A3" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prepaid Orders</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H973BAC4CECD24C31A849642C42BD771A" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary shall accept prepaid orders for the coins minted under this Act before the issuance of such coins.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8D6920B99D634D6C93CB9CD097FDACD4" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Discount</inline>.—</heading><content>Sale prices with respect to prepaid orders under paragraph (1) shall be at a reasonable discount.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H53197403B6784887B68B7344FABCAB13" styleType="OLC"><num value="107">SEC. 107. </num><heading>SURCHARGES.</heading>
<subsection id="H54C01AEC30494C57ABD4799E665BE904" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>All sales of coins issued under this Act shall include a surcharge of—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H8357BBE329DF4CFD808A1558669B9429" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>$35 per coin for the $5 coin;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H54A7C109861F4DCEB8EB50078159C552" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>$10 per coin for the $1 coin; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1BA8462ABE4D4ED288A0A1D480223943" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>$5 per coin for the half-dollar coin.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H163BC1D063D04EDA921CFB86724CA44F" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Distribution</inline>.—</heading><content>Subject to section 5134(f)(1) of title 31, United States Code, all surcharges received by the Secretary from the sale of coins issued under this Act shall be promptly paid by the Secretary to the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Fund, Inc., for educational and outreach programs and exhibits.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H89AE77BABB124F668B07FF883B825065" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Audits</inline>.—</heading><content>The National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Fund, Inc., shall be subject to the audit requirements of section 5134(f)(2) of title 31, United States Code, with regard to the amounts received under subsection (b).</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H31ED1434FD5F4F859F08476BAF9D15C7" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitation</inline>.—</heading><content>Notwithstanding subsection (a), no surcharge may be included with respect to the issuance under this Act of any coin during a calendar year if, as of the time of such issuance, the issuance of such coin would result in the number of commemorative coin programs issued during such year to exceed the annual two commemorative coin program issuance limitation under section 5112(m)(1) of title 31, United States Code (as in effect on the date of the enactment of this Act). The Secretary of the Treasury may issue guidance to carry out this subsection.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="H34CEA10CFEE449BCB3BA327827ED61B1" styleType="OLC"><num value="108">SEC. 108. </num><heading>FINANCIAL ASSURANCES.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">The Secretary shall take such actions as may be necessary to ensure that—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HC7DD8D2B64504679A4A1894FDF6EFC5C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>minting and issuing coins under this Act will not result in any net cost to the United States Government; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H233BB192059448098B30AB18FCD5D1BE" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>no funds, including applicable surcharges, are disbursed to any recipient designated in section 107 until the total cost of designing and issuing all of the coins authorized by this Act (including labor, materials, dies, use of machinery, overhead expenses, marketing, and shipping) is recovered by the United States Treasury, consistent with sections 5112(m) and 5134(f) of title 31, United States Code. </content></paragraph></section></division>

<paragraph id="H328BD72DE39C4FB2969A5DD37CDAFF8C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>in paragraph (3)(A), by striking “$490,000,000” and inserting “$750,000,000”;</content></paragraph>

<subparagraph id="H2DDA15C2CF5B4300A7E770DDEE6CA932" class="indent2"><num value="E">“(E) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Treatment of transfers for purposes of withdrawal liability under erisa</inline>.—</heading><content>The amount of any transfer made under subparagraph (A) (and any earnings attributable thereto) shall be disregarded in determining the unfunded vested benefits of the 1974 UMWA Pension Plan and the allocation of such unfunded vested benefits to an employer for purposes of determining the employer’s withdrawal liability under section 4201 of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974.</content></subparagraph>

<subsection id="HEA4BEF5852A849DCA70FC25BB1EC1E8A" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 2404 of Public Law 111–148 (42 U.S.C. 1396r–5 note) is amended by striking “December 31, 2019” and inserting “May 22, 2020”.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HBACB84987E5941F8A2B56A28B70CCE59" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Rule of Construction</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Nothing in section 2404 of Public Law 111–148 (42 U.S.C. 1396r–5 note) or section 1902(a)(17) or 1924 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(17), 1396r–5) shall be construed as prohibiting a State from—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HA236D660838948E4B224EF8C3F0604A6" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><chapeau>applying an income or resource disregard under a methodology authorized under section 1902(r)(2) of such Act (42 U.S.C. 1396a(r)(2))—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H45407F54AFA94FB28E62AA356E045F75" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>to the income or resources of an individual described in section 1902(a)(10)(A)(ii)(VI) of such Act (42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(10)(A)(ii)(VI)) (including a disregard of the income or resources of such individual’s spouse); or</content></subparagraph>

<subsection id="H9941408DDD8D446E957AF2DDE4C3ACBD" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Combating Vector-borne Diseases</inline>.—</heading><content>Title III of the Public Health Service Act is amended by inserting after section 317T (42 U.S.C. 247b–22) the following:
<quotedContent id="H1B3C1C4F9D8040DA981E825E9442367B" styleType="OLC">
<section id="HAA8FC64870B5453BABC5FABB1486C556"><num value="317U">“SEC. 317U. </num><heading>NATIONAL STRATEGY AND REGIONAL CENTERS OF EXCELLENCE IN VECTOR-BORNE DISEASES.</heading>
<subsection id="H55912D0482CC42B4ABF3A7A881DEFED1" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Secretary shall—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H6B6DB0EA3BB24FD896FCCBB277072507" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1)</num><subparagraph id="HEF98C3B40B4840CF9D44AD7A6A7352A1" class="inline"><num value="A">(A) </num><chapeau>ensure the development and implementation of a national strategy to address vector-borne diseases, including tick-borne diseases, that—</chapeau>
<clause id="HA8B991FD81C647AEA3978D76B51706AE" class="indent2"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>identifies and assesses gaps and any unnecessary duplication in federally-funded programs; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H974E3D242F2B4D42B9BC1CC98ACC40D6" class="indent2"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>identifies strategic goals to address such diseases and appropriate benchmarks to measure progress toward achieving such goals; and</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H0A85B07B41E14FE6A43FDFA54E5FD827" class="indent1"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>update such strategy, as appropriate; and</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3FB661A3AD624764B47C7D2F9CA75748" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>coordinate programs and activities, including related to data collection, research, and the development of diagnostics, treatments, vaccines, and other related activities, to address vector-borne diseases, including tick-borne diseases, across the Department of Health and Human Services and with other Federal agencies or departments, as appropriate.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H5B994B5373D74D16AC439E24AC2354BB" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Consultation</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In carrying out subsection (a)(1), the Secretary shall consult with the Tick-Borne Disease Working Group established under section 2062 of the 21st Century Cures Act (42 U.S.C. 284s) and other individuals, as appropriate, such as—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HB9D1AA4B335543FDAFF204E31EBE1712" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>epidemiologists with experience in vector-borne diseases;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HDC8144519C354DFE8F567519B2AAE361" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>representatives of patient advocacy and research organizations that focus on vector-borne diseases, including such organizations that have demonstrated experience in related research, public health, data collection, or patient access to care;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H007ED36BC5244A4C9A0FBE4C161C5A01" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><content>health information technology experts or other information management specialists;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8AF4E7BB6CB048F5850FB05B225CDFC9" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><content>clinicians, entomologists, vector management professionals, public health professionals, and others with expertise in vector-borne diseases; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4654B69AD8D54D8691875CDEAF20E7EF" class="indent1"><num value="5">“(5) </num><content>researchers, including researchers with experience conducting translational research.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HF0263D801A1A40399659E9595DC34D62" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Centers of Excellence</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Secretary, in coordination with the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, shall award grants, contracts, or cooperative agreements to institutions of higher education for the establishment or continued support of regional centers of excellence in vector-borne diseases to address vector-borne diseases, including tick-borne diseases, by—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H4D5D5B61D5D3470E97207DB7E05EF86F" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>facilitating collaboration between academia and public health organizations for public health surveillance, prevention, and response activities related to vector-borne diseases, including tick-borne diseases;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD9EA4C6875AC48778284D1B5FB042919" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>providing training for public health entomologists and other health care professionals, as appropriate, to address vector-borne diseases, including tick-borne diseases;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD1697315205A4CC6A629BE8388B98490" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><content>conducting research to develop and validate prevention and control tools and methods, including evidence-based and innovative, evidence-informed tools and methods to anticipate and respond to disease outbreaks; or</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5656B7DCB00944FE8CAE854B6A0A65AE" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><content>preparing for and responding to outbreaks of vector-borne diseases, including tick-borne diseases.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H379A25103CEF4354AD3A0933EBFCC9F0" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Eligibility</inline>.—</heading><content>To be eligible to receive a grant, contract, or cooperative agreement under subsection (c), an entity shall submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require, including a description of how the entity will conduct the activities described in such subsection.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H7A603AFED631430CA26817182E77874B" class="indent0"><num value="e">“(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reports</inline>.—</heading>

<paragraph id="HCF9CB14571DF453DB38A1831E616BDBA" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Progress report</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 4 years after the date of enactment of this section, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions of the Senate and the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives, a report on the progress made in addressing vector-borne diseases, including tick-borne diseases, through activities carried out under this section.</content></paragraph></subsection>

<subparagraph id="HB4BB338742C64C9DADF385EB25714FC7" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Out of any money in the Treasury of the United States not otherwise appropriated, there are appropriated to the Secretary, for payment to each State that was operating a demonstration project approved under section 1130 of the Social Security Act on September 30, 2019, for each fiscal year specified in subparagraph (B) of this paragraph, an amount equal to the amount (if any) by which—</chapeau>
<clause id="HDEF2D4F0E3074E10815D771BD6D0CA03" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i)</num><subclause id="HB708E2ED197C443A8AB637E430B4B421" class="inline"><num value="I">(I) </num><content>the applicable percentage for the fiscal year so specified of the maximum capped allocation due to the State or sub-State jurisdiction for fiscal year 2019 for foster care maintenance, administration, or training costs, under the demonstration project, as specified in section 4.3 of the State waiver terms and conditions document capped allocation payment table in effect on August 31, 2019; or</content></subclause>
<subclause id="H2532BF7168894D2DBB5A6733A25ED7DA" class="indent3"><num value="II">(II) </num><content>if the terms and conditions do not specify a maximum amount payable for fiscal year 2019 for the State or sub-State jurisdiction (due to the use of a comparison jurisdiction to ensure cost neutrality), the final cost neutrality limit for the State or sub-State jurisdiction for fiscal year 2018, as most recently reported by the State or sub-State jurisdiction as of September 30, 2019, for foster care maintenance, administration, or training costs under the demonstration project that were included in the waiver; exceeds</content></subclause></clause>
<clause id="HD2FB5B5F63BF47DBAFC5C193E4897E57" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>the total amount payable to the State or sub-State jurisdiction under part E of title IV of such Act for the fiscal year so specified for foster care expenditures (whether payable under paragraph (1) or (3) of section 474(a) of such Act) that were maintenance, administration, or training costs of the demonstration project taken into account by the Secretary in determining the total amount referred to in clause (i) of this subparagraph.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H25B270E74CDB4109BC8E601856725E9F" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Applicable percentage defined</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this subparagraph, the term “applicable percentage” means—</chapeau>
<clause id="H18E8EF78D1044C59979BE189B1BD8621" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>90 percent, in the case of fiscal year 2020; or</content></clause>
<clause id="HD81CF2A319B143759EB9B1DC29EE26F5" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>75 percent, in the case of fiscal year 2021.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H5D9AE73DBC9F434BAE0D3BC980F72F2F" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Special rule</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The calculation under subparagraph (A) with respect to a State shall be made without regard to—</chapeau>
<clause id="H4D0151B331F04201B23D55A79F9645E6" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>any change approved after August 31, 2019, in the capped allocation or the terms and conditions referred to in clause (i) of subparagraph (A) with respect to the State; or</content></clause>
<clause id="H62FB1F90B1354393AEE1ED5AEA6A7C1A" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>any change made after such date to the financial form submitted by the State that is used in determining the capped allocation.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H12DB660696564E2580BA96E044A01C9F" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Distribution of funds</inline>.—</heading><content>Each State that receives funds under this paragraph shall distribute the funds to jurisdictions in the State that were operating demonstration projects under section 1130 of the Social Security Act in a manner consistent with each sub-State jurisdiction’s proportionate loss as compared with fiscal year 2019.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H8BA4289307FA45079944E0C023747082" class="indent2"><num value="E">(E) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reconciliation process</inline>.—</heading><content>Each State seeking a payment under this paragraph shall report expenditures pursuant to part E of title IV of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 670 et seq.) in a manner determined by the Secretary and the Secretary shall account for any revisions to spending for fiscal years 2020 and 2021 after the end of the respective fiscal year that are reported by the State agency administering the State plan approved under such part, and received by the Department of Health and Human Services, within 2 years after the last day of the fiscal quarter in which the expenditure was made.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HEBB494D214084E31A9E8ED92D90CC660" class="indent2"><num value="F">(F) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Availability of funds</inline>.—</heading><content>The amounts made available for payments to States under this paragraph for a fiscal year shall remain available through the end of the third succeeding fiscal year.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3D1AB61B9EAD44C98A0E5A8DDDFBA0F0" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Use of funds</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H6D574F26B3E64DE19877A03BA1A421FB" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>In addition to the purposes specified in part B of title IV of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 671 et seq.), a State may use funds provided under this subsection for activities previously funded under a demonstration project under section 1130 of such Act (42 U.S.C. 1320a–9) to reduce any adverse fiscal impacts as jurisdictions transition funding sources for the projects, and for activities directly associated with the implementation of title VII of division E of Public Law 115–123 (also known as the Family First Prevention Services Act).</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H3E590CDDC0544F8486C3F096D09A8601" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitation</inline>.—</heading><content>None of the funds provided under this subsection may be used to match Federal funds under any program.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HC06DA1E016BB4EA0B5D731F3D871B3F5" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reporting on Enhanced Funding for Transition Activities</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HA2168AA3BEF44BA19A3E22A7E6106983" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Each State to which funds are paid under subsection (c) of this section shall submit to the Secretary, in a manner specified by the Secretary, a written report on—</chapeau>

<subparagraph id="H6801B6B262744BF0A388B1143B4A551E" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>all programs, services, and operational costs to which the grant is put;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H9AA833ED7D014D83A614C7D062AA021C" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>the characteristics of the families and children served by use of the grant; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H5A2757BA4748494E9F22C37936AAF359" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D)</num><clause id="H6E56DE45C0EE4DA586F00DC2051763A6" class="inline"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>the use by the State of amounts provided for each fiscal year to continue activities previously funded under a waiver provided under section 1130 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1320a–9); and</content></clause>
<clause id="H858E4556FECD4AD19DE7C04AC7CCB30A" class="indent2"><num value="ii">(ii)</num><subclause id="HD0721180D2894EB8A638BC713F0C92FF" class="inline"><num value="I">(I) </num><content>the plan of the State to transition the activities so that needed activities can be provided under the State plan approved under part E of title IV of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 670 et seq.); or</content></subclause>
<subclause id="HD6B32ACEC1A74F00B4F23EBD027C29DF" class="indent2"><num value="II">(II) </num><chapeau>if expenditures for the activities would not be eligible for payment under the State plan approved under such part E—</chapeau>
<item id="HF68904788C1A47EBB8421031D37D6A57" class="indent3"><num value="aa">(aa) </num><content>the reason therefor; and</content></item>
<item id="HB9FF1171C528464B9EC729FD1C4CECD3" class="indent3"><num value="bb">(bb) </num><content>the funding sources the State plans to use to cover the costs of needed activities.</content></item></subclause></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD442210755374F5787A3824215C985A5" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Applicability of other laws</inline>.—</heading><content>For purposes of subpart 2 of part B of title IV of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 629 et seq.), each report required by paragraph (1) of this subsection shall be considered to be required by section 432(a)(8) of such Act (42 U.S.C. 629b(a)(8)), and shall contain such additional information as the Secretary may require.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="definitions" id="H2DD89E70C0D946328319FE7F6F0A57AB" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definition of State</inline>.—</heading><content>In this section, the term “<term>State</term>” has the meaning given the term in section 431(a)(4) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 629a(a)(4)).</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H379A22D275454E3082A16EB3A010CDCA" class="indent0"><num value="f">(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Renaming of Title IV–B–2 of the Social Security Act</inline>.—</heading><content>The subpart heading for subpart 2 of part B of title IV of the Social Security Act is amended by striking “<headingText role="subpart" styleType="OLC">Promoting Safe and Stable Families</headingText>” and inserting “<headingText role="subpart" styleType="OLC">MaryLee Allen Promoting Safe and Stable Families Program</headingText>”.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HC7DB482FF5AF4B77AB708CB8730D37A1" class="indent0"><num value="g">(g) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective Date</inline>.—</heading><content>This section and the amendments made by this section shall take effect as if included in the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2018 on the date of the enactment of such Act.</content></subsection>

<subsection id="HE3D63938BA1A4ACEA58035C162A8DFD0" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 906(d) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 387f(d)) is amended—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HAC0CFA8EABB043CBA65B1757106CE0B3" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>in paragraph (3)(A)(ii), by striking “18 years” and inserting “21 years”; and</content></paragraph>

<paragraph id="H1055F4D6007B4017AC5F754FA4D3CAC5" class="indent1"><num value="5">“(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Minimum age of sale</inline>.—</heading><content>It shall be unlawful for any retailer to sell a tobacco product to any person younger than 21 years of age.”</content></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H1F17789660284C7E88F0C28B854A1591" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Regulations</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H142CF24EE7DF49FCA59D8BE5EBAFDFB6" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Health and Human Services (referred to in this section as the “Secretary”) shall publish in the Federal Register a final rule to update the regulations issued under chapter IX of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 387 et seq.) as appropriate, only to carry out the amendments made by subsection (a), including to update all references to persons younger than 18 years of age in subpart B of part 1140 of title 21, Code of Federal Regulations, and to update the relevant age verification requirements under such part 1140 to require age verification for individuals under the age of 30. Such final rule shall—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H46C95E65B6884BD48CFDA3F89D0F6B6E" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>take full effect not later than 90 days after the date on which such final rule is published; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H20547768640B4855A379A53AFF3A8380" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>be deemed to be in compliance with all applicable provisions of chapter 5 of title 5, United States Code and all other provisions of law relating to rulemaking procedures.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H18A90F980BF44C2C8FA6419A624831A5" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Other regulations</inline>.—</heading><content>Prior to making amendments to part 1140 of title 21, Code of Federal Regulations other than the amendments described in paragraph (1), the Secretary shall promulgate a proposed rule in accordance with chapter 5 of title 5, United States Code.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H411C1F2ED15D41658A92D13A5BD327F0" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Notification</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall provide written notification to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions of the Senate and the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives regarding the progress of the Department of Health and Human Services towards promulgating the final rule under subsection (b). If, 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, such rule has not been promulgated in accordance with subsection (b), the Secretary shall provide a written notification and a justification for the delay in rulemaking to such committees.</content></subsection>
