<section id="H9013FABC5BA64B8DB41F9A42814DA106"><num value="642">“SEC. 642. </num><heading>REQUIREMENTS RELATING TO CHARGES FOR COVERED SERVICES.</heading>
<subsection id="HBFAFCE23914E436FBF2A747EE1BCAD99" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Consumer Rights in Sales</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HEEC49CBA4EA946B89AE04529E6BE56FB" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Right to transparency</inline>.—</heading><content>Before entering into a contract with a consumer for the provision of a covered service, a provider of a covered service shall provide the consumer, by phone, in person, online, or by other reasonable means, the total monthly charge for the covered service, whether offered individually or as part of a bundled service, selected by the consumer (explicitly noting the amount of any applicable promotional discount reflected in such charge and when such discount will expire), including any related administrative fees, equipment fees, or other charges, a good faith estimate of any tax, fee, or charge imposed by the Federal Government or a State or local government (whether imposed on the provider or imposed on the consumer but collected by the provider), and a good faith estimate of any fee or charge that is used to recover any other assessment imposed on the provider by the Federal Government or a State or local government.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE28225AFBE694BDE81D8822D69CEC4D5" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Right to formal notice</inline>.—</heading><content>A provider of a covered service that enters into a contract described in paragraph (1) shall, not later than 24 hours after entering into the contract, send the consumer, by email, online link, or other reasonably comparable means, a copy of the information described in such paragraph.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H890933A3A2504AD2ABCEE68CB9114657" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Right to cancel</inline>.—</heading><content>A provider of a covered service that enters into a contract described in paragraph (1) shall permit the consumer to cancel the contract, without paying early cancellation fees or other disconnection fees or penalties, during the 24-hour period beginning when the provider of the covered service sends the copy required by paragraph (2).</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HABE8859A87B04D94AAEBE828356B5F89" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Consumer Rights in E-billing</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>If a provider of a covered service provides a bill to a consumer in an electronic format, the provider shall include in the bill—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H3BDA22FA8763440DADC21C7444BF44C5" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>an itemized statement that breaks down the total amount charged for or relating to the provision of the covered service by the amount charged for the provision of the service itself and the amount of all related taxes, administrative fees, equipment fees, or other charges;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H60DEAA7522FF4431894F2910FF2EB180" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>the termination date of the contract for the provision of the covered service entered into between the consumer and the provider; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H63AE13B5FF7244EAB336030674406EC6" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><content>the termination date of any applicable promotional discount.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H66F7797E1E87477C8211B9615DBFB352" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Consumer Rights to Accurate Equipment Charges</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>A provider of a covered service or fixed broadband internet access service may not charge a consumer for—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HEBBEABDDF288473580F5B62D5DF28EB4" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>using covered equipment provided by the consumer; or</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE1348E5BDDC84913B02D87268416FFF0" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><chapeau>renting, leasing, or otherwise providing to the consumer covered equipment if—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HCE092438E92F4FC0B3BDE9C99784DEF3" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>the provider has not provided the equipment to the consumer; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD34EEA2F2F094FF7972A9F175956910F" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>the consumer has returned the equipment to the provider, except to the extent that the charge relates to the period beginning on the date when the provider provided the equipment to the consumer and ending on the date when the consumer returned the equipment to the provider.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HD8BF515B95FD4012AD45EF410184BD94" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definitions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H0162F39C29BA4B13B5656EF4CFB41FD7" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Broadband internet access service</inline>.—</heading><content>The term ‘broadband internet access service’ has the meaning given such term in section 8.1(b) of title 47, Code of Federal Regulations, or any successor regulation.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H2A7863A54647453D8964DA4B5CF9509F" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Covered equipment</inline>.—</heading><content>The term ‘covered equipment’ means equipment (such as a router) employed on the premises of a person (other than a provider of a covered service or fixed broadband internet access service) to provide a covered service or to provide fixed broadband internet access service.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H59DBF9BA31A74FC0AA6E204BFC1FE1B0" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Covered service</inline>.—</heading><content>The term ‘covered service’ means service provided by a multichannel video programming distributer, to the extent such distributor is acting as a multichannel video programming distributor.”</content></paragraph></subsection></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>

<title id="H962D9BF4F7D34F09BA5A90D1B16E481D" styleType="OLC"><num value="XII">TITLE XII—</num><heading class="inline">GROUNDFISH TRAWL FISHERY</heading>
<section id="HF98593C3954642359F4B8F54E7F06D30" styleType="OLC"><num value="1201">SEC. 1201. </num><heading>GROUNDFISH TRAWL FISHERY.</heading><content class="block">The Secretary of Commerce shall forgive the interest accrued on the Groundfish Trawl fishery sub-loan regarding fishing capacity reduction in the West Coast groundfish fishery authorized by section 212 of division B, title II, of Public Law 108–7 from December 4, 2003, through September 8, 2005, and the portion of additional interest accrued in the Groundfish Trawl fishery sub-loan since September 8, 2005, that is directly attributable to the delay in implementing a repayment system. The Secretary of the Treasury shall make available, out of any funds in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, such sums necessary for any loan modification under this provision.</content></section></title>
<title id="H829C436236AC4EA59B23486A7B4F17FC" styleType="OLC"><num value="XIII">TITLE XIII—</num><heading class="inline">TEMPORARY RELIEF FROM CERTAIN ERISA REQUIREMENTS</heading>
<section id="H28689240A5634D248A937C778D3E37F8" styleType="OLC"><num value="1301">SEC. 1301. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This title may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="title">Temporary Relief from Certain ERISA Requirements Act of 2020</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section id="H84F4DD871673415DB4282DCF09ECC648" styleType="OLC"><num value="1302">SEC. 1302. </num><heading>EXEMPTION.</heading>
<subsection id="HAC399435E0AD42A69C694B0DFB6FC172" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 408 of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (29 U.S.C. 1108) is amended by adding at the end the following:
<quotedContent id="H6BE86BECB02F4AABB160350F5F970C71" styleType="OLC">
<subsection id="H89B70386E8BF4BA8ACB23B404B2D5CCB" class="indent0"><num value="h">“(h) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Provision of Pharmacy Benefit Services</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H03D8760BE5CE47A4B2F76B73F98234F3" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Provided that all of the conditions described in paragraph (2) are met, the restrictions imposed by subsections (a), (b)(1), and (b)(2) of section 406 shall not apply to—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H0268CE6878CD445795603991AC78C50A" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>the offering of pharmacy benefit services to a group health plan that is sponsored by an entity described in section 3(37)(G)(vi) or to any other group health plan that is sponsored by a regional council, local union, or other labor organization affiliated with such entity;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H42124971F88B4C408A8B17AE6225CA23" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>the purchase of pharmacy benefit services by plan participants and beneficiaries of a group health plan that is sponsored by an entity described in section 3(37)(G)(vi) or of any other group health plan that is sponsored by a regional council, local union, or other labor organization affiliated with such entity; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H2176BD7D2B2140229B4D106E79BE93E5" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>the operation or implementation of pharmacy benefit services by an entity described in section 3(37)(G)(vi) or by any other group health plan that is sponsored by a regional council, local union, or other labor organization affiliated with such entity,</content></subparagraph>
<continuation class="indent0" role="paragraph">in any arrangement where such entity described in section 3(37)(G)(vi) or any related organization or subsidiary of such entity provides pharmacy benefit services that include prior authorization and appeals, a retail pharmacy network, pharmacy benefit administration, mail order fulfillment, formulary support, manufacturer payments, audits, and specialty pharmacy and goods, to any such group health plan.</continuation></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H2CE71651A6134880835A6561EA3F35C8" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Conditions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The conditions described in this paragraph are the following:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H63F9066A036240439A9C70DF91098D04" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>The terms of the arrangement are at least as favorable to the group health plan as such group health plan could obtain in a similar arm’s length arrangement with an unrelated third party.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H9B55531AB3F84FA091159158A56EC5F3" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>At least 50 percent of the providers participating in the pharmacy benefit services offered by the arrangement are unrelated to the contributing employers or any other party in interest with respect to the group health plan.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HBD3D6B0724F548E3BE9118F349C2B5B0" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>The group health plan retains an independent fiduciary who will be responsible for monitoring the group health plan’s consultants, contractors, subcontractors, and other service providers for purposes of pharmacy benefit services described in paragraph (1) offered by such entity or any of its related organizations or subsidiaries and monitors the transactions of such entity and any of its related organizations or subsidiaries to ensure that all conditions of this exemption are satisfied during each plan year.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HBCE25AC41A2048D291D57B41C4507138" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><content>Any decisions regarding the provision of pharmacy benefit services described in paragraph (1) are made by the group health plan’s independent fiduciary, based on objective standards developed by the independent fiduciary in reliance on information provided by the arrangement.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H12BFEA17892A4C8B8DE12D08DA56AE14" class="indent2"><num value="E">“(E) </num><content>The independent fiduciary of the group health plan provides an annual report to the Secretary and the congressional committees of jurisdiction attesting that the conditions described in subparagraphs (C) and (D) have been met for the applicable plan year, together with a statement that use of the arrangement’s services are in the best interest of the participants and beneficiaries in the aggregate for that plan year compared to other similar arrangements the group health plan could have obtained in transactions with an unrelated third party.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HCF42F7DAFED14C799F82BB0A8FBBEBB3" class="indent2"><num value="F">“(F) </num><content>The arrangement is not designed to benefit any party in interest with respect to the group health plan.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFEA4B906E2DD47068061A906E4C8A855" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Violations</inline>.—</heading><content>In the event an entity described in section 3(37)(G)(vi) or any affiliate of such entity violates any of the conditions of such exemption, such exemption shall not apply with respect to such entity or affiliate and all enforcement and claims available under this Act shall apply with respect to such entity or affiliate.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFA7D826AB71E4EE69FFC380515BAC7EF" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Rule of construction</inline>.—</heading><content>Nothing in this subsection shall be construed to modify any obligation of a group health plan otherwise set forth in this Act.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H11E0EF8A2E3D445096256DE4C077A38A" class="indent1"><num value="5">“(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Group health plan</inline>.—</heading><content>In this subsection, the term ‘<term>group health plan</term>’ has the meaning given such term in section 733(a).”</content></paragraph></subsection></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>
<subsection id="H7C6C9C63904A485D9DF5F580FCA7168B" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Amendment to Internal Revenue Code of 1986</inline>.—</heading><content>Subsection (c) of section 4975 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following new paragraph:
<quotedContent id="H58D85A75FAEF439488FEE585DD1106C7" styleType="OLC">
<paragraph id="H3604AF5DD88E44DF8A131A83C04F2954" class="indent1"><num value="7">“(7) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Special rule for provision of pharmacy benefit services</inline>.—</heading><content>Any party to an arrangement which satisfies the requirements of section 408(h) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 shall be exempt from the tax imposed by this section with respect to such arrangement.”</content></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>
<subsection id="H377F10AFA56A441EAAA5AD246F7FFB93" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Applicability</inline>.—</heading><content>With respect to a group health plan subject to subsection (h) of section 408 of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (29 U.S.C. 1108) (as amended by subsection (a)) and subsection (c) of section 4975 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 (as amended by subsection (b)), beginning at the end of the fifth plan year of such group health plan that begins after the date of enactment of this Act, such subsection (h) of such section 408 and such subsection (c) of such shall have no force or effect.</content></subsection></section></title>

<section id="H74837847A8F84CB993FA9EA07A28B6CB" styleType="OLC"><num value="1403">SEC. 1403. </num><heading>NATIONAL LIBRARY SERVICE FOR THE BLIND AND PRINT DISABLED.</heading>
<subsection id="H6AF9984EB5394A6DACE9C63FD2088612" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>The Act entitled “An Act to provide books for the adult blind”, approved March 3, 1931 (2 U.S.C. 135a et seq.), is amended to read as follows:
<quotedContent id="H48BEB0534B4E40FB9CC8FA6C54B5D9DF" styleType="OLC">
<section id="H292CFD7A571D4C1FBF766D0E45A957DD"><num value="1">“SECTION 1. </num><heading>NATIONAL LIBRARY SERVICE FOR THE BLIND AND PRINT DISABLED.</heading>
<subsection id="HA194D70204314B4E9C61456B51A0C8AC" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Accessible Materials and Reproducers</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H19EBAAF5AF194553A31A7B3E8692BFDE" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Librarian of Congress is authorized to provide to eligible persons who are residents of the United States (including residents of the several States, insular possessions, and the District of Columbia) and to eligible persons who are United States citizens residing outside the United States the following items:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HF342A7F22C2A42DF8DA355948BB89B7E" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>Literary works published in raised characters, on sound-reproduction recordings, or in any other accessible format.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H4B5C6EB0F4734706A9121341110D4E9E" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>Musical scores, instructional texts, and other specialized materials used in furthering educational, vocational, and cultural opportunities in the field of music published in any accessible format.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HFA11329DAB9145F9B6F9DC782CF85CF9" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>Reproducers for such formats.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HCBB2A7D068744F03BEC4E569704B3CDE" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Ownership</inline>.—</heading><content>Any item provided under paragraph (1) shall be provided on a loan basis and shall remain the property of the Library of Congress.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HAADA1F2321824EB8847FB7669778C585" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Lending Preference</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In the lending of items under subsection (a), the Librarian shall at all times give preference to—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H9C570EEB15BD4BD39BB63D5146368665" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>the needs of the blind and visually disabled; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HDEE40C979E3749EBB3C2E4457BB19E36" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>the needs of eligible persons who have been honorably discharged from the Armed Forces of the United States.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H6BE1FFDB04D345BCA11D76E6CE5882D2" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Network</inline>.—</heading><content>The Librarian of Congress may contract or otherwise arrange with such public or other nonprofit libraries, agencies, or organizations as the Librarian may determine appropriate to serve as local or regional centers for the circulation of items described in subsection (a)(1).</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HAF9104AFA7E34974B2FEC6503FC7DE1E" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">International Service</inline>.—</heading><content>The Librarian of Congress is authorized to provide items described in subparagraphs (A) and (B) of subsection (a)(1) to authorized entities located in a country that is a party to the Marrakesh Treaty, if any such items are delivered to authorized entities through online, not physical, means. The Librarian may contract or otherwise arrange with such authorized entities to deliver such items to eligible persons located in their countries in any accessible format and consistent with section 121A of title 17, United States Code.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H8BD4C20164F044CB93620756456FAC31" class="indent0"><num value="e">“(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Contracting Preference</inline>.—</heading><content>In the purchase and maintenance of items described in subsection (a), the Librarian of Congress, without regard to section 6101 of title 41, United States Code, shall give preference to nonprofit institutions or agencies whose activities are primarily concerned with the blind and with other physically disabled persons, in all cases where, considering all the circumstances and needs involved, the Librarian determines that the prices submitted are fair and reasonable.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H1E96D7B70BBD4A68A3CDB5DE684549D6" class="indent0"><num value="f">“(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Regulations</inline>.—</heading><content>The Librarian of Congress shall prescribe regulations for services under this section, in consultation with eligible persons and authorized entities. Such regulations shall include procedures that shall be used by an individual to establish that the individual is an eligible person.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HDE20E260F8AB41A7A782826C1177468D" class="indent0"><num value="g">“(g) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definitions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section—</chapeau>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HF9B58C37D9CF407EA523EEE5BB44515F" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>the terms ‘<term>accessible format</term>’, ‘<term>authorized entity</term>’, and ‘<term>eligible person</term>’ have the meanings given those terms in section 121 of title 17, United States Code; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H5B915C3340664B749BAB06FBD84DA9BA" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>the term ‘<term>Marrakesh Treaty</term>’ has the meaning given in section 121A of such title 17.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H2FD69053793B4F21828D2EEA85618371" class="indent0"><num value="h">“(h) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorization of Appropriations</inline>.—</heading><content>There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section such sums as may be necessary.”</content></subsection></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>

<section id="HF5A8FCBF4AF844BCB85C340B5201C7B7" styleType="OLC"><num value="1603">SEC. 1603. </num><heading>LAW ENFORCEMENT AUTHORITY.</heading>
<subsection id="H9FBDFBD5474A42FDADB17FF9E042C039" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Library of Congress</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 1307(d) of the Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 2006 (2 U.S.C. 185(d)) is amended by adding at the end the following:
<quotedContent id="H1551BAA068474C32AC432FBFB44F8A68" styleType="OLC">
<paragraph id="HFDCFDB7C33904616AE4AC49DA7D2300B" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Law enforcement authority</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H56AAC5CED2014DD98375D561A3D4CEBD" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Subject to subparagraph (B), any supervisory special agent under the Inspector General and any special agent supervised by such a supervisory special agent is authorized to—</chapeau>
<clause id="HE10D6BD3EFC24A5F8C6E8FAF7E8B6A9C" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>make an arrest without a warrant while engaged in official duties as authorized under this section or any other statute for any offense against the United States committed in the presence of such supervisory special agent or special agent, or for any felony cognizable under the laws of the United States if such supervisory special agent or special agent has reasonable grounds to believe that the person to be arrested has committed or is committing such felony;</content></clause>
<clause id="H123FC4C7C6FE4048915CDC434414A08D" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>seek and execute warrants for arrest, search of a premises, or seizure of evidence issued under the authority of the United States upon probable cause to believe that a violation has been committed; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H6C15D104E3794001AFDA307796FC1182" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>carry a firearm while engaged in official duties as authorized under this section or any other statute.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H78A2F8BE2BF54598AB31614135829C5C" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requirements to exercise authority</inline>.—</heading>
<clause id="H556BFF35DD784974A4B46AED55DAA6EE" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Required certification</inline>.—</heading>
<subclause id="H279C48B966B2431597D6A0C6636FBF7E" class="indent4"><num value="I">“(I) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In order to exercise the authority under subparagraph (A), a supervisory special agent or a special agent supervised by such a supervisory special agent shall certify that he or she—</chapeau>
<item id="H5E2A1481D8D44330B07746B4F8C63DAC" class="indent5"><num value="aa">“(aa) </num><content>is a citizen of the United States;</content></item>
<item id="H63796D0EFDC64B35A698C5EFC9F12A05" class="indent5"><num value="bb">“(bb) </num><content>has successfully completed a basic law enforcement training program or military or other equivalent; and</content></item>
<item id="HBFEA3DC2F1F74042A2D32FF203CE81ED" class="indent5"><num value="cc">“(cc) </num><content>is not prohibited from receiving a firearm under Federal law, including under section 922(g)(9) of title 18, United States Code, because of a conviction of a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence.</content></item></subclause>
<subclause id="HE89D9751DB4C412B8A584B7F56247D2A" class="indent4"><num value="II">“(II) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Additional requirements</inline>.—</heading><content>After providing notice to the appropriate committees of Congress, the Inspector General may add requirements to the certification required under subclause (I), as determined appropriate by the Inspector General.</content></subclause></clause>
<clause id="H1C6BF462C6F34F22A83330445A67CD9A" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Maintenance of requirements</inline>.—</heading><content>The Inspector General shall maintain firearms-related requirements (including quarterly firearms qualifications) and use of force training requirements that, except to the extent the Inspector General determines necessary to effectively carry out the duties of the Office of the Inspector General, are in accordance with the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency use of force policies, which incorporate Department of Justice guidelines.</content></clause>
<clause id="H1B8EBF05C94A4C178EE0EE7EB7256066" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Eligibility determination</inline>.—</heading>
<subclause id="HFE2B2A82817C4208BBAD2ABBC63B94D4" class="indent4"><num value="I">“(I) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Inspector General shall—</chapeau>
<item id="HD18AE216F458439DAB6789EF0F30661F" class="indent5"><num value="aa">“(aa) </num><content>determine whether an individual meets the requirements under this paragraph; and</content></item>
<item id="H4597333A9A5C44918F958214726B5BC5" class="indent5"><num value="bb">“(bb) </num><content>revoke any authority granted to an individual under subparagraph (A) if the individual is not in compliance with the requirements of this paragraph.</content></item></subclause>
<subclause id="H3A89F17BF39A41DD82A625885929CEDD" class="indent4"><num value="II">“(II) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reauthorization</inline>.—</heading><content>The Inspector General may reauthorize an individual to exercise the authority granted under subparagraph (A) if the Inspector General determines the individual has achieved compliance with the requirements under this paragraph.</content></subclause>
<subclause id="HB3CF4F76015649308FAF487D060979AE" class="indent4"><num value="III">“(III) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitation on appeal</inline>.—</heading><content>A revocation of the authority granted under subparagraph (A) shall not be subject to administrative, judicial, or other review, unless the revocation results in an adverse action. Such an adverse action may, at the election of the applicable individual, be reviewed in accordance with the otherwise applicable procedures.</content></subclause></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HA3A125BAD7764C809F756CA4E21C083B" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Semiannual certification of program</inline>.—</heading>
<clause id="HF1E4F71266384C348560E8413FB538F5" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Before the first grant of authority under subparagraph (A), and semiannually thereafter as part of the report under section 5 of the Inspector General Act of 1978 (5 U.S.C. App.), the Inspector General shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a written certification that adequate internal safeguards and management procedures exist that, except to the extent the Inspector General determines necessary to effectively carry out the duties of the Office of the Inspector General, are in compliance with standards established by the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency, which incorporate Department of Justice guidelines, to ensure proper exercise of the powers authorized under this paragraph.</content></clause>
<clause id="H713EA5ADBC57423096A61B6C537CAD97" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Suspension of authority</inline>.—</heading><content>The authority granted under this paragraph (including any grant of authority to an individual under subparagraph (A), without regard to whether the individual is in compliance with subparagraph (B)) may be suspended by the Inspector General if the Office of Inspector General fails to comply with the reporting and review requirements under clause (i) of this subparagraph or subparagraph (D). Any suspension of authority under this clause shall be reported to the appropriate committees of Congress.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HEC8B75D3C38443E1BC8BEF13A42582D2" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Peer review</inline>.—</heading><content>To ensure the proper exercise of the law enforcement powers authorized under this paragraph, the Office of Inspector General shall submit to and participate in the external review process established by the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency for ensuring that adequate internal safeguards and management procedures continue to exist. Under the review process, the exercise of the law enforcement powers by the Office of Inspector General shall be reviewed periodically by another Office of Inspector General or by a committee of Inspectors General. The results of each review shall be communicated in writing to the Inspector General, the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency, and the appropriate committees of Congress.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H7EB2A549E8564A8A820F098674951F0A" class="indent2"><num value="E">“(E) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Alleged misconduct</inline>.—</heading><content>Any allegation of misconduct by an individual granted authority under subparagraph (A) may be reviewed by the Integrity Committee of the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph role="definitions" id="HC44D6B458F8441FCAF8599B6AFF5075C" class="indent2"><num value="F">“(F) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Appropriate committees of congress</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this paragraph, the term ‘<term>appropriate committees of Congress</term>’ means—</chapeau>
<clause id="H9D53F6AD2D344370BBB03A84A052687A" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the Committee on Rules and Administration and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H70DE16949F964B4BAC0E63DD6B362916" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>the Committee on House Administration and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives.”</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>

<title id="H1069984496774E3DA9FBF0D15EE3B6FA" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="XVIII">TITLE XVIII—</num><heading class="inline">KENTUCKY WILDLANDS NATIONAL HERITAGE AREA STUDY</heading>
<section id="H47C21885F32E4F16B2F11233E5F24963" styleType="OLC"><num value="1801">SEC. 1801. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This title may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="title">Kentucky Wildlands National Heritage Area Study Act</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section id="HFB2F812650894306A9BE948294F5718A" styleType="OLC"><num value="1802">SEC. 1802. </num><heading>DEFINITIONS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">In this Act:</chapeau>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HE557C044D83346529D5A5354ECC25E31" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Heritage area</inline>.—</heading><content>The term “<term>Heritage Area</term>” means the Kentucky Wildlands National Heritage Area.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HDBF58EF89A0340D28D936DB5500ABC00" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Secretary</inline>.—</heading><content>The term “<term>Secretary</term>” means the Secretary of the Interior.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HE59D3498A940463B9F0029F29F51F795" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">State</inline>.—</heading><content>The term “<term>State</term>” means the State of Kentucky.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HD285FC7407E34CA08F38BF379D9DEEE5" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Study area</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term “<term>study area</term>” means—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H27F742E583DF45C3941BE9077AAC16F9" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Adair, Bath, Bell, Boyd, Breathitt, Carter, Casey, Clay, Clinton, Cumberland, Elliott, Floyd, Green, Harlan, Jackson, Johnson, Knott, Knox, Laurel, Lawrence, Lee, Leslie, Letcher, Lincoln, Magoffin, Martin, McCreary, Menifee, Metcalfe, Monroe, Morgan, Owsley, Perry, Pike, Pulaski, Rockcastle, Rowan, Russell, Wayne, Whitley, and Wolfe Counties in the State; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H92B9A1A4807F44AD948D33F48DC47D51" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><chapeau>any other areas in the State that—</chapeau>
<clause id="HC3BD5A12F3F74F379400C43F60184033" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>have heritage aspects that are similar to the heritage aspects of the areas described in subparagraph (A); and</content></clause>
<clause id="H7E6391784F774A5FB2F19730DB4D5B75" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>are adjacent to, or in the vicinity of, the areas described in that subparagraph.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></section>
<section id="H3D94664A2E33448CAACA1FFE416849CA" styleType="OLC"><num value="1803">SEC. 1803. </num><heading>STUDY.</heading>
<subsection id="H080F82F083E1423EB2328212F08DC3A6" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary, in consultation with State and local historic preservation officers, State and local historical societies, State and local tourism offices, and other appropriate organizations and governmental agencies, shall conduct a study to assess the suitability and feasibility of designating the study area as a National Heritage Area, to be known as the “Kentucky Wildlands National Heritage Area”.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H68AD2CBFDBC441429A548D5F8F64A74A" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requirements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The study shall include analysis, documentation, and determinations on whether the study area—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H3E52A067B3BE4051960D69BFEF0A1C07" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><chapeau>has an assemblage of natural, historic, and cultural resources that—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HC1E4A12E08F64F679D561B3C5F54784E" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>represent distinctive aspects of the heritage of the United States;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H2F47140C8E2742308E760AA546EB99E5" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>are worthy of recognition, conservation, interpretation, and continuing use; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HAEC4374678944FAAAF44B6BF9BC43474" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><chapeau>would be best managed—</chapeau>
<clause id="H3D0912B2C0554C0B941B84A8C9C3E55D" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>through partnerships among public and private entities; and</content></clause>
<clause id="HE7CF81AADCD14CA4AA3A9D269EA9EA9A" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>by linking diverse and sometimes noncontiguous resources and active communities;</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H822BA33D43A44308B70DF59D612C5322" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>reflects traditions, customs, beliefs, and folklife that are a valuable part of the story of the United States;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H13410FD242644A86B7F3807618CBD760" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><chapeau>provides outstanding opportunities—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H0E28D5DD9C934EF7ACAE4547FF714F92" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>to conserve natural, historic, cultural, or scenic features; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HE3E94150F5154C80BEE0B6F405F0B75A" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>for recreation and education;</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H82F0CDFD77824F1ABAC2D28DE53E9EAA" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><chapeau>contains resources that—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H7A21E69E1E4C478F8BF335038B62F1A2" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>are important to any identified themes of the study area; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HE9CA3391F180458C88966F233BF6927C" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>retain a degree of integrity capable of supporting interpretation;</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HA8654A25A68A4644986C32C09CED3C2D" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><chapeau>includes residents, business interests, nonprofit organizations, and State and local governments that—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H5B322D487CD843D28B9534E44EAD7927" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>are involved in the planning of the Heritage Area;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HDC95982DEFDA4244A8F4BDB9A46031C8" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>have developed a conceptual financial plan that outlines the roles of all participants in the Heritage Area, including the Federal Government; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H9BFC155A35E2420FA66AFF0D60C3B23E" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>have demonstrated support for the designation of the Heritage Area;</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H59790683FE1B417EA7B02A3037739012" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>has a potential management entity to work in partnership with the individuals and entities described in paragraph (5) to develop the Heritage Area while encouraging State and local economic activity;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H0CCF915BAF6041418FBCE1AFBFD95156" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>could impact the rights of private property owners with respect to private property; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1371C8C94C8A4CE79CF21E63043406E3" class="indent1"><num value="8">(8) </num><content>has a conceptual boundary map that is supported by the public.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="HA666775E9DC648CAB6B7DB37DE367A20" styleType="OLC"><num value="1804">SEC. 1804. </num><heading>REPORT.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">Not later than 3 years after the date on which funds are first made available to carry out this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate and the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives a report that describes—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H9EFB1E14BF564D65BA80DED3AD60F1F9" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the findings of the study under section 1803; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8B6B59EC2D0C4E099137E60EA0D7D664" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>any conclusions and recommendations of the Secretary.</content></paragraph></section></title>

<title id="H5B256E0F021B4795B2A2E1A8D6F551A6" styleType="OLC" changed="added"><num value="XX">TITLE XX—</num><heading class="inline">EUROPEAN ENERGY SECURITY AND DIVERSIFICATION ACT OF 2019</heading>
<section changed="added" id="HB0FED6F6F7784BB5A0A5C153C1881DD8" styleType="OLC"><num value="2001">SEC. 2001. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This title may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="title">European Energy Security and Diversification Act of 2019</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section changed="added" id="H7171931B19114C2F8408782A858425B6" styleType="OLC"><num value="2002">SEC. 2002. </num><heading>DEFINITIONS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">In this title:</chapeau>
<paragraph role="definitions" changed="added" id="HD5CF504F6E934C049CC5CCB1DB03A7B3" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Early-stage project support</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term “<term>early-stage project support</term>” includes—</chapeau>
<subparagraph changed="notChanged" id="H9C3D33F801244CC4B50D570403612387" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>feasibility studies;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HDA35518752FE48C5AB53E3D6EA451193" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>resource evaluations;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HE5DAFB2F2F1F4621A672B915C11BB8E8" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>project appraisal and costing;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HFBA685E85AFC45678B01EEB4D7D177F8" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>pilot projects;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H54F5CD81DC494F75B8C4AE6E39FEBCD7" class="indent2"><num value="E">(E) </num><content>commercial support, such as trade missions, reverse trade missions, technical workshops, international buyer programs, and international partner searchers to link suppliers to projects;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H5176BE0AC7714BB1A7B4BCE33A1D4EBD" class="indent2"><num value="F">(F) </num><content>technical assistance and other guidance to improve the local regulatory environment and market frameworks to encourage transparent competition and enhance energy security; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HEC139606D2754FB8A1FABB71325BF885" class="indent2"><num value="G">(G) </num><content>long-term energy sector planning.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" changed="added" id="H6D54C342C4424A3FBA60765F4B0FCFBF" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Late-stage project support</inline>.—</heading><content>The term “<term>late-stage project support</term>” includes debt financing, insurance, and transaction advisory services.</content></paragraph></section>
<section changed="added" id="H4D22C9BC9F37415799543E2A560F25C4" styleType="OLC"><num value="2003">SEC. 2003. </num><heading>STATEMENT OF POLICY.</heading>
<subsection changed="added" id="HD46CC02717C549C085C05396A6560FF9" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress</inline>.—</heading><content>It is the sense of Congress that the United States has economic and national security interests in assisting European and Eurasian countries achieve energy security through diversification of their energy sources and supply routes.</content></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="HF351AECB3EBE4DABAD4B7F4D441A907E" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Statement of Policy</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>It is the policy of the United States—</chapeau>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H763408D05A8740C5BA0FC0AD2ADA8012" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>to advance United States foreign policy and development goals by assisting European and Eurasian countries to reduce their dependence on energy resources from countries that use energy dependence for undue political influence, such as the Russian Federation, which has used natural gas to coerce, intimidate, and influence other countries;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HD2272FADB5FF4454A8910AC529839CE7" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>to promote the energy security of allies and partners of the United States by encouraging the development of accessible, transparent, and competitive energy markets that provide diversified sources, types, and routes of energy;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HB7D600E61C234EBB95211C6C3368BBE6" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>to encourage United States public and private sector investment in European energy infrastructure projects to bridge the gap between energy security requirements and commercial demand in a way that is consistent with the region’s absorptive capacity; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H28E48F57E8904DFEB04092F4F0640D81" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>to help facilitate the export of United States energy resources, technology, and expertise to global markets in a way that benefits the energy security of allies and partners of the United States, including in Europe and Eurasia.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section changed="added" id="H0E7A523D5F694A0CB56AF305010A9F20" styleType="OLC"><num value="2004">SEC. 2004. </num><heading>PRIORITIZATION OF EFFORTS AND ASSISTANCE FOR ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS IN EUROPE AND EURASIA.</heading>
<subsection changed="added" id="H166B519236DD430D98C6F7E00612CF61" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In pursuing the policy described in section 2003, the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of Energy and the heads of other relevant United States agencies, shall, as appropriate, prioritize and expedite the efforts of the Department of State and those agencies in supporting the efforts of the European Commission and the governments of European and Eurasian countries to increase their energy security, including through—</chapeau>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HB4D45F04F6894D0C82B519BE96131760" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><chapeau>providing diplomatic and political support to the European Commission and those governments, as necessary—</chapeau>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H18C3E8926FB74DB594971420F0B1659F" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>to facilitate international negotiations concerning cross-border infrastructure;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HBA6B30BE3374423AB7481AE8C1DE04A0" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>to enhance Europe’s regulatory environment with respect to energy; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H6E752E1E0C3043DEAAD8C86BCAE7E809" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>to develop accessible, transparent, and competitive energy markets supplied by diverse sources, types, and routes of energy; and</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H3B17B5DD21CF48E3B2011F3BA8883301" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><chapeau>providing support to improve European and Eurasian energy markets, including early-stage project support and late-stage project support for the construction or improvement of energy and related infrastructure, as necessary—</chapeau>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H0AB85CD5F0144AE08F34BF74AC8A0A8F" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>to diversify the energy sources and supply routes of European and Eurasian countries;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H27EDB8E79D6A4509AF9CCC491A9081CD" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>to enhance energy market integration across the region; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H39B91F42543F440FA52F1DCE75122471" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>to increase competition within energy markets.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H6DFE7F397AB84E68B284DE973F2A461C" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Project Selection</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HC346197F170A4A76973161F92A609D3E" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>The agencies described in subsection (a) shall identify energy infrastructure projects that would be appropriate for United States assistance under this section.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HFC159468D23B427EB1898F641C3BB8EF" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Project eligibility</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>A project is eligible for United States assistance under this section if the project—</chapeau>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H43AF6FFF7E084479A4E121B520C77887" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A)</num><clause id="HBCA9DF405F5C4B1EA8A6F90B1EF60AA7" class="inline"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>improves electricity transmission infrastructure, power generation through the use of a broad power mix (including fossil fuel and renewable energy), or energy efficiency; or</content></clause>
<clause changed="added" id="H8CAE372553D5413ABF3E7A509AB6B01F" class="indent2"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><content>advances electricity storage projects, smart grid projects, distributed generation models, or other technological innovations, as appropriate; and</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HBF0F9DF510114543AE261AA205BF7337" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>is located in a European or Eurasian country.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H6BB79B8C9BF34682BE08FD65DC189661" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Preference</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In selecting among projects that are eligible under paragraph (2), the agencies described in subsection (a) shall give preference to projects that—</chapeau>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HB314D49ACF7247C18978840F6DB989A0" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>link the energy systems of 2 or more European or Eurasian countries;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H091436C7EBFF4A6591498EBB8448443A" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>have already been identified by the European Commission as being integral for the energy security of European countries;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H05242085A5C541F9A1F8C117B1BFB2B1" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>are expected to enhance energy market integration;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H26C72B539B76442393A40A5CDDF6684C" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>can attract funding from the private sector, an international financial institution, the government of the country in which the project will be carried out, or the European Commission; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H91F6B6659EF843B2A31BA2D993B2579A" class="indent2"><num value="E">(E) </num><content>have the potential to use United States goods and services during project implementation.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H2B9DD6295E184FCEB4A21D95C8C68BEF" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Types of Assistance</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph changed="added" id="HA7FFE05243B64CAAA1AFAA4A532D3C35" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Diplomatic and political support</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of State shall provide diplomatic and political support to the European Commission and the governments of European and Eurasian countries, as necessary, including by using the diplomatic and political influence and expertise of the Department of State to build the capacity of those countries to resolve any impediments to the development of projects selected under subsection (b).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H6AF57256EBE544888EAE0A1AB30685EA" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Early-stage project support</inline>.—</heading><content>The Director of the Trade and Development Agency shall provide early-stage project support with respect to projects selected under subsection (b), as necessary.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="notChanged" id="HEB50FB00691A45DAB02994C0C538C9AC" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Late-stage project support</inline>.—</heading><content>Agencies described in subsection (a) that provide late-stage project support shall do so with respect to projects selected under subsection (b), as necessary.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H7569BBE7A61643F89877CB7C6985F2C3" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Funding</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H0F75EFED79864604859EC74D60390223" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Trade and development agency</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 661(f)(1)(A) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2421(f)(1)(A)) is amended by striking “$48,000,000 for fiscal year 2000” and inserting “$79,500,000 for fiscal year 2020”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H0768C191299048CE82839FCA60DE8820" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Countering russian influence fund</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 254 of the Countering Russian Influence in Europe and Eurasia Act of 2017 (22 U.S.C. 9543) is amended—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HC6A3C2D4E4BA44838ED0CF01D195D190" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>in subsection (a), by striking “fiscal years 2018 and 2019” and inserting “fiscal years 2020, 2021, 2022, and 2023”; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H2A1A7D6140ED4FFC9A8B770EF9B8E95B" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>in subsection (b), by adding at the end the following new paragraph:
<quotedContent id="H32C202DCD1B146CEADC096814FF411CB" styleType="OLC">
<paragraph id="HD6F8C96EB20A42FA879AB7921BE0FAB2" class="indent1"><num value="7">“(7) </num><content>To assist United States agencies that operate under the foreign policy guidance of the Secretary of State in providing assistance under section 2004 of the European Energy Security and Diversification Act of 2019.”</content></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" id="H67EEEAD8607648D29589E269970BB01D" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exception From Certain Limitation Under BUILD Act</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H7F44FD3CEA4742E4AFAB541413F4051B" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>For purposes of providing support for projects under this section—</chapeau>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H34C19DFB83874B4CAE83863D07EDCAF2" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the United States International Development Finance Corporation may provide support for projects in countries with upper-middle-income economies or high-income economies (as those terms are defined by the World Bank);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HDA346241910445E595810FAFE7052272" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the restriction under section 1412(c)(2) of the Better Utilization of Investments Leading to Development Act of 2018 (22 U.S.C. 9612(c)(2)) shall not apply; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H0925CD6242664B0DABBBFC95AF7A731B" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><chapeau>the Corporation shall restrict the provision of such support in a country described in subparagraph (A) unless—</chapeau>
<clause changed="added" id="H6508BCE0E8444C138C95C72855A04DBC" class="indent3"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>the President certifies to the appropriate congressional committees that such support furthers the national economic or foreign policy interests of the United States; and</content></clause>
<clause changed="added" id="HA6C5E6C6FBAE4FC2A99BB8284D8400A8" class="indent3"><num value="ii">(ii) </num><chapeau>such support is—</chapeau>
<subclause changed="added" id="H8C85BB894DA249ED9251E80FA06A0B1D" class="indent4"><num value="I">(I) </num><content>designed to produce significant developmental outcomes or provide developmental benefits to the poorest population of that country; or</content></subclause>
<subclause changed="added" id="H7AB66A18FB494AB59E064D034A9677A1" class="indent4"><num value="II">(II) </num><content>necessary to preempt or counter efforts by a strategic competitor of the United States to secure significant political or economic leverage or acquire national security-sensitive technologies or infrastructure in a country that is an ally or partner of the United States.</content></subclause></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" changed="added" id="H777CD3CD4F1C4998B73330C03E4AC9AB" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definitions</inline>.—</heading><content>In this subsection, the terms “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” and “<term>less developed country</term>” have the meanings given those terms in section 1402 of the Better Utilization of Investments Leading to Development Act of 2018 (22 U.S.C. 9601).</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section changed="added" id="H55541319191A437DBB9E4412AE3B726F" styleType="OLC"><num value="2005">SEC. 2005. </num><heading>PROGRESS REPORTS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter, the President shall submit to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives a report on progress made in providing assistance for projects under section 2004 that includes—</chapeau>
<paragraph changed="notChanged" id="H235E9ED7995D43FDA37CCB55417976D1" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>a description of the energy infrastructure projects the United States has identified for such assistance; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph changed="added" id="H5599ECCE4AAB4CB5A9188DA8411BBFE7" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><chapeau>for each such project—</chapeau>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H709CFDD6C809486BAF50F83B8EBBB991" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>a description of the role of the United States in the project, including in early-stage project support and late-stage project support;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="H79A76E6FDA3A4F77B74D2734D90CEDEE" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the amount and form of any debt financing and insurance provided by the United States Government for the project;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HA687FE289B2641D19559A98B6022F9B3" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>the amount and form of any early-stage project support; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" id="HFA4AE315F6CF465D8229D6740B06C872" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>an update on the progress made on the project as of the date of the report.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></section></title></division>
