<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt4/s1041/a" id="H6E3D6425851244A39C69BE9D97B26FE4" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Minimum Information Required for Removal Under Cross-check</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 8(c)(2) of the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20507/c/2">52 U.S.C. 20507(c)(2)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt4/s1041/a/1" id="H94CC8C721F6044CE9304CBF896A5CDA2" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="redesignate">redesignating</amendingAction> subparagraph (B) as subparagraph (D); and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt4/s1041/a/2" id="H14747F04764D4400A56832F5B1BA3AA0" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> after subparagraph (A) the following new subparagraphs:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H9DC1896A5E7A404F8963C182DE5BEF01" styleType="traditional">
<subparagraph id="HB5B9220465554F97934A47046A39C0DC" class="indent0"><num value="B">“(B) </num><chapeau>To the extent that the program carried out by a State under subparagraph (A) to systematically remove the names of ineligible voters from the official lists of eligible voters uses information obtained in an interstate cross-check, in addition to any other conditions imposed under this Act on the authority of the State to remove the name of the voter from such a list, the State may not remove the name of the voter from such a list unless—</chapeau>
<clause id="H15774DE914CC4FB2AD102D1E3A98A262" class="indent1"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the State obtained the voter’s full name (including the voter’s middle name, if any) and date of birth, and the last 4 digits of the voter’s social security number, in the interstate cross-check; or</content></clause>
<clause id="HAC3C90B314164901B303F11FC04B9F67" class="indent1"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>the State obtained documentation from the ERIC system that the voter is no longer a resident of the State.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H1FF2B323347A4F6EB6E8BA9921CC608D" class="indent0"><num value="C">“(C) </num><chapeau>In this paragraph—</chapeau>
<clause role="definitions" id="HAE4A499D21B949ADBFE6D7BDD1B37DAD" class="indent1"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the term ‘<term>interstate cross-check</term>’ means the transmission of information from an election official in one State to an election official of another State; and</content></clause>
<clause role="definitions" id="H08AE3C45B26447B1AA1B8734924BBC41" class="indent1"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>the term ‘<term>ERIC system</term>’ means the system operated by the Electronic Registration Information Center to share voter registration information and voter identification information among participating States.”</content></clause></subparagraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt4/s1041/b" id="H5664EBA58E0B4919922D44F75D929DEA" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requiring Completion of Cross-checks Not Later Than 6 Months Prior to Election</inline>.—</heading><content>Subparagraph (A) of section 8(c)(2) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20507/c/2">52 U.S.C. 20507(c)(2)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>not later than 90 days</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> the following: “<quotedText>not later than 90 days (or, in the case of a program in which the State uses interstate cross-checks, not later than 6 months)</quotedText>”.</content></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt4/s1041/c" id="H7A2E89967CB240519878811C809F95BA" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Conforming Amendment</inline>.—</heading><content>Subparagraph (D) of section 8(c)(2) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20507/c/2">52 U.S.C. 20507(c)(2)</ref>), as redesignated by subsection (a)(1), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>Subparagraph (A)</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>This paragraph</quotedText>”.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt4/s1041/d" id="HAB7B08A3AD0F4D6AAA5FFBF767F0F292" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective Date</inline>.—</heading><content>The amendments made by this Act shall apply with respect to elections held on or after the expiration of the 6-month period which begins on the date of the enactment of this Act.</content></subsection></section></part><part identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt5" id="H608A943B40A7495B83A4ED81DB28199B"><num value="5">PART 5—</num><heading>OTHER INITIATIVES TO PROMOTE VOTER REGISTRATION</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt5/s1051" id="H555811141D57472B936B8B683BBA788E"><num value="1051">SEC. 1051. </num><heading>ANNUAL REPORTS ON VOTER REGISTRATION STATISTICS.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt5/s1051/a" id="H99DB8D848F8B4FE4AE0DC7F0BDC6BD02" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Annual Report</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 90 days after the end of each year, each State shall submit to the Election Assistance Commission and Congress a report containing the following categories of information for the year:</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt5/s1051/a/1" id="H3190DBCD3716483B9C782BD2D689073B" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>The number of individuals who were registered under part 2.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt5/s1051/a/2" id="H388DE1893107407B8DC2B7188D499F2E" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>The number of voter registration application forms completed by individuals that were transmitted by motor vehicle authorities in the State (pursuant to section 5(d) of the National Voter Registration Act of 1993) and voter registration agencies in the State (as designated under section 7 of such Act) to the chief State election official of the State, broken down by each such authority and agency.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt5/s1051/a/3" id="H90C6E6E503DE4B3FA2BCB1ACB1C09047" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>The number of such individuals whose voter registration application forms were accepted and who were registered to vote in the State and the number of such individuals whose forms were rejected and who were not registered to vote in the State, broken down by each such authority and agency.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt5/s1051/a/4" id="H58FFA9246A6642CA8E01CC7521D807AD" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>The number of change of address forms and other forms of information indicating that an individual’s identifying information has been changed that were transmitted by such motor vehicle authorities and voter registration agencies to the chief State election official of the State, broken down by each such authority and agency and the type of form transmitted.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt5/s1051/a/5" id="HDC2FAEAAF14E4328BBC43D662A8B82CC" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>The number of individuals on the Statewide computerized voter registration list (as established and maintained under section 303 of the Help America Vote Act of 2002) whose voter registration information was revised by the chief State election official as a result of the forms transmitted to the official by such motor vehicle authorities and voter registration agencies (as described in paragraph (3)), broken down by each such authority and agency and the type of form transmitted.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt5/s1051/a/6" id="H6D143F988B4049508F63C8B3233ABD40" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>The number of individuals who requested the chief State election official to revise voter registration information on such list, and the number of individuals whose information was revised as a result of such a request.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt5/s1051/b" id="HA274B57CC9CE4A529D7D2E4F24BCFAA8" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Breakdown of Information by Race and Ethnicity of Individuals</inline>.—</heading><content>In preparing the report under this section, the State shall, for each category of information described in subsection (a), include a breakdown by race and ethnicity of the individuals whose information is included in the category, to the extent that information on the race and ethnicity of such individuals is available to the State.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt5/s1051/c" id="HD6DFBAB430024C7F81C06B1DDA03A892" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Confidentiality of Information</inline>.—</heading><content>In preparing and submitting a report under this section, the chief State election official shall ensure that no information regarding the identification of any individual is revealed.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt5/s1051/d" id="H929DB55DD2D74511AB6A00F88DB8A2CC" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">State Defined</inline>.—</heading><content>In this section, a “State” includes the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the United States Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, but does not include any State in which, under a State law in effect continuously on and after the date of the enactment of this Act, there is no voter registration requirement for individuals in the State with respect to elections for Federal office.</content></subsection></section></part><part identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stA/pt6" id="H880FEC5DF1E64329A4D64116EC1DF22E"><num value="6">PART 6—</num><heading>AVAILABILITY OF HAVA REQUIREMENTS PAYMENTS</heading>

For purposes of this subsection, the term “<term>State</term>” includes the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, Guam, American Samoa, the United States Virgin Islands, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.</content></subsection>

<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stB" id="HE6A0788151AD4089A8FAC09ABB8FB154"><num value="B">Subtitle B—</num><heading>Access to Voting for Individuals With Disabilities</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stB/s1101" id="HCE2747AFBAB54D1DBD1E8DED3BC09CC8"><num value="1101">SEC. 1101. </num><heading>REQUIREMENTS FOR STATES TO PROMOTE ACCESS TO VOTER REGISTRATION AND VOTING FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH DISABILITIES.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stB/s1101/a" id="H9F8D8CECEC224397837A489AD1977384" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requirements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Subtitle A of title III of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21081/etseq">52 U.S.C. 21081 et seq.</ref>), as amended by section 1031(a), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stB/s1101/a/1" id="HB62493FC757142CD9372F51203047778" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="redesignate">redesignating</amendingAction> sections 305 and 306 as sections 306 and 307; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stB/s1101/a/2" id="H7B54BB4D25674233A478407C0280B761" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> after section 304 the following new section:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H0F09690B6F7549439124B0EA18C1D57E" styleType="OLC">
<section id="H6D6C04C479E74BD687CFD3AF62A7A01D"><num value="305">“SEC. 305. </num><heading>ACCESS TO VOTER REGISTRATION AND VOTING FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH DISABILITIES.</heading>
<subsection id="HCC90428BDA11435588716834E393F45F" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Treatment of Applications and Ballots</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Each State shall—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HBBB733D334984F368926F05E2A4706EF" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>permit individuals with disabilities to use absentee registration procedures and to vote by absentee ballot in elections for Federal office;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6BE62BAC577147938B7F31AE71D0D988" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>accept and process, with respect to any election for Federal office, any otherwise valid voter registration application and absentee ballot application from an individual with a disability if the application is received by the appropriate State election official within the deadline for the election which is applicable under Federal law;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HEC334FBBBE444B848DB21E2181ED2ABA" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><chapeau>in addition to any other method of registering to vote or applying for an absentee ballot in the State, establish procedures—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H59CDF5C25E3D4E4DA7E8D8887005E88C" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>for individuals with disabilities to request by mail and electronically voter registration applications and absentee ballot applications with respect to elections for Federal office in accordance with subsection (c);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HE232984C1C6B4173A9AACA8939613777" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>for States to send by mail and electronically (in accordance with the preferred method of transmission designated by the individual under subparagraph (C)) voter registration applications and absentee ballot applications requested under subparagraph (A) in accordance with subsection (c); and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H412CCD47A6BB4FCFBBB766CDC41B0AEF" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>by which such an individual can designate whether the individual prefers that such voter registration application or absentee ballot application be transmitted by mail or electronically;</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6734FE0A05404B368C34CA447AF9D314" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><content>in addition to any other method of transmitting blank absentee ballots in the State, establish procedures for transmitting by mail and electronically blank absentee ballots to individuals with disabilities with respect to elections for Federal office in accordance with subsection (d);</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H917ED2749B0C40A9B931982B05DE05A8" class="indent1"><num value="5">“(5) </num><chapeau>transmit a validly requested absentee ballot to an individual with a disability—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H7D5A6D6EBFAE4CB995DBC724484BD20A" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>except as provided in subsection (e), in the case in which the request is received at least 45 days before an election for Federal office, not later than 45 days before the election; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H0297AA4A8F92458B9E9371E43090CBB9" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><chapeau>in the case in which the request is received less than 45 days before an election for Federal office—</chapeau>
<clause id="H3EEA440DE13946EDA150AA935D939808" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>in accordance with State law; and</content></clause>
<clause id="HCD52A3BE0612454FAC3FE4A277361373" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>if practicable and as determined appropriate by the State, in a manner that expedites the transmission of such absentee ballot; and</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4A5788F8A6CD4825B8430F5624524DCE" class="indent1"><num value="6">“(6) </num><content>if the State declares or otherwise holds a runoff election for Federal office, establish a written plan that provides absentee ballots are made available to individuals with disabilities in a manner that gives them sufficient time to vote in the runoff election.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HF81C4901F1174C1FB46AE57B59A15C71" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Designation of Single State Office To Provide Information on Registration and Absentee Ballot Procedures for All Disabled Voters in State</inline>.—</heading><content>Each State shall designate a single office which shall be responsible for providing information regarding voter registration procedures and absentee ballot procedures to be used by individuals with disabilities with respect to elections for Federal office to all individuals with disabilities who wish to register to vote or vote in any jurisdiction in the State.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HA6F0140FFBB64D7CA3411C236C7F2793" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Designation of Means of Electronic Communication for Individuals With Disabilities To Request and for States To Send Voter Registration Applications and Absentee Ballot Applications, and for Other Purposes Related to Voting Information</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H4328569F26E2457296E04762D60F2921" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Each State shall, in addition to the designation of a single State office under subsection (b), designate not less than 1 means of electronic communication—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H8A8349272F2C4A6FBB130C1B58D36081" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>for use by individuals with disabilities who wish to register to vote or vote in any jurisdiction in the State to request voter registration applications and absentee ballot applications under subsection (a)(3);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H65E34761D6F7484FAEBFB61469467056" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>for use by States to send voter registration applications and absentee ballot applications requested under such subsection; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H6703B2F35DE8400C8501605B0EFAAA9E" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>for the purpose of providing related voting, balloting, and election information to individuals with disabilities.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF844128BCF7D436494518D6D7E237229" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Clarification regarding provision of multiple means of electronic communication</inline>.—</heading><content>A State may, in addition to the means of electronic communication so designated, provide multiple means of electronic communication to individuals with disabilities, including a means of electronic communication for the appropriate jurisdiction of the State.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H023B00685D1545A092AC88B36821ADF5" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Inclusion of designated means of electronic communication with informational and instructional materials that accompany balloting materials</inline>.—</heading><content>Each State shall include a means of electronic communication so designated with all informational and instructional materials that accompany balloting materials sent by the State to individuals with disabilities.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE72CCB9F280347E488F78AA468422156" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Transmission if no preference indicated</inline>.—</heading><content>In the case where an individual with a disability does not designate a preference under subsection (a)(3)(C), the State shall transmit the voter registration application or absentee ballot application by any delivery method allowable in accordance with applicable State law, or if there is no applicable State law, by mail.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HEFA4020421004874AF6D9EB978AA51AD" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Transmission of Blank Absentee Ballots by Mail and Electronically</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H4EB1581C34D74EC592D9A2690B8E456B" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Each State shall establish procedures—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H63363F15B0C8454FA695681D0B7F2F8A" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>to securely transmit blank absentee ballots by mail and electronically (in accordance with the preferred method of transmission designated by the individual with a disability under subparagraph (B)) to individuals with disabilities for an election for Federal office; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD7A1351483C4430187CE25D60F7FB0A5" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>by which the individual with a disability can designate whether the individual prefers that such blank absentee ballot be transmitted by mail or electronically.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H2BCC61E35A734481A297D116A597C19C" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Transmission if no preference indicated</inline>.—</heading><content>In the case where an individual with a disability does not designate a preference under paragraph (1)(B), the State shall transmit the ballot by any delivery method allowable in accordance with applicable State law, or if there is no applicable State law, by mail.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H724CC903444140CEB9D701D628EF16F9" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Application of methods to track delivery to and return of ballot by individual requesting ballot</inline>.—</heading><content>Under the procedures established under paragraph (1), the State shall apply such methods as the State considers appropriate, such as assigning a unique identifier to the ballot, to ensure that if an individual with a disability requests the State to transmit a blank absentee ballot to the individual in accordance with this subsection, the voted absentee ballot which is returned by the individual is the same blank absentee ballot which the State transmitted to the individual.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HD7954B7F0A8347BB9D0EE1D3DACA0340" class="indent0"><num value="e">“(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Hardship Exemption</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HE6982E198BE443AF935EB1D0D3CD7400" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>If the chief State election official determines that the State is unable to meet the requirement under subsection (a)(5)(A) with respect to an election for Federal office due to an undue hardship described in paragraph (2)(B), the chief State election official shall request that the Attorney General grant a waiver to the State of the application of such subsection. Such request shall include—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HDC6601A20B34479EA2EDB263F6A26B60" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>a recognition that the purpose of such subsection is to individuals with disabilities enough time to vote in an election for Federal office;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H3ABB890621F94076BEDFA952CCB6DE38" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>an explanation of the hardship that indicates why the State is unable to transmit such individuals an absentee ballot in accordance with such subsection;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HB15070D6D6224F77A2F69D1B18F1BEBF" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>the number of days prior to the election for Federal office that the State requires absentee ballots be transmitted to such individuals; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HB12DF61284004D71B8F6524C2BB2F470" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><chapeau>a comprehensive plan to ensure that such individuals are able to receive absentee ballots which they have requested and submit marked absentee ballots to the appropriate State election official in time to have that ballot counted in the election for Federal office, which includes—</chapeau>
<clause id="HC48896E5820D43C09A3C0963A7A33285" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the steps the State will undertake to ensure that such individuals have time to receive, mark, and submit their ballots in time to have those ballots counted in the election;</content></clause>
<clause id="H397BE0639BB0408890ACD207C6F51030" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>why the plan provides such individuals sufficient time to vote as a substitute for the requirements under such subsection; and</content></clause>
<clause id="HB400AA03AB09497BB016A4AE60FDED9D" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>the underlying factual information which explains how the plan provides such sufficient time to vote as a substitute for such requirements.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB65F05B1B765453E93E93C42C1F31505" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Approval of waiver request</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Attorney General shall approve a waiver request under paragraph (1) if the Attorney General determines each of the following requirements are met:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HE052D0EF790D43EE877CB3210307ACF2" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>The comprehensive plan under subparagraph (D) of such paragraph provides individuals with disabilities sufficient time to receive absentee ballots they have requested and submit marked absentee ballots to the appropriate State election official in time to have that ballot counted in the election for Federal office.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HDEB742B36D6147B799E6011985DEDEDB" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><chapeau>One or more of the following issues creates an undue hardship for the State:</chapeau>
<clause id="H5227657C1CD443308F343EA36FDE3669" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>The State’s primary election date prohibits the State from complying with subsection (a)(5)(A).</content></clause>
<clause id="H9F742A05782A497BA2025714021D1614" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>The State has suffered a delay in generating ballots due to a legal contest.</content></clause>
<clause id="H5DA9E2BF06CA49BE9EC008A3C898B22A" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>The State Constitution prohibits the State from complying with such subsection.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H09387DD8A73F427981DCED5820DAD8FD" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Timing of waiver</inline>.—</heading>

<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stF/s1501" id="HC8542B11B82F402489AE3FD4BC4E2D6C"><num value="1501">SEC. 1501. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This subtitle may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="subtitle">Voter Confidence and Increased Accessibility Act of 2019</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stF/s1502" id="HA7654DB6A0B34CAA9F83DAB379D417B3"><num value="1502">SEC. 1502. </num><heading>PAPER BALLOT AND MANUAL COUNTING REQUIREMENTS.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stF/s1502/a" id="H9789A73A8E9D473B96C3C0E6BD9430B9" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 301(a)(2) of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21081/a/2">52 U.S.C. 21081(a)(2)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> to read as follows:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HAC6347FAB03B4AEA9AEFADD1FE10DFA1" styleType="OLC">
<paragraph id="H2AD8E19ACA0D47A3B6618B1674545678" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Paper ballot requirement</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H7F51773972B340A3A66BA519BCC03C39" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Voter-verified paper ballots</inline>.—</heading>
<clause id="H54AF6BA6C90B4EADBC3FF690881AA888" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Paper ballot requirement</inline>.—</heading><subclause role="definitions" id="H89B3E6FAA8B14430AE5489B13D63657F" class="inline"><num value="I">(I) </num><content>The voting system shall require the use of an individual, durable, voter-verified paper ballot of the voter’s vote that shall be marked and made available for inspection and verification by the voter before the voter’s vote is cast and counted, and which shall be counted by hand or read by an optical character recognition device or other counting device. For purposes of this subclause, the term ‘<term>individual, durable, voter-verified paper ballot</term>’ means a paper ballot marked by the voter by hand or a paper ballot marked through the use of a nontabulating ballot marking device or system, so long as the voter shall have the option to mark his or her ballot by hand.</content></subclause>
<subclause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H249E4CE0190C49229E43F467FA3E9100" class="indent3"><num value="II">“(II) </num><content>The voting system shall provide the voter with an opportunity to correct any error on the paper ballot before the permanent voter-verified paper ballot is preserved in accordance with clause (ii).</content></subclause>
<subclause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H56D4B7F83058422796720377029E571D" class="indent3"><num value="III">“(III) </num><content>The voting system shall not preserve the voter-verified paper ballots in any manner that makes it possible, at any time after the ballot has been cast, to associate a voter with the record of the voter’s vote without the voter’s consent.</content></subclause></clause>
<clause id="H5BD46C1985A8447DA6B05FFFAAF8DA4E" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Preservation as official record</inline>.—</heading><content>The individual, durable, voter-verified paper ballot used in accordance with clause (i) shall constitute the official ballot and shall be preserved and used as the official ballot for purposes of any recount or audit conducted with respect to any election for Federal office in which the voting system is used.</content></clause>
<clause id="HCD61C14BC45B4CFBAC9A83715178DC71" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Manual counting requirements for recounts and audits</inline>.—</heading><subclause id="H2B49F61858944E339852A1E7A6884A41" class="inline"><num value="I">(I) </num><content>Each paper ballot used pursuant to clause (i) shall be suitable for a manual audit, and shall be counted by hand in any recount or audit conducted with respect to any election for Federal office.</content></subclause>
<subclause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H4480F55E0839451E847BEC96CFBB77D6" class="indent3"><num value="II">“(II) </num><content>In the event of any inconsistencies or irregularities between any electronic vote tallies and the vote tallies determined by counting by hand the individual, durable, voter-verified paper ballots used pursuant to clause (i), and subject to subparagraph (B), the individual, durable, voter-verified paper ballots shall be the true and correct record of the votes cast.</content></subclause></clause>
<clause id="H9930D91E7D0F43799C2AEFDAD743E888" class="indent3"><num value="iv">“(iv) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Application to all ballots</inline>.—</heading><content>The requirements of this subparagraph shall apply to all ballots cast in elections for Federal office, including ballots cast by absent uniformed services voters and overseas voters under the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act and other absentee voters.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H383F5FA88B5441C78F52A1361F7F9434" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Special rule for treatment of disputes when paper ballots have been shown to be compromised</inline>.—</heading>
<clause id="HCCAC2D431E6C436A8C7F8972C5B98B2E" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In the event that—</chapeau>
<subclause id="HB9D5B50A421345D8A6CB0FA0D7033BA9" class="indent4"><num value="I">“(I) </num><content>there is any inconsistency between any electronic vote tallies and the vote tallies determined by counting by hand the individual, durable, voter-verified paper ballots used pursuant to subparagraph (A)(i) with respect to any election for Federal office; and</content></subclause>
<subclause id="H7A3A31E968794F64AC746967CC36C5BA" class="indent4"><num value="II">“(II) </num><content>it is demonstrated by clear and convincing evidence (as determined in accordance with the applicable standards in the jurisdiction involved) in any recount, audit, or contest of the result of the election that the paper ballots have been compromised (by damage or mischief or otherwise) and that a sufficient number of the ballots have been so compromised that the result of the election could be changed,</content></subclause>
<continuation class="indent0" role="clause">the determination of the appropriate remedy with respect to the election shall be made in accordance with applicable State law, except that the electronic tally shall not be used as the exclusive basis for determining the official certified result.</continuation></clause>
<clause id="H73A7489F111A4166A4AC11CCBA0BCBAF" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Rule for consideration of ballots associated with each voting machine</inline>.—</heading><content>For purposes of clause (i), only the paper ballots deemed compromised, if any, shall be considered in the calculation of whether or not the result of the election could be changed due to the compromised paper ballots.”</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>

<paragraph id="H69AAB94D42584B91A22DD0C7E40D6893" class="indent1"><num value="7">“(7) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Durability and readability requirements for ballots</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="HAC236F6771084B7D944213C7F2337C19" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Durability requirements for paper ballots</inline>.—</heading>
<clause id="H1DF89118D4974E9A9707F1CC59E7302B" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>All voter-verified paper ballots required to be used under this Act shall be marked or printed on durable paper.</content></clause>
<clause id="HDAC21488553640DEBDA36B00441EC727" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definition</inline>.—</heading><content>For purposes of this Act, paper is ‘durable’ if it is capable of withstanding multiple counts and recounts by hand without compromising the fundamental integrity of the ballots, and capable of retaining the information marked or printed on them for the full duration of a retention and preservation period of 22 months.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H5C39276CF66941D883C15655704C029C" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Readability requirements for paper ballots marked by ballot marking device</inline>.—</heading><content>All voter-verified paper ballots completed by the voter through the use of a ballot marking device shall be clearly readable by the voter without assistance (other than eyeglasses or other personal vision enhancing devices) and by an optical character recognition device or other device equipped for individuals with disabilities.”</content></subparagraph></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></section>

<clause id="H468204E695B64B2F8454444AE6DEAFB2" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Mandatory availability of paper ballots at polling places using grandfathered printers and systems</inline>.—</heading>
<subclause id="HE7607866AF5745CBA16ADCD37B89B1AF" class="indent4"><num value="I">“(I) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requiring ballots to be offered and provided</inline>.—</heading><content>The appropriate election official at each polling place that uses a printer or system described in clause (ii)(I) for the administration of elections for Federal office shall offer each individual who is eligible to cast a vote in the election at the polling place the opportunity to cast the vote using a blank pre-printed paper ballot which the individual may mark by hand and which is not produced by the direct recording electronic voting machine or other such system. The official shall provide the individual with the ballot and the supplies necessary to mark the ballot, and shall ensure (to the greatest extent practicable) that the waiting period for the individual to cast a vote is the lesser of 30 minutes or the average waiting period for an individual who does not agree to cast the vote using such a paper ballot under this clause.</content></subclause>
<subclause id="HC951348895E74359BB1DFF1E33989BBA" class="indent4"><num value="II">“(II) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Treatment of ballot</inline>.—</heading><content>Any paper ballot which is cast by an individual under this clause shall be counted and otherwise treated as a regular ballot for all purposes (including by incorporating it into the final unofficial vote count (as defined by the State) for the precinct) and not as a provisional ballot, unless the individual casting the ballot would have otherwise been required to cast a provisional ballot.</content></subclause>
<subclause id="HBDEFF1A1511641B89E70A3D51AB39D02" class="indent4"><num value="III">“(III) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Posting of notice</inline>.—</heading><content>The appropriate election official shall ensure there is prominently displayed at each polling place a notice that describes the obligation of the official to offer individuals the opportunity to cast votes using a pre-printed blank paper ballot.</content></subclause>

<subsection id="H17ED786AA8B1474E80A106F2C94F467E" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Statewide Counting of Provisional Ballots</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H464B97C741F04B28833F8CB87E42EC79" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>For purposes of subsection (a)(4), notwithstanding the precinct or polling place at which a provisional ballot is cast within the State, the appropriate election official shall count each vote on such ballot for each election in which the individual who cast such ballot is eligible to vote.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9569F1F7DC6648B383ED8562DDAAFD99" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective date</inline>.—</heading><content>This subsection shall apply with respect to elections held on or after January 1, 2020.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H7153D4AB89E74AC38E3656F35789B321" class="indent0"><num value="e">“(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Uniform and Nondiscriminatory Standards</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H2F494A812DB847E78DAD8AFBC50D62B8" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Consistent with the requirements of this section, each State shall establish uniform and nondiscriminatory standards for the issuance, handling, and counting of provisional ballots.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HAC33175EE8004C9ABBDA52B4278C404E" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective date</inline>.—</heading><content>This subsection shall apply with respect to elections held on or after January 1, 2020.”</content></paragraph></subsection></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph></subsection>

<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stH/s1611" id="HDF5D1D039D52449A87C72F7ADF1C39BA"><num value="1611">SEC. 1611. </num><heading>EARLY VOTING.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stH/s1611/a" id="H8FDE0C96F115497DBA5AAD7E9B53C480" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requirements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Subtitle A of title III of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21081/etseq">52 U.S.C. 21081 et seq.</ref>), as amended by section 1031(a) and section 1101(a), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stH/s1611/a/1" id="HBDF226B845A14CAC98CA0EC2A3512BBC" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="redesignate">redesignating</amendingAction> sections 306 and 307 as sections 307 and 308; and</content></paragraph>

<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HBFE6FB6B14E04088AF454CC4E3F93F82" styleType="OLC">
<section id="HE03F8D26F2C242918714E60423D5D89A"><num value="306">“SEC. 306. </num><heading>EARLY VOTING.</heading>
<subsection id="HB03F87F2B13A4BBD886FB59AB3401F07" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requiring Voting Prior to Date of Election</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H3D473450BB5C42E4BE5F066A2A4F1B86" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Each State shall allow individuals to vote in an election for Federal office during an early voting period which occurs prior to the date of the election, in the same manner as voting is allowed on such date.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB789FF0BEE7E43709D7AA3E66F468583" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Length of period</inline>.—</heading><content>The early voting period required under this subsection with respect to an election shall consist of a period of consecutive days (including weekends) which begins on the 15th day before the date of the election (or, at the option of the State, on a day prior to the 15th day before the date of the election) and ends on the date of the election.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HA18E0D41ACEA480A9744790B8B045CA0" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Minimum Early Voting Requirements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Each polling place which allows voting during an early voting period under subsection (a) shall—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HEF1A655DF68A4E0CA9DD15943F354CF7" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>allow such voting for no less than 4 hours on each day, except that the polling place may allow such voting for fewer than 4 hours on Sundays; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3EDEE942C14548B4A587453B8B80BAC1" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>have uniform hours each day for which such voting occurs.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H98827D895A324E85AD0F0A4F636508F4" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Location of Polling Places Near Public Transportation</inline>.—</heading><content>To the greatest extent practicable, a State shall ensure that each polling place which allows voting during an early voting period under subsection (a) is located within walking distance of a stop on a public transportation route.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HC5321F0A257F47C0988BB1FC41414EE0" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Standards</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H7E56E0177F1B4F4D9F16261B1201DA07" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>The Commission shall issue standards for the administration of voting prior to the day scheduled for a Federal election. Such standards shall include the nondiscriminatory geographic placement of polling places at which such voting occurs.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF9F32E7874D64D81A2DC51A0FE126B23" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Deviation</inline>.—</heading><content>The standards described in paragraph (1) shall permit States, upon providing adequate public notice, to deviate from any requirement in the case of unforeseen circumstances such as a natural disaster, terrorist attack, or a change in voter turnout.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HA1290CB93FB1460FB43D6D5FE91D9FA5" class="indent0"><num value="e">“(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective Date</inline>.—</heading><content>This section shall apply with respect to elections held on or after January 1, 2020.”</content></subsection></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stH/s1611/b" id="H51A051466801447CA6091661BB75A73B" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Conforming Amendment Relating to Issuance of Voluntary Guidance by Election Assistance Commission</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 311(b) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21101/b">52 U.S.C. 21101(b)</ref>), as amended by section 1101(b), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stH/s1611/b/1" id="HB6E6156A1F2A474C8738C8A4EE99E150" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>and</quotedText>” at the end of paragraph (3);</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stH/s1611/b/2" id="H374D3D359DA944C280B58B0C8EBCFEA7" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> the period at the end of paragraph (4) and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>; and</quotedText>”; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stH/s1611/b/3" id="H2FD5A7BB8F984D0BAEF1657BBCEA87AB" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new paragraph:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HDDB7327A453C401A8F9DFAB649E7F667" styleType="OLC">
<paragraph id="HC2A277675D0D4D04930C4837AC6E92F8" class="indent1"><num value="5">“(5) </num><content>in the case of the recommendations with respect to section 306, June 30, 2020.”</content></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stH/s1611/c" id="HD9DB3E0AE2CF4649A6C71DE607438C25" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Clerical Amendment</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The table of contents of such Act, as amended by section 1031(c) and section 1101(d), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stH/s1611/c/1" id="H7430EC5BC05646738712DC13AC8B314C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="redesignate">redesignating</amendingAction> the items relating to sections 306 and 307 as relating to sections 307 and 308; and</content></paragraph>

<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI" id="HDAB0724110094D808D2D3484C75055F4"><num value="I">Subtitle I—</num><heading>Voting by Mail</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621" id="H6ABDA5F4AD794A1A81EE6E589D582209"><num value="1621">SEC. 1621. </num><heading>VOTING BY MAIL.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621/a" id="HF9FA0F3559964C80A4134DD8211244CC" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requirements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Subtitle A of title III of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21081/etseq">52 U.S.C. 21081 et seq.</ref>), as amended by section 1031(a), section 1101(a), and section 1611(a), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621/a/1" id="H72A97B6DFC3042CAAEE075A88BDF63B6" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="redesignate">redesignating</amendingAction> sections 307 and 308 as sections 308 and 309; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621/a/2" id="H0245E6BFA95F48EBA2C9EB3EA5C6C129" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> after section 306 the following new section:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H5EBFFE06DFEB4F3DA3274B9C23F31FB8" styleType="OLC">
<section id="HD05602A4558C48C2B6A68E2F071C8AC1"><num value="307">“SEC. 307. </num><heading>PROMOTING ABILITY OF VOTERS TO VOTE BY MAIL.</heading>
<subsection id="HA9955E82E02949768145D3FD2F71A124" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>If an individual in a State is eligible to cast a vote in an election for Federal office, the State may not impose any additional conditions or requirements on the eligibility of the individual to cast the vote in such election by absentee ballot by mail, except as required under subsection (b) and except to the extent that the State imposes a deadline for requesting the ballot and related voting materials from the appropriate State or local election official and for returning the ballot to the appropriate State or local election official.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H761520AF341540798407F69A12921CE5" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requiring Signature Verification</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H2221A318635242B88348144817BADC77" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requirement</inline>.—</heading><content>A State may not accept and process an absentee ballot submitted by any individual with respect to an election for Federal office unless the State verifies the identification of the individual by comparing the individual’s signature on the absentee ballot with the individual’s signature on the official list of registered voters in the State, in accordance with such procedures as the State may adopt (subject to the requirements of paragraph (2)).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD1EBDD50A68D48BCBAFE43FB7F5027FA" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Due process requirements</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H31F9B9B5C72948BCAD3DA26CD234F27D" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Notice and opportunity to cure discrepancy</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>If an individual submits an absentee ballot and the appropriate State or local election official determines that a discrepancy exists between the signature on such ballot and the signature of such individual on the official list of registered voters in the State, such election official, prior to making a final determination as to the validity of such ballot, shall make a good faith effort to immediately notify such individual by mail, telephone, and (if available) electronic mail that—</chapeau>
<clause id="H1E9C93AED57F4977AF499ACF82BA0DC4" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>a discrepancy exists between the signature on such ballot and the signature of such individual on the official list of registered voters in the State;</content></clause>
<clause id="HD44E6207631E4F8A929D26A1A5CDB39A" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>such individual may provide the official with information to cure such discrepancy, either in person, by telephone, or by electronic methods; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H3D95646621194CEDB8A286377106F31B" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>if such discrepancy is not cured prior to the expiration of the 7-day period which begins on the date of the election, such ballot will not be counted.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H49DD01076F9641858B647E74212A733B" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Other requirements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>An election official may not make a determination that a discrepancy exists between the signature on an absentee ballot and the signature of the individual who submits the ballot on the official list of registered voters in the State unless—</chapeau>
<clause id="H437F1F24CEED4AFEA1D84387CF8137A3" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>at least 2 election officials make the determination; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H28B5C498618A4605B629AEBE2FE5E4D8" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>each official who makes the determination has received training in procedures used to verify signatures.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HD533C341695F4EB6921E9F61301FC570" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Deadline for Providing Balloting Materials</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>If an individual requests to vote by absentee ballot in an election for Federal office, the appropriate State or local election official shall ensure that the ballot and relating voting materials are received by the individual—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H235F035326864956A74FDF9059097894" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>not later than 2 weeks before the date of the election; or</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4A7592E907C14C39A0F649B9F7DC8696" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>in the case of a State which imposes a deadline for requesting an absentee ballot and related voting materials which is less than 2 weeks before the date of the election, as expeditiously as possible.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H141D748A27B048DF8747EA8E83458DBB" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Accessibility for Individuals With Disabilities</inline>.—</heading><content>Consistent with section 305, the State shall ensure that all absentee ballots and related voting materials in elections for Federal office are accessible to individuals with disabilities in a manner that provides the same opportunity for access and participation (including with privacy and independence) as for other voters.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HE2438F86274A45919872D5D2028D66A7" class="indent0"><num value="e">“(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Uniform Deadline for Acceptance of Mailed Ballots</inline>.—</heading><content>If a ballot submitted by an individual by mail with respect to an election for Federal office in a State is postmarked on or before the date of the election, the State may not refuse to accept or process the ballot on the grounds that the individual did not meet a deadline for returning the ballot to the appropriate State or local election official.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HD3FCB14B904D4DA8A0679863C370F616" class="indent0"><num value="f">“(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">No Effect on Ballots Submitted by Absent Military and Overseas Voters</inline>.—</heading><content>Nothing in this section may be construed to affect the treatment of any ballot submitted by an individual who is entitled to vote by absentee ballot under the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20301/etseq">52 U.S.C. 20301 et seq.</ref>).</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H439245B6D85D456EABBDA62DAA2E91FA" class="indent0"><num value="g">“(g) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective Date</inline>.—</heading><content>This section shall apply with respect to elections held on or after January 1, 2020.”</content></subsection></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621/b" id="HA8F9330693634FB1878F4AC45396D98C" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Conforming Amendment Relating to Issuance of Voluntary Guidance by Election Assistance Commission</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 311(b) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21101/b">52 U.S.C. 21101(b)</ref>), as amended by section 1101(b) and section 1611(b), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621/b/1" id="H1869FC5E555E4072948B0E3A01AF585A" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>and</quotedText>” at the end of paragraph (4);</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621/b/2" id="HEC4DCC5924EC458C9219CB6A44817F72" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> the period at the end of paragraph (5) and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>; and</quotedText>”; and</content></paragraph>

<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H705081B32F5744B38311AC1A7B0B038B" styleType="OLC">
<paragraph id="H43BDFAA445C24193B2D3EE2662CA4186" class="indent1"><num value="6">“(6) </num><content>in the case of the recommendations with respect to section 307, June 30, 2020.”</content></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621/c" id="H9C7295D228624510A3327C5A8E4F463D" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Clerical Amendment</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The table of contents of such Act, as amended by section 1031(c), section 1101(d), and section 1611(c), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621/c/1" id="H86092AD2CE574CEC9CE8D7E506445EEC" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="redesignate">redesignating</amendingAction> the items relating to sections 307 and 308 as relating to sections 308 and 309; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621/c/2" id="H7EE2EFA7E03443FE9F42F5D98DF77C76" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> after the item relating to section 306 the following new item:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H02D3D4675A61466B80BB9F30372E3F2C" styleType="OLC">

<designator>“Sec. 307. </designator>
<label>Promoting ability of voters to vote by mail.”</label>
