<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621/d" id="H2C22E76D915448C794A5060DB4C26757" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Development of Biometric Verification</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621/d/1" id="HC36111565B5048F4839549A20DE149EF" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Development of standards</inline>.—</heading><content>The National Institute of Standards, in consultation with the Election Assistance Commission, shall develop standards for the use of biometric methods which could be used voluntarily in place of the signature verification requirements of section 307(b) of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (as added by subsection (a)) for purposes of verifying the identification of an individual voting by absentee ballot in elections for Federal office.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621/d/2" id="HBDFA6A2BD7E648978881AB3B40FEB1BA" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Public notice and comment</inline>.—</heading><content>The National Institute of Standards shall solicit comments from the public in the development of standards under paragraph (1).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stI/s1621/d/3" id="H97D335596D334DB7820AC8B5E26B6716" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Deadline</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the National Institute of Standards shall publish the standards developed under paragraph (1).</content></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ" id="H7D7FE6B248B84E82B0EB02A8C0098A9A"><num value="J">Subtitle J—</num><heading>Absent Uniformed Services Voters and Overseas Voters</heading>
<section role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1701" id="H403FAE50948B46D8BAF6F32137DB475D"><num value="1701">SEC. 1701. </num><heading>PRE-ELECTION REPORTS ON AVAILABILITY AND TRANSMISSION OF ABSENTEE BALLOTS.</heading><content>Section 102(c) of the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20302/c">52 U.S.C. 20302(c)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> to read as follows:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H72D2A7F44BA545D3A62BD1C64A4D82EB" styleType="OLC">
<subsection id="H9C6031F5F5FB45628BE905FF80F4B347" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reports on Availability, Transmission, and Receipt of Absentee Ballots</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H14053DE567714CB8950E7DEA8178EA54" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Pre-election report on absentee ballot availability</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 55 days before any regularly scheduled general election for Federal office, each State shall submit a report to the Attorney General, the Election Assistance Commission (hereafter in this subsection referred to as the ‘Commission’), and the Presidential Designee, and make that report publicly available that same day, certifying that absentee ballots for the election are or will be available for transmission to absent uniformed services voters and overseas voters by not later than 45 days before the election. The report shall be in a form prescribed jointly by the Attorney General and the Commission and shall require the State to certify specific information about ballot availability from each unit of local government which will administer the election.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF4FD1BCAF4E143DE8BC1DAD3C39D6567" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Pre-election report on absentee ballot transmission</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 43 days before any regularly scheduled general election for Federal office, each State shall submit a report to the Attorney General, the Commission, and the Presidential Designee, and make that report publicly available that same day, certifying whether all absentee ballots have been transmitted by not later than 45 days before the election to all qualified absent uniformed services and overseas voters whose requests were received at least 45 days before the election. The report shall be in a form prescribed jointly by the Attorney General and the Commission, and shall require the State to certify specific information about ballot transmission, including the total numbers of ballot requests received and ballots transmitted, from each unit of local government which will administer the election.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H39AEE6B7181C47E6879C01E93C366781" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Post-election report on number of absentee ballots transmitted and received</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 90 days after the date of each regularly scheduled general election for Federal office, each State and unit of local government which administered the election shall (through the State, in the case of a unit of local government) submit a report to the Attorney General, the Commission, and the Presidential Designee on the combined number of absentee ballots transmitted to absent uniformed services voters and overseas voters for the election and the combined number of such ballots which were returned by such voters and cast in the election, and shall make such report available to the general public that same day.”</content></paragraph></subsection></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1702" id="H84837E828E594EBC9E3253725A0A1F59"><num value="1702">SEC. 1702. </num><heading>ENFORCEMENT.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1702/a" id="HAE383D3E532F48C5B683B08C2B432732" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Availability of Civil Penalties and Private Rights of Action</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 105 of the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20307">52 U.S.C. 20307</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> to read as follows:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H28410819A1D447CF8ABD4B94273938E5" styleType="OLC">
<section id="HA9CBCA69192F41F1B15C708ED68FC41D"><num value="105">“SEC. 105. </num><heading>ENFORCEMENT.</heading>
<subsection id="H75B048894F1C4A8D8BD05855CB7CFC09" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Action by Attorney General</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HC5A5D1801F2A44FDBC3EFC906F8BE753" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>The Attorney General may bring civil action in an appropriate district court for such declaratory or injunctive relief as may be necessary to carry out this title.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6DF0628199A647A1AE02CDE70CE18597" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Penalty</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In a civil action brought under paragraph (1), if the court finds that the State violated any provision of this title, it may, to vindicate the public interest, assess a civil penalty against the State—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H1C7DA526DF714B2789800706A0913E5C" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>in an amount not to exceed $110,000 for each such violation, in the case of a first violation; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H3430E77E3A9E4DBFA221ED891AD35935" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>in an amount not to exceed $220,000 for each such violation, for any subsequent violation.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H4A7A0E0DB266482A8F0128C9595886D9" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report to congress</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than December 31 of each year, the Attorney General shall submit to Congress an annual report on any civil action brought under paragraph (1) during the preceding year.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H3951D9F000254799AF38354882F6A224" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Private Right of Action</inline>.—</heading><content>A person who is aggrieved by a State’s violation of this title may bring a civil action in an appropriate district court for such declaratory or injunctive relief as may be necessary to carry out this title.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H68DCCDB14C3E417D9AB5B51264F120D0" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">State as Only Necessary Defendant</inline>.—</heading><content>In any action brought under this section, the only necessary party defendant is the State, and it shall not be a defense to any such action that a local election official or a unit of local government is not named as a defendant, notwithstanding that a State has exercised the authority described in section 576 of the Military and Overseas Voter Empowerment Act to delegate to another jurisdiction in the State any duty or responsibility which is the subject of an action brought under this section.”</content></subsection></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1702/b" id="H5FE48DF412DE402189AE3F512A6E1ED9" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective Date</inline>.—</heading><content>The amendments made by this section shall apply with respect to violations alleged to have occurred on or after the date of the enactment of this Act.</content></subsection></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1703" id="H70601E53608C4DD7B1B03357BBE9CB7F"><num value="1703">SEC. 1703. </num><heading>REVISIONS TO 45-DAY ABSENTEE BALLOT TRANSMISSION RULE.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1703/a" id="HB9F972A7E2914718A43BCF0BFD22C8B1" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Repeal of Waiver Authority</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1703/a/1" id="H3E3B0A138A884DCD986AFD40D5AC7BE7" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 102 of the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20302">52 U.S.C. 20302</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> subsection (g).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1703/a/2" id="H510C1844FD3F4C5790DF15823399F2CA" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Conforming amendment</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 102(a)(8)(A) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20302/a/8/A">52 U.S.C. 20302(a)(8)(A)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>except as provided in subsection (g),</quotedText>”.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1703/b" id="H3E177608AD7D4E42A373088FEBE1B245" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requiring Use of Express Delivery in Case of Failure to Meet Requirement</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 102 of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20302">52 U.S.C. 20302</ref>), as amended by subsection (a), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> after subsection (f) the following new subsection:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H16DC7DCA7E9D471894318B87E8D18148" styleType="OLC">
<subsection id="H4A52DDED74434B6BB86CE95054CF2DCE" class="indent0"><num value="g">“(g) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requiring Use of Express Delivery in Case of Failure To Transmit Ballots Within Deadlines</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HF7C827F550E94F1C8BF36098D1AC0C91" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Transmission of ballot by express delivery</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>If a State fails to meet the requirement of subsection (a)(8)(A) to transmit a validly requested absentee ballot to an absent uniformed services voter or overseas voter not later than 45 days before the election (in the case in which the request is received at least 45 days before the election)—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H70A494834BD04F1FB4A44C947EDC31DB" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>the State shall transmit the ballot to the voter by express delivery; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HA43533AB4922455C8683B235CA632EBB" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>in the case of a voter who has designated that absentee ballots be transmitted electronically in accordance with subsection (f)(1), the State shall transmit the ballot to the voter electronically.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8370841E4FB14EB7854F70F78FE4CB5F" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Special rule for transmission fewer than 40 days before the election</inline>.—</heading><content>If, in carrying out paragraph (1), a State transmits an absentee ballot to an absent uniformed services voter or overseas voter fewer than 40 days before the election, the State shall enable the ballot to be returned by the voter by express delivery, except that in the case of an absentee ballot of an absent uniformed services voter for a regularly scheduled general election for Federal office, the State may satisfy the requirement of this paragraph by notifying the voter of the procedures for the collection and delivery of such ballots under section 103A.”</content></paragraph></subsection></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1703/c" id="H8958EDCBC83B46BFAAB0483E953FA918" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Clarification of Treatment of Weekends</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 102(a)(8)(A) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20302/a/8/A">52 U.S.C. 20302(a)(8)(A)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>the election;</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> the following: “<quotedText>the election (or, if the 45th day preceding the election is a weekend or legal public holiday, not later than the most recent weekday which precedes such 45th day and which is not a legal public holiday, but only if the request is received by at least such most recent weekday);</quotedText>”.</content></subsection></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1704" id="HA5A8E32C75424DCA98A5426B65B19E83"><num value="1704">SEC. 1704. </num><heading>USE OF SINGLE ABSENTEE BALLOT APPLICATION FOR SUBSEQUENT ELECTIONS.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1704/a" id="H57EB6ED5E45F460AA9AA0B2242D82BE9" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 104 of the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20306">52 U.S.C. 20306</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> to read as follows:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H11F8056634A04EDFA5DD9E899E229244" styleType="OLC">
<section id="HD09A76D13CFE4DDA891F6D119C0F9BCA"><num value="104">“SEC. 104. </num><heading>USE OF SINGLE APPLICATION FOR SUBSEQUENT ELECTIONS.</heading>
<subsection id="H5C36889A069147E1A43D1151DEE97D60" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>If a State accepts and processes an official post card form (prescribed under section 101) submitted by an absent uniformed services voter or overseas voter for simultaneous voter registration and absentee ballot application (in accordance with section 102(a)(4)) and the voter requests that the application be considered an application for an absentee ballot for each subsequent election for Federal office held in the State through the next regularly scheduled general election for Federal office (including any runoff elections which may occur as a result of the outcome of such general election), the State shall provide an absentee ballot to the voter for each such subsequent election.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HCF0D3C51E0094BAE9A7A466D09C0AE03" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exception for Voters Changing Registration</inline>.—</heading><content>Subsection (a) shall not apply with respect to a voter registered to vote in a State for any election held after the voter notifies the State that the voter no longer wishes to be registered to vote in the State or after the State determines that the voter has registered to vote in another State or is otherwise no longer eligible to vote in the State.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H05C11427A4E54869BFFE2297B1543592" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prohibition of Refusal of Application on Grounds of Early Submission</inline>.—</heading><content>A State may not refuse to accept or to process, with respect to any election for Federal office, any otherwise valid voter registration application or absentee ballot application (including the postcard form prescribed under section 101) submitted by an absent uniformed services voter or overseas voter on the grounds that the voter submitted the application before the first date on which the State otherwise accepts or processes such applications for that election which are submitted by absentee voters who are not members of the uniformed services or overseas citizens.”</content></subsection></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1704/b" id="HB1574771657A4EA3ADDE4293D456C807" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective Date</inline>.—</heading><content>The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply with respect to voter registration and absentee ballot applications which are submitted to a State or local election official on or after the date of the enactment of this Act.</content></subsection></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stJ/s1705" id="H0195CB52E4EB439083A36C9A3DDD64F1"><num value="1705">SEC. 1705. </num><heading>EFFECTIVE DATE.</heading><content class="block">The amendments made by this subtitle shall apply with respect to elections occurring on or after January 1, 2020.</content></section></subtitle>

<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1801" id="H755147672F43495DB187F9E19F49D2B2"><num value="1801">SEC. 1801. </num><heading>[RESERVED].</heading><content/></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802" id="HE206A14BF98443DB851D4EC2F45350E0"><num value="1802">SEC. 1802. </num><heading>GRANTS TO STATES FOR POLL WORKER RECRUITMENT AND TRAINING.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/a" id="H61DF4BDB2F1D49B783572D976AA55748" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Grants by Election Assistance Commission</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/a/1" id="H0BD094E41D684BFE9AAB764335B2002C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>The Election Assistance Commission (hereafter referred to as the “Commission”) shall make a grant to each eligible State for recruiting and training individuals to serve as poll workers on dates of elections for public office.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/a/2" id="H0FAA17D38C3D4F709124E96C3A1FF2C1" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Use of commission materials</inline>.—</heading><content>In carrying out activities with a grant provided under this section, the recipient of the grant shall use the manual prepared by the Commission on successful practices for poll worker recruiting, training and retention as an interactive training tool, and shall develop training programs with the participation and input of experts in adult learning.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/b" id="HE5770EBDEEDA4692A61B7C4383453EBD" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requirements for Eligibility</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/b/1" id="HBC536B60AA464BF5B474EE3739E709D2" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Application</inline>.—</heading><content>Each State that desires to receive a payment under this section shall submit an application for the payment to the Commission at such time and in such manner and containing such information as the Commission shall require.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/b/2" id="H110F4B7D044D4F889EC99EEF6AD356F0" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Contents of application</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Each application submitted under paragraph (1) shall—</chapeau>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/b/2/A" id="H0B8CC40E240D4F51B2E40BD63F7FEA05" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>describe the activities for which assistance under this section is sought;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/b/2/B" id="H0D40DEFD222D40F7BB24433D93C0D565" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>provide assurances that the funds provided under this section will be used to supplement and not supplant other funds used to carry out the activities;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/b/2/C" id="H26B2502138DD49F7BB678688008C931A" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>provide assurances that the State will furnish the Commission with information on the number of individuals who served as poll workers after recruitment and training with the funds provided under this section; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/b/2/D" id="H8C09C10404FD4F2D9CCEDB734F4C7BBA" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>provide such additional information and certifications as the Commission determines to be essential to ensure compliance with the requirements of this section.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/c" id="H46D78B0F0A9545DBBE2D501E0C99BC5B" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Amount of Grant</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/c/1" id="H7374F1D9955F49CCB3E5C52243253507" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The amount of a grant made to a State under this section shall be equal to the product of—</chapeau>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/c/1/A" id="HCF9556914EDC42369296EC8BEFDA1780" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the aggregate amount made available for grants to States under this section; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/c/1/B" id="H40C34717A341456E9A48D3A5FE3866A1" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the voting age population percentage for the State.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/c/2" id="H1484EE7B604249EE958FC8DEA82418A0" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Voting age population percentage defined</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In paragraph (1), the “voting age population percentage” for a State is the quotient of—</chapeau>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/c/2/A" id="H5120B07B74CB4957AD756A5653D9B953" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>the voting age population of the State (as determined on the basis of the most recent information available from the Bureau of the Census); and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/c/2/B" id="H06F74BC2F2CD40F49AD375B442EFA0A3" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>the total voting age population of all States (as determined on the basis of the most recent information available from the Bureau of the Census).</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/d" id="H681189E89C754A909840D981C40C2D7B" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reports to Congress</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/d/1" id="H7347DF8ED08C46499D4290E765CB76BE" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reports by recipients of grants</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 6 months after the date on which the final grant is made under this section, each recipient of a grant shall submit a report to the Commission on the activities conducted with the funds provided by the grant.</content></paragraph>

<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stK/s1802/e" id="HB70284A5E5C94A1ABBC52F7312EF62D1" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Funding</inline>.—</heading>

<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stL/s1811/a" id="H9239A075D5B842E6A9F6D75CCFF2EB14" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Complaints; Availability of Private Right of Action</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 401 of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21111">52 U.S.C. 21111</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stL/s1811/a/1" id="H14C64F7A28EB42419FCB2393553D2FC9" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>The Attorney General</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>(a) <headingText role="subsection" styleType="OLC" class="smallCaps">In General.—</headingText>The Attorney General</quotedText>”; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stL/s1811/a/2" id="H5A1541C44B26463CA9BC052A159A30D5" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new subsections:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HC483F25CD55D4C5FA8A7766794760433" styleType="OLC">
<subsection id="H697DA8BDC83842AFBC0AD6DA8AC7F645" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Filing of Complaints by Aggrieved Persons</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H7540EE02089C499F80CC6C58A2986B63" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>A person who is aggrieved by a violation of title III which has occurred, is occurring, or is about to occur may file a written, signed, notarized complaint with the Attorney General describing the violation and requesting the Attorney General to take appropriate action under this section. The Attorney General shall immediately provide a copy of a complaint filed under the previous sentence to the entity responsible for administering the State-based administrative complaint procedures described in section 402(a) for the State involved.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB39B3CB7938542179A4F31A144FC4E16" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Response by attorney general</inline>.—</heading><content>The Attorney General shall respond to each complaint filed under paragraph (1), in accordance with procedures established by the Attorney General that require responses and determinations to be made within the same (or shorter) deadlines which apply to a State under the State-based administrative complaint procedures described in section 402(a)(2). The Attorney General shall immediately provide a copy of the response made under the previous sentence to the entity responsible for administering the State-based administrative complaint procedures described in section 402(a) for the State involved.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H2DE6BE930F2141A8A98C2F71F9A42CA6" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Availability of Private Right of Action</inline>.—</heading><content>Any person who is authorized to file a complaint under subsection (b)(1) (including any individual who seeks to enforce the individual’s right to a voter-verified paper ballot, the right to have the voter-verified paper ballot counted in accordance with this Act, or any other right under title III) may file an action under section 1979 of the Revised Statutes of the United States (<ref href="/us/usc/t42/s1983">42 U.S.C. 1983</ref>) to enforce the uniform and nondiscriminatory election technology and administration requirements under subtitle A of title III.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H0EA1B08CE08F466D9788140C0DB77607" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">No Effect on State Procedures</inline>.—</heading><content>Nothing in this section may be construed to affect the availability of the State-based administrative complaint procedures required under section 402 to any person filing a complaint under this subsection.”</content></subsection></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stL/s1811/b" id="H9BFFD3EC71A140D888BC5423B07506B5" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective Date</inline>.—</heading><content>The amendments made by this section shall apply with respect to violations occurring with respect to elections for Federal office held in 2020 or any succeeding year.</content></subsection></section></subtitle>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stM" id="H47DAF37E07CC4231B76A0D567A5821E7"><num value="M">Subtitle M—</num><heading>Federal Election Integrity</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stM/s1821" id="H14E49AC589B84C3BBBF5D0D2980B751B"><num value="1821">SEC. 1821. </num><heading>PROHIBITION ON CAMPAIGN ACTIVITIES BY CHIEF STATE ELECTION ADMINISTRATION OFFICIALS.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stM/s1821/a" id="H111241E2B17643B79C51098132D48337" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Title III of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30101/etseq">52 U.S.C. 30101 et seq.</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> after section 319 the following new section:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H1567E60F21C549439CD2ED036C257A55" styleType="traditional">
<section id="HF04921BCF9924F27B32A9F8F994CFCA7"><heading><inline class="smallCaps">“campaign activities by chief state election administration officials</inline></heading><num value="319A"><inline class="smallCaps">“Sec. 319A. </inline></num><subsection id="H89BFE6FB614D404B99567C415580CC98" class="inline"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prohibition</inline>.—</heading><content>It shall be unlawful for a chief State election administration official to take an active part in political management or in a political campaign with respect to any election for Federal office over which such official has supervisory authority.</content></subsection>
<subsection role="definitions" changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H23EA4F8BC3C2498BACD010C2DEA47DA0" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Chief State Election Administration Official</inline>.—</heading><content>The term ‘<term>chief State election administration official</term>’ means the highest State official with responsibility for the administration of Federal elections under State law.</content></subsection>
<subsection role="definitions" changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H56E5D702A83141578053993D4FD41F07" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Active Part in Political Management or in a Political Campaign</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term ‘<term>active part in political management or in a political campaign</term>’ means—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H3174190E1AC048F89074E6248A824127" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>serving as a member of an authorized committee of a candidate for Federal office;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H054F9D5196574A53B668B73D79C86DE0" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>the use of official authority or influence for the purpose of interfering with or affecting the result of an election for Federal office;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H368E5711B19845DB96AD46E55AEB662B" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><content>the solicitation, acceptance, or receipt of a contribution from any person on behalf of a candidate for Federal office; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H558C20AF4BE04317ACBB8230BADA77DD" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><content>any other act which would be prohibited under paragraph (2) or (3) of <ref href="/us/usc/t5/s7323/b">section 7323(b) of title 5, United States Code</ref>, if taken by an individual to whom such paragraph applies (other than any prohibition on running for public office).</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HDBC27A78022C4D4BB29926B4C60AF70E" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exception in Case of Recusal From Administration of Elections Involving Official or Immediate Family Member</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HB956A082E53948899BC30240540898C4" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>This section does not apply to a chief State election administration official with respect to an election for Federal office in which the official or an immediate family member of the official is a candidate, but only if—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H97D1EAFF67A54C26A4E3B2B591997A9C" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>such official recuses himself or herself from all of the official’s responsibilities for the administration of such election; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HF12E063A1CE74DF8B9BC94B6510D4FEF" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>the official who assumes responsibility for supervising the administration of the election does not report directly to such official.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H9AB09D50F01540AE86B872C4EEEBACDB" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Immediate family member defined</inline>.—</heading><content>In paragraph (1), the term ‘<term>immediate family member</term>’ means, with respect to a candidate, a father, mother, son, daughter, brother, sister, husband, wife, father-in-law, or mother-in-law.”</content></paragraph></subsection></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stM/s1821/b" id="H342031F708134EE2948C0B1C918E1E14" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective Date</inline>.—</heading><content>The amendments made by subsection (a) shall apply with respect to elections for Federal office held after December 2019.</content></subsection></section></subtitle>

<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901" id="H7017B4835A9D4225B2A92572432A38B9"><num value="1901">SEC. 1901. </num><heading>TREATMENT OF INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/a" id="H5740842288FD41F198133C877012E0C7" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Treatment of Certain Institutions as Voter Registration Agencies Under National Voter Registration Act of 1993</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 7(a) of the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20506/a">52 U.S.C. 20506(a)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>

<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/a/1/A" id="HCAFBD1DEC5004C99BACE75FFECA71EB6" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>and</quotedText>” at the end of subparagraph (A);</content></subparagraph>

<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/b" id="HFBF199FECEDB42448B06E9BC029961C1" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Responsibilities of Institutions Under Higher Education Act of 1965</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/b/1" id="H537AD4E859EF4E76B3AC05832A2F94F1" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 487(a)(23) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (<ref href="/us/usc/t20/s1094/a/23">20 U.S.C. 1094(a)(23)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> to read as follows:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H91DDF1672C3740F7BE2BC5237814741D" styleType="traditional">
<paragraph id="H15B84AAF32264A8F838E08DF0AB452AF" class="indent1"><num value="23">“(23)</num><subparagraph id="H23691564C6A04320A19A8225F4547975" class="inline"><num value="A">(A)</num><clause id="H335F95B2509F4C1D890460F5900FF46D" class="inline"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>The institution will ensure that an appropriate staff person or office is designated publicly as a ‘Campus Vote Coordinator’ and will ensure that such person’s or office’s contact information is included on the institution’s website.</content></clause>
<clause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H854CD996413540CC840335B101D753A4" class="indent1"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><chapeau>Not fewer than twice during each calendar year (beginning with 2020), the Campus Vote Coordinator shall transmit electronically to each student enrolled in the institution (including students enrolled in distance education programs) a message containing the following information:</chapeau>
<subclause id="HFB32C262EBCA4E87B1BE7633161416E2" class="indent2"><num value="I">“(I) </num><content>Information on the location of polling places in the jurisdiction in which the institution is located, together with information on available methods of transportation to and from such polling places.</content></subclause>
<subclause id="HAD33617EDB8F485381418ABEA697A0F9" class="indent2"><num value="II">“(II) </num><content>A referral to a government-affiliated website or online platform which provides centralized voter registration information for all States, including access to applicable voter registration forms and information to assist individuals who are not registered to vote in registering to vote.</content></subclause>
<subclause id="HEFD594054F0042F8A8FBE00E2B1C7FCD" class="indent2"><num value="III">“(III) </num><content>Any additional voter registration and voting information the Coordinator considers appropriate, in consultation with the appropriate State election official.</content></subclause></clause>
<clause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H427B634F99B04F679D61918AB4222410" class="indent1"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>In addition to transmitting the message described in clause (ii) not fewer than twice during each calendar year, the Campus Vote Coordinator shall transmit the message under such clause not fewer than 30 days prior to the deadline for registering to vote for any election for Federal, State, or local office in the State.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H4CFC8D6A3D4549DA9F4A665E567966B1" class="indent1"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>If the institution in its normal course of operations requests each student registering for enrollment in a course of study, including students registering for enrollment in a program of distance education, to affirm whether or not the student is a United States citizen, the institution will comply with the applicable requirements for a contributing agency under the Automatic Voter Registration Act of 2019.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H524B212EB0904E4AA4C3BD14303C6009" class="indent1"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>If the institution is not described in subparagraph (B), the institution will comply with the requirements for a voter registration agency in the State in which it is located in accordance with section 7 of the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20506">52 U.S.C. 20506</ref>).</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HCE2CD3BDDFEF42C4B925C35400E7B902" class="indent1"><num value="D">“(D) </num><content>This paragraph applies only with respect to an institution which is located in a State to which section 4(b) of the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20503/b">52 U.S.C. 20503(b)</ref>) does not apply.”</content></subparagraph></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/b/2" id="H107097DC96024CF39D5F2003FD942D5A" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective date</inline>.—</heading><content>The amendments made by this subsection shall apply with respect to elections held on or after January 1, 2020.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/c" id="HF3FF1B34C0F74387A6CF8A7EB6AF4C65" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Grants to Institutions Demonstrating Excellence in Student Voter Registration</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/c/1" id="H585BB1AFF75D43E29D56A985150BCA33" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Grants authorized</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary of Education may award competitive grants to public and private nonprofit institutions of higher education that are subject to the requirements of section 487(a)(23) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (<ref href="/us/usc/t20/s1094/a/23">20 U.S.C. 1094(a)(23)</ref>), as amended by subsection (a) and that the Secretary determines have demonstrated excellence in registering students to vote in elections for public office beyond meeting the minimum requirements of such section.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/c/2" id="H745E82CE5DD648B8AF821E10D5D896AF" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Eligibility</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>An institution of higher education is eligible to receive a grant under this subsection if the institution submits to the Secretary of Education, at such time and in such form as the Secretary may require, an application containing such information and assurances as the Secretary may require to make the determination described in paragraph (1), including information and assurances that the institution carried out activities to promote voter registration by students, such as the following:</chapeau>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/c/2/A" id="H7C1EEF726B98498BB9C7F78E5084B3B3" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Sponsoring large on-campus voter mobilization efforts.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/c/2/B" id="HC571734660A54BB897752CFECF979881" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Engaging the surrounding community in nonpartisan voter registration and get out the vote efforts.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/c/2/C" id="H363623DA7309412B975C10BFFC6A217A" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>Creating a website for students with centralized information about voter registration and election dates.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/c/2/D" id="H5BD0BC4DAD904BB4A4460006CDA4D013" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>Inviting candidates to speak on campus.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/c/2/E" id="H8F9985937660429BA42F91ECAC8E71C2" class="indent2"><num value="E">(E) </num><content>Offering rides to students to the polls to increase voter education, registration, and mobilization.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/c/3" id="H2100EF261002425894F12036803FEF72" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorization of appropriations</inline>.—</heading><content>There are authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2020 and each succeeding fiscal year such sums as may be necessary to award grants under this subsection.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1901/d" id="H1B4896F9D12C4406A193517C54D5ECCA" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress Relating to Option of Students to Register in Jurisdiction of Institution of Higher Education or Jurisdiction of Domicile</inline>.—</heading><content>It is the sense of Congress that, as provided under existing law, students who attend an institution of higher education and reside in the jurisdiction of the institution while attending the institution should have the option of registering to vote in elections for Federal office in that jurisdiction or in the jurisdiction of their own domicile.</content></subsection></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1902" id="H8C338F1BCDD940C980A9015DE9AC790D"><num value="1902">SEC. 1902. </num><heading>MINIMUM NOTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS FOR VOTERS AFFECTED BY POLLING PLACE CHANGES.</heading>

<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1902/a/1" id="H2CF7E1FF87B0486A8D7C39D13BF8DBC4" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="redesignate">redesignating</amendingAction> subsection (f) as subsection (g); and</content></paragraph>

<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HDF6C58BA8D51483785F2378405D58980" styleType="OLC">
<subsection id="HDCF167D388BD4398B841594A0B2AE20C" class="indent0"><num value="f">“(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Minimum Notification Requirements for Voters Affected by Polling Place Changes</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H5BFFD504D0CD4391A72EE9ED3AC35E8E" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>If a State assigns an individual who is a registered voter in a State to a polling place with respect to an election for Federal office which is not the same polling place to which the individual was previously assigned with respect to the most recent election for Federal office in the State in which the individual was eligible to vote—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H6DE8AC6B16774C269A4B1C483D8D51F2" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>the State shall notify the individual of the location of the polling place not later than 7 days before the date of the election; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD5AE263C775649C59B41F270B2F16A61" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>if the State makes such an assignment fewer than 7 days before the date of the election and the individual appears on the date of the election at the polling place to which the individual was previously assigned, the State shall make every reasonable effort to enable the individual to vote on the date of the election.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HDCF631C8D27C442AB71677BCFB7CBE3E" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective date</inline>.—</heading><content>This subsection shall apply with respect to elections held on or after January 1, 2020.”</content></paragraph></subsection></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph></subsection>

<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1904" id="H4666C5B55047496F9A50F236A65EAFEB"><num value="1904">SEC. 1904. </num><heading>PERMITTING USE OF SWORN WRITTEN STATEMENT TO MEET IDENTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS FOR VOTING.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1904/a" id="HE94D6905D49C41C2906ADB172167F363" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Permitting Use of Statement</inline>.—</heading><content>Title III of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21081/etseq">52 U.S.C. 21081 et seq.</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> after section 303 the following new section:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H0BE3A7EEA8914703AEA933259A300343" styleType="OLC">
<section id="H5B0610888E8D458CBBFF5B3584366F68"><num value="303A">“SEC. 303A. </num><heading>PERMITTING USE OF SWORN WRITTEN STATEMENT TO MEET IDENTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS.</heading>
<subsection id="H842933C022B641528A6EA1B745A550B9" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Use of Statement</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H1AE039C79D33492B8AE99DE3925F83EE" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Except as provided in subsection (c), if a State has in effect a requirement that an individual present identification as a condition of receiving and casting a ballot in an election for Federal office, the State shall permit the individual to meet the requirement—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H6761CC057642467C94602C83B341ABFE" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>in the case of an individual who desires to vote in person, by presenting the appropriate State or local election official with a sworn written statement, signed by the individual under penalty of perjury, attesting to the individual’s identity and attesting that the individual is eligible to vote in the election; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HEC2B8F12DBA047489BBAD1F158CAEA20" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>in the case of an individual who desires to vote by mail, by submitting with the ballot the statement described in subparagraph (A).</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H11170F097A7F4B279FD4A7468D1151AC" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Development of pre-printed version of statement by commission</inline>.—</heading><content>The Commission shall develop a pre-printed version of the statement described in paragraph (1)(A) which includes a blank space for an individual to provide a name and signature for use by election officials in States which are subject to paragraph (1).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD86BF2E665214E68B1C437D3C6EA7B41" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Providing pre-printed copy of statement</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>A State which is subject to paragraph (1) shall—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H80E61C00FBBB4BCEB6D2F42332873794" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>make copies of the pre-printed version of the statement described in paragraph (1)(A) which is prepared by the Commission available at polling places for election officials to distribute to individuals who desire to vote in person; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H4601F6ABA013450F8F27D8690987B2C1" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>include a copy of such pre-printed version of the statement with each blank absentee or other ballot transmitted to an individual who desires to vote by mail.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HB11BB5079AC246E1A0AFA208EBCA6CAE" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requiring Use of Ballot in Same Manner as Individuals Presenting Identification</inline>.—</heading><content>An individual who presents or submits a sworn written statement in accordance with subsection (a)(1) shall be permitted to cast a ballot in the election in the same manner as an individual who presents identification.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H6B91A0075C994C32B11A1CF704281BAA" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exception for First-time Voters Registering by Mail</inline>.—</heading><content>Subsections (a) and (b) do not apply with respect to any individual described in paragraph (1) of section 303(b) who is required to meet the requirements of paragraph (2) of such section.”</content></subsection></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1904/b" id="H608C4A71B5B348F0AED48116A87A2EDF" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requiring States to Include Information on Use of Sworn Written Statement in Voting Information Material Posted at Polling Places</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 302(b)(2) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21082/b/2">52 U.S.C. 21082(b)(2)</ref>), as amended by section 1072(b) and section 1202(b), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1904/b/1" id="H2D539D6B0865487784007178CE474E37" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>and</quotedText>” at the end of subparagraph (G);</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1904/b/2" id="H8221005F08DC434983DE91E0C41EE73A" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> the period at the end of subparagraph (H) and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>; and</quotedText>”; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1904/b/3" id="HA2BBDB6E20024C8E8F54139069376E06" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new subparagraph:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HF7A4ACD45CC54729960B5362FA7DD2F6" styleType="OLC">

<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1906/a" id="HC3FEBB788A1B4B76BD4FB5CC1B9D41CC" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reimbursement</inline>.—</heading><content>Subtitle D of title II of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t42/s15401/etseq">42 U.S.C. 15401 et seq.</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new part:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HA7CEF78CD0FE4CE7A6B9F90CFAC317BF" styleType="OLC"><part id="H2424920C822D45CAB42C4EBCCAB7CC06"><num value="7">“PART 7—</num><heading>PAYMENTS TO REIMBURSE STATES FOR COSTS INCURRED IN ESTABLISHING PROGRAM TO TRACK AND CONFIRM RECEIPT OF ABSENTEE BALLOTS</heading>
<section id="HB435B7717825412C96E99BF3DAA5B1C4"><num value="297">“SEC. 297. </num><heading>PAYMENTS TO STATES.</heading>
<subsection id="HB747B649122D4951ADF87D58A9236952" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Payments For Costs of Establishing Program</inline>.—</heading><content>In accordance with this section, the Commission shall make a payment to a State to reimburse the State for the costs incurred in establishing, if the State so chooses to establish, an absentee ballot tracking program with respect to elections for Federal office held in the State (including costs incurred prior to the date of the enactment of this part).</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H3B57D7C0828A4B008ADF31ED6C7D6735" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Absentee Ballot Tracking Program Described</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HB0A867F60021493492F8F282920EB344" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Program described</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H7AC357A1FE6446FD88DC02BCD013F9BD" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>In this part, an ‘absentee ballot tracking program’ is a program to track and confirm the receipt of absentee ballots in an election for Federal office under which the State or local election official responsible for the receipt of voted absentee ballots in the election carries out procedures to track and confirm the receipt of such ballots, and makes information on the receipt of such ballots available to the individual who cast the ballot, by means of online access using the Internet site of the official’s office.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H5F4CC4DC69744FC78F8412785CDE0480" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Information on whether vote was counted</inline>.—</heading><content>The information referred to under subparagraph (A) with respect to the receipt of an absentee ballot shall include information regarding whether the vote cast on the ballot was counted, and, in the case of a vote which was not counted, the reasons therefor.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H88E805F0F03144269C5FAF48189B7A3D" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Use of toll-free telephone number by officials without internet site</inline>.—</heading><content>A program established by a State or local election official whose office does not have an Internet site may meet the description of a program under paragraph (1) if the official has established a toll-free telephone number that may be used by an individual who cast an absentee ballot to obtain the information on the receipt of the voted absentee ballot as provided under such paragraph.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HD37CB71061C7447D88775F6E16A4E0BD" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Certification of Compliance and Costs</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H1EE9013C4F8A469E9845947BE5712D37" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Certification required</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In order to receive a payment under this section, a State shall submit to the Commission a statement containing—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H07CE245B003041BA9FE9E3AAE48F90AF" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>a certification that the State has established an absentee ballot tracking program with respect to elections for Federal office held in the State; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HC5B0E027DB02427CBA7521C0C8A3830C" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>a statement of the costs incurred by the State in establishing the program.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9D5A39488F2446C5B0E28B0828DEBC56" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Amount of payment</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The amount of a payment made to a State under this section shall be equal to the costs incurred by the State in establishing the absentee ballot tracking program, as set forth in the statement submitted under paragraph (1), except that such amount may not exceed the product of—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H3B2B966562A94C30A7A224E9C5380D8E" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>the number of jurisdictions in the State which are responsible for operating the program; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H3DDFB8D5E9D447BA9532B4264E7C364C" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>$3,000.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF7B59C532E12456DA6D106D69B1EA7FF" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limit on number of payments received</inline>.—</heading><content>A State may not receive more than one payment under this part.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="HED5C2B0FC4D94900ADF393089DD2D1CA"><num value="297A">“SEC. 297A. </num><heading>AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS.</heading>
<subsection id="H025E7DAABA4A4A108016CDBA749198BC" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorization</inline>.—</heading><content>There are authorized to be appropriated to the Commission for fiscal year 2020 and each succeeding fiscal year such sums as may be necessary for payments under this part.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H8E65838FA7C64475A2C131F90149B2AF" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Continuing Availability of Funds</inline>.—</heading><content>Any amounts appropriated pursuant to the authorization under this section shall remain available until expended.”</content></subsection></section></part></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>

<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907" id="H592861FE85A3429F8AA5713BB0F372A3"><num value="1907">SEC. 1907. </num><heading>VOTER INFORMATION RESPONSE SYSTEMS AND HOTLINE.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/a" id="HAD25CE18F98041E8B52D6E4769A631A6" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Establishment and Operation of Systems and Services</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/a/1" id="H100CD42AC1BF41388B9ABDC6C811E086" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">State-based response systems</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Attorney General shall coordinate the establishment of a State-based response system for responding to questions and complaints from individuals voting or seeking to vote, or registering to vote or seeking to register to vote, in elections for Federal office. Such system shall provide—</chapeau>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/a/1/A" id="H3B8A7E54FC1E4A51970C5FAA1884A838" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>State-specific, same-day, and immediate assistance to such individuals, including information on how to register to vote, the location and hours of operation of polling places, and how to obtain absentee ballots; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/a/1/B" id="H1ED7C5C61A2548AA92664278F10201D1" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>State-specific, same-day, and immediate assistance to individuals encountering problems with registering to vote or voting, including individuals encountering intimidation or deceptive practices.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/a/2" id="HF9C62E64897E4D3CBAF74604A88EDD14" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Hotline</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Attorney General, in consultation with State election officials, shall establish and operate a toll-free telephone service, using a telephone number that is accessible throughout the United States and that uses easily identifiable numerals, through which individuals throughout the United States—</chapeau>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/a/2/A" id="H3B7E1168FDD84B008BCEAC4C46800CA2" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>may connect directly to the State-based response system described in paragraph (1) with respect to the State involved;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/a/2/B" id="H913056AE8D784778A200973134995C43" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>may obtain information on voting in elections for Federal office, including information on how to register to vote in such elections, the locations and hours of operation of polling places, and how to obtain absentee ballots; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/a/2/C" id="H3E02442CCC6344BF8F906AA49FC3D945" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>may report information to the Attorney General on problems encountered in registering to vote or voting, including incidences of voter intimidation or suppression.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/a/3" id="H876AC0031073474482D6047779EA435D" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Collaboration with state and local election officials</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/a/3/A" id="H2FA598CE917448F68953B22914A465AF" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Collection of information from states</inline>.—</heading><content>The Attorney General shall coordinate the collection of information on State and local election laws and policies, including information on the Statewide computerized voter registration lists maintained under title III of the Help America Vote Act of 2002, so that individuals who contact the free telephone service established under paragraph (2) on the date of an election for Federal office may receive an immediate response on that day.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/a/3/B" id="H0282E8D9665240E68BAD2A6D54A70247" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Forwarding questions and complaints to states</inline>.—</heading><content>If an individual contacts the free telephone service established under paragraph (2) on the date of an election for Federal office with a question or complaint with respect to a particular State or jurisdiction within a State, the Attorney General shall forward the question or complaint immediately to the appropriate election official of the State or jurisdiction so that the official may answer the question or remedy the complaint on that date.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/a/4" id="H63530F2136944E00A6E425C7397E9F9E" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Consultation requirements for development of systems and services</inline>.—</heading><content>The Attorney General shall ensure that the State-based response system under paragraph (1) and the free telephone service under paragraph (2) are each developed in consultation with civil rights organizations, voting rights groups, State and local election officials, voter protection groups, and other interested community organizations, especially those that have experience in the operation of similar systems and services.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/b" id="HAA0BBC1088644424AAA15691021F0E69" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Use of Service by Individuals With Disabilities and Individuals With Limited English Language Proficiency</inline>.—</heading><content>The Attorney General shall design and operate the telephone service established under this section in a manner that ensures that individuals with disabilities are fully able to use the service, and that assistance is provided in any language in which the State (or any jurisdiction in the State) is required to provide election materials under section 203 of the Voting Rights Act of 1965..</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/c" id="H50F791EF6AA84DCDABAE7AFA37F33AF9" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Voter Hotline Task Force</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/c/1" id="H9D8A0C5BFB0A440E8593E668F7886AA4" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Appointment by attorney general</inline>.—</heading><content>The Attorney General shall appoint individuals (in such number as the Attorney General considers appropriate but in no event fewer than 3) to serve on a Voter Hotline Task Force to provide ongoing analysis and assessment of the operation of the telephone service established under this section, and shall give special consideration in making appointments to the Task Force to individuals who represent civil rights organizations. At least one member of the Task Force shall be a representative of an organization promoting voting rights or civil rights which has experience in the operation of similar telephone services or in protecting the rights of individuals to vote, especially individuals who are members of racial, ethnic, or linguistic minorities or of communities who have been adversely affected by efforts to suppress voting rights.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/c/2" id="H3C4D2259F5F34077B65D69A507E43B3F" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Eligibility</inline>.—</heading><content>An individual shall be eligible to serve on the Task Force under this subsection if the individual meets such criteria as the Attorney General may establish, except that an individual may not serve on the task force if the individual has been convicted of any criminal offense relating to voter intimidation or voter suppression.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/c/3" id="H61D9D7D2F527445B8B4B94CD625110CD" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Term of service</inline>.—</heading><content>An individual appointed to the Task Force shall serve a single term of 2 years, except that the initial terms of the members first appointed to the Task Force shall be staggered so that there are at least 3 individuals serving on the Task Force during each year. A vacancy in the membership of the Task Force shall be filled in the same manner as the original appointment.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/c/4" id="H042E8699ED42492AA462CD86EAA9C4E0" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">No compensation for service</inline>.—</heading><content>Members of the Task Force shall serve without pay, but shall receive travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, in accordance with applicable provisions under <ref href="/us/usc/t5/ch57/schI">subchapter I of chapter 57 of title 5, United States Code</ref>.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/d" id="HFCB5C51CD45E440A9446D10AF6109A9D" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Bi-Annual Report to Congress</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than March 1 of each odd-numbered year, the Attorney General shall submit a report to Congress on the operation of the telephone service established under this section during the previous 2 years, and shall include in the report—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/d/1" id="H82B08D97931F49BAAE3AD65FD6B8311A" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>an enumeration of the number and type of calls that were received by the service;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/d/2" id="HE84A0046D8724F9698BDCFCDA216DA1B" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>a compilation and description of the reports made to the service by individuals citing instances of voter intimidation or suppression;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/d/3" id="H076E57163DBF422FB7ABF7930344E5A2" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>an assessment of the effectiveness of the service in making information available to all households in the United States with telephone service;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/d/4" id="H72C77AD0AE3644D58E281A1D95AD75DD" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>any recommendations developed by the Task Force established under subsection (c) with respect to how voting systems may be maintained or upgraded to better accommodate voters and better ensure the integrity of elections, including but not limited to identifying how to eliminate coordinated voter suppression efforts and how to establish effective mechanisms for distributing updates on changes to voting requirements; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/d/5" id="H2C58B00C590E4463BD2649A7C6826D80" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>any recommendations on best practices for the State-based response systems established under subsection (a)(1).</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/e" id="H49DF82F031D349D5842EADF49EFB898B" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorization of Appropriations</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/e/1" id="HD618DF94FEBD4E0E8FA0FF18FB82F111" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorization</inline>.—</heading><content>There are authorized to be appropriated to the Attorney General for fiscal year 2019 and each succeeding fiscal year such sums as may be necessary to carry out this section.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt1/s1907/e/2" id="HADD37F849E9E4B1F8DEE8CE7A300DA17" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Set-aside for outreach</inline>.—</heading><content>Of the amounts appropriated to carry out this section for a fiscal year pursuant to the authorization under paragraph (1), not less than 15 percent shall be used for outreach activities to make the public aware of the availability of the telephone service established under this section, with an emphasis on outreach to individuals with disabilities and individuals with limited proficiency in the English language.</content></paragraph></subsection></section></part><part identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt2" id="HEBF19D7C62DB4DC8A5A994A5E72F956A"><num value="2">PART 2—</num><heading>IMPROVEMENTS IN OPERATION OF ELECTION ASSISTANCE COMMISSION</heading>

<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt3/s1922" id="HA74B1FF31E734115A9210BCB38FA76B3"><num value="1922">SEC. 1922. </num><heading>NO EFFECT ON OTHER LAWS.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt3/s1922/a" id="H08F864C688C342FAB6C3696FC6E9FB9D" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Except as specifically provided, nothing in this title may be construed to authorize or require conduct prohibited under any of the following laws, or to supersede, restrict, or limit the application of such laws:</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt3/s1922/a/1" id="HE72EE86022934EDA96922491392709BF" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>The Voting Rights Act of 1965 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s10301/etseq">52 U.S.C. 10301 et seq.</ref>).</content></paragraph>

<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt3/s1922/b" id="H7FB785FF959345FEA569916A7B66585C" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">No Effect on Preclearance or Other Requirements Under Voting Rights Act</inline>.—</heading><content>The approval by any person of a payment or grant application under this title, or any other action taken by any person under this title, shall not be considered to have any effect on requirements for preclearance under section 5 of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s10304">52 U.S.C. 10304</ref>) or any other requirements of such Act.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tI/stN/pt3/s1922/c" id="H244E7067736F4009897C380D5CFFAFCF" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">No Effect on Authority of States to Provide Greater Opportunities for Voting</inline>.—</heading><content>Nothing in this title or the amendments made by this title may be construed to prohibit any State from enacting any law which provides greater opportunities for individuals to register to vote and to vote in elections for Federal office than are provided by this title and the amendments made by this title.</content></subsection></section></part></subtitle>
