<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tII/stF/s2501" id="H41792651354C452194A811CB4CB22D2C"><num value="2501">SEC. 2501. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This subtitle may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="subtitle">Stop Automatically Voiding Eligible Voters Off Their Enlisted Rolls in States Act</shortTitle>” or the “<shortTitle role="subtitle">Save Voters Act</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tII/stF/s2502" id="H2FBDE20169694F81946A6BBCBFA9382B"><num value="2502">SEC. 2502. </num><heading>CONDITIONS FOR REMOVAL OF VOTERS FROM LIST OF REGISTERED VOTERS.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tII/stF/s2502/a" id="HCFD38566658941C7A1254A4376F39B4F" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Conditions Described</inline>.—</heading><content>The National Voter Registration Act of 1993 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20501/etseq">52 U.S.C. 20501 et seq.</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> after section 8 the following new section:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H0B636655DFBD48BCA3AA7D6248D5F5DA" styleType="OLC">
<section id="HF3B20A1C24654DD685FC7756B887C546"><num value="8A">“SEC. 8A. </num><heading>CONDITIONS FOR REMOVAL OF VOTERS FROM OFFICIAL LIST OF REGISTERED VOTERS.</heading>
<subsection id="H29AF38CB3E23478DA5F3D7ED6099CB98" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Verification on Basis of Objective and Reliable Evidence of Ineligibility</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HD403CA88781443FD8987E3689A2F67F9" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requiring verification</inline>.—</heading><content>Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, a State may not remove the name of any registrant from the official list of voters eligible to vote in elections for Federal office in the State unless the State verifies, on the basis of objective and reliable evidence, that the registrant is ineligible to vote in such elections.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HBF0BEFD5AE634F34932BE911E8EFC4B5" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Factors not considered as objective and reliable evidence of ineligibility</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>For purposes of paragraph (2), the following factors, or any combination thereof, shall not be treated as objective and reliable evidence of a registrant’s ineligibility to vote:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H1CE0FF25D36C4625B60159035E00C4C5" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>The failure of the registrant to vote in any election.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H308C4255A5AD4004B0BB457C4E8D956F" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>The failure of the registrant to respond to any notice sent under section 8(d), unless the notice has been returned as undeliverable.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HEB50988FD6624D4B97148523391440B6" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>The failure of the registrant to take any other action with respect to voting in any election or with respect to the registrant’s status as a registrant.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H4A51E0B5014246B98723D426981CFA20" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Notice After Removal</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H157000F124464B3FB699A3F27600A690" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Notice to individual removed</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H62556A5AA3204DDCA92B9A2753E01EB2" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 48 hours after a State removes the name of a registrant from the official list of eligible voters for any reason (other than the death of the registrant), the State shall send notice of the removal to the former registrant, and shall include in the notice the grounds for the removal and information how the former registrant may contest the removal, including a telephone number for the appropriate election official., and how to contest the removal or be reinstated, including a contact phone number.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H602294E006FB434FAB9D0BDCCB5B773A" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exceptions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Subparagraph (A) does not apply in the case of a registrant—</chapeau>
<clause id="H2E2FD9136EC240A598065EEC323F10BB" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>who sends written confirmation to the State that the registrant is no longer eligible to vote in the registrar’s jurisdiction in which the registrant was registered; or</content></clause>
<clause id="HE451998D58D7468DA961C0E71EB64952" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>who is removed from the official list of eligible voters by reason of the death of the registrant.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H378F7AB9E9F049418286C4BB777527DB" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Public notice</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 48 hours after conducting any general program to remove the names of ineligible voters from the official list of eligible voters (as described in section 8(a)(4)), the State shall disseminate a public notice through such methods as may be reasonable to reach the general public (including by publishing the notice in a newspaper of wide circulation or posting the notice on the websites of the appropriate election officials) that list maintenance is taking place and that registrants should check their registration status to ensure no errors or mistakes have been made. The State shall ensure that the public notice disseminated under this paragraph is in a format that is reasonably convenient and accessible to voters with disabilities, including voters who have low vision or are blind.”</content></paragraph></subsection></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tII/stF/s2502/b" id="H47437BE3D5724CF683EFA5E62606C1A8" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Conditions for Transmission of Notices of Removal</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 8(d) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20507/d">52 U.S.C. 20507(d)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new paragraph:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H40F6C0CC5CCE40779713E03035F0EBF7" styleType="traditional">
<paragraph id="H5BEC196F0DFB43E1ADB7AF220844FBF0" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><content>A State may not transmit a notice to a registrant under this subsection unless the State obtains objective and reliable evidence (in accordance with the standards for such evidence which are described in section 8A(a)(2)) that the registrant has changed residence to a place outside the registrar’s jurisdiction in which the registrant is registered.”</content></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tII/stF/s2502/c" id="HF710758423D7468995F64232CBC70C8F" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Conforming Amendments</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tII/stF/s2502/c/1" id="H970F209F501A4085A5D085B5BE0C2671" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">National voter registration act of 1993</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 8(a) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20507/a">52 U.S.C. 20507(a)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tII/stF/s2502/c/1/A" id="HFBD9E21F91594FE793DB89B486C1F795" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>in paragraph (3), by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>provide</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>subject to section 8A, provide</quotedText>”; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tII/stF/s2502/c/1/B" id="HAB59E5E95C764CF0A462EE2427B4D083" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>in paragraph (4), by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>conduct</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>subject to section 8A, conduct</quotedText>”.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tII/stF/s2502/c/2" id="H85742B51C0FB420598F56EF62EFAE4BD" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Help america vote act of 2002</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 303(a)(4)(A) of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21083/a/4/A">52 U.S.C. 21083(a)(4)(A)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>, registrants</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>, and subject to section 8A of such Act, registrants</quotedText>”.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tII/stF/s2502/d" id="H2D4170BF7A2044B9A43085E87440F353" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective Date</inline>.—</heading><content>The amendments made by this section shall take effect on the date of the enactment of this Act.</content></subsection></section></subtitle>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tII/stG" id="HEEB013B786424B7EA7FF800B11E6814E"><num value="G">Subtitle G—</num><heading>No Effect on Authority of States to Provide Greater Opportunities for Voting</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tII/stG/s2601" id="H63DCB64D9E344198BE6E7232012F0A2F"><num value="2601">SEC. 2601. </num><heading>NO EFFECT ON AUTHORITY OF STATES TO PROVIDE GREATER OPPORTUNITIES FOR VOTING.</heading><content class="block">Nothing in this title or the amendments made by this title may be construed to prohibit any State from enacting any law which provides greater opportunities for individuals to register to vote and to vote in elections for Federal office than are provided by this title and the amendments made by this title.</content></section></subtitle>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tII/stH" id="HD1E086BA90A9402581114ADB5061E014"><num value="H">Subtitle H—</num><heading>Severability</heading>

<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/s3000" id="H85DD12EE476F49CBBF9A89AF0B41B214"><num value="3000">SEC. 3000. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE; SENSE OF CONGRESS.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/s3000/a" id="H755132AD69DF412881B9CD9A2AB47626" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Short Title</inline>.—</heading><content>This title may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="title">Election Security Act</shortTitle>”.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/s3000/b" id="HAD600B7FE28649BC9D4F793A2E156C4C" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Sense of Congress on Need to Improve Election Infrastructure Security</inline>.—</heading><content>It is the sense of Congress that, in light of the lessons learned from Russian interference in the 2016 Presidential election, the Federal Government should intensify its efforts to improve the security of election infrastructure in the United States, including through the use of individual, durable, paper ballots marked by the voter by hand.</content></subsection></section>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stA" id="HC0D09AEC40374F34937D777DC85C7412"><num value="A">Subtitle A—</num><heading>Financial Support for Election Infrastructure</heading><part identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stA/pt1" id="H4C638B73C6A541DE8ED8378BE8125DC4"><num value="1">PART 1—</num><heading>VOTING SYSTEM SECURITY IMPROVEMENT GRANTS</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stA/pt1/s3001" id="HEA832F99A0E94B929AE97DB939D0F876"><num value="3001">SEC. 3001. </num><heading>GRANTS FOR OBTAINING COMPLIANT PAPER BALLOT VOTING SYSTEMS AND CARRYING OUT VOTING SYSTEM SECURITY IMPROVEMENTS.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stA/pt1/s3001/a" id="HBA83FD7AF36E416190841058755726CF" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Availability of Grants</inline>.—</heading><content>Subtitle D of title II of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21001/etseq">52 U.S.C. 21001 et seq.</ref>), as amended by section 1906(a), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new part:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H2CB0E248F09F4902B1E2A8D171AC6891" styleType="OLC"><part id="H2A8B966256F4430DA13DEC16898D33A9"><num value="8">“PART 8—</num><heading>GRANTS FOR OBTAINING COMPLIANT PAPER BALLOT VOTING SYSTEMS AND CARRYING OUT VOTING SYSTEM SECURITY IMPROVEMENTS</heading>
<section id="H4D34860EED0240E49B762AFFB5B4CD3E"><num value="298">“SEC. 298. </num><heading>GRANTS FOR OBTAINING COMPLIANT PAPER BALLOT VOTING SYSTEMS AND CARRYING OUT VOTING SYSTEM SECURITY IMPROVEMENTS.</heading>
<subsection id="H1F09676C4A2E4632ABA66E3F56F5FF94" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Availability and Use of Grant</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Commission shall make a grant to each eligible State—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H9994514BA427459DBDE1F2914D363562" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><chapeau>to replace a voting system—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HC8714E80E9544D3C9A08DD4045667C58" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>which does not meet the requirements which are first imposed on the State pursuant to the amendments made by the Voter Confidence and Increased Accessibility Act of 2019 with a voting system which does meet such requirements, for use in the regularly scheduled general elections for Federal office held in November 2020, or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H75F84326E53A410A9597C1F76DE88A2C" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>which does meet such requirements but which is not in compliance with the most recent voluntary voting system guidelines issued by the Commission prior to the regularly scheduled general election for Federal office held in November 2020 with another system which does meet such requirements and is in compliance with such guidelines; and</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3720938D74FE4D6AA4EB50CFD0DBD592" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>to carry out voting system security improvements described in section 298A with respect to the regularly scheduled general elections for Federal office held in November 2020 and each succeeding election for Federal office.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HAA9779D6C5234C5FB7707E5B6F511A03" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Amount of Grant</inline>.—</heading><content>The amount of a grant made to a State under this section shall be such amount as the Commission determines to be appropriate, except that such amount may not be less than the product of $1 and the average of the number of individuals who cast votes in any of the two most recent regularly scheduled general elections for Federal office held in the State.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H75CA58F86AC74F08A52D1A22A8E4037F" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Pro Rata Reductions</inline>.—</heading><content>If the amount of funds appropriated for grants under this part is insufficient to ensure that each State receives the amount of the grant calculated under subsection (b), the Commission shall make such pro rata reductions in such amounts as may be necessary to ensure that the entire amount appropriated under this part is distributed to the States.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H21150BDB13BE4387BFEB73E2D3DA19CB" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Ability of Replacement Systems to Administer Ranked Choice Elections</inline>.—</heading><content>To the greatest extent practicable, an eligible State which receives a grant to replace a voting system under this section shall ensure that the replacement system is capable of administering a system of ranked choice voting under which each voter shall rank the candidates for the office in the order of the voter’s preference.</content></subsection></section>
<section id="H4F7BD37033C14D989BA77D569A3A51EA"><num value="298A">“SEC. 298A. </num><heading>VOTING SYSTEM SECURITY IMPROVEMENTS DESCRIBED.</heading>
<subsection id="H5BE21DC2411146EE8AFCC9744C6E480C" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Permitted Uses</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>A voting system security improvement described in this section is any of the following:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HB28B09F0DBA54CA18ED346E45862009E" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>The acquisition of goods and services from qualified election infrastructure vendors by purchase, lease, or such other arrangements as may be appropriate.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H21E74B2479E14B3EBE7B3F99A4D4A829" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>Cyber and risk mitigation training.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3264633458C64CA8A5020D2EB5844230" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><content>A security risk and vulnerability assessment of the State’s election infrastructure which is carried out by a provider of cybersecurity services under a contract entered into between the chief State election official and the provider.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5ED5DB6F826B4AE982AC45D8715714CE" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><content>The maintenance of election infrastructure, including addressing risks and vulnerabilities which are identified under either of the security risk and vulnerability assessments described in paragraph (3), except that none of the funds provided under this part may be used to renovate or replace a building or facility which is used primarily for purposes other than the administration of elections for public office.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H73AD7E3D93DF4F5DA7CC69DCA4743FDD" class="indent1"><num value="5">“(5) </num><content>Providing increased technical support for any information technology infrastructure that the chief State election official deems to be part of the State’s election infrastructure or designates as critical to the operation of the State’s election infrastructure.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC7557665084F41B68BC248E0D6B4A1FE" class="indent1"><num value="6">“(6) </num><content>Enhancing the cybersecurity and operations of the information technology infrastructure described in paragraph (4).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC266CEAFD69D4A448FDD77F50076E641" class="indent1"><num value="7">“(7) </num><content>Enhancing the cybersecurity of voter registration systems.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H1E7DCA4AD1B24F888E7ED33C67FFF116" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Qualified Election Infrastructure Vendors Described</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H75B9A53083FA49F99FD3F0A29B473206" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>For purposes of this part, a ‘qualified election infrastructure vendor’ is any person who provides, supports, or maintains, or who seeks to provide, support, or maintain, election infrastructure on behalf of a State, unit of local government, or election agency (as defined in section 3501 of the Election Security Act) who meets the criteria described in paragraph (2).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HAB26FB8D5B9F470EA18A785EBD4514FE" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Criteria</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The criteria described in this paragraph are such criteria as the Chairman, in coordination with the Secretary of Homeland Security, shall establish and publish, and shall include each of the following requirements:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H209A871DCC0648F1A9C321CB7A998901" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>The vendor must be owned and controlled by a citizen or permanent resident of the United States.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H79E5338CD56C4D839BE4CD48B5151CC7" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>The vendor must disclose to the Chairman and the Secretary, and to the chief State election official of any State to which the vendor provides any goods and services with funds provided under this part, of any sourcing outside the United States for parts of the election infrastructure.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HAE6E8099264A4D8593D0C5B4C8BD847B" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>The vendor agrees to ensure that the election infrastructure will be developed and maintained in a manner that is consistent with the cybersecurity best practices issued by the Technical Guidelines Development Committee.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H7D4622685FED45258D4FA840AACE79DA" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><content>The vendor agrees to maintain its information technology infrastructure in a manner that is consistent with the cybersecurity best practices issued by the Technical Guidelines Development Committee.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H555A61D2DA4E4B1D80AC086815B20205" class="indent2"><num value="E">“(E) </num><content>The vendor agrees to meet the requirements of paragraph (3) with respect to any known or suspected cybersecurity incidents involving any of the goods and services provided by the vendor pursuant to a grant under this part.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H62F27978F03641D2B5D859478663CAB6" class="indent2"><num value="F">“(F) </num><content>The vendor agrees to permit independent security testing by the Commission (in accordance with section 231(a)) and by the Secretary of the goods and services provided by the vendor pursuant to a grant under this part.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE4A6D00BA66B4FB19E5548C2192A6AC1" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Cybersecurity incident reporting requirements</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H196C0DDB0FD44682A3D64C7B242C4CFE" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>A vendor meets the requirements of this paragraph if, upon becoming aware of the possibility that an election cybersecurity incident has occurred involving any of the goods and services provided by the vendor pursuant to a grant under this part—</chapeau>
<clause id="H22EAD8690A7F443EBE928615EE7F6C4A" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the vendor promptly assesses whether or not such an incident occurred, and submits a notification meeting the requirements of subparagraph (B) to the Secretary and the Chairman of the assessment as soon as practicable (but in no case later than 3 days after the vendor first becomes aware of the possibility that the incident occurred);</content></clause>
<clause id="HDECAA88DDFD24F22A7CDE8A9C26ADBB5" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>if the incident involves goods or services provided to an election agency, the vendor submits a notification meeting the requirements of subparagraph (B) to the agency as soon as practicable (but in no case later than 3 days after the vendor first becomes aware of the possibility that the incident occurred), and cooperates with the agency in providing any other necessary notifications relating to the incident; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H075E15C71B53417290D90797141C9A7E" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>the vendor provides all necessary updates to any notification submitted under clause (i) or clause (ii).</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD2825DE463D54A3786F988C38A6F51ED" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Contents of notifications</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Each notification submitted under clause (i) or clause (ii) of subparagraph (A) shall contain the following information with respect to any election cybersecurity incident covered by the notification:</chapeau>
<clause id="HE838C90066E346FF98B9B26F4787E41F" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>The date, time, and time zone when the election cybersecurity incident began, if known.</content></clause>
<clause id="HB0ACEBD90DCA48099DD3514ABAB38A9C" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>The date, time, and time zone when the election cybersecurity incident was detected.</content></clause>
<clause id="H8A39F912C0894DEDA33733D13B918467" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>The date, time, and duration of the election cybersecurity incident.</content></clause>
<clause id="H402AB064BA2746C9B936482D815B848A" class="indent3"><num value="iv">“(iv) </num><content>The circumstances of the election cybersecurity incident, including the specific election infrastructure systems believed to have been accessed and information acquired, if any.</content></clause>
<clause id="H35641CB787E348F9B9A3A238397F9BED" class="indent3"><num value="v">“(v) </num><content>Any planned and implemented technical measures to respond to and recover from the incident.</content></clause>
<clause id="HCF149B4094C348918F2FB2C17073D022" class="indent3"><num value="vi">“(vi) </num><content>In the case of any notification which is an update to a prior notification, any additional material information relating to the incident, including technical data, as it becomes available.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H692FE45D45344D38B096BAA460C70477"><num value="298B">“SEC. 298B. </num><heading>ELIGIBILITY OF STATES.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">“A State is eligible to receive a grant under this part if the State submits to the Commission, at such time and in such form as the Commission may require, an application containing—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H613BF09F5DF64EEFB5641D53FE8D9528" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>a description of how the State will use the grant to carry out the activities authorized under this part;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HAF89B204814E424C9584651B0F2D668F" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>a certification and assurance that, not later than 5 years after receiving the grant, the State will carry out risk-limiting audits and will carry out voting system security improvements, as described in section 298A; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H2C7E29579A37425D82B06CDC1242EF86" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><content>such other information and assurances as the Commission may require.</content></paragraph></section>
<section id="H2438C16241D941419970464655D93771"><num value="298C">“SEC. 298C. </num><heading>REPORTS TO CONGRESS.</heading><content class="block">“Not later than 90 days after the end of each fiscal year, the Commission shall submit a report to the appropriate congressional committees, including the Committees on Homeland Security, House Administration, and the Judiciary of the House of Representatives and the Committees on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, the Judiciary, and Rules and Administration of the Senate, on the activities carried out with the funds provided under this part.</content></section>
<section id="HE7FB889FE0A74EEBB322294E11B6DB67"><num value="298D">“SEC. 298D. </num><heading>AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS.</heading>
<subsection id="H8270BC87E31E4485BAB83369F03750CB" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authorization</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>There are authorized to be appropriated for grants under this part—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H6522F43390B44328B4C4CF120A005597" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>$1,000,000,000 for fiscal year 2019; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H089DD807FAD34A0086601903DEE22D5D" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>$175,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 2020, 2022, 2024, and 2026.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H7A253A7B037B44329F5283356F37B8F6" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Continuing Availability of Amounts</inline>.—</heading><content>Any amounts appropriated pursuant to the authorization of this section shall remain available until expended.”</content></subsection></section></part></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>

<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stA/pt1/s3002/a" id="H063E2C80826E40179826BF9271562AC5" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Duties of Election Assistance Commission</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 202 of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20922">52 U.S.C. 20922</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> in the matter preceding paragraph (1) by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>by</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>and the security of election infrastructure by</quotedText>”.</content></subsection>

<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stA/pt1/s3003/a" id="HA1313F952D4F4150B9AF579BD47BC1B4" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 901 of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21141">52 U.S.C. 21141</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> to read as follows:

<section id="HE5A910CDAC2E4518BFD5A7C6EE5C85B6"><num value="901">“SEC. 901. </num><heading>DEFINITIONS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">“In this Act, the following definitions apply:</chapeau>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H835D8FDEC9414F1789B0995C7D3617DA" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>The term ‘<term>cybersecurity incident</term>’ has the meaning given the term ‘<term>incident</term>’ in section 227 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t6/s148">6 U.S.C. 148</ref>).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H5AF99132AE9A4CC9B649BE5D77EF39A3" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>The term ‘<term>election infrastructure</term>’ has the meaning given such term in section 3501 of the Election Security Act.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HAAB70E76783C43C5B8662C476513AC2F" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><content>The term ‘<term>State</term>’ means each of the several States, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, Guam, American Samoa, the United States Virgin Islands, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.”</content></paragraph></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>

<referenceItem role="section">
<designator>“Sec. 901. </designator>
<label>Definitions.”</label>
</referenceItem></toc></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection></section></part><part identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stA/pt2" id="H2F9409FDBCC94B71BAD7D8A09DE8A806"><num value="2">PART 2—</num><heading>GRANTS FOR RISK-LIMITING AUDITS OF RESULTS OF ELECTIONS</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stA/pt2/s3011" id="H3293FFA5CDF74248B612E781F35B8783"><num value="3011">SEC. 3011. </num><heading>GRANTS TO STATES FOR CONDUCTING RISK-LIMITING AUDITS OF RESULTS OF ELECTIONS.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stA/pt2/s3011/a" id="H3FFD30F7F6894E00AC4A6F508367D862" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Availability of Grants</inline>.—</heading><content>Subtitle D of title II of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21001/etseq">52 U.S.C. 21001 et seq.</ref>), as amended by sections 1906(a) and 3001(a), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new part:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HDAD86D7E9ABC4DB6B18311D5F2EBA59A" styleType="OLC"><part id="H7F31914094354C4BB0DBB8016B182D8A"><num value="9">“PART 9—</num><heading>GRANTS FOR CONDUCTING RISK-LIMITING AUDITS OF RESULTS OF ELECTIONS</heading>
<section id="H58C0A989AB82488F9A8E8EF1F6B88278"><num value="299">“SEC. 299. </num><heading>GRANTS FOR CONDUCTING RISK-LIMITING AUDITS OF RESULTS OF ELECTIONS.</heading>
<subsection id="H5DE5F35791224B3E8AEE2D165A970EC3" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Availability of Grants</inline>.—</heading><content>The Commission shall make a grant to each eligible State to conduct risk-limiting audits as described in subsection (b) with respect to the regularly scheduled general elections for Federal office held in November 2020 and each succeeding election for Federal office.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HC197A94268704A60A0CED4E568F56CD8" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Risk-limiting Audits Described</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this part, a ‘risk-limiting audit’ is a post-election process—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H7A0318E0F93247549C6D47E0D5F401E3" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>which is conducted in accordance with rules and procedures established by the chief State election official of the State which meet the requirements of subsection (c); and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H79D9CAA8CF244226967DC7C46C730880" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>under which, if the reported outcome of the election is incorrect, there is at least a predetermined percentage chance that the audit will replace the incorrect outcome with the correct outcome as determined by a full, hand-to-eye tabulation of all votes validly cast in that election that ascertains voter intent manually and directly from voter-verifiable paper records.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HF7F64E7074D44C508DEB34D1BF601620" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requirements for Rules and Procedures</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The rules and procedures established for conducting a risk-limiting audit shall include the following elements:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HCDF1CB90796940A9BECBB6DECF4C2CDF" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>Rules for ensuring the security of ballots and documenting that prescribed procedures were followed.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3494D40471CD49FE8EAE42AE72816FB4" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>Rules and procedures for ensuring the accuracy of ballot manifests produced by election agencies.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HEF4AF673F2C44E468A48323F450B0A93" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><content>Rules and procedures for governing the format of ballot manifests, cast vote records, and other data involved in the audit.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF64BDE602ABD42AFBF0909CD257B7E3A" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><content>Methods to ensure that any cast vote records used in the audit are those used by the voting system to tally the election results sent to the chief State election official and made public.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H958F94B73A39442190A7702EF7586D12" class="indent1"><num value="5">“(5) </num><content>Procedures for the random selection of ballots to be inspected manually during each audit.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFA021B266CBA45D395E550715FB7A2FE" class="indent1"><num value="6">“(6) </num><content>Rules for the calculations and other methods to be used in the audit and to determine whether and when the audit of an election is complete.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1588CB87DB60409E97B9EEFF9331C4FE" class="indent1"><num value="7">“(7) </num><content>Procedures and requirements for testing any software used to conduct risk-limiting audits.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HF455E37987114C328163E9016AD9D43A" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definitions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this part, the following definitions apply:</chapeau>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HAC4085F77FA44158B8C89888FA402610" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><chapeau>The term ‘<term>ballot manifest</term>’ means a record maintained by each election agency that meets each of the following requirements:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H9F6690C9F46848F189664FD706387D38" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>The record is created without reliance on any part of the voting system used to tabulate votes.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H1BF6F5E247634398B802DD5100E43D92" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>The record functions as a sampling frame for conducting a risk-limiting audit.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HF3BDF043D29F4833A5769A9A9C614CFF" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><chapeau>The record contains the following information with respect to the ballots cast and counted in the election:</chapeau>
<clause id="HB5084525C55649D8BFC25FDB61584F54" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>The total number of ballots cast and counted by the agency (including undervotes, overvotes, and other invalid votes).</content></clause>
<clause id="HBD013DAE92C3442A8C4C4DDE29B6E03E" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>The total number of ballots cast in each election administered by the agency (including undervotes, overvotes, and other invalid votes).</content></clause>
<clause id="H7C6E6F1205B043BB8D3D3D25F121BCBD" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>A precise description of the manner in which the ballots are physically stored, including the total number of physical groups of ballots, the numbering system for each group, a unique label for each group, and the number of ballots in each such group.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H69111B23042C46558B7311FE3C710624" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>The term ‘<term>incorrect outcome</term>’ means an outcome that differs from the outcome that would be determined by a full tabulation of all votes validly cast in the election, determining voter intent manually, directly from voter-verifiable paper records.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H1F71E8746B7B41B1B5FA97792279C458" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><content>The term ‘<term>outcome</term>’ means the winner of an election, whether a candidate or a position.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H9D9119DD3F4C4952A634D1509B52FF64" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><content>The term ‘<term>reported outcome</term>’ means the outcome of an election which is determined according to the canvass and which will become the official, certified outcome unless it is revised by an audit, recount, or other legal process.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section id="H02378791E52D44D1A1F80D940461249E"><num value="299A">“SEC. 299A. </num><heading>ELIGIBILITY OF STATES.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">“A State is eligible to receive a grant under this part if the State submits to the Commission, at such time and in such form as the Commission may require, an application containing—</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H6F060C55BE854280B9294C31D3D9EAC9" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>a certification that, not later than 5 years after receiving the grant, the State will conduct risk-limiting audits of the results of elections for Federal office held in the State as described in section 299;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HDEBB79CC1E5943C1806A3832627961FF" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>a certification that, not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this section, the chief State election official of the State has established or will establish the rules and procedures for conducting the audits which meet the requirements of section 299(c);</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5D0CFF0FC6FE44EB807F163F21623D2E" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><content>a certification that the audit shall be completed not later than the date on which the State certifies the results of the election;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3D828D77FA19446489883B56F9367E71" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><content>a certification that, after completing the audit, the State shall publish a report on the results of the audit, together with such information as necessary to confirm that the audit was conducted properly;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HFCB65EE1FB96427BBEE869E6EFEF4993" class="indent1"><num value="5">“(5) </num><content>a certification that, if a risk-limiting audit conducted under this part leads to a full manual tally of an election, State law requires that the State or election agency shall use the results of the full manual tally as the official results of the election; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H7B5622107AFE4B6296FAAA3B9A88F430" class="indent1"><num value="6">“(6) </num><content>such other information and assurances as the Commission may require.</content></paragraph></section>
<section id="H5C85DEF0D94C4182A8834647CCD99117"><num value="299B">“SEC. 299B. </num><heading>AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS.</heading><content class="block">“There are authorized to be appropriated for grants under this part $20,000,000 for fiscal year 2019, to remain available until expended.”</content></section></part></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>

<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stA/pt2/s3012" id="HDBB8636A06484475944E5B6A94FC93D0"><num value="3012">SEC. 3012. </num><heading>GAO ANALYSIS OF EFFECTS OF AUDITS.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stA/pt2/s3012/a" id="HCFDE29991E6E4CBCA94502F201CE7B6F" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Analysis</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 6 months after the first election for Federal office is held after grants are first awarded to States for conducting risk-limiting under part 9 of subtitle D of title II of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (as added by section 3011) for conducting risk-limiting audits of elections for Federal office, the Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct an analysis of the extent to which such audits have improved the administration of such elections and the security of election infrastructure in the States receiving such grants.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stA/pt2/s3012/b" id="HB9332F4C035E4774B134FC1C1EBFB0A5" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report</inline>.—</heading><content>The Comptroller General of the United States shall submit a report on the analysis conducted under subsection (a) to the appropriate congressional committees.</content></subsection></section></part><part identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stA/pt3" id="H0250F370CFA04AC7BBCD54FC08573C47"><num value="3">PART 3—</num><heading>[RESERVED]</heading></part></subtitle>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB" id="HC3B87FEF92404BCFBAD6D46665E6DB31"><num value="B">Subtitle B—</num><heading>Security Measures</heading>
<section role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3101" id="HE36D84309B25409A8CC558171863857E"><num value="3101">SEC. 3101. </num><heading>ELECTION INFRASTRUCTURE DESIGNATION.</heading><content class="block">Subparagraph (J) of section 2001(3) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t6/s601/3">6 U.S.C. 601(3)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>, including election infrastructure</quotedText>” before the period at the end.</content></section>
<section role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3102" id="H216BF56F69CB4D45B559C592BDB23421"><num value="3102">SEC. 3102. </num><heading>TIMELY THREAT INFORMATION.</heading><content>Subsection (d) of section 201 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t6/s121">6 U.S.C. 121</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new paragraph:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H681A5AD219D6400A93A2A50F0D6DAD38" styleType="OLC">
<paragraph id="HDC9A5267027149E498097612CFDD0B91" class="indent1"><num value="24">“(24) </num><content>To provide timely threat information regarding election infrastructure to the chief State election official of the State with respect to which such information pertains.”</content></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">. </inline></content></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3103" id="H1DE16353B49641D39C726C087FED7E5A"><num value="3103">SEC. 3103. </num><heading>SECURITY CLEARANCE ASSISTANCE FOR ELECTION OFFICIALS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">In order to promote the timely sharing of information on threats to election infrastructure, the Secretary may—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3103/1" id="HABBEC1620AC04FA984D9D733E79492B1" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>help expedite a security clearance for the chief State election official and other appropriate State personnel involved in the administration of elections, as designated by the chief State election official;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3103/2" id="HB3293A4C12D149A0AAFF8294E6B6A74E" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>sponsor a security clearance for the chief State election official and other appropriate State personnel involved in the administration of elections, as designated by the chief State election official; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3103/3" id="H9021AACD5D844BDD9BF8E917E67895EC" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>facilitate the issuance of a temporary clearance to the chief State election official and other appropriate State personnel involved in the administration of elections, as designated by the chief State election official, if the Secretary determines classified information to be timely and relevant to the election infrastructure of the State at issue.</content></paragraph></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3104" id="H901A56B5A2EC45EEA7A4A382A79F8ACD"><num value="3104">SEC. 3104. </num><heading>SECURITY RISK AND VULNERABILITY ASSESSMENTS.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3104/a" id="H920012491317436BB928A2B9245DD39D" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Paragraph (6) of section 2209(c) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t6/s659/c">6 U.S.C. 659(c)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>(including by carrying out a security risk and vulnerability assessment)</quotedText>” after “<quotedText>risk management support</quotedText>”.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3104/b" id="HED3163CA142548779282817DC8978553" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prioritization to Enhance Election Security</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3104/b/1" id="HE01CB575FB2C41619F6A689E47BB5988" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 90 days after receiving a written request from a chief State election official, the Secretary shall, to the extent practicable, commence a security risk and vulnerability assessment (pursuant to paragraph (6) of section 227(c) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002, as amended by subsection (a)) on election infrastructure in the State at issue.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3104/b/2" id="H9B1B38640615482E910341634E7C048C" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Notification</inline>.—</heading><content>If the Secretary, upon receipt of a request described in paragraph (1), determines that a security risk and vulnerability assessment cannot be commenced within 90 days, the Secretary shall expeditiously notify the chief State election official who submitted such request.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3105" id="H532EBABA8C9D4FD18A9216C169C51C33"><num value="3105">SEC. 3105. </num><heading>ANNUAL REPORTS.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3105/a" id="H9C08619150074A9D84D9A2E01AE6AC05" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reports on Assistance and Assessments</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act and annually thereafter through 2026, the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3105/a/1" id="HAC27D38C26C3496EBFAEC7CFCAEC3147" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>efforts to carry out section 203 during the prior year, including specific information on which States were helped, how many officials have been helped in each State, how many security clearances have been sponsored in each State, and how many temporary clearances have been issued in each State; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3105/a/2" id="H183DD48B6BC045598DCC337A4F9E9A53" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>efforts to carry out section 205 during the prior year, including specific information on which States were helped, the dates on which the Secretary received a request for a security risk and vulnerability assessment pursuant to such section, the dates on which the Secretary commenced each such request, and the dates on which the Secretary transmitted a notification in accordance with subsection (b)(2) of such section.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3105/b" id="H0015505D805A437580A58277383A6E3D" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reports on Foreign Threats</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 90 days after the end of each fiscal year (beginning with fiscal year 2019), the Secretary and the Director of National Intelligence, in coordination with the heads of appropriate offices of the Federal government, shall submit a joint report to the appropriate congressional committees on foreign threats to elections in the United States, including physical and cybersecurity threats.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stB/s3105/c" id="HD84AA2F22831443A83E6D049804BB954" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Information From States</inline>.—</heading><content>For purposes of preparing the reports required under this section, the Secretary shall solicit and consider information and comments from States and election agencies, except that the provision of such information and comments by a State or election agency shall be voluntary and at the discretion of the State or agency.</content></subsection></section></subtitle>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC" id="HE7DEC1F184224568A07247DD7CB5256E"><num value="C">Subtitle C—</num><heading>Enhancing Protections for United States Democratic Institutions</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201" id="HE9E8F6766A694261B181F0B42AC86A79"><num value="3201">SEC. 3201. </num><heading>NATIONAL STRATEGY TO PROTECT UNITED STATES DEMOCRATIC INSTITUTIONS.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/a" id="HED8CC12EDCF342FD9A7036395BC2DD60" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the President, acting through the Secretary, in consultation with the Chairman, the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of State, the Attorney General, the Secretary of Education, the Director of National Intelligence, the Chairman of the Federal Election Commission, and the heads of any other appropriate Federal agencies, shall issue a national strategy to protect against cyber attacks, influence operations, disinformation campaigns, and other activities that could undermine the security and integrity of United States democratic institutions.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/b" id="H9F8940C2E739481183F6C070EE510948" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Considerations</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The national strategy required under subsection (a) shall include consideration of the following:</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/b/1" id="HB09925D946A14396A9E1C1FB8A862B52" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>The threat of a foreign state actor, foreign terrorist organization (as designated pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t8/s1189">8 U.S.C. 1189</ref>)), or a domestic actor carrying out a cyber attack, influence operation, disinformation campaign, or other activity aimed at undermining the security and integrity of United States democratic institutions.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/b/2" id="HE358D684ED554296BB477BF6E4950D27" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>The extent to which United States democratic institutions are vulnerable to a cyber attack, influence operation, disinformation campaign, or other activity aimed at undermining the security and integrity of such democratic institutions.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/b/3" id="H93DAD12A910C400F951EC695F9427167" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>Potential consequences, such as an erosion of public trust or an undermining of the rule of law, that could result from a successful cyber attack, influence operation, disinformation campaign, or other activity aimed at undermining the security and integrity of United States democratic institutions.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/b/4" id="H02C6627484FD48B2AF5688F5488A20F8" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>Lessons learned from other Western governments the institutions of which were subject to a cyber attack, influence operation, disinformation campaign, or other activity aimed at undermining the security and integrity of such institutions, as well as actions that could be taken by the United States Government to bolster collaboration with foreign partners to detect, deter, prevent, and counter such activities.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/b/5" id="H5950D896596240C7B9FB267B4EF162FB" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>Potential impacts such as an erosion of public trust in democratic institutions as could be associated with a successful cyber breach or other activity negatively-affecting election infrastructure.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/b/6" id="HA163B42D52074E6AA7DC22E9DF81D3FF" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>Roles and responsibilities of the Secretary, the Chairman, and the heads of other Federal entities and non-Federal entities, including chief State election officials and representatives of multi-state information sharing and analysis center.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/b/7" id="HBF1AABB778794748A92800F057EDDA81" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>Any findings, conclusions, and recommendations to strengthen protections for United States democratic institutions that have been agreed to by a majority of Commission members on the National Commission to Protect United States Democratic Institutions, authorized pursuant to section 32002.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/c" id="H8C71C316ECC5436DB68F44B1DAEC8640" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Implementation Plan</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 90 days after the issuance of the national strategy required under subsection (a), the President, acting through the Secretary, in coordination with the Chairman, shall issue an implementation plan for Federal efforts to implement such strategy that includes the following:</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/c/1" id="HE32C501BE1BD4D32A284D23EE77D08B1" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>Strategic objectives and corresponding tasks.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/c/2" id="H3C05665242AA444F9762D0B140726456" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>Projected timelines and costs for the tasks referred to in paragraph (1).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/c/3" id="H849B587845D24E86AC49E17AD028BD3D" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>Metrics to evaluate performance of such tasks.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3201/d" id="H7E02E3233D2745B29DEA118BFEE2BCD6" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Classification</inline>.—</heading><content>The national strategy required under subsection (a) shall be in unclassified form but may contain a classified annex.</content></subsection></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202" id="HA14CA4BA1B8242809D0B9E2F8977BCDC"><num value="3202">SEC. 3202. </num><heading>NATIONAL COMMISSION TO PROTECT UNITED STATES DEMOCRATIC INSTITUTIONS.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/a" id="H87AFBD6E7FD34ECBA672F307E7FD6D1E" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Establishment</inline>.—</heading><content>There is established within the legislative branch the National Commission to Protect United States Democratic Institutions (hereafter in this section referred to as the “Commission”).</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/b" id="H00EE1BE29F42438BB4BCDB0EBD3709D3" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Purpose</inline>.—</heading><content>The purpose of the Commission is to counter efforts to undermine democratic institutions within the United States.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/c" id="H8D1485237F3C483484E4CFAB85426846" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Composition</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/c/1" id="HC619B562AEB844AAB909F1F79B156904" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Membership</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The Commission shall be composed of 10 members appointed for the life of the Commission as follows:</chapeau>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/c/1/A" id="H3C8ED4E7B8444792B9C7B3DB42D79114" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>One member shall be appointed by the Secretary.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/c/1/B" id="HABDC747426BD4EF5AF28A50087CA5EA6" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>One member shall be appointed by the Chairman.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/c/1/C" id="HD389010042314A64BE0609AB8CBBDD27" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>2 members shall be appointed by the majority leader of the Senate, in consultation with the Chairman of the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, the Chairman of the Committee on the Judiciary, and the Chairman of the Committee on Rules and Administration.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/c/1/D" id="H6C3F9718F971484B8C343730A95B4764" class="indent2"><num value="D">(D) </num><content>2 members shall be appointed by the minority leader of the Senate, in consultation with the ranking minority member of the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, the ranking minority member of the Committee on the Judiciary, and the ranking minority member of the Committee on Rules and Administration.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/c/1/E" id="H03FFDCF66C0848F5905FE251A70F4869" class="indent2"><num value="E">(E) </num><content>2 members shall be appointed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives, in consultation with the Chairman of the Committee on Homeland Security, the Chairman of the Committee on House Administration, and the Chairman of the Committee on the Judiciary.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/c/1/F" id="H557038FBFEA14A579EB25F7EA0B43360" class="indent2"><num value="F">(F) </num><content>2 members shall be appointed by the minority leader of the House of Representatives, in consultation with the ranking minority member of the Committee on Homeland Security, the ranking minority member of the Committee on the Judiciary, and the ranking minority member of the Committee on House Administration.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/c/2" id="HFE92C77210844911997B7FEA480BF31A" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Qualifications</inline>.—</heading><content>Individuals shall be selected for appointment to the Commission solely on the basis of their professional qualifications, achievements, public stature, experience, and expertise in relevant fields, including, but not limited to cybersecurity, national security, and the Constitution of the United States.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/c/3" id="HB0C7FD4441284ACBADDD941732ADCB18" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">No compensation for service</inline>.—</heading><content>Members shall not receive compensation for service on the Commission, but shall receive travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, in accordance with <ref href="/us/usc/t5/ch57">chapter 57 of title 5, United States Code</ref>.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/c/4" id="HA1F7349142234BD5BB05695A3B75527E" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Deadline for appointment</inline>.—</heading><content>All members of the Commission shall be appointed no later than 60 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/c/5" id="H2998D048433043BD938006FEB94B7821" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Vacancies</inline>.—</heading><content>A vacancy on the Commission shall not affect its powers and shall be filled in the manner in which the original appointment was made. The appointment of the replacement member shall be made not later than 60 days after the date on which the vacancy occurs.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/d" id="HB45E0E6F90F543B3B345D29A5BADD88F" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Chair and Vice Chair</inline>.—</heading><content>The Commission shall elect a Chair and Vice Chair from among its members.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/e" id="H00D1D5E7825F48BB95B31C4224EE4F04" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Quorum and Meetings</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/e/1" id="H84F653B523E64EBCBF6ABCCF57EF9D26" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Quorum</inline>.—</heading><content>The Commission shall meet and begin the operations of the Commission not later than 30 days after the date on which all members have been appointed or, if such meeting cannot be mutually agreed upon, on a date designated by the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President pro Tempore of the Senate. Each subsequent meeting shall occur upon the call of the Chair or a majority of its members. A majority of the members of the Commission shall constitute a quorum, but a lesser number may hold meetings.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/e/2" id="H923E93280E5749D48F898F2AB29F4717" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Authority of individuals to act for commission</inline>.—</heading><content>Any member of the Commission may, if authorized by the Commission, take any action that the Commission is authorized to take under this section.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/f" id="H23230F3F6657493B9B605A00F4ECEF3B" class="indent0"><num value="f">(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Powers</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/f/1" id="H0B1D76428A8E4BF8B0D31879416C9C25" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Hearings and evidence</inline>.—</heading><content>The Commission (or, on the authority of the Commission, any subcommittee or member thereof) may, for the purpose of carrying out this section, hold hearings and sit and act at such times and places, take such testimony, receive such evidence, and administer such oaths as the Commission considers advisable to carry out its duties.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/f/2" id="HCF91243B3F824CA8BA1811134D2A691C" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Contracting</inline>.—</heading><content>The Commission may, to such extent and in such amounts as are provided in appropriation Acts, enter into contracts to enable the Commission to discharge its duties under this section.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/g" id="H573E5D7B9609432F892EAF673D3796E6" class="indent0"><num value="g">(g) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Assistance From Federal Agencies</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/g/1" id="HD102006C5A9E45E8991935E91F2CA2B9" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">General services administration</inline>.—</heading><content>The Administrator of General Services shall provide to the Commission on a reimbursable basis administrative support and other services for the performance of the Commission’s functions.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/g/2" id="HC41277525E3C4A22ACEB628F4D78AD8A" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Other departments and agencies</inline>.—</heading><content>In addition to the assistance provided under paragraph (1), the Department of Homeland Security, the Election Assistance Commission, and other appropriate departments and agencies of the United States shall provide to the Commission such services, funds, facilities, and staff as they may determine advisable and as may be authorized by law.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/h" id="HC51A90BB8454499C97180BA9F62A35A6" class="indent0"><num value="h">(h) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Public Meetings</inline>.—</heading><content>Any public meetings of the Commission shall be conducted in a manner consistent with the protection of information provided to or developed for or by the Commission as required by any applicable statute, regulation, or Executive order.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/i" id="HBEDE4D90CD094729948217B3DADFE104" class="indent0"><num value="i">(i) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Security Clearances</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/i/1" id="HD5864ED6F7C14986847EE4D3F7BAC25F" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>The heads of appropriate departments and agencies of the executive branch shall cooperate with the Commission to expeditiously provide Commission members and staff with appropriate security clearances to the extent possible under applicable procedures and requirements.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/i/2" id="H672CA8F57E124CC38D63DB1359BCA5EE" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Preferences</inline>.—</heading><content>In appointing staff, obtaining detailees, and entering into contracts for the provision of services for the Commission, the Commission shall give preference to individuals otherwise who have active security clearances.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/j" id="HD25F8544FDC744DCAB7F5011F4324D5D" class="indent0"><num value="j">(j) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reports</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/j/1" id="H4B78CAD1D82E476E996C3783125EB940" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Interim reports</inline>.—</heading><content>At any time prior to the submission of the final report under paragraph (2), the Commission may submit interim reports to the President and Congress such findings, conclusions, and recommendations to strengthen protections for democratic institutions in the United States as have been agreed to by a majority of the members of the Commission.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/j/2" id="H008F8E2011F148BCBABF0C5C95D08AB7" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Final report</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 18 months after the date of the first meeting of the Commission, the Commission shall submit to the President and Congress a final report containing such findings, conclusions, and recommendations to strengthen protections for democratic institutions in the United States as have been agreed to by a majority of the members of the Commission.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/k" id="H498A6AAF000C4895B5F5516A94FDA79D" class="indent0"><num value="k">(k) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Termination</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/k/1" id="H71A2062ACC194A8FB27B35B9BC59CF31" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>The Commission shall terminate upon the expiration of the 60-day period which begins on the date on which the Commission submits the final report required under subsection (j)(2).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stC/s3202/k/2" id="HC47FE4FD9BBD4A8E9C11E6201BE1CC77" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Administrative activities prior to termination</inline>.—</heading><content>During the 60-day period described in paragraph (2), the Commission may carry out such administrative activities as may be required to conclude its work, including providing testimony to committees of Congress concerning the final report and disseminating the final report.</content></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle>

<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stD/s3301/a" id="HEA309561AB3A41D39A3CB915FCA59117" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requiring Testing of Existing Voting Systems</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stD/s3301/a/1" id="HE5E7EF1C704045BB8F234CF64972BA54" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 231(a) of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20971/a">52 U.S.C. 20971(a)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new paragraph:

<paragraph id="HD6FCC15B33D34A64BA6DDB715945A198" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Testing to ensure compliance with guidelines</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="HFD59E20F1B844C76AB081A422364CD27" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Testing</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 9 months before the date of each regularly scheduled general election for Federal office, the Commission shall provide for the testing by accredited laboratories under this section of the voting system hardware and software which was certified for use in the most recent such election, on the basis of the most recent voting system guidelines applicable to such hardware or software (including election cybersecurity guidelines) issued under this Act.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HE69B8C063118451AAD3357D2AAF8E497" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Decertification of hardware or software failing to meet guidelines</inline>.—</heading><content>If, on the basis of the testing described in subparagraph (A), the Commission determines that any voting system hardware or software does not meet the most recent guidelines applicable to such hardware or software issued under this Act, the Commission shall decertify such hardware or software.”</content></subparagraph></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph>
