<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE" id="HC2B5DF3238014A299902ADAAB5D027E6"><num value="E">Subtitle E—</num><heading>Preventing Election Hacking</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3401" id="HE4B99C7E84C74620A087D310B5D6113C"><num value="3401">SEC. 3401. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This subtitle may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="subtitle">Prevent Election Hacking Act of 2019</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402" id="H57BE1A1C9A154EB1A4CB8BB7AA26CDA5"><num value="3402">SEC. 3402. </num><heading>ELECTION SECURITY BUG BOUNTY PROGRAM.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402/a" id="H25870B88914B490784F7B6EF1C8D1ED9" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Establishment</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall establish a program to be known as the “Election Security Bug Bounty Program” (hereafter in this subtitle referred to as the “Program”) to improve the cybersecurity of the systems used to administer elections for Federal office by facilitating and encouraging assessments by independent technical experts, in cooperation with State and local election officials and election service providers, to identify and report election cybersecurity vulnerabilities.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402/b" id="HF53D49D577044BEE92AE6020AA3C8085" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Voluntary Participation by Election Officials and Election Service Providers</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402/b/1" id="HD5F07EF190704C54A17F69E2DAEBDBB4" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">No requirement to participate in program</inline>.—</heading><content>Participation in the Program shall be entirely voluntary for State and local election officials and election service providers.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402/b/2" id="H6380A1971D42428BB0220FC513533766" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Encouraging participation and input from election officials</inline>.—</heading><content>In developing the Program, the Secretary shall solicit input from, and encourage participation by, State and local election officials.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402/c" id="HE97DEFC2FA1F4C848AA97B8C8AABB374" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Activities Funded</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In establishing and carrying out the Program, the Secretary shall—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402/c/1" id="H17BDFB4C8D3C4E858F768DCD7F5FE065" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>establish a process for State and local election officials and election service providers to voluntarily participate in the Program;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402/c/2" id="H10F8F053E34549048C71DC1F40B0C880" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>designate appropriate information systems to be included in the Program;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402/c/3" id="HC503710F08E94F30B54B87483AE26E5F" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>provide compensation to eligible individuals, organizations, and companies for reports of previously unidentified security vulnerabilities within the information systems designated under subparagraph (A) and establish criteria for individuals, organizations, and companies to be considered eligible for such compensation in compliance with Federal laws;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402/c/4" id="H33B912E8040445B39145B083F43334E0" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>consult with the Attorney General on how to ensure that approved individuals, organizations, or companies that comply with the requirements of the Program are protected from prosecution under <ref href="/us/usc/t18/s1030">section 1030 of title 18, United States Code</ref>, and similar provisions of law, and from liability under civil actions for specific activities authorized under the Program;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402/c/5" id="H35A140198B5741BA98BED7E3E5B0D95A" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>consult with the Secretary of Defense and the heads of other departments and agencies that have implemented programs to provide compensation for reports of previously undisclosed vulnerabilities in information systems, regarding lessons that may be applied from such programs;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402/c/6" id="H9DA69FE3601E4924955F2CF5B256AC40" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>develop an expeditious process by which an individual, organization, or company can register with the Department, submit to a background check as determined by the Department, and receive a determination as to eligibility for participation in the Program; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402/c/7" id="H814836CE66D3498EB8640E3567F86EE2" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>engage qualified interested persons, including representatives of private entities, about the structure of the Program and, to the extent practicable, establish a recurring competition for independent technical experts to assess election systems for the purpose of identifying and reporting election cybersecurity vulnerabilities;</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3402/d" id="H4BB7EA4ACE42435AA2E7B87B05A60DE5" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Use of Service Providers</inline>.—</heading><content>The Secretary may award competitive contracts as necessary to manage the Program.</content></subsection></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3403" id="H41DF6D2B368641F4AB0BF446F331EC3F"><num value="3403">SEC. 3403. </num><heading>DEFINITIONS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">In this subtitle, the following definitions apply:</chapeau>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3403/1" id="HAFE2A67DE89E4D7EBFF1FAE77BE9707F" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>The terms “<term>election</term>” and “<term>Federal office</term>” have the meanings given such terms in section 301 of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30101">52 U.S.C. 30101</ref>).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3403/2" id="H13F9477540364811A22E9B90EFB78A72" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>The term “<term>election cybersecurity vulnerability</term>” means any security vulnerability (as defined in section 102 of the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015 (<ref href="/us/usc/t6/s1501">6 U.S.C. 1501</ref>)) that affects an election system.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3403/3" id="HA7C67F2D77444F0BAD4BC1C0F7DD549A" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>The term “<term>election service provider</term>” means any person providing, supporting, or maintaining an election system on behalf of a State or local election official, such as a contractor or vendor.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3403/4" id="H6AC6D75C56724F388BB13FF7920D2C2E" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>The term “<term>election system</term>” means any information system (as defined in <ref href="/us/usc/t44/s3502">section 3502 of title 44, United States Code</ref>) which is part of an election infrastructure.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3403/5" id="HD30BB8E26CE04001842EB0880E740598" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>The term “<term>Secretary</term>” means the Secretary of Homeland Security, or, upon designation by the Secretary of Homeland Security, the Deputy Secretary of Homeland Security, the Director of Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security of the Department of Homeland Security, or a Senate-confirmed official that reports to the Director.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3403/6" id="H28DC0A132149466F951EBB252DD3922A" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>The term “<term>State</term>” means each of the several States, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, Guam, American Samoa, the Commonwealth of Northern Mariana Islands, and the United States Virgin Islands.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stE/s3403/7" id="H77273EDE4C0D4655BDE8C81EFDBFB7B1" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>The term “<term>voting system</term>” has the meaning given such term in section 301(b) of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21081/b">52 U.S.C. 21081(b)</ref>).</content></paragraph></section></subtitle>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stF" id="H32AD6611C0C84132ACA7A562C609248F"><num value="F">Subtitle F—</num><heading>Miscellaneous Provisions</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stF/s3501" id="HE275763513FC476F91D02D2BD7DA1EF6"><num value="3501">SEC. 3501. </num><heading>DEFINITIONS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">Except as provided in section 3404, in this title, the following definitions apply:</chapeau>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stF/s3501/1" id="H4E454082C0EB43CD87AB25B0CBBC0678" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>The term “<term>Chairman</term>” means the chair of the Election Assistance Commission.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stF/s3501/2" id="H24A276BCF4DE40FDA76E2C515E8C5EC4" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>The term “<term>appropriate congressional committees</term>” means the Committees on Homeland Security and House Administration of the House of Representatives and the Committees on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and Rules and Administration of the Senate.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stF/s3501/3" id="H8815D2457C0D4AADA8629B27EDA934B3" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>The term “<term>chief State election official</term>” means, with respect to a State, the individual designated by the State under section 10 of the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s20509">52 U.S.C. 20509</ref>) to be responsible for coordination of the State’s responsibilities under such Act.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stF/s3501/4" id="H26A76BBB696843139FE482A83878A393" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>The term “<term>Commission</term>” means the Election Assistance Commission.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stF/s3501/5" id="HFA59807B8A7340CD8D0354002AD20E99" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>The term “<term>democratic institutions</term>” means the diverse range of institutions that are essential to ensuring an independent judiciary, free and fair elections, and rule of law.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stF/s3501/6" id="H1A5321C5D7F44A9A8C06658022A2EA9F" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>The term “<term>election agency</term>” means any component of a State, or any component of a unit of local government in a State, which is responsible for the administration of elections for Federal office in the State.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stF/s3501/7" id="H345C930291344C678630E6C4BA1F071D" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>The term “<term>election infrastructure</term>” means storage facilities, polling places, and centralized vote tabulation locations used to support the administration of elections for public office, as well as related information and communications technology, including voter registration databases, voting machines, electronic mail and other communications systems (including electronic mail and other systems of vendors who have entered into contracts with election agencies to support the administration of elections, manage the election process, and report and display election results), and other systems used to manage the election process and to report and display election results on behalf of an election agency.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stF/s3501/8" id="H1435990114934C8281103D740AA403DE" class="indent1"><num value="8">(8) </num><content>The term “<term>Secretary</term>” means the Secretary of Homeland Security.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stF/s3501/9" id="HC932ABC146514B388A77328F9C5B8060" class="indent1"><num value="9">(9) </num><content>The term “<term>State</term>” has the meaning given such term in section 901 of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s21141">52 U.S.C. 21141</ref>).</content></paragraph></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stF/s3502" id="H5DCA0DB420D54F2EB4934CB6327C1741"><num value="3502">SEC. 3502. </num><heading>INITIAL REPORT ON ADEQUACY OF RESOURCES AVAILABLE FOR IMPLEMENTATION.</heading><content class="block">Not later than 120 days after enactment of this Act, the Chairman and the Secretary shall submit a report to the appropriate committees of Congress, including the Committees on Homeland Security and House Administration of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate, analyzing the adequacy of the funding, resources, and personnel available to carry out this title and the amendments made by this title.</content></section></subtitle>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stG" id="H07B1E3CB6F98430FAF8107C47BAB7AE9"><num value="G">Subtitle G—</num><heading>Severability</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dA/tIII/stG/s3601" id="H5614F47683AB481EA3D72994129C3328"><num value="3601">SEC. 3601. </num><heading>SEVERABILITY.</heading><content class="block">If any provision of this title or amendment made by this title, or the application of a provision or amendment to any person or circumstance, is held to be unconstitutional, the remainder of this title and amendments made by this title, and the application of the provisions and amendment to any person or circumstance, shall not be affected by the holding.</content></section></subtitle></title></division>

<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stA" id="H311F788B7182476784131238BB12BD00"><num value="A">Subtitle A—</num><heading>Findings Relating to Illicit Money Undermining Our Democracy</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stA/s4001" id="H2EC0B4808BDC4285B135AA8075E3EFC6"><num value="4001">SEC. 4001. </num><heading>FINDINGS RELATING TO ILLICIT MONEY UNDERMINING OUR DEMOCRACY.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">Congress finds the following:</chapeau>
<paragraph role="definitions" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stA/s4001/1" id="HB7EDBA527DEE4764B8B193C7CCA7D032" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>Criminals, terrorists, and corrupt government officials frequently abuse anonymously held Limited Liability Companies (LLCs), also known as “<term>shell companies,</term>” to hide, move, and launder the dirty money derived from illicit activities such as trafficking, bribery, exploitation, and embezzlement. Ownership and control of the finances that run through shell companies are obscured to regulators and law enforcement because little information is required and collected when establishing these entities.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stA/s4001/2" id="HA4BAE772D11F43019AF0EDB03DDEA5D9" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>The public release of the “Panama Papers” in 2016 and the “Paradise Papers” in 2017 revealed that these shell companies often purchase and sell United States real estate. United States anti-money laundering laws do not apply to cash transactions involving real estate effectively concealing the beneficiaries and transactions from regulators and law enforcement.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stA/s4001/3" id="HC96D4C1EAF6446E8A92523987F70AE41" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>Congress should curb the use of anonymous shell companies for illicit purposes by requiring United States companies to disclose their beneficial owners, strengthening anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism finance laws.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stA/s4001/4" id="HD4B64E0187DC481B9BA2D0F5D3D31CD3" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>Congress should examine the money laundering and terrorist financing risks in the real estate market, including the role of anonymous parties, and review legislation to address any vulnerabilities identified in this sector.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stA/s4001/5" id="H7E848AD58D3648AEB666DD741413E813" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>Congress should examine the methods by which corruption flourishes and the means to detect and deter the financial misconduct that fuels this driver of global instability. Congress should monitor government efforts to enforce United States anti-corruption laws and regulations.</content></paragraph></section></subtitle>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB" id="HFBDD875EA34842F98869E53E7C3F38ED"><num value="B">Subtitle B—</num><heading>DISCLOSE Act</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/s4100" id="H004DF051A431494699C05B55660CE4F0"><num value="4100">SEC. 4100. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This subtitle may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="subtitle">Democracy Is Strengthened by Casting Light On Spending in Elections Act of 2019</shortTitle>” or the “<shortTitle role="subtitle">DISCLOSE Act of 2019</shortTitle>”.</content></section><part identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt1" id="H9DCD95EE28C442AE8B8BF7B6327B6AA9"><num value="1">PART 1—</num><heading>REGULATION OF CERTAIN POLITICAL SPENDING</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt1/s4101" id="H49ACBDE1F96140C4A649D6F499ECEE23"><num value="4101">SEC. 4101. </num><heading>APPLICATION OF BAN ON CONTRIBUTIONS AND EXPENDITURES BY FOREIGN NATIONALS TO DOMESTIC CORPORATIONS, LIMITED LIABILITY CORPORATIONS, AND PARTNERSHIPS THAT ARE FOREIGN-CONTROLLED, FOREIGN-INFLUENCED, AND FOREIGN-OWNED.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt1/s4101/a" id="HD15900AC4D134F89AE637E9B6FD773B7" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Application of Ban</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt1/s4101/a/1" id="HE5A0BD14262B4BF1ACB26713E935B527" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 319(b) of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30121/b">52 U.S.C. 30121(b)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt1/s4101/a/1/A" id="H4C2566FC6BD74496A81848259155ABD8" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>or</quotedText>” at the end of paragraph (1);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt1/s4101/a/1/B" id="H50922AE745E1474AA373ED677FB13261" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> the period at the end of paragraph (2) and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>; or</quotedText>”; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt1/s4101/a/1/C" id="H716D38507BF84DB58F2743506FD93A79" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new paragraph:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H51FDB08FFB664C51962A13D8A1814AF0" styleType="OLC">
<paragraph id="HF2F7C964F5794EBCA866EAE4FF51A27E" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><chapeau>except as provided under subsection (c), any corporation, limited liability corporation, or partnership which is not a foreign national described in paragraph (1) and—</chapeau>

<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt2/s4111/a" id="H93533C99C5964099A7452F6202FD84EF" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Disclosure Requirements for Corporations, Labor Organizations, and Certain Other Entities</inline>.—</heading>

<section id="H547592A0EAA440688C75C7BF82298FB1"><num value="324">“SEC. 324. </num><heading>DISCLOSURE OF CAMPAIGN-RELATED DISBURSEMENTS BY COVERED ORGANIZATIONS.</heading>
<subsection id="H6B10961C8D064236B29FF438808AD247" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Disclosure Statement</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HB6E59AC251EC4A63BD4BBD2A149B8B65" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Any covered organization that makes campaign-related disbursements aggregating more than $10,000 in an election reporting cycle shall, not later than 24 hours after each disclosure date, file a statement with the Commission made under penalty of perjury that contains the information described in paragraph (2)—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H62A3DA2302C14D8494916356DB9D59CD" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>in the case of the first statement filed under this subsection, for the period beginning on the first day of the election reporting cycle (or, if earlier, the period beginning one year before the first such disclosure date) and ending on the first such disclosure date; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H504541F2E2314B20B6BA7863AA06091A" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>in the case of any subsequent statement filed under this subsection, for the period beginning on the previous disclosure date and ending on such disclosure date.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H0ADFF45F656C480989862B8520B11D17" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Information described</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The information described in this paragraph is as follows:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HC3ACDFDC08B7406D8B6BD3FA3F9130EB" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><chapeau>The name of the covered organization and the principal place of business of such organization and, in the case of a covered organization that is a corporation (other than a business concern that is an issuer of a class of securities registered under section 12 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (<ref href="/us/usc/t15/s78l">15 U.S.C. 78l</ref>) or that is required to file reports under section 15(d) of that Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t15/s78o/d">15 U.S.C. 78o(d)</ref>)) or an entity described in subsection (e)(2), a list of the beneficial owners (as defined in paragraph (4)(A)) of the entity that—</chapeau>
<clause id="HB91FCB9189764893A0479A6082224619" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>identifies each beneficial owner by name and current residential or business street address; and</content></clause>
<clause id="HE269C1C6E2FA4C2F818926A44474C837" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>if any beneficial owner exercises control over the entity through another legal entity, such as a corporation, partnership, limited liability company, or trust, identifies each such other legal entity and each such beneficial owner who will use that other entity to exercise control over the entity.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H6E3E5632298F4E3282E6EEDBB47A5D71" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>The amount of each campaign-related disbursement made by such organization during the period covered by the statement of more than $1,000, and the name and address of the person to whom the disbursement was made.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H3C9851ADEF1B485384803A4E6D5C0B94" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>In the case of a campaign-related disbursement that is not a covered transfer, the election to which the campaign-related disbursement pertains and if the disbursement is made for a public communication, the name of any candidate identified in such communication and whether such communication is in support of or in opposition to a candidate.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H6C502F3458AC43C6904A2EA6AB722CC8" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><content>A certification by the chief executive officer or person who is the head of the covered organization that the campaign-related disbursement is not made in cooperation, consultation, or concert with or at the request or suggestion of a candidate, authorized committee, or agent of a candidate, political party, or agent of a political party.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H5B42690EA92E466E8B9CE858B242F7A5" class="indent2"><num value="E">“(E)</num><clause id="H213621A8C08A42E0ABA3F279D1F4EBD1" class="inline"><num value="i">(i) </num><chapeau>If the covered organization makes campaign-related disbursements using exclusively funds in a segregated bank account consisting of funds that were paid directly to such account by persons other than the covered organization that controls the account, for each such payment to the account—</chapeau>
<subclause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H419D19D836064DF3BB197E5FD722A1BA" class="indent4"><num value="I">“(I) </num><content>the name and address of each person who made such payment during the period covered by the statement;</content></subclause>
<subclause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H734B9523B90F4C2C8F3B38D189C32B53" class="indent4"><num value="II">“(II) </num><content>the date and amount of such payment; and</content></subclause>
<subclause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HDFE1187C0E1B40BA9AEEFA02C252B88A" class="indent4"><num value="III">“(III) </num><content>the aggregate amount of all such payments made by the person during the period beginning on the first day of the election reporting cycle (or, if earlier, the period beginning one year before the disclosure date) and ending on the disclosure date,</content></subclause></clause>
<continuation class="indent0" changed="added" origin="#HHA00" role="subparagraph">but only if such payment was made by a person who made payments to the account in an aggregate amount of $10,000 or more during the period beginning on the first day of the election reporting cycle (or, if earlier, the period beginning one year before the disclosure date) and ending on the disclosure date.</continuation>
<clause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H525EAE7CD8154BD09534F88FDBA465B7" class="indent2"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>In any calendar year after 2020, section 315(c)(1)(B) shall apply to the amount described in clause (i) in the same manner as such section applies to the limitations established under subsections (a)(1)(A), (a)(1)(B), (a)(3), and (h) of such section, except that for purposes of applying such section to the amounts described in subsection (b), the ‘base period’ shall be 2020.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HF16E2A52B634426299E3E34411592546" class="indent2"><num value="F">“(F)</num><clause id="H042549D8B7D24F02A89B5C82DA7600EE" class="inline"><num value="i">(i) </num><chapeau>If the covered organization makes campaign-related disbursements using funds other than funds in a segregated bank account described in subparagraph (E), for each payment to the covered organization—</chapeau>
<subclause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H4E966E7037F349128E94289E5FA737C6" class="indent4"><num value="I">“(I) </num><content>the name and address of each person who made such payment during the period covered by the statement;</content></subclause>
<subclause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H4B95BE00E56144FBA48DB5B0BA31B8DF" class="indent4"><num value="II">“(II) </num><content>the date and amount of such payment; and</content></subclause>
<subclause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H0AA902F5ACF24C569EDB54390469D7B9" class="indent4"><num value="III">“(III) </num><content>the aggregate amount of all such payments made by the person during the period beginning on the first day of the election reporting cycle (or, if earlier, the period beginning one year before the disclosure date) and ending on the disclosure date,</content></subclause></clause>
<continuation class="indent0" changed="added" origin="#HHA00" role="subparagraph">but only if such payment was made by a person who made payments to the covered organization in an aggregate amount of $10,000 or more during the period beginning on the first day of the election reporting cycle (or, if earlier, the period beginning one year before the disclosure date) and ending on the disclosure date.</continuation>

<subparagraph id="H26FCF80511624DBCB59413950C421C4C" class="indent2"><num value="G">“(G) </num><content>Such other information as required in rules established by the Commission to promote the purposes of this section.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HE9125DF83A80462FA770CCF3180E2588" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exceptions</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="HE504A7047F05427F8096543A1F571D1F" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Amounts received in ordinary course of business</inline>.—</heading><content>The requirement to include in a statement filed under paragraph (1) the information described in paragraph (2) shall not apply to amounts received by the covered organization in commercial transactions in the ordinary course of any trade or business conducted by the covered organization or in the form of investments (other than investments by the principal shareholder in a limited liability corporation) in the covered organization. For purposes of this subparagraph, amounts received by a covered organization as remittances from an employee to the employee’s collective bargaining representative shall be treated as amounts received in commercial transactions in the ordinary course of the business conducted by the covered organization.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H618E3983637E412BB51493536EEE8EE2" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Donor restriction on use of funds</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The requirement to include in a statement submitted under paragraph (1) the information described in subparagraph (F) of paragraph (2) shall not apply if—</chapeau>
<clause id="HD4BC7AEDD0CC4124BCF58C650B68D98F" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the person described in such subparagraph prohibited, in writing, the use of the payment made by such person for campaign-related disbursements; and</content></clause>
<clause id="HFDA221D46B34423F81C63C95C4949D2B" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>the covered organization agreed to follow the prohibition and deposited the payment in an account which is segregated from any account used to make campaign-related disbursements.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H47DD44971EE54CB78C03B5C94DFD015E" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Threat of harassment or reprisal</inline>.—</heading><content>The requirement to include any information relating to the name or address of any person (other than a candidate) in a statement submitted under paragraph (1) shall not apply if the inclusion of the information would subject the person to serious threats, harassment, or reprisals.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HBF93FE6C1DA94BC3B3141801F9B1624C" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Other definitions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>For purposes of this section:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H6EA69964CE774FC1B5BE7CB149D60CE5" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Beneficial owner defined</inline>.—</heading>
<clause role="definitions" id="H3D07F8DE604D4315B1EF615484341B38" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Except as provided in clause (ii), the term ‘<term>beneficial owner</term>’ means, with respect to any entity, a natural person who, directly or indirectly—</chapeau>
<subclause id="HFB4E847D7A284A9AB116D82489AB092F" class="indent4"><num value="I">“(I) </num><content>exercises substantial control over an entity through ownership, voting rights, agreement, or otherwise; or</content></subclause>
<subclause id="H9ED010DFB5734CD0A43B29D2322C7281" class="indent4"><num value="II">“(II) </num><content>has a substantial interest in or receives substantial economic benefits from the assets of an entity.</content></subclause></clause>
<clause role="definitions" id="HD24684A74A444E9AB344DD76EA68C8C9" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exceptions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term ‘<term>beneficial owner</term>’ shall not include—</chapeau>
<subclause id="H3B5E9A1F0D9E454FAA18D3DEF738EA64" class="indent4"><num value="I">“(I) </num><content>a minor child;</content></subclause>
<subclause id="H275447A107C74C8882983BCC8F77B1F6" class="indent4"><num value="II">“(II) </num><content>a person acting as a nominee, intermediary, custodian, or agent on behalf of another person;</content></subclause>
<subclause id="HBCDE542BD333492CA3A7B66E85BB10E7" class="indent4"><num value="III">“(III) </num><content>a person acting solely as an employee of an entity and whose control over or economic benefits from the entity derives solely from the employment status of the person;</content></subclause>
<subclause id="H091FDB6CACAE4A45A2054AF255EE7121" class="indent4"><num value="IV">“(IV) </num><content>a person whose only interest in an entity is through a right of inheritance, unless the person also meets the requirements of clause (i); or</content></subclause>
<subclause id="HBB211BDE06E548B1B1871B48F9740295" class="indent4"><num value="V">“(V) </num><content>a creditor of an entity, unless the creditor also meets the requirements of clause (i).</content></subclause></clause>
<clause id="H1FC237949E8B47868E6157987A39A4C0" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Anti-abuse rule</inline>.—</heading><content>The exceptions under clause (ii) shall not apply if used for the purpose of evading, circumventing, or abusing the provisions of clause (i) or paragraph (2)(A).</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph role="definitions" id="HD31CC5D674D4431A970A1CF601B6B54C" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Disclosure date</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term ‘<term>disclosure date</term>’ means—</chapeau>
<clause id="H22FD74563DB34E3794743456EF511D4E" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the first date during any election reporting cycle by which a person has made campaign-related disbursements aggregating more than $10,000; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H294D4937AE88450E9ED9683AF9CEA5FF" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>any other date during such election reporting cycle by which a person has made campaign-related disbursements aggregating more than $10,000 since the most recent disclosure date for such election reporting cycle.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph role="definitions" id="H672CC6B84E494CF58917466008342740" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Election reporting cycle</inline>.—</heading><content>The term ‘<term>election reporting cycle</term>’ means the 2-year period beginning on the date of the most recent general election for Federal office.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph role="definitions" id="H163526722B1A4E098F02FD49AC5CF8E1" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Payment</inline>.—</heading><content>The term ‘<term>payment</term>’ includes any contribution, donation, transfer, payment of dues, or other payment.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H9A647521099543F38546F893DD01F28A" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Coordination With Other Provisions</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HD5B7509AC3EA4299AFC7B4D16BA555DB" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Other reports filed with the commission</inline>.—</heading><content>Information included in a statement filed under this section may be excluded from statements and reports filed under section 304.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HC183A270ECC94EA18021FF3D79F4B5B9" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Treatment as separate segregated fund</inline>.—</heading><content>A segregated bank account referred to in subsection (a)(2)(E) may be treated as a separate segregated fund for purposes of section 527(f)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H50BFC9D07B5D459BA000049B66C12D32" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Filing</inline>.—</heading><content>Statements required to be filed under subsection (a) shall be subject to the requirements of section 304(d) to the same extent and in the same manner as if such reports had been required under subsection (c) or (g) of section 304.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="HDC727F8601BD4DB0A9992F89750E8B4B" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Campaign-Related Disbursement Defined</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H00A384223E4C41359CD30E095300BF33" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section, the term ‘<term>campaign-related disbursement</term>’ means a disbursement by a covered organization for any of the following:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HD0F9FD0F44744CCF931BB5ADDD62C74E" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>An independent expenditure which expressly advocates the election or defeat of a clearly identified candidate for election for Federal office, or is the functional equivalent of express advocacy because, when taken as a whole, it can be interpreted by a reasonable person only as advocating the election or defeat of a candidate for election for Federal office.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HC2DB5A381F2C41358B1B6DCCB00B35D9" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>Any public communication which refers to a clearly identified candidate for election for Federal office and which promotes or supports the election of a candidate for that office, or attacks or opposes the election of a candidate for that office, without regard to whether the communication expressly advocates a vote for or against a candidate for that office.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H8F6C26EEA45F444BA93CF165EE95B1BD" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>An electioneering communication, as defined in section 304(f)(3).</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H85B0141CDA844DF38B8A5F563FCAF9B0" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><content>A covered transfer.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB7C4603D9E444EB78B7139D98B081199" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Intent not required</inline>.—</heading><content>A disbursement for an item described in subparagraph (A), (B), (C), or (D) of paragraph (1) shall be treated as a campaign-related disbursement regardless of the intent of the person making the disbursement.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="definitions" id="HAA1D8226885A4792874B5E05EE3A583F" class="indent0"><num value="e">“(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Covered Organization Defined</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section, the term ‘<term>covered organization</term>’ means any of the following:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HA29D02E98BAC46FC8EB067A242A56FA9" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>A corporation (other than an organization described in section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3414037E2EC449E4A422AADA8705124C" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>A limited liability corporation that is not otherwise treated as a corporation for purposes of this Act (other than an organization described in section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6F5CB80B4B3247419436F273E3302FE4" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><content>An organization described in section 501(c) of such Code and exempt from taxation under section 501(a) of such Code (other than an organization described in section 501(c)(3) of such Code).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H85EC770BAC8D42A4A8CAD7544D7E9A37" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><content>A labor organization (as defined in section 316(b)).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9EE2E565EC9343478189DC3D4727C305" class="indent1"><num value="5">“(5) </num><content>Any political organization under section 527 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, other than a political committee under this Act (except as provided in paragraph (6)).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9B2947D279894CEABF8A8B739D9D2A8C" class="indent1"><num value="6">“(6) </num><content>A political committee with an account that accepts donations or contributions that do not comply with the contribution limits or source prohibitions under this Act, but only with respect to such accounts.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H3DF7EF1836CE4F3796D513B7F02DA13A" class="indent0"><num value="f">“(f) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Covered Transfer Defined</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HD2DD64B520C6439E87E4220FFC080B69" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In this section, the term ‘<term>covered transfer</term>’ means any transfer or payment of funds by a covered organization to another person if the covered organization—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H1D709CDD3EA64C68B737F809115F8B77" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><chapeau>designates, requests, or suggests that the amounts be used for—</chapeau>
<clause id="H379CD69682F847B4B7BE0F77932C23F0" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>campaign-related disbursements (other than covered transfers); or</content></clause>
<clause id="H74FD0005602F48008C2431B15AB1C2B2" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>making a transfer to another person for the purpose of making or paying for such campaign-related disbursements;</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H682903B4B888445F927B14CBB38E60B4" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><chapeau>made such transfer or payment in response to a solicitation or other request for a donation or payment for—</chapeau>
<clause id="H6A8047FF8F6B44E8A8D9C5C535CC9F41" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the making of or paying for campaign-related disbursements (other than covered transfers); or</content></clause>
<clause id="HFBE0658E11C546658D6EEC09F88CD123" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>making a transfer to another person for the purpose of making or paying for such campaign-related disbursements;</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H839672E61C294F7CAA601CA1B35745D5" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><chapeau>engaged in discussions with the recipient of the transfer or payment regarding—</chapeau>
<clause id="H15D6A39136134463ADCA49C4E0C2CB62" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the making of or paying for campaign-related disbursements (other than covered transfers); or</content></clause>
<clause id="H62D37B7842854BAC86837C10442198F3" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>donating or transferring any amount of such transfer or payment to another person for the purpose of making or paying for such campaign-related disbursements;</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H38506AD0384E4CBEAE2EE4FAC7ED2D59" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><content>made campaign-related disbursements (other than a covered transfer) in an aggregate amount of $50,000 or more during the 2-year period ending on the date of the transfer or payment, or knew or had reason to know that the person receiving the transfer or payment made such disbursements in such an aggregate amount during that 2-year period; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H7F19F764912E4049ACD361CE2FAB9AD6" class="indent2"><num value="E">“(E) </num><content>knew or had reason to know that the person receiving the transfer or payment would make campaign-related disbursements in an aggregate amount of $50,000 or more during the 2-year period beginning on the date of the transfer or payment.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H32B1ABEBE37E4517B0A9554397EA8C8E" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exclusions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term ‘<term>covered transfer</term>’ does not include any of the following:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H697A74560E754E56A00CC0ACD0F2346A" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>A disbursement made by a covered organization in a commercial transaction in the ordinary course of any trade or business conducted by the covered organization or in the form of investments made by the covered organization.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H1A6F54FB724A427C9436AFB466503B9F" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><chapeau>A disbursement made by a covered organization if—</chapeau>
<clause id="HCBF76A639969497C84B89CD01EF9C839" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the covered organization prohibited, in writing, the use of such disbursement for campaign-related disbursements; and</content></clause>
<clause id="HEA63C4321CB44EABAF63BAE90296C521" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>the recipient of the disbursement agreed to follow the prohibition and deposited the disbursement in an account which is segregated from any account used to make campaign-related disbursements.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HEDBA1295B512431DA18E83EE3C408E07" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Special rule regarding transfers among affiliates</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H29284C02F1E444C28147AA05D0D163F9" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Special rule</inline>.—</heading><content>A transfer of an amount by one covered organization to another covered organization which is treated as a transfer between affiliates under subparagraph (C) shall be considered a covered transfer by the covered organization which transfers the amount only if the aggregate amount transferred during the year by such covered organization to that same covered organization is equal to or greater than $50,000.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HBD5B367D047C49CBA0AE1D09E151F632" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Determination of amount of certain payments among affiliates</inline>.—</heading><content>In determining the amount of a transfer between affiliates for purposes of subparagraph (A), to the extent that the transfer consists of funds attributable to dues, fees, or assessments which are paid by individuals on a regular, periodic basis in accordance with a per-individual calculation which is made on a regular basis, the transfer shall be attributed to the individuals paying the dues, fees, or assessments and shall not be attributed to the covered organization.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H5D8AB61A6F714CD59A5F166E977AF9E6" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Description of transfers between affiliates</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>A transfer of amounts from one covered organization to another covered organization shall be treated as a transfer between affiliates if—</chapeau>
<clause id="HC9DC652848FC4ADB9C54FAFE8E3A114A" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>one of the organizations is an affiliate of the other organization; or</content></clause>
<clause id="H5D411EA2151D4AC99BF8756187E088A4" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>each of the organizations is an affiliate of the same organization,</content></clause>
<continuation class="indent0" role="subparagraph">except that the transfer shall not be treated as a transfer between affiliates if one of the organizations is established for the purpose of making campaign-related disbursements.</continuation></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H2A449F0AA44A4D669B5B96F619A79383" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Determination of affiliate status</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>For purposes of subparagraph (C), a covered organization is an affiliate of another covered organization if—</chapeau>
<clause id="H652FADDCCF7844DCB27334E88C35014C" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the governing instrument of the organization requires it to be bound by decisions of the other organization;</content></clause>
<clause id="HC6378AC5F21B4DFC87127F477F65EF7C" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>the governing board of the organization includes persons who are specifically designated representatives of the other organization or are members of the governing board, officers, or paid executive staff members of the other organization, or whose service on the governing board is contingent upon the approval of the other organization; or</content></clause>
<clause id="H43B59D9CAEC64841A4717B27A0DFEDB0" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>the organization is chartered by the other organization.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H2A3ACFFBD0E5493F9674A35A56162E52" class="indent2"><num value="E">“(E) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Coverage of transfers to affiliated section 501(c)(3) organizations</inline>.—</heading><content>This paragraph shall apply with respect to an amount transferred by a covered organization to an organization described in paragraph (3) of section 501(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 and exempt from tax under section 501(a) of such Code in the same manner as this paragraph applies to an amount transferred by a covered organization to another covered organization.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HE376B2B8A4E846CAAE379F40D93E71F4" class="indent0"><num value="g">“(g) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">No Effect on Other Reporting Requirements</inline>.—</heading><content>Nothing in this section shall be construed to waive or otherwise affect any other requirement of this Act which relates to the reporting of campaign-related disbursements.”</content></subsection></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt2/s4111/a/2" id="H15A7A8FABAB14899818F917F89B4FA2E" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Conforming amendment</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 304(f)(6) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30104">52 U.S.C. 30104</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>Any requirement</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>Except as provided in section 324(b), any requirement</quotedText>”.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt2/s4111/b" id="H665A2FBBB380497083F0A49D3DD3E33F" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Coordination With FinCEN</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt2/s4111/b/1" id="H9267B11809564816AA6C36C05204958C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>The Director of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network of the Department of the Treasury shall provide the Federal Election Commission with such information as necessary to assist in administering and enforcing section 324 of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971, as added by this section.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt2/s4111/b/2" id="HFEE4411BF5284A3EAE00F6D6E2CFF041" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Report</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 6 months after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Chairman of the Federal Election Commission, in consultation with the Director of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network of the Department of the Treasury, shall submit to Congress a report with recommendations for providing further legislative authority to assist in the administration and enforcement of such section 324.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>

<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt2/s4113" id="HB8D4026E67404A85888279708F3FF970"><num value="4113">SEC. 4113. </num><heading>EFFECTIVE DATE.</heading><content class="block">The amendments made by this part shall apply with respect to disbursements made on or after January 1, 2020, and shall take effect without regard to whether or not the Federal Election Commission has promulgated regulations to carry out such amendments.</content></section></part><part identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt3" id="H477174D254C444C69AC50BC46AD919D1"><num value="3">PART 3—</num><heading>OTHER ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS</heading>
<section role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt3/s4121" id="HFC9F98F128AF45EEB0344D6851D58DC1"><num value="4121">SEC. 4121. </num><heading>PETITION FOR CERTIORARI.</heading><content class="block">Section 307(a)(6) of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30107/a/6">52 U.S.C. 30107(a)(6)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>(including a proceeding before the Supreme Court on certiorari)</quotedText>” after “<quotedText>appeal</quotedText>”.</content></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt3/s4122" id="HFBD71907892745FC81A9935E023B838B"><num value="4122">SEC. 4122. </num><heading>JUDICIAL REVIEW OF ACTIONS RELATED TO CAMPAIGN FINANCE LAWS.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt3/s4122/a" id="H84F54A5ADBA44E74A4FB2FD15142890A" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Title IV of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30141/etseq">52 U.S.C. 30141 et seq.</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> after section 406 the following new section:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H337C7914F071442F94E34DA20861AD7D" styleType="OLC">
<section id="H7E6814B94283421A8588ECBED1AFD026"><num value="407">“SEC. 407. </num><heading>JUDICIAL REVIEW.</heading>
<subsection id="H872111A9BCE24726AFCAB964B9A47C0A" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Notwithstanding section 373(f), if any action is brought for declaratory or injunctive relief to challenge the constitutionality of any provision of this Act or of chapter 95 or 96 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, or is brought to with respect to any action of the Commission under chapter 95 or 96 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, the following rules shall apply:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="H6C923A07D2DA4677890372BC89116A1B" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><content>The action shall be filed in the United States District Court for the District of Columbia and an appeal from the decision of the district court may be taken to the Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H94C17E9CDDD14A279816C5D3A3804FEE" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><chapeau>In the case of an action relating to declaratory or injunctive relief to challenge the constitutionality of a provision—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H3887E5B1FAFD41E88ED0901FBD4AE999" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>a copy of the complaint shall be delivered promptly to the Clerk of the House of Representatives and the Secretary of the Senate; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HDB6BFF9673404D8DA719E93398CF5268" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>it shall be the duty of the United States District Court for the District of Columbia, the Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia, and the Supreme Court of the United States to advance on the docket and to expedite to the greatest possible extent the disposition of the action and appeal.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H7C37B11AF5144670826A76AD38E6A1C6" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Intervention by Members of Congress</inline>.—</heading><content>In any action in which the constitutionality of any provision of this Act or chapter 95 or 96 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is raised, any Member of the House of Representatives (including a Delegate or Resident Commissioner to the Congress) or Senate shall have the right to intervene either in support of or opposition to the position of a party to the case regarding the constitutionality of the provision. To avoid duplication of efforts and reduce the burdens placed on the parties to the action, the court in any such action may make such orders as it considers necessary, including orders to require interveners taking similar positions to file joint papers or to be represented by a single attorney at oral argument.</content></subsection>
<subsection id="H8DA8841C4FD34ABC8143A351FB312CBD" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Challenge by Members of Congress</inline>.—</heading><content>Any Member of Congress may bring an action, subject to the special rules described in subsection (a), for declaratory or injunctive relief to challenge the constitutionality of any provision of this Act or chapter 95 or 96 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.”</content></subsection></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt3/s4122/b" id="H7D8BF5CCF95C4E6FA58D0FC0151D5982" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Conforming Amendments</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt3/s4122/b/1" id="HF93F55F014E44BC881E49AD21A6B6EB5" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt3/s4122/b/1/A" id="H1C6AAFF1BAE04349926BAB31E652F403" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>Section 9011 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> to read as follows:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H37A5503CF3DD4C25A6704906714FCF82" styleType="OLC">
<section id="HD201EFEB00CF4A9AA0AA47922DC330FA"><num value="9011">“SEC. 9011. </num><heading>JUDICIAL REVIEW.</heading><content class="block">“For provisions relating to judicial review of certifications, determinations, and actions by the Commission under this chapter, see section 407 of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971.”</content></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt3/s4122/b/1/B" id="H8FF308B12E3E40A2A3293039BA52E021" class="indent2"><num value="B">(B) </num><content>Section 9041 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> to read as follows:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H22774C8AC5364014A3B9ABCCA1016139" styleType="OLC">
<section id="HFD04C03A581042D48A66E561748A02EF"><num value="9041">“SEC. 9041. </num><heading>JUDICIAL REVIEW.</heading><content class="block">“For provisions relating to judicial review of actions by the Commission under this chapter, see section 407 of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971.”</content></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt3/s4122/b/1/C" id="HB9FE12214C144F698EF9A5423924D5A4" class="indent2"><num value="C">(C) </num><content>Section 403 of the Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act of 2002 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30110">52 U.S.C. 30110 note</ref>) is <amendingAction type="repeal">repealed</amendingAction>.</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stB/pt3/s4122/c" id="HAE0089A019AD4BC6BE70BB567F6A3179" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective Date</inline>.—</heading><content>The amendments made by this section shall apply to actions brought on or after January 1, 2019.</content></subsection></section></part></subtitle>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC" id="H2CA0429E6C25415E8D920682489F3304"><num value="C">Subtitle C—</num><heading>Honest Ads</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4201" id="H2E7C2A4020464A52BE814D8EC1664381"><num value="4201">SEC. 4201. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This subtitle may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="subtitle">Honest Ads Act</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4202" id="H9D290F3211EF4759B6C00A3B8407EE5E"><num value="4202">SEC. 4202. </num><heading>PURPOSE.</heading><content class="block">The purpose of this subtitle is to enhance the integrity of American democracy and national security by improving disclosure requirements for online political advertisements in order to uphold the Supreme Court’s well-established standard that the electorate bears the right to be fully informed.</content></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203" id="HDD199EC299FF45EE80BBA62EBC36DABE"><num value="4203">SEC. 4203. </num><heading>FINDINGS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">Congress makes the following findings:</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203/1" id="H9BAB34DBE3F743618624B85345C7985C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>On January 6, 2017, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence published a report titled “Assessing Russian Activities and Intentions in Recent U.S. Elections”, noting that “Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered an influence campaign in 2016 aimed at the US presidential election . . .”. Moscow’s influence campaign followed a Russian messaging strategy that blends covert intelligence operation—such as cyber activity—with overt efforts by Russian Government agencies, state-funded media, third-party intermediaries, and paid social media users or “trolls”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203/2" id="H2B7A0EFDA39B48BE8400B62F9DA3512B" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>On November 24, 2016, The Washington Post reported findings from 2 teams of independent researchers that concluded Russians “exploited American-made technology platforms to attack U.S. democracy at a particularly vulnerable moment . . . as part of a broadly effective strategy of sowing distrust in U.S. democracy and its leaders.”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203/3" id="H5C6308613BF1496ABD5D1F45CDB57046" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>Findings from a 2017 study on the manipulation of public opinion through social media conducted by the Computational Propaganda Research Project at the Oxford Internet Institute found that the Kremlin is using pro-Russian bots to manipulate public discourse to a highly targeted audience. With a sample of nearly 1,300,000 tweets, researchers found that in the 2016 election’s 3 decisive States, propaganda constituted 40 percent of the sampled election-related tweets that went to Pennsylvanians, 34 percent to Michigan voters, and 30 percent to those in Wisconsin. In other swing States, the figure reached 42 percent in Missouri, 41 percent in Florida, 40 percent in North Carolina, 38 percent in Colorado, and 35 percent in Ohio.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203/4" id="HC2102E2A34B44FB2959FB00CE1EE3D63" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>On September 6, 2017, the nation’s largest social media platform disclosed that between June 2015 and May 2017, Russian entities purchased $100,000 in political advertisements, publishing roughly 3,000 ads linked to fake accounts associated with the Internet Research Agency, a pro-Kremlin organization. According to the company, the ads purchased focused “on amplifying divisive social and political messages . . .”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203/5" id="H2F2DA2A1EEEB4168975F08BB9E9B5C8E" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>In 2002, the Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act became law, establishing disclosure requirements for political advertisements distributed from a television or radio broadcast station or provider of cable or satellite television. In 2003, the Supreme Court upheld regulations on electioneering communications established under the Act, noting that such requirements “provide the electorate with information and insure that the voters are fully informed about the person or group who is speaking.”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203/6" id="H0984BE5C0B584A33AB3FEE2CC8A6D50F" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>According to a study from Borrell Associates, in 2016, $1,415,000,000 was spent on online advertising, more than quadruple the amount in 2012.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203/7" id="H45FAF06830AB4D9FB4F4F9D1DF84C31B" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>The reach of a few large internet platforms—larger than any broadcast, satellite, or cable provider—has greatly facilitated the scope and effectiveness of disinformation campaigns. For instance, the largest platform has over 210,000,000 Americans users—over 160,000,000 of them on a daily basis. By contrast, the largest cable television provider has 22,430,000 subscribers, while the largest satellite television provider has 21,000,000 subscribers. And the most-watched television broadcast in United States history had 118,000,000 viewers.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203/8" id="H4A8A8744555F48BC832B111AD9216BCA" class="indent1"><num value="8">(8) </num><content>The public nature of broadcast television, radio, and satellite ensures a level of publicity for any political advertisement. These communications are accessible to the press, fact-checkers, and political opponents; this creates strong disincentives for a candidate to disseminate materially false, inflammatory, or contradictory messages to the public. Social media platforms, in contrast, can target portions of the electorate with direct, ephemeral advertisements often on the basis of private information the platform has on individuals, enabling political advertisements that are contradictory, racially or socially inflammatory, or materially false.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203/9" id="H4EC0EDB138FD40A6A3B8CC1716261252" class="indent1"><num value="9">(9) </num><content>According to comScore, 2 companies own 8 of the 10 most popular smartphone applications as of June 2017, including the most popular social media and email services—which deliver information and news to users without requiring proactivity by the user. Those same 2 companies accounted for 99 percent of revenue growth from digital advertising in 2016, including 77 percent of gross spending. 79 percent of online Americans—representing 68 percent of all Americans—use the single largest social network, while 66 percent of these users are most likely to get their news from that site.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203/10" id="HFC82ADE0AC0B4631966EE7C4C8AE3B66" class="indent1"><num value="10">(10) </num><content>In its 2006 rulemaking, the Federal Election Commission noted that only 18 percent of all Americans cited the internet as their leading source of news about the 2004 Presidential election; by contrast, the Pew Research Center found that 65 percent of Americans identified an internet-based source as their leading source of information for the 2016 election.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203/11" id="H868CB9D30E6F483B9C5959ECCFA3A248" class="indent1"><num value="11">(11) </num><content>The Federal Election Commission, the independent Federal agency charged with protecting the integrity of the Federal campaign finance process by providing transparency and administering campaign finance laws, has failed to take action to address online political advertisements.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203/12" id="H88ED30FDC3994C0BA3477F2BA6582061" class="indent1"><num value="12">(12) </num><content>In testimony before the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence titled, “Disinformation: A Primer in Russian Active Measures and Influence Campaigns”, multiple expert witnesses testified that while the disinformation tactics of foreign adversaries have not necessarily changed, social media services now provide “platform[s] practically purpose-built for active measures[.]” Similarly, as Gen. Keith B. Alexander (RET.), the former Director of the National Security Agency, testified, during the Cold War “if the Soviet Union sought to manipulate information flow, it would have to do so principally through its own propaganda outlets or through active measures that would generate specific news: planting of leaflets, inciting of violence, creation of other false materials and narratives. But the news itself was hard to manipulate because it would have required actual control of the organs of media, which took long-term efforts to penetrate. Today, however, because the clear majority of the information on social media sites is uncurated and there is a rapid proliferation of information sources and other sites that can reinforce information, there is an increasing likelihood that the information available to average consumers may be inaccurate (whether intentionally or otherwise) and may be more easily manipulable than in prior eras.”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4203/13" id="HBFAF965301944A5F9DEECC17C936729E" class="indent1"><num value="13">(13) </num><content>Current regulations on political advertisements do not provide sufficient transparency to uphold the public’s right to be fully informed about political advertisements made online.</content></paragraph></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4204" id="HE6D690712E414C9CBD4EBD90F4ED576C"><num value="4204">SEC. 4204. </num><heading>SENSE OF CONGRESS.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">It is the sense of Congress that—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4204/1" id="HD67EB8BDD6AC4D96ADB8C3928182B66B" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>the dramatic increase in digital political advertisements, and the growing centrality of online platforms in the lives of Americans, requires the Congress and the Federal Election Commission to take meaningful action to ensure that laws and regulations provide the accountability and transparency that is fundamental to our democracy;.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4204/2" id="H79D8D1120C4043A2A8F8E78962554E5D" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>free and fair elections require both transparency and accountability which give the public a right to know the true sources of funding for political advertisements in order to make informed political choices and hold elected officials accountable; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4204/3" id="H09AB14A29A6049D695176A968FE50372" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>transparency of funding for political advertisements is essential to enforce other campaign finance laws, including the prohibition on campaign spending by foreign nationals.</content></paragraph></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4205" id="HAF9C9CDB11154439949E69F9728FB914"><num value="4205">SEC. 4205. </num><heading>EXPANSION OF DEFINITION OF PUBLIC COMMUNICATION.</heading>

<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4206" id="HCC524FA713A841F5B54F37FDBB83CF4C"><num value="4206">SEC. 4206. </num><heading>EXPANSION OF DEFINITION OF ELECTIONEERING COMMUNICATION.</heading>
