<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4207" id="HBEBA901D1CE84388B3090C30E34CE7D6"><num value="4207">SEC. 4207. </num><heading>APPLICATION OF DISCLAIMER STATEMENTS TO ONLINE COMMUNICATIONS.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4207/a" id="H7C94B7FF0C4F4EF3A4140E55FACE27B3" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Clear and Conspicuous Manner Requirement</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Subsection (a) of section 318 of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30120/a">52 U.S.C. 30120(a)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4207/a/1" id="H9498EA999C65437EA9CDE9F6C771BA7D" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>shall clearly state</quotedText>” each place it appears in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>shall state in a clear and conspicuous manner</quotedText>”; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4207/a/2" id="H06628A74C09041D8AC8BA58ACA35CA24" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following flush sentence: “<quotedText>For purposes of this section, a communication does not make a statement in a clear and conspicuous manner if it is difficult to read or hear or if the placement is easily overlooked.</quotedText>”.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4207/b" id="H4E7373325D9F48CD905B37B9D1A7B242" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Special Rules for Qualified Internet or Digital Communications</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4207/b/1" id="H2331710A281F430F841FC8392F11465B" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 318 of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30120">52 U.S.C. 30120</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new subsection:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H3D635F27E8134DFCA24E0515EF72AB85" styleType="OLC">
<subsection id="H435CDDE707B44F9EB16656203A3D29B6" class="indent0"><num value="e">“(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Special Rules for Qualified Internet or Digital Communications</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H7621376917AD40358E039B8AB215011D" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Special rules with respect to statements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In the case of any qualified internet or digital communication (as defined in section 304(f)(3)(D)) which is disseminated through a medium in which the provision of all of the information specified in this section is not possible, the communication shall, in a clear and conspicuous manner—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HF10BBEB0BCBC4FA3BB9AFA9B60788253" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>state the name of the person who paid for the communication; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H588D379E8E2C4E8A8769EF61634F4A59" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>provide a means for the recipient of the communication to obtain the remainder of the information required under this section with minimal effort and without receiving or viewing any additional material other than such required information.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H010484A023404E9BB673B27AE137AA9E" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Safe harbor for determining clear and conspicuous manner</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>A statement in qualified internet or digital communication (as defined in section 304(f)(3)(D)) shall be considered to be made in a clear and conspicuous manner as provided in subsection (a) if the communication meets the following requirements:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HE11F75A461CE4044873524F2F035DD33" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Text or graphic communications</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In the case of a text or graphic communication, the statement—</chapeau>
<clause id="HB63338A025334AE3813359B737A0F5E6" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>appears in letters at least as large as the majority of the text in the communication; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H5B5F909626F7437BAD15BABD919B593B" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>meets the requirements of paragraphs (2) and (3) of subsection (c).</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H526B137E9753409D9E0B2265B3674AA6" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Audio communications</inline>.—</heading><content>In the case of an audio communication, the statement is spoken in a clearly audible and intelligible manner at the beginning or end of the communication and lasts at least 3 seconds.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H641DB21850B74E59A9647D4AC388D40D" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Video communications</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In the case of a video communication which also includes audio, the statement—</chapeau>
<clause id="H560F89EDAF8E4C6A84F572B4C773B6C2" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>is included at either the beginning or the end of the communication; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H194534CC3A0F4555B0E4AF4257BF5535" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><chapeau>is made both in—</chapeau>
<subclause id="H351F005DDAC54088AAA2CD8A0A413B62" class="indent4"><num value="I">“(I) </num><content>a written format that meets the requirements of subparagraph (A) and appears for at least 4 seconds; and</content></subclause>
<subclause id="H0789424FB5514CD3BCA1EB58C5406C12" class="indent4"><num value="II">“(II) </num><content>an audible format that meets the requirements of subparagraph (B).</content></subclause></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H60FAAB33F4BD475798DAA455C0218FAB" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Other communications</inline>.—</heading><content>In the case of any other type of communication, the statement is at least as clear and conspicuous as the statement specified in subparagraph (A), (B), or (C).”</content></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4207/b/2" id="HDCBDF4DA7D0844CEBA01B1E4896F183C" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Nonapplication of certain exceptions</inline>.—</heading><content>The exceptions provided in <ref href="/us/cfr/t11/s110.11/f/1/i) and (ii">section 110.11(f)(1)(i) and (ii) of title 11, Code of Federal Regulations</ref>, or any successor to such rules, shall have no application to qualified internet or digital communications (as defined in section 304(f)(3)(D) of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971).</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4207/c" id="HC69541EDB4A94839ACFF45A93F646BCC" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Modification of Additional Requirements for Certain Communications</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 318(d) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30120/d">52 U.S.C. 30120(d)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4207/c/1" id="HE2BBF03B5D854DE099DE33B5D6D3C636" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><chapeau>in paragraph (1)(A)—</chapeau>
<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4207/c/1/A" id="H6D0784BD556A42E5BD9718DF5215AC7F" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>which is transmitted through radio</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>which is in an audio format</quotedText>”; and</content></subparagraph>

<subparagraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4207/c/2/A" id="HC9F465CCCFF6419DB8E1BA5AEDD49093" class="indent2"><num value="A">(A) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>which is transmitted through television</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>which is in video format</quotedText>”; and</content></subparagraph>

<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4207/c/3" id="HE21E55608AEE483387BDF9AD8C293E38" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><chapeau>in paragraph (2)—</chapeau>

<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4208" id="HE6A2BA7189BD4E5E8B6931AA7880B1D0"><num value="4208">SEC. 4208. </num><heading>POLITICAL RECORD REQUIREMENTS FOR ONLINE PLATFORMS.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4208/a" id="H933EDB89CAC84037AF7924E54104ABFA" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In General</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 304 of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30104">52 U.S.C. 30104</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new subsection:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H3DA23235FCD24BEFA82797B5F48D9D77" styleType="OLC">
<subsection id="HE074B367B73D48B2AFE0C64662685AB8" class="indent0"><num value="j">“(j) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Disclosure of Certain Online Advertisements</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HBFAAE63A661C480FA63CAF099A46AC15" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H80CD5321B307460C8A5ABDF67707888B" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requirements for online platforms</inline>.—</heading><content>An online platform shall maintain, and make available for online public inspection in machine readable format, a complete record of any request to purchase on such online platform a qualified political advertisement which is made by a person whose aggregate requests to purchase qualified political advertisements on such online platform during the calendar year exceeds $500.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H7F37340D596A4408808304708128B0FF" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requirements for advertisers</inline>.—</heading><content>Any person who requests to purchase a qualified political advertisement on an online platform shall provide the online platform with such information as is necessary for the online platform to comply with the requirements of subparagraph (A).</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H5AB41E4698EE46DF9330E3076F661DCB" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Contents of record</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>A record maintained under paragraph (1)(A) shall contain—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H34F40BAC09A54C71811E286D7510D8D5" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>a digital copy of the qualified political advertisement;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H44E824672D5C428BAAD428FEDE7D596E" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>a description of the audience targeted by the advertisement, the number of views generated from the advertisement, and the date and time that the advertisement is first displayed and last displayed; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HC7EC7C272B8147D693C2BFE3EB17C6B8" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><chapeau>information regarding—</chapeau>
<clause id="HEDE30DC115DE4B98922AB145674CD179" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the average rate charged for the advertisement;</content></clause>
<clause id="HB223FC7F8848428FA9456F1806FF7C8B" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>the name of the candidate to which the advertisement refers and the office to which the candidate is seeking election, the election to which the advertisement refers, or the national legislative issue to which the advertisement refers (as applicable);</content></clause>
<clause id="H1B85A9DF33FF4D5DB1EDC8695D5D8ECF" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>in the case of a request made by, or on behalf of, a candidate, the name of the candidate, the authorized committee of the candidate, and the treasurer of such committee; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H0149CB701B5F4701AD9201E2B0144E02" class="indent3"><num value="iv">“(iv) </num><content>in the case of any request not described in clause (iii), the name of the person purchasing the advertisement, the name and address of a contact person for such person, and a list of the chief executive officers or members of the executive committee or of the board of directors of such person.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H9897426C905644DC9C3C8C4AD5C0A2CF" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Online platform</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>For purposes of this subsection, the term ‘<term>online platform</term>’ means any public-facing website, web application, or digital application (including a social network, ad network, or search engine) which—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H49A6CD494DAB4F8A9E7B6DD13F278E30" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>sells qualified political advertisements; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H05F3D2C1E5774FF0AD605B481B78C07A" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>has 50,000,000 or more unique monthly United States visitors or users for a majority of months during the preceding 12 months.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HCC421F3754444424A9BD70B174CF8A72" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Qualified political advertisement</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>For purposes of this subsection, the term ‘<term>qualified political advertisement</term>’ means any advertisement (including search engine marketing, display advertisements, video advertisements, native advertisements, and sponsorships) that—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="H56EFE507D0654D4E8E0C7A73D8A704A8" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>is made by or on behalf of a candidate; or</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H1E1407EF62534D73A34F1E47AC8D6A9F" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><chapeau>communicates a message relating to any political matter of national importance, including—</chapeau>
<clause id="H8334A41532CF476EAEBA32A60150FDF3" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>a candidate;</content></clause>
<clause id="H86C1F91CBEC145B0A939D012C04C2B4F" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>any election to Federal office; or</content></clause>
<clause id="HFD01E7AEA50C464C93B902F7A45853CA" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>a national legislative issue of public importance.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HBAFFEE5CAE7D49CAB2E858B728D39038" class="indent1"><num value="5">“(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Time to maintain file</inline>.—</heading><content>The information required under this subsection shall be made available as soon as possible and shall be retained by the online platform for a period of not less than 4 years.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD98314F0D07C467696D19F6D48D9F453" class="indent1"><num value="6">“(6) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Safe harbor for platforms making best efforts to identify requests which are subject to record maintenance requirements</inline>.—</heading><content>In accordance with rules established by the Commission, if an online platform shows that the platform used best efforts to determine whether or not a request to purchase a qualified political advertisement was subject to the requirements of this subsection, the online platform shall not be considered to be in violation of such requirements.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H05FBDB991B77496294DDB6C3D534C095" class="indent1"><num value="7">“(7) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Penalties</inline>.—</heading><content>For penalties for failure by online platforms, and persons requesting to purchase a qualified political advertisement on online platforms, to comply with the requirements of this subsection, see section 309.”</content></paragraph></subsection></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4208/b" id="H600DF493C14C4BC895CC57F8A7E3864C" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Rulemaking</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Federal Election Commission shall establish rules—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4208/b/1" id="H8DFFD2AB8BF248259C289E2412FDC1DF" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>requiring common data formats for the record required to be maintained under section 304(j) of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (as added by subsection (a)) so that all online platforms submit and maintain data online in a common, machine-readable and publicly accessible format; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4208/b/2" id="H3B2C1E3630EF444D862BFDD556A101F7" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>establishing search interface requirements relating to such record, including searches by candidate name, issue, purchaser, and date; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4208/b/3" id="H594A9E71785549B6AA690F9881764CFD" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>establishing the criteria for the safe harbor exception provided under paragraph (6) of section 304(j) of such Act (as added by subsection (a)).</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4208/c" id="H8738480BB16F4B3586D0E5C5A28C588F" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Reporting</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than 2 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, and biannually thereafter, the Chairman of the Federal Election Commission shall submit a report to Congress on—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4208/c/1" id="H3A4B428BA31D4541BA56B95B3F0129A6" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>matters relating to compliance with and the enforcement of the requirements of section 304(j) of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971, as added by subsection (a);</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4208/c/2" id="HA63C8733D1A14337A7EA48E977751FF0" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>recommendations for any modifications to such section to assist in carrying out its purposes; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4208/c/3" id="H2D41D6A32AD94355BB63CDF4D0D17E6C" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>identifying ways to bring transparency and accountability to political advertisements distributed online for free.</content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stC/s4209" id="HC5295BEEF7AF45B38D6186616389E8BC"><num value="4209">SEC. 4209. </num><heading>PREVENTING CONTRIBUTIONS, EXPENDITURES, INDEPENDENT EXPENDITURES, AND DISBURSEMENTS FOR ELECTIONEERING COMMUNICATIONS BY FOREIGN NATIONALS IN THE FORM OF ONLINE ADVERTISING.</heading><content>Section 319 of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30121">52 U.S.C. 30121</ref>), as amended by section 4101(a)(2) and section 4101(b), is further amended by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new subsection:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HCC1F856105B34896BF945DC67080E1D5" styleType="OLC">
<subsection id="HF25A3CC341F74E05BE88EBE9B91B4BB4" class="indent0"><num value="e">“(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Responsibilities of Broadcast Stations, Providers of Cable and Satellite Television, and Online Platforms</inline>.—</heading><content>Each television or radio broadcast station, provider of cable or satellite television, or online platform (as defined in section 304(j)(3)) shall make reasonable efforts to ensure that communications described in section 318(a) and made available by such station, provider, or platform are not purchased by a foreign national, directly or indirectly.”</content></subsection></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></section></subtitle>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD" id="HB42A9A7BB0D243B793D38F2993E3913F"><num value="D">Subtitle D—</num><heading>Stand By Every Ad</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4301" id="H2D42A24113024762BDE6A78F804BFD38"><num value="4301">SEC. 4301. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This Act may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="act">Stand By Every Ad Act</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4302" id="HC3F5CEBA96824D0C8A1531BF92D7E4C7"><num value="4302">SEC. 4302. </num><heading>STAND BY EVERY AD.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4302/a" id="HBB25426881804C759AADC1EA4D726FE1" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Expanded Disclaimer Requirements for Certain Communications</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 318 of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30120">52 U.S.C. 30120</ref>), as amended by section 4207(b)(1), is further amended—</chapeau>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4302/a/1" id="HC05FA44107984E8BAEE4177E9B7DA110" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="redesignate">redesignating</amendingAction> subsection (e) as subsection (f); and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4302/a/2" id="H3BFD3F11C8C948E0B1C47B8B9EBDFB1C" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> after subsection (d) the following new subsection:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H2D58B81AFB874C7EB5CF467BDD60F0EF" styleType="OLC">
<subsection id="H8BBCEAC75C59435AB5CF9BFDCCEBE7DF" class="indent0"><num value="e">“(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Expanded Disclaimer Requirements for Communications Not Authorized by Candidates or Committees</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H37BE08C84087419EB4A802D9891F0B35" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Except as provided in paragraph (6), any communication described in paragraph (3) of subsection (a) which is transmitted in an audio or video format (including an Internet or digital communication), or which is an Internet or digital communication transmitted in a text or graphic format, shall include, in addition to the requirements of paragraph (3) of subsection (a), the following:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HD72AF69AEF274AEE84C1ED5FA75F8F63" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>The individual disclosure statement described in paragraph (2)(A) (if the person paying for the communication is an individual) or the organizational disclosure statement described in paragraph (2)(B) (if the person paying for the communication is not an individual).</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H81718A5FD528489CBBE7FBEBD9A75425" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><chapeau>If the communication is transmitted in a video format, or is an Internet or digital communication which is transmitted in a text or graphic format, and is paid for in whole or in part with a payment which is treated as a campaign-related disbursement under section 324—</chapeau>
<clause id="H61F3FB57E465414CAB2F4DF34A051097" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the Top Five Funders list (if applicable); or</content></clause>
<clause id="H94341677AA45414BA77273C765F7F70B" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>in the case of a communication which, as determined on the basis of criteria established in regulations issued by the Commission, is of such short duration that including the Top Five Funders list in the communication would constitute a hardship to the person paying for the communication by requiring a disproportionate amount of the content of the communication to consist of the Top Five Funders list, the name of a website which contains the Top Five Funders list (if applicable) or, in the case of an Internet or digital communication, a hyperlink to such website.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HCC1C8D53BF0345359CACCA448497810E" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><chapeau>If the communication is transmitted in an audio format and is paid for in whole or in part with a payment which is treated as a campaign-related disbursement under section 324—</chapeau>
<clause id="HC067585A7CE64655BF7C8D67BCD1D252" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the Top Two Funders list (if applicable); or</content></clause>
<clause id="HF8D49127D3D04405885624D2C408B480" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>in the case of a communication which, as determined on the basis of criteria established in regulations issued by the Commission, is of such short duration that including the Top Two Funders list in the communication would constitute a hardship to the person paying for the communication by requiring a disproportionate amount of the content of the communication to consist of the Top Two Funders list, the name of a website which contains the Top Two Funders list (if applicable).</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HAEB2EF577C83403BA315F8171A774447" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Disclosure statements described</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H15FB3243054B4E06B71A77AF7EBB42CB" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Individual disclosure statements</inline>.—</heading><content>The individual disclosure statement described in this subparagraph is the following: ‘I am ________, and I approve this message.’, with the blank filled in with the name of the applicable individual.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H9EB9AB097E34498DBF5F81EDC22862ED" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Organizational disclosure statements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The organizational disclosure statement described in this subparagraph is the following: ‘I am ________, the ________ of ________, and ________ approves this message.’, with—</chapeau>
<clause id="H9B182A1EFAC248D98F0ECFE5C3CF25C6" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the first blank to be filled in with the name of the applicable individual;</content></clause>
<clause id="HDE7A3E6227FB4CA2A6DCB9D10FA6DE26" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>the second blank to be filled in with the title of the applicable individual; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H8F39E74650064DE2AF205F5600942B05" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>the third and fourth blank each to be filled in with the name of the organization or other person paying for the communication.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1D5A818A24C0462AADF9C4EEBFD3BDB6" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Method of conveyance of statement</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H1364A095540D4484A8C4258B34536FD3" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Communications in text or graphic format</inline>.—</heading><content>In the case of a communication to which this subsection applies which is transmitted in a text or graphic format, the disclosure statements required under paragraph (1) shall appear in letters at least as large as the majority of the text in the communication.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H8E32F9B12E704A17ACADD092C0A674A6" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Communications transmitted in audio format</inline>.—</heading><content>In the case of a communication to which this subsection applies which is transmitted in an audio format, the disclosure statements required under paragraph (1) shall be made by audio by the applicable individual in a clear and conspicuous manner.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H79DCCE22441649929794F2A4F7DCB026" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Communications transmitted in video format</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In the case of a communication to which this subsection applies which is transmitted in a video format, the information required under paragraph (1)—</chapeau>
<clause id="HCE058ADDDE2F4408B3F5178730BD83ED" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>shall appear in writing at the end of the communication or in a crawl along the bottom of the communication in a clear and conspicuous manner, with a reasonable degree of color contrast between the background and the printed statement, for a period of at least 6 seconds; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H7055128413F442F8A9C7A454E554072D" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>shall also be conveyed by an unobscured, full-screen view of the applicable individual or by the applicable individual making the statement in voice-over accompanied by a clearly identifiable photograph or similar image of the individual, except in the case of a Top Five Funders list.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H2072186F3786458CBF7CEEEB4467629A" class="indent1"><num value="4">“(4) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Applicable individual defined</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>The term ‘<term>applicable individual</term>’ means, with respect to a communication to which this subsection applies—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HAC747697C7FE46B6B12D561F2E5495F2" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><content>if the communication is paid for by an individual, the individual involved;</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H180DBB29C47B4355A91786C09E5DD107" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>if the communication is paid for by a corporation, the chief executive officer of the corporation (or, if the corporation does not have a chief executive officer, the highest ranking official of the corporation);</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H3E27DB20C10D4B42ABFA20FFE1CF39C3" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>if the communication is paid for by a labor organization, the highest ranking officer of the labor organization; and</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H7A0190DCED3E47E191CF93A328EC9489" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><content>if the communication is paid for by any other person, the highest ranking official of such person.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HACA2A44981314322BBEEBD0F5E3DAB26" class="indent1"><num value="5">“(5) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Top five funders list and top two funders list defined</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph role="definitions" id="HB5459B1976D44E68B66E8C664D5F6B0C" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Top five funders list</inline>.—</heading><content>The term ‘<term>Top Five Funders list</term>’ means, with respect to a communication which is paid for in whole or in part with a campaign-related disbursement (as defined in section 324), a list of the five persons who, during the 12-month period ending on the date of the disbursement, provided the largest payments of any type in an aggregate amount equal to or exceeding $10,000 to the person who is paying for the communication and the amount of the payments each such person provided. If two or more people provided the fifth largest of such payments, the person paying for the communication shall select one of those persons to be included on the Top Five Funders list.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph role="definitions" id="HEDB56D7082E842C0BAFF017571EF87C9" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Top two funders list</inline>.—</heading><content>The term ‘<term>Top Two Funders list</term>’ means, with respect to a communication which is paid for in whole or in part with a campaign-related disbursement (as defined in section 324), a list of the persons who, during the 12-month period ending on the date of the disbursement, provided the largest and the second largest payments of any type in an aggregate amount equal to or exceeding $10,000 to the person who is paying for the communication and the amount of the payments each such person provided. If two or more persons provided the second largest of such payments, the person paying for the communication shall select one of those persons to be included on the Top Two Funders list.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H2E767B9CD8F24F4E83C7C0CE95E5FA96" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exclusion of certain payments</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>For purposes of subparagraphs (A) and (B), in determining the amount of payments made by a person to a person paying for a communication, there shall be excluded the following:</chapeau>
<clause id="H50F07AA9491C44D59A0E489B6121ACA6" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>Any amounts provided in the ordinary course of any trade or business conducted by the person paying for the communication or in the form of investments in the person paying for the communication.</content></clause>
<clause id="H2AA62EDBEC2B4B1AB18BCC70C671DD21" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>Any payment which the person prohibited, in writing, from being used for campaign-related disbursements, but only if the person paying for the communication agreed to follow the prohibition and deposited the payment in an account which is segregated from any account used to make campaign-related disbursements.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H77D2B407811A45DAAC6868933C9C037D" class="indent1"><num value="6">“(6) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Special rules for certain communications</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H5AE648B355594E8F8DCBD42F4017E472" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exception for communications paid for by political parties and certain political committees</inline>.—</heading><content>This subsection does not apply to any communication to which subsection (d)(2) applies.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H083FD72B7C82480FAC8E724DEEFADA03" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Treatment of video communications lasting 10 seconds or less</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>In the case of a communication to which this subsection applies which is transmitted in a video format, or is an Internet or digital communication which is transmitted in a text or graphic format, the communication shall meet the following requirements:</chapeau>
<clause id="H495CBAEC934D4AE09BB73C4CEED9371C" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>The communication shall include the individual disclosure statement described in paragraph (2)(A) (if the person paying for the communication is an individual) or the organizational disclosure statement described in paragraph (2)(B) (if the person paying for the communication is not an individual).</content></clause>
<clause id="H613AB02CB70B4D929DB6638D6AE4A8F8" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>The statement described in clause (i) shall appear in writing at the end of the communication, or in a crawl along the bottom of the communication, in a clear and conspicuous manner, with a reasonable degree of color contrast between the background and the printed statement, for a period of at least 4 seconds.</content></clause>
<clause id="HAF40E5A8D1504C8A9C6FB5CE88A98DDD" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>The communication shall include, in a clear and conspicuous manner, a website address with a landing page which will provide all of the information described in paragraph (1) with respect to the communication. Such address shall appear for the full duration of the communication.</content></clause>
<clause id="HB33E3C494EB4454EA5769FD107E5B839" class="indent3"><num value="iv">“(iv) </num><content>To the extent that the format in which the communication is made permits the use of a hyperlink, the communication shall include a hyperlink to the website address described in clause (iii).”</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4302/b" id="HE7070C878BDE409A98B73B686F9B46B9" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Application of Expanded Requirements to Public Communications Consisting of Campaign-Related Disbursements</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 318(a) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30120/a">52 U.S.C. 30120(a)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>for the purpose of financing communications expressly advocating the election or defeat of a clearly identified candidate</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>for a campaign-related disbursement, as defined in section 324, consisting of a public communication</quotedText>”.</content></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4302/c" id="H3DB8C36801B84CD1BF1ED82EE33D3BCD" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Exception for Communications Paid for by Political Parties and Certain Political Committees</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 318(d)(2) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30120/d/2">52 U.S.C. 30120(d)(2)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>

<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4302/c/2" id="HA3C92A97C4A44C3794F8617AC66C835C" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>Any communication</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>(A) Any communication</quotedText>”;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4302/c/3" id="H2C267FF3E35A4B14BDC833661F30A7C5" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>which (except to the extent provided in subparagraph (B)) is paid for by a political committee (including a political committee of a political party) and</quotedText>” after “<quotedText>subsection (a)</quotedText>”;</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4302/c/4" id="HE4B08564D9244C318996E26ECB75287F" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>or other person</quotedText>” each place it appears; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4302/c/5" id="H396F7EFDFF4C474FB4947A7BE9BECAB0" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new subparagraph:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HC24F2A19865C4517BC86AEF73AE08782" styleType="traditional">
<subparagraph id="H0C0DCC11567D46FBB0F7817252128E01" class="indent1"><num value="B">“(B)</num><clause id="HB35F163151944F50A023187E153CF636" class="inline"><num value="i">(i) </num><content>This paragraph does not apply to a communication paid for in whole or in part during a calendar year with a campaign-related disbursement, but only if the covered organization making the campaign-related disbursement made campaign-related disbursements (as defined in section 324) aggregating more than $10,000 during such calendar year.</content></clause>
<clause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HDC09788BE86D4EA5BFB2BF822BC990FA" class="indent1"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><chapeau>For purposes of clause (i), in determining the amount of campaign-related disbursements made by a covered organization during a year, there shall be excluded the following:</chapeau>
<subclause id="HB086C5CCC3B64FF1A9CD8577DCFF925E" class="indent2"><num value="I">“(I) </num><content>Any amounts received by the covered organization in the ordinary course of any trade or business conducted by the covered organization or in the form of investments in the covered organization.</content></subclause>

<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4303" id="H830B3F3EA0044C6D85CB4D8735EEAECF"><num value="4303">SEC. 4303. </num><heading>DISCLAIMER REQUIREMENTS FOR COMMUNICATIONS MADE THROUGH PRERECORDED TELEPHONE CALLS.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4303/a" id="H829FF6DBC701432599DC7562B90D0B8B" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Application of Requirements</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4303/a/1" id="H08C84AAFCB544765B64B276185050DD6" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 318(a) of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30120/a">52 U.S.C. 30120(a)</ref>), as amended by section 4205(c), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> after “<quotedText>public communication</quotedText>” each place it appears the following: “<quotedText>(including a telephone call consisting in substantial part of a prerecorded audio message)</quotedText>”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4303/a/2" id="H324EC99CFE284480BB58597E1BB3F949" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Application to communications subject to expanded disclaimer requirements</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 318(e)(1) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30120/e/1">52 U.S.C. 30120(e)(1)</ref>), as added by section 4302(a), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> in the matter preceding subparagraph (A) by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> “<quotedText>which is transmitted in an audio or video format</quotedText>” and <amendingAction type="insert">inserting</amendingAction> “<quotedText>which is transmitted in an audio or video format or which consists of a telephone call consisting in substantial part of a prerecorded audio message</quotedText>”.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4303/b" id="HED8C73E386364A0AB466D1A98419AA77" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Treatment as Communication Transmitted in Audio Format</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4303/b/1" id="HC2913FACA2CA44359E7ADCCEDF4CC2D0" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Communications by candidates or authorized persons</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 318(d) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30120/d">52 U.S.C. 30120(d)</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new paragraph:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HC161B611FFB64C309A749468E53C4763" styleType="OLC">
<paragraph id="H3EE5A66FA4CE4C98AC5217C74F99964E" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prerecorded telephone calls</inline>.—</heading><content>Any communication described in paragraph (1), (2), or (3) of subsection (a) (other than a communication which is subject to subsection (e)) which is a telephone call consisting in substantial part of a prerecorded audio message shall include, in addition to the requirements of such paragraph, the audio statement required under subparagraph (A) of paragraph (1) or the audio statement required under paragraph (2) (whichever is applicable), except that the statement shall be made at the beginning of the telephone call.”</content></paragraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4303/b/2" id="HC7D5577D63784BB3BA40C24088A26075" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Communications subject to expanded disclaimer requirements</inline>.—</heading><content>Section 318(e)(3) of such Act (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30120/e/3">52 U.S.C. 30120(e)(3)</ref>), as added by section 4302(a), <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new subparagraph:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H613AA126394A4214984CF83FF0EACD14" styleType="OLC">
<subparagraph id="H3517163FD7364B76828E8D970921813F" class="indent2"><num value="D">“(D) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prerecorded telephone calls</inline>.—</heading><content>In the case of a communication to which this subsection applies which is a telephone call consisting in substantial part of a prerecorded audio message, the communication shall be considered to be transmitted in an audio format.”</content></subparagraph></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></paragraph></subsection></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4304" id="HD54E5EF632D744FC8B63E66C61B8219F"><num value="4304">SEC. 4304. </num><heading>NO EXPANSION OF PERSONS SUBJECT TO DISCLAIMER REQUIREMENTS ON INTERNET COMMUNICATIONS.</heading><content class="block">Nothing in this subtitle or the amendments made by this subtitle may be construed to require any person who is not required under section 318 of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (as provided under section 110.11 of <ref href="/us/cfr/t11">title 11 of the Code of Federal Regulations</ref>) to include a disclaimer on communications made by the person through the internet to include any disclaimer on any such communications.</content></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stD/s4305" id="HB0AE7B8F84D043179ED5D676A9397CCE"><num value="4305">SEC. 4305. </num><heading>EFFECTIVE DATE.</heading><content class="block">The amendments made by this subtitle shall apply with respect to communications made on or after January 1, 2020, and shall take effect without regard to whether or not the Federal Election Commission has promulgated regulations to carry out such amendments.</content></section></subtitle>

<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stH" id="H3F5F1DDCE9EB4D11B5B50A1D9DB88741"><num value="H">Subtitle H—</num><heading>Limitation and Disclosure Requirements for Presidential Inaugural Committees</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stH/s4701" id="H28285817F7CE4145A4EC6435B469645E"><num value="4701">SEC. 4701. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This subtitle may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="subtitle">Presidential Inaugural Committee Oversight Act</shortTitle>”.</content></section>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stH/s4702" id="H94D3C772514D499F958E5FE6F7805DE9"><num value="4702">SEC. 4702. </num><heading>LIMITATIONS AND DISCLOSURE OF CERTAIN DONATIONS TO, AND DISBURSEMENTS BY, INAUGURAL COMMITTEES.</heading>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stH/s4702/a" id="HB2B815EF404D46FD8CA2C0E88FD3C02E" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Requirements for Inaugural Committees</inline>.—</heading><content>Title III of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30101/etseq">52 U.S.C. 30101 et seq.</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> by <amendingAction type="add">adding</amendingAction> at the end the following new section:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="HB1B3B639E436497492B3E0D5339E8C05" styleType="OLC">
<section id="HEA4C217969EE42A58529BE4C75293F04"><num value="325">“SEC. 325. </num><heading>INAUGURAL COMMITTEES.</heading>
<subsection id="HB82B337AC18A48A487071FED6EA4E009" class="indent0"><num value="a">“(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Prohibited Donations</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="HFC8573C89FD0423697819DFCA92B7231" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>It shall be unlawful—</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HB8AE40D89AD74B27BBF4BA92FCAD96A1" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><chapeau>for an Inaugural Committee—</chapeau>
<clause id="H316B0EDA5D3340188FB26D764358439B" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>to solicit, accept, or receive a donation from a person that is not an individual; or</content></clause>
<clause id="H97BA56AB640C4A80BD29DBC73F1B0BE2" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>to solicit, accept, or receive a donation from a foreign national;</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H3F48CFCF2ECA4AD293300B89F54558FC" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><chapeau>for a person—</chapeau>
<clause id="H938DAED7948A4A5EAAA9AA7C99E82F0B" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>to make a donation to an Inaugural Committee in the name of another person, or to knowingly authorize his or her name to be used to effect such a donation;</content></clause>
<clause id="H90BC916D28C54AB687ADFB52051286C4" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>to knowingly accept a donation to an Inaugural Committee made by a person in the name of another person; or</content></clause>
<clause id="HBD5F3DB8CC7F49059C871F43EA51003C" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>to convert a donation to an Inaugural Committee to personal use as described in paragraph (2); and</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HDA4DB9804A634E5F8A7665D7E0E5626C" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><content>for a foreign national to, directly or indirectly, make a donation, or make an express or implied promise to make a donation, to an Inaugural Committee.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H0393C5E4D3734EF4A7466F6CD9383424" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Conversion of donation to personal use</inline>.—</heading><content>For purposes of paragraph (1)(B)(iii), a donation shall be considered to be converted to personal use if any part of the donated amount is used to fulfill a commitment, obligation, or expense of a person that would exist irrespective of the responsibilities of the Inaugural Committee under <ref href="/us/usc/t36/ch5">chapter 5 of title 36, United States Code</ref>.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H68485BD5D77E46B68422A41116E319F9" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">No effect on disbursement of unused funds to nonprofit organizations</inline>.—</heading><content>Nothing in this subsection may be construed to prohibit an Inaugural Committee from disbursing unused funds to an organization which is described in section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 and is exempt from taxation under section 501(a) of such Code.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H9E2DD71225734370B80EEAC285B1BDA9" class="indent0"><num value="b">“(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Limitation on Donations</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H8293495ACE7741EC87838CC7FB87249A" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>It shall be unlawful for an individual to make donations to an Inaugural Committee which, in the aggregate, exceed $50,000.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H929932DE00404725B127DEB573DDD912" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Indexing</inline>.—</heading><content>At the beginning of each Presidential election year (beginning with 2024), the amount described in paragraph (1) shall be increased by the cumulative percent difference determined in section 315(c)(1)(A) since the previous Presidential election year. If any amount after such increase is not a multiple of $1,000, such amount shall be rounded to the nearest multiple of $1,000.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H02EAE7DEBDB2411FA03CA97A1F6CAC24" class="indent0"><num value="c">“(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Disclosure of Certain Donations and Disbursements</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph id="H494E8ECC9A56417A850DB6EE2FEE038C" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Donations over $1,000</inline>.—</heading>
<subparagraph id="H11CE2501841B4D61BECFB85A0D29748A" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>An Inaugural Committee shall file with the Commission a report disclosing any donation by an individual to the committee in an amount of $1,000 or more not later than 24 hours after the receipt of such donation.</content></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HA913A44B33164A26A1BD4A5662B6F6F6" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Contents of report</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>A report filed under subparagraph (A) shall contain—</chapeau>
<clause id="H61662AF81A904EAB9045796F12AEBC41" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the amount of the donation;</content></clause>
<clause id="HBB47F3D1B9F6477D830AAD8D3380F641" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>the date the donation is received; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H9DEA992B99C54898939D4B69A2C44010" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>the name and address of the individual making the donation.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HBE4FB09DED5E45F8B577652B0CB31863" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Final report</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Not later than the date that is 90 days after the date of the Presidential inaugural ceremony, the Inaugural Committee shall file with the Commission a report containing the following information:</chapeau>
<subparagraph id="HDF467F9221004063ADC89B30857827CD" class="indent2"><num value="A">“(A) </num><chapeau>For each donation of money or anything of value made to the committee in an aggregate amount equal to or greater than $200—</chapeau>
<clause id="H14F13CDD92BB49DEAF17972478EDD300" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>the amount of the donation;</content></clause>
<clause id="H6D6C791A7F4F4A7F95EB364643FF84BF" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>the date the donation is received; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H14558358929B49E6A7526899BE7EB16E" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>the name and address of the individual making the donation.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H76C696D0DC6F4852866E4BC195532778" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><chapeau>The total amount of all disbursements, and all disbursements in the following categories:</chapeau>
<clause id="HF08AA0E42BB74DCA970CA146AF7C1BE9" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>Disbursements made to meet committee operating expenses.</content></clause>
<clause id="HA9620238F3D54482819E98489018C863" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>Repayment of all loans.</content></clause>
<clause id="H558D50B5407542C698A4FB2980E5C2B3" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>Donation refunds and other offsets to donations.</content></clause>
<clause id="H0D154014978F4A7CBB065787E156E266" class="indent3"><num value="iv">“(iv) </num><content>Any other disbursements.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HDF6638E175C646B8BDBDB4FA9E56A566" class="indent2"><num value="C">“(C) </num><chapeau>The name and address of each person—</chapeau>
<clause id="HF7C4AD54558E4D209E0C62C78F7D85CD" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>to whom a disbursement in an aggregate amount or value in excess of $200 is made by the committee to meet a committee operating expense, together with date, amount, and purpose of such operating expense;</content></clause>
<clause id="HE8197C2966104473A281FDA6E8CE4CCA" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>who receives a loan repayment from the committee, together with the date and amount of such loan repayment;</content></clause>
<clause id="HD2138D0EE9A74DD3B59FE04015059668" class="indent3"><num value="iii">“(iii) </num><content>who receives a donation refund or other offset to donations from the committee, together with the date and amount of such disbursement; and</content></clause>
<clause id="H497AF0B7F52E4DDA85FF4E20F1355025" class="indent3"><num value="iv">“(iv) </num><content>to whom any other disbursement in an aggregate amount or value in excess of $200 is made by the committee, together with the date and amount of such disbursement.</content></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H35F3E149DD974B878876B54FE2417EA8" class="indent0"><num value="d">“(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Definitions</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>For purposes of this section:</chapeau>
<paragraph id="HF3BFB03009A842869A80E7CAC21F6870" class="indent1"><num value="1">“(1)</num><subparagraph role="definitions" id="HB5A46AC409F241C4A0DCB8CD861B5387" class="inline"><num value="A">(A) </num><chapeau>The term ‘<term>donation</term>’ includes—</chapeau>
<clause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H1825E36F3E294073A869DEFF9C2F5DF2" class="indent3"><num value="i">“(i) </num><content>any gift, subscription, loan, advance, or deposit of money or anything of value made by any person to the committee; or</content></clause>
<clause changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H08B21E8208C849B99A91B8D51F2A5821" class="indent3"><num value="ii">“(ii) </num><content>the payment by any person of compensation for the personal services of another person which are rendered to the committee without charge for any purpose.</content></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph role="definitions" changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H8A99A00FFA664F4898CAE92309B75B05" class="indent2"><num value="B">“(B) </num><content>The term ‘<term>donation</term>’ does not include the value of services provided without compensation by any individual who volunteers on behalf of the committee.</content></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="HCAC8A22B6C9B4A5E96BE7788EE2F8213" class="indent1"><num value="2">“(2) </num><content>The term ‘<term>foreign national</term>’ has the meaning given that term by section 319(b).</content></paragraph>
<paragraph role="definitions" id="H47F4DFF0D8C6402AB1E06AFC5C10779D" class="indent1"><num value="3">“(3) </num><content>The term ‘<term>Inaugural Committee</term>’ has the meaning given that term by <ref href="/us/usc/t36/s501">section 501 of title 36, United States Code</ref>.”</content></paragraph></subsection></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">.</inline></content></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stH/s4702/b" id="H38E8923BCDA7470F9A0520AC5375E807" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Confirming Amendment Related to Reporting Requirements</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>Section 304 of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (<ref href="/us/usc/t52/s30104">52 U.S.C. 30104</ref>) <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction>—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stH/s4702/b/1" id="HD8FF3642826F404EB343FD21087E0E92" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="delete">striking</amendingAction> subsection (h); and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stH/s4702/b/2" id="H5592520480BA46F89376EC1214C45323" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>by <amendingAction type="redesignate">redesignating</amendingAction> subsection (i) as subsection (h).</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection role="instruction" identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stH/s4702/c" id="H21473E3DB23E4CEFA944EDA635F395DE" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Conforming Amendment Related to Status of Committee</inline>.—</heading><content><ref href="/us/usc/t36/s510">Section 510 of title 36, United States Code</ref>, <amendingAction type="amend">is amended</amendingAction> to read as follows:
<quotedContent changed="added" origin="#HHA00" id="H2E79F5818BEC4CAD9CEC27521603D590" styleType="USC">
<section id="H99DB5D32D2744AD5A6B8FF2B005247AB"><num value="510">“§ 510. </num><heading>Disclosure of and prohibition on certain donations</heading><content class="block">“A committee shall not be considered to be the Inaugural Committee for purposes of this chapter unless the committee agrees to, and meets, the requirements of section 325 of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971.”</content></section></quotedContent><inline role="after-quoted-block">. </inline></content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stH/s4702/d" id="HF8419C7953E342A4A240DF0645D9ECDF" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Effective Date</inline>.—</heading><content>The amendments made by this Act shall apply with respect to Inaugural Committees established under <ref href="/us/usc/t36/ch5">chapter 5 of title 36, United States Code</ref>, for inaugurations held in 2021 and any succeeding year.</content></subsection></section></subtitle>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stI" id="HEBA2C0FA026E4E6AA23DB7440EC80691"><num value="I">Subtitle I—</num><heading>Severability</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tIV/stI/s4801" id="H865DDC6928B348248929133278B83B14"><num value="4801">SEC. 4801. </num><heading>SEVERABILITY.</heading><content class="block">If any provision of this title or amendment made by this title, or the application of a provision or amendment to any person or circumstance, is held to be unconstitutional, the remainder of this title and amendments made by this title, and the application of the provisions and amendment to any person or circumstance, shall not be affected by the holding.</content></section></subtitle></title>

<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA" id="H65CE6BEF2F2943FA8B6A0020FCCA42F7"><num value="A">Subtitle A—</num><heading>Findings Relating to <i>Citizens United</i> Decision</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001" id="H26B32E2122724F8ABC890E4D39EA3FB3"><num value="5001">SEC. 5001. </num><heading>FINDINGS RELATING TO <i>CITIZENS UNITED</i> DECISION.</heading>
<chapeau class="indent0">Congress finds the following:</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001/1" id="H244B5238E1814375B6A75F9C98C6D60F" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>The American Republic was founded on the principle that all people are created equal, with rights and responsibilities as citizens to vote, be represented, speak, debate, and participate in self-government on equal terms regardless of wealth. To secure these rights and responsibilities, our Constitution not only protects the equal rights of all Americans but also provides checks and balances to prevent corruption and prevent concentrated power and wealth from undermining effective self-government.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001/2" id="H8E7744DC36EE49E7BE901FDAA622CCF0" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>The Supreme Court’s decisions in <i>Citizens United</i> v. <i>Federal Election Commission</i>, 558 U.S. 310 (2010) and <i>McCutcheon</i> v. <i>FEC</i>, 572 U.S. 185 (2014), as well as other court decisions, erroneously invalidated even-handed rules about the spending of money in local, State, and Federal elections. These flawed decisions have empowered large corporations, extremely wealthy individuals, and special interests to dominate election spending, corrupt our politics, and degrade our democracy through tidal waves of unlimited and anonymous spending. These decisions also stand in contrast to a long history of efforts by Congress and the States to regulate money in politics to protect democracy, and they illustrate a troubling deregulatory trend in campaign finance-related court decisions. Additionally, an unknown amount of foreign money continues to be spent in our political system as subsidiaries of foreign-based corporations and hostile foreign actors sometimes connected to nation-States work to influence our elections.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001/3" id="H3F359A7E95BA4C128747B4E083CDCE6B" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>The Supreme Court’s misinterpretation of the Constitution to empower monied interests at the expense of the American people in elections has seriously eroded over 100 years of congressional action to promote fairness and protect elections from the toxic influence of money.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001/4" id="HDC85869CFD38463AA85A1B0102442002" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>In 1907, Congress passed the Tillman Act in response to the concentration of corporate power in the post-Civil War Gilded Age. The Act prohibited corporations from making contributions in connection with Federal elections, aiming “not merely to prevent the subversion of the integrity of the electoral process [but] … to sustain the active, alert responsibility of the individual citizen in a democracy for the wise conduct of government”.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001/5" id="H1FCFDF93130446B19E62CB0D0195DCE7" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>By 1910, Congress began passing disclosure requirements and campaign expenditure limits, and dozens of States passed corrupt practices Acts to prohibit corporate spending in elections. States also enacted campaign spending limits, and some States limited the amount that people could contribute to campaigns.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001/6" id="HDCE4BEEEB57C446B889BF9477586CA62" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>In 1947, the Taft-Hartley Act prohibited corporations and unions from making campaign contributions or other expenditures to influence elections. In 1962, a Presidential commission on election spending recommended spending limits and incentives to increase small contributions from more people.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001/7" id="HF0995D77169243D88FA9F87E5CD1AB5E" class="indent1"><num value="7">(7) </num><content>The Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (FECA), as amended in 1974, required disclosure of contributions and expenditures, imposed contribution and expenditure limits for individuals and groups, set spending limits for campaigns, candidates, and groups, implemented a public funding system for Presidential campaigns, and created the Federal Election Commission to oversee and enforce the new rules.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001/8" id="H2212949FA02244EABAE57CF0AAE0DCC3" class="indent1"><num value="8">(8) </num><content>In the wake of <i>Citizens United</i> and other damaging Federal court decisions, Americans have witnessed an explosion of outside spending in elections. Outside spending increased nearly 900 percent between the 2008 and 2016 Presidential election years. Indeed, the 2018 elections once again made clear the overwhelming political power of wealthy special interests, to the tune of over $5,000,000,000. And as political entities adapt to a post-<i>Citizens United</i>, post-<i>McCutcheon</i> landscape, these trends are getting worse, as evidenced by the experience in the 2018 midterm congressional elections, where outside spending more than doubled from the previous midterm cycle.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001/9" id="HF980E16411294A1AAE304B101F3C342A" class="indent1"><num value="9">(9) </num><content>The torrent of money flowing into our political system has a profound effect on the democratic process for everyday Americans, whose voices and policy preferences are increasingly being drowned out by those of wealthy special interests. The more campaign cash from wealthy special interests can flood our elections, the more policies that favor those interests are reflected in the national political agenda. When it comes to policy preferences, our Nation’s wealthiest tend to have fundamentally different views than do average Americans when it comes to issues ranging from unemployment benefits to the minimum wage to health care coverage.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001/10" id="HF2F09B80A6C742428FF56E198EE1D87D" class="indent1"><num value="10">(10) </num><content>The Court has tied the hands of Congress and the States, severely restricting them from setting reasonable limits on campaign spending. For example, the Court has held that only the Government’s interest in preventing quid pro quo corruption, like bribery, or the appearance of such corruption, can justify limits on campaign contributions. More broadly, the Court has severely curtailed attempts to reduce the ability of the Nation’s wealthiest and most powerful to skew our democracy in their favor by buying outsized influence in our elections. Because this distortion of the Constitution has prevented truly meaningful regulation or reform of the way we finance elections in America, a constitutional amendment is needed to achieve a democracy for all the people.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001/11" id="H4704ED74C4E54D46BAF34265C3DCA2E5" class="indent1"><num value="11">(11) </num><content>Since the landmark <i>Citizens United</i> decision, 19 States and nearly 800 municipalities, including large cities like New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, and Philadelphia, have gone on record supporting a constitutional amendment. Transcending political leanings and geographic location, voters in States and municipalities across the country that have placed amendment questions on the ballot have routinely supported these initiatives by considerably large margins.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001/12" id="H4FBDEE48F5BD4FAF8CC46170FDC16E9B" class="indent1"><num value="12">(12) </num><content>At the same time millions of Americans have signed petitions, marched, called their Members of Congress, written letters to the editor, and otherwise demonstrated their public support for a constitutional amendment to overturn <i>Citizens United</i> that will allow Congress to reign in the outsized influence of unchecked money in politics. Dozens of organizations, representing tens of millions of individuals, have come together in a shared strategy of supporting such an amendment.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stA/s5001/13" id="H9ED13AEC6A034341BC2448CC13FCD6F9" class="indent1"><num value="13">(13) </num><content>In order to protect the integrity of democracy and the electoral process and to ensure political equality for all, the Constitution should be amended so that Congress and the States may regulate and set limits on the raising and spending of money to influence elections and may distinguish between natural persons and artificial entities, like corporations, that are created by law, including by prohibiting such artificial entities from spending money to influence elections.</content></paragraph></section></subtitle>
<subtitle identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB" id="H7A90D12C23064104AC09DFE0B7D69676"><num value="B">Subtitle B—</num><heading>Congressional Elections</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/s5100" id="H3669ACD4BE7C48F5BDD4309FDF433E65"><num value="5100">SEC. 5100. </num><heading>SHORT TITLE.</heading><content class="block">This subtitle may be cited as the “<shortTitle role="subtitle">Government By the People Act of 2019</shortTitle>”.</content></section><part identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1" id="H13CEC2F859664816A42783F92AFE31B3"><num value="1">PART 1—</num><heading>MY VOICE VOUCHER PILOT PROGRAM</heading>
<section identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101" id="HB3369FB740504A1CA3582F5639CA659C"><num value="5101">SEC. 5101. </num><heading>ESTABLISHMENT OF PILOT PROGRAM.</heading>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/a" id="H7B065EB434C941E8BE18C962281E2C2E" class="indent0"><num value="a">(a) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Establishment</inline>.—</heading><content>The Federal Election Commission (hereafter in this part referred to as the “Commission”) shall establish a pilot program under which the Commission shall select 3 eligible States to operate a voucher pilot program which is described in section 5102 during the program operation period.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/b" id="H6C29E900F17047A88FE694D26728A085" class="indent0"><num value="b">(b) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Eligibility of States</inline>.—</heading><chapeau>A State is eligible to be selected to operate a voucher pilot program under this part if, not later than 180 days after the beginning of the program application period, the State submits to the Commission an application containing—</chapeau>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/b/1" id="HB675AC0D7FA14D1EB731E4E80427C944" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><content>information and assurances that the State will operate a voucher program which contains the elements described in section 5102(a);</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/b/2" id="HD07385FFB54F48209E5C483465C456D6" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><content>information and assurances that the State will establish fraud prevention mechanisms described in section 5102(b);</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/b/3" id="H4545A7D126CA4026A79C096F9567063A" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><content>information and assurances that the State will establish a commission to oversee and implement the program as described in section 5102(c);</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/b/4" id="HCAC8E6803B7044E8A81FE372029A4CAD" class="indent1"><num value="4">(4) </num><content>information and assurances that the State will carry out a public information campaign as described in section 5102(d);</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/b/5" id="HA8670D7804264B6E95A0CC924E990079" class="indent1"><num value="5">(5) </num><content>information and assurances that the State will submit reports as required under section 5103; and</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/b/6" id="HC3C7D3EDE26249E6A27AD5D5FEAA51BE" class="indent1"><num value="6">(6) </num><content>such other information and assurances as the Commission may require.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/c" id="H4E064557458C46C788CE0B832F3B68F1" class="indent0"><num value="c">(c) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Selection of Participating States</inline>.—</heading>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/c/1" id="H9AB051E68D654E659A60F267607FBB2C" class="indent1"><num value="1">(1) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">In general</inline>.—</heading><content>Not later than 1 year after the beginning of the program application period, the Commission shall select the 3 States which will operate voucher pilot programs under this part.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/c/2" id="H1B6134E7C45749CEA99D69D9C3B2CAB5" class="indent1"><num value="2">(2) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Criteria</inline>.—</heading><content>In selecting States for the operation of the voucher pilot programs under this part, the Commission shall apply such criteria and metrics as the Commission considers appropriate to determine the ability of a State to operate the program successfully, and shall attempt to select States in a variety of geographic regions and with a variety of political party preferences.</content></paragraph>
<paragraph identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/c/3" id="HFE1422F94318491CB8812C487C257868" class="indent1"><num value="3">(3) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">No supermajority required for selection</inline>.—</heading><content>The selection of States by the Commission under this subsection shall require the approval of only half of the Members of the Commission.</content></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/d" id="H92E6687323D04974B93E2B86F5B27426" class="indent0"><num value="d">(d) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Duties of States During Program Preparation Period</inline>.—</heading><content>During the program preparation period, each State selected to operate a voucher pilot program under this part shall take such actions as may be necessary to ensure that the State will be ready to operate the program during the program operation period, and shall complete such actions not later than 90 days before the beginning of the program operation period.</content></subsection>
<subsection identifier="/us/bill/116/hr/1/dB/tV/stB/pt1/s5101/e" id="HB3E4F0C80CCD4C86917E28A3F5DE0143" class="indent0"><num value="e">(e) </num><heading><inline class="smallCaps">Termination</inline>.—</heading><content>Each voucher pilot program under this part shall terminate as of the first day after the program operation period.</content></subsection>
